items.title: RSH finds serious failings at Bury Metropolitan Borough Council
items.summary: The Regulator of Social Housing has given Bury Metropolitan Borough Council a C3 consumer grade after finding serious failings relating to health and safety, engagement with tenants, and service and performance information. During an inspec
items.bodyHtml:
The Regulator of Social Housing has given Bury Metropolitan Borough Council a C3 consumer grade after finding serious failings relating to health and safety, engagement with tenants, and service and performance information.

During an inspection, RSH found limited evidence of meaningful opportunities for tenants to scrutinise their landlord’s performance or influence how its services are delivered.

Significant improvement is also needed in the accessibility of information about landlord services and how services are performing. Bury MBC had also failed to meet the technical and survey requirements of the Tenant Satisfaction Measures.

Additionally, the Greater Manchester local authority was unable to provide sufficient assurance on the accuracy of its health and safety compliance information.

RSH identified weaknesses in Bury MBC’s repairs service (including meeting legal timescales for investigating, identifying and repairing hazards like damp and mould), the approach to anti-social behaviour and hate incidents, understanding and responding to tenants’ diverse needs and complaint handling. While a range of improvements are in progress, processes and systems were still being embedded and Bury MBC was unable to demonstrate that these improvements had consistently translated into better outcomes for tenants.

RSH did, however, find evidence that Bury MBC was reducing its backlog of overdue repairs, taking action to improve the quality of its data and had further service improvements planned. Bury MBC has worked constructively with RSH, and RSH will continue to engage intensively with the council as it addresses these issues and delivers the improvements required. 

RSH Deputy Chief Executive Kate Dodsworth said:

“It’s really important that landlords give tenants meaningful opportunities to scrutinise their performance.

“They should listen carefully to what tenants say and act on this to improve their services.

“They also need to have accurate health and safety information to make sure tenants’ homes are safe and carry out repairs promptly when needed.”

RSH also published stability checks for 19 landlords today including Peabody Trust, Sanctuary Housing Association, The Guinness Partnership, Southern Housing and Hyde Housing Association Limited.

Stability checks are the annual assessment of a landlord’s financial position, business plan and risk profile, used to determine whether its financial viability grading remains appropriate.

The process no longer includes a review of governance gradings and is focused solely on financial viability.

Kate Dodsworth said:

“A strong financial footing underpins everything a landlord does.

“Stability checks are an important part of our ongoing oversight, helping to ensure landlords remain financially viable and able to deliver for current and future tenants.”

ENDS

items.title: “‘喝大水’越多越健康”系谣言丨中新真探
items.summary: 中新网11月11日电 “多喝水有益”不等于“水喝得越多越好”。如果短时间内摄入大量水分，超过身体排水能力，血液中的钠浓度就可能被稀释，进而引发低钠血症，也就是俗称的“水中毒”。此外，肾病、心脏病等基础疾病的患者，以及服用某些可能影响水钠平衡的药物的人群，盲目大量饮水的风险更高。(来源：@科学辟谣 中国新闻网微博)

items.title: Prime Minister hails major investment in UK renewables
items.summary: Prime Minister welcomes green light for two major new UK offshore wind projects ahead of attendance at COP31 Includes major £12 billion investment in UK renewables, believed to be the biggest in UK history, powering millions of homes and su
items.bodyHtml:
• Prime Minister welcomes green light for two major new UK offshore wind projects ahead of attendance at COP31 
  • Includes major £12 billion investment in UK renewables, believed to be the biggest in UK history, powering millions of homes and supporting thousands of jobs 
  • Seizing the opportunities of the green transition is boosting our energy security, bringing long-term growth for communities across the country and tackling the climate crisis.  

Thousands of jobs will be supported as two major offshore wind projects mark progress towards delivering clean homegrown energy for millions of homes, ahead of the Prime Minister’s travel to the COP31 Leaders’ Summit in Türkiye. 

Energy company RWE, together with global investment firm KKR, have announced a total investment of £12 billion, believed to be the biggest of its kind in UK history to date. It will give the green light to its Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore wind farms, set to be operational by 2030 and delivering clean, secure, homegrown power to homes and businesses that will protect families from global fossil fuel price shocks.  

The investment comes as the Prime Minister heads to the COP31 summit, underlining how Britain’s action on climate change and clean energy is bringing good, skilled jobs and new opportunities for local people in industrial and coastal communities across the country. 

On top of bolstering the UK’s green energy future, the investment will support more than 2,400 jobs during construction and operation, and once operational, the wind farms will have the capacity to supply the equivalent of around three million UK homes. Alongside making an important contribution to domestic energy security, clean, homegrown power will protect the UK from global energy shocks raising energy prices and bring down bills for good. 

The decision marks a major milestone for the project, with the developers now making their final investment commitment to deliver the projects. Onshore works are already well advanced, with construction offshore set to begin in early 2027. 

The financing for these projects includes a £1 billion investment from the UK’s National Wealth Fund - the UK’s publicly-owned policy bank that aims to drive more than £100 billion of finance into the UK economy. This investment, the National Wealth Fund’s largest in offshore wind to date, demonstrates how the right use of public money can help unlock private investment and generate a return for the taxpayer, as well as powering homes with clean homegrown power Britain controls.  

The government recently announced a new, additional Energy Wealth Fund to take this mission further. The fund will be linked to the Government’s future revenues from the North Sea, investing in renewable and low carbon energy projects and support the net zero transition – starting with a £2 billion injection of funding. 

On top of this, Scottish-headquartered SSE has announced that the latest phase of its major offshore wind farm, Berwick Bank B, will back 2,677 skilled jobs in manufacturing, engineering and project delivery across the north of England and Scotland, with the company contracting Siemens Energy for the manufacturing of wind turbines and substation platforms. This includes the creation of 130 new project delivery roles in Glasgow and Montrose.

At its full capacity, Berwick Bank, off the East coast of Scotland, could become the world’s largest offshore wind farm, capable of meeting more than 6% of current UK electricity demand. Its delivery would strengthen long-term energy security and help deliver the homegrown, affordable energy the country needs. 

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

This major investment in UK renewables is a vote of confidence for building in Britain. And it is great news for billpayers because every turbine we put up is power under British control, not at the mercy of events on the other side of the world.

With coastal communities from Scotland to East Anglia powering Britain’s future, the places that host this energy benefit from the jobs and opportunities that it brings.

Our National Wealth Fund means that public investment is working alongside private capital to build homegrown energy and bring a return for the taxpayer. Because for me, a clean energy future is one that brings down bills.

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said:

This is another vote of confidence in British homegrown, clean energy.

Investment in offshore wind and clean power is creating quality jobs and rebuilding industry, while delivering the clean power we need to lower bills and reach net zero.

As the world gathers at COP31, Britain is leading from the front as a renewable energy powerhouse, turning the fight against climate change into a brighter future for British companies, industrial communities, and future generations.

CEO of RWE AG Markus Krebber said:

Together with KKR, we are delivering two of the UK’s largest offshore wind projects, strengthening domestic electricity generation and making an important contribution to the country’s long-term energy security.

Co-Head of European Infrastructure at KKR, Vincent Policard, continued:

Our work with RWE demonstrates how private capital can help turn the UK’s energy ambitions into reality, supporting economic growth and delivering critical infrastructure capable of powering around three million UK homes.

SSE Chief Executive Martin Pibworth said:

This is public-private partnership in action. Clear political direction, matched by businesses prepared to invest, is translating into real-world investment in British jobs, skills and manufacturing. From Hull, Newcastle and Manchester to Glasgow and Montrose, you can see what that means for communities across the country.

Berwick Bank B is a huge opportunity for the UK and, working with Siemens Energy, we’re backing those industrial capabilities while building the infrastructure needed for a more affordable and secure energy system.

And it’s a powerful and timely example as world leaders gather at COP31. There is already a clear acknowledgement that clean electrification is the route to decarbonisation, greater energy security and sustainably lower bills. We hope to see the ambition needed to turn that recognition into more investment like this.

The announcement is part of the government’s efforts towards a more affordable, clean energy system, with stronger consumer protections, greater public control and communities sharing in the benefits of renewable and low carbon power. 

Last week saw the introduction of the Energy Independence Bill, a down payment on reforms that will put affordability at the heart of the energy system and unlock barriers to delivering clean power. 

Measures include bringing rogue operators under greater public oversight, strengthening protections for households and businesses, and giving local people more control over and a greater stake in the clean energy projects built around them. 

The government is protecting households from rising costs through removing standing charges and giving households £100 to help them pay their bills this winter, and putting Britain in control of its energy future, through a fair transition to green energy and seizing on the opportunities presented by renewables.

items.title: New Royal Navy-Led Northern Navies Initiative
items.summary: Royal Navy spearheads landmark Northern Navies Initiative, with Joint Expeditionary Force allies to increase collective security The initiative gets allied navies working more closely together, adding to NATO’s deterrence and defence in the
items.bodyHtml:
• Royal Navy spearheads landmark Northern Navies Initiative, with Joint Expeditionary Force allies to increase collective security
  • The initiative gets allied navies working more closely together, adding to NATO’s deterrence and defence in the Baltic Sea, High North and North Atlantic
  • First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins signed the agreement onboard HMS Prince of Wales at a historic International Sea Power Conference in Oslo, Norway

The Royal Navy and its Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) allies have signed a historic Northern Navies Initiative agreement that will increase security across northern Europe, the North Atlantic and Baltic Sea. This agreement aims to support maritime deterrence and defence for the citizens of the UK and other JEF nations. The historic agreement also sends a powerful signal of unity in response to a changing threat landscape

The Northern Navies Initiative also seeks to make the JEF NATO’s maritime vanguard in the North Atlantic, High North and Baltic, able to act early, combine quickly and transition seamlessly into NATO command should the Alliance need to mobilise at scale.

Signed amid an increasingly challenging security environment, the Northern Navies Initiative shows how the UK is working with its allies to step up European security and deterrence. 

Speaking after signing the historic Northern Navies Initiative on board HMS Prince of Wales during the International Sea Power Conference in Oslo, First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins said: 

After nine months of hard work, I’m delighted that the JEF Northern Navies Initiative has today taken a huge step forward.

Together, we have shown what is possible when like-minded nations are united by a common purpose.

The threats we face are multiplying and that we must rise to the challenge before us.

The agreement signals closer maritime co-operation among JEF partners. They will operate in the same way, train to the same standard, plan together before a crisis and support one another, including by developing compatible equipment. The High North is a challenging environment where closer co-operation with JEF partners will allow each nation to learn lessons quickly and efficiently from each other, using the shared experience to rapidly develop capabilities that could help win a war.

The High North is changing fast, shaped by climate change, growing economic interest and increased geopolitical competition. What happens there affects UK weather, food supply and national security. The UK will respond as a reliable neighbour, a partner in science and stewardship, and a steadfast ally, working with JEF partners to keep the region peaceful, stable and cooperative.

It also recognises the growing threat posed by hostile activity below the threshold of armed conflict. This includes risks to critical undersea infrastructure, malicious seabed activity and other forms of hybrid aggression.

In practice, greater interoperability means a Royal Navy frigate could transfer operational responsibility to another JEF member without losing momentum. This would let allied navies to work seamlessly together. One nation’s task group could direct allied sensors and uncrewed vessels, while a warship could repair, refuel and resupply in an allied port rather than returning home.

The JEF will make its equipment interoperable by design. This will let future autonomous platforms plug in and out of each other’s command and control systems, creating one large maritime force instead of 10 separate ones. It will also let the JEF bring large numbers of platforms to bear in a co-ordinated way.

This initiative, signed by representatives of all 10 JEF maritime nations, delivers on a Statement of Intent proposed by the First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins in London last April.

The Royal Navy will also bring the first phase of Atlantic Net, part of Atlantic Bastion, into operation within months. Working with Ocean Infinity, it will help detect hostile underwater activity earlier and protect critical infrastructure. Allies in NATO and the JEF will also benefit from a clearer picture of what is happening beneath the surface.

NATO provides the foundation, including the standards, plans and framework for collective defence. The JEF brings a smaller group of closely aligned navies together so they can work more closely, more routinely and at a higher state of readiness.

The Royal Navy is also renewing its own fleet. It is embarking on its most extensive rebuilding programme since the Second World War. The existing programme will use 280,000 tonnes of new steel, rising to around 450,000 tonnes when planned programmes are included.

The UK is also putting in £100m of new investment to progress the transformation of the UK Commando Force into a Warfighting Formation focused on the High North because of its growing importance, including aiming to increase the number of Royal Marines regularly deployed in the region.

NATO provides the foundation, including the standards, plans and framework for collective defence. The JEF brings a smaller group of closely aligned navies together so they can work more closely, more routinely and at a higher state of readiness.

The Royal Navy is also renewing its own fleet. It is embarking on its most extensive rebuilding programme since the Second World War. The existing programme will use 280,000 tonnes of new steel, rising to around 450,000 tonnes when planned programmes are included.

The UK is also putting in £100m of new investment to progress the transformation of the UK Commando Force into a Warfighting Formation focused on the High North because of its growing importance, including aiming to increase the number of Royal Marines regularly deployed in the region.

items.title: RAF handed keys to new facilities at RAF Leeming
items.summary: New facilities have been handed over to the Air C2 (Command and Control) Force, at RAF Leeming in Northallerton, marking the first project to do so under a landmark contract with the Ministry of Defence (MOD). The Air C2 (Command and Contro
items.bodyHtml:
New facilities have been handed over to the Air C2 (Command and Control) Force, at RAF Leeming in Northallerton, marking the first project to do so under a landmark contract with the Ministry of Defence (MOD).

The Air C2 (Command and Control) Force is responsible for 24/7 air surveillance of the UK, assigned NATO airspace, and other overseas locations, as well as directing military air systems to safeguard the UK and its NATO allies.

Construction began in September 2025 on the c£15 million project to deliver new offices and a 32-bed Single Living Accommodation (SLA) block; essential infrastructure that will enable the RAF to make best use of its estate while also delivering capabilities which are critical to Defence.

Construction has been managed on behalf of the MOD by the Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO), with Galliford Try awarded the contract to develop the design and deliver the required infrastructure at RAF Leeming, and Arcadis supporting with design assurance.

This was both the first project to break ground and the first to complete under a contract that was signed in 2023 to deliver key projects under the MOD’s Defence Estate Optimisation (DEO) Portfolio. DEO is the single biggest estates change programme within Defence, investing in a smaller, more efficient estate.

This landmark contract for MOD saw seven contractors agree to deliver a large number of regional packages of work in one process. This allows them to share best practice and innovative design options that focus on meeting the needs of our military personnel while enabling a consistent approach to sustainable building practices. 

Both the office and SLA buildings at RAF Leeming used a pre-cast concrete construction system which delivers high levels of air tightness and energy efficiency. The buildings are heated with air source heat pumps, powered in part by solar panels, and utilise harvested rainwater, creating sustainable facilities that are cost-effective to operate and maintain.

At an event to mark the occasion, the buildings were handed over to Air Officer Commanding 2 Group Air Vice-Marshal Anthony Lyle and Commander Air Bases, Air Commodore Simon Blackwell, by DIO, with the project team and contractors in attendance.

DIO’s project manager Nicola Bond said:

Air C2 Force can now complete their move to RAF Leeming, where we have delivered new sustainable infrastructure to support their vital work. Since relocating from RAF Scampton in 2022, Air C2 Force has been based at RAF Leeming, RAF Boulmer and RRH Staxton Wold, and it is wonderful to be bringing this journey to a successful conclusion.

This project, like any, has brought challenges but the collaboration between the RAF, DIO and external partners has been key to a successful build completion and handover, and I am very proud of the infrastructure my team has delivered.

Outside of the project, Galliford Try has given back to our RAF personnel stationed at RAF Leeming by funding and refurbishing the site’s Cinebowl as part of a social value initiative. The Cinebowl provides entertainment and recreation facilities to the Service families based at the remote site and contains a cinema and ten-pin bowling.

items.title: Joint Statement on the Withdrawal Agreement Joint Committee, 10 November 2026
items.summary: The European Union (EU) and United Kingdom (UK) today held a meeting of the Withdrawal Agreement Joint Committee in Brussels. The Joint Committee co-chairs took stock of the state of play of the implementation of the Withdrawal Agreement si
items.bodyHtml:
The European Union (EU) and United Kingdom (UK) today held a meeting of the Withdrawal Agreement Joint Committee in Brussels. The Joint Committee co-chairs took stock of the state of play of the implementation of the Withdrawal Agreement since the last meeting on 2 February 2026. They reaffirmed the EU and UK’s shared commitment to the full, timely, and faithful implementation of the Agreement in all its parts and agreed to undertake all the necessary action to reflect that in practice. 

The co-chairs reiterated their joint commitment to protecting citizens’ rights, which are of utmost priority for both sides, noting that almost 6 million EU citizens and 1 million UK nationals are protected by the Withdrawal Agreement. They highlighted the importance of ensuring a smooth transition for citizens from temporary to permanent residence over the course of 2027, so that citizens can fully enjoy the protections provided by the Agreement. The co-chairs expressed their strong joint commitment to step up work with a view to finding solutions to all structural issues impacting everyday lives of citizens, so they can fully enjoy their rights to live, work and travel, their benefits and safeguards, now and for the decades to come. The co-chairs also underscored the importance of the work on social security coordination for the full protection of citizens on both sides of the Channel.

The co-chairs recalled the fundamental role of the Windsor Framework in avoiding a hard border on the island of Ireland and ensuring the protection of the EU Single Market, to which Northern Ireland has a unique access, and the integrity of the UK’s Internal Market. They reaffirmed their strong commitment to implementing all the elements of the Windsor Framework, for the benefit of people and businesses in Northern Ireland and for the protection of the EU Single Market. They welcomed the progress made which delivers new benefits across areas, including in facilitating the movements of consumer parcels delivered to Northern Ireland, the protected access to steel for Northern Ireland traders under new measures and the simplifications in the operation of duty-related schemes for goods that stay in the UK. They agreed to accelerate the delivery of the safeguards for the protection of the EU Single Market in all areas. In particular, they agreed to strengthen efforts in the implementation of the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures, with a view to ensuring that all agri-foods are moved to Northern Ireland in accordance with the Windsor Framework rules. They underscored the importance of respecting existing agreements and commitments, including in the SPS area, as the EU and the UK work to strengthen their bilateral partnership, which would also bring additional benefits to Northern Ireland.

The co-chairs discussed the progress made at technical level under the auspices of the Specialised Committee on the Protocol relating to the Sovereign Base Areas in Cyprus and agreed that it is important to finalise the work by the next meeting of the Joint Committee.

The co-chairs adopted three Joint Committee decisions relating to Social Security Coordination, Artificial Intelligence and Forced Labour. They welcomed an EU-UK declaration on the application of Windsor Framework provisions, which clarifies that handling fees for consumer parcels would be treated like customs duties, thus ensuring that they would not be paid on goods staying in the UK and any fees would be collected and kept by UK authorities for goods at risk of entering the EU. As regards the addition of the Cyber Resilience Act to the Windsor Framework, the co-chairs agreed to examine all possibilities to maintain the good functioning of the Framework and take the needed decisions in the future to this effect. Finally, they adopted the Joint Committee Annual Report for the year 2025.

The co-chairs agreed to continue working at pace on implementing the Withdrawal Agreement, which constitutes, together with the Trade and Cooperation Agreement and the recent Agreement in respect of Gibraltar, a solid foundation for strengthening bilateral relations in view of the EU-UK Summit on 20 November 2026.

Notes

  1. Decision No 2/2026 of the Joint Committee established by the Agreement on the withdrawal of the UK from the EU: amending Part I of Annex I to the Agreement
  2. Decision No 3/2026 of the Joint Committee established by the Agreement on the withdrawal of the UK from the EU: adding a newly adopted Union act to Annex 2 to the Windsor Framework
  3. Decision No 4/2026 of the Joint Committee established by the Agreement on the withdrawal of the UK from the EU: adding a newly adopted Union act to Annex 2 to the Windsor Framework
  4. Joint Declaration on the application of Article 5 of the Windsor Framework

items.title: Inspection report published: An inspection of the UK-France Agreement on the Prevention of Dangerous Journeys (Operation Hillmore) (March – June 2026)
items.summary: Initially established as a ten-month pilot, Operation Hillmore tested ways of returning to France individuals who arrived in the UK illegally by small boats, while simultaneously providing a controlled legal route for eligible migrants in F
items.bodyHtml:
Initially established as a ten-month pilot, Operation Hillmore tested ways of returning to France individuals who arrived in the UK illegally by small boats, while simultaneously providing a controlled legal route for eligible migrants in France to enter the UK. The pilot was established with considerable speed and was due to end on 11 June 2026 but was extended until 1 October 2026.

The inspection examined whether the pilot was meeting its aims, the arrangements in place to evaluate its effectiveness, including how lessons learned were identified and applied, and the challenges associated with any transition from pilot to full implementation.

The inspection found that the pilot demonstrated that a jointly linked IN and OUT agreement could be established and made to work using existing practices and ways of working that were legally robust. Key contributors were the high priority and availability of resources given to Hillmore within the Home Office and strong leadership of the pilot coordinating work across the migration and borders system.

However, the inspection also found that clear criteria for assessing the overall success of the pilot were not established at the outset. The pilot’s overtly stated aims focused on high-level strategic objectives such as deterring migrants from using small boats where multiple other factors were in play. This makes it difficult to evaluate Operation Hillmore’s specific contribution to any reduction in small boat arrivals.

There is much to be learnt from Operation Hillmore that could inform future work within the Home Office and an extensive lessons learnt exercise needs to be held as soon as possible, before the redeployment of key staff.

The report makes three recommendations intended to strengthen the design, delivery and evaluation of future Home Office pilots. The inspection report was sent to the Home Secretary on 16 July 2026. The Home Office has fully accepted all three recommendations. I am encouraged to see that work is already taking place to deliver on my recommendations.

John Tuckett, Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration 

10 November 2026

items.title: Strengthened guidance to take the next leap to phone-free schools
items.summary: Children will benefit from distraction-free learning under strengthened mobile phone guidance to help schools take the next step towards a truly phone-free school day. The strengthened guidance will make clear that schools should go beyond
items.bodyHtml:
Children will benefit from distraction-free learning under strengthened mobile phone guidance to help schools take the next step towards a truly phone-free school day.

The strengthened guidance will make clear that schools should go beyond ‘not seen, not heard’ - where phones may remain in pupils’ bags - and adopt whole-school strategies that keep phones out of use and inaccessible throughout the school day.

Access to mobile phones risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other. Evidence shows phones can cause distraction and disruption in lessons, making it harder for pupils to focus and engage with learning.

Polling published in March this year found that 40% of children aged 9–16 were turning down real-world opportunities to spend time online. The latest PISA evidence also found a significant international decline in reading and maths performance, alongside growing concerns about digital distraction.

And the problem goes beyond the classroom. The Milburn review interim report warned that disengagement can begin as early as 12 or 13 years old, with pupils saying they stayed up as late as 3am scrolling on their phones.

Schools should be a place that provides a clear break from those pressures, protecting the school day as a time to learn, connect and engage with others.

While most schools set out that phones should be not seen and not heard, only 16% of secondary pupils say phone rules are followed all of the time, and with the rapid increase in technology take-up and emerging evidence, pupils, schools and parents need more clarity.

Some schools are already putting stronger whole-school approaches into practice through lockable pouches, collection at the start of the day, secure storage or prohibiting phones onsite altogether. The strengthened guidance will build on this leadership, giving every school clearer backing to keep phones inaccessible and helping parents and pupils understand what a truly phone-free school day means.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said:

Children should not be using smartphones at any point during the school day, full stop. That’s why we’re strengthening our guidance to take the next leap towards truly phone-free schools.

Schools are already leading the way. We’re backing heads and teachers with a clear message for parents and pupils: school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling.

Alongside our curriculum reforms, this is about making school unmissable – giving every child more chances to learn, connect and thrive.

Dame Rachel de Souza, Children’s Commissioner for England said:

I’ve spoken to children across the country and have had a million responses to my final survey – young people see the benefits and the risks of technology, including in school.

I welcome strong action to stop phones distracting pupils and disrupting the school day. I know most headteachers already restrict phone use in their schools and I would like to see support for all heads to apply this important policy.

This must be part of a bigger conversation about giving children the best possible start to life. We all have a responsibility to make sure young people can explore the online world safely, but they also need and want more opportunities to learn, connect and play without the need for a screen.

Caty Reid, Headteacher of Clayton Hall Academy, said:

Students deserve time in their school day to concentrate on learning and enjoy being with their friends. We welcome the Department for Education’s plans to make the expectation of a fully phone-free school day clearer.

At Clayton Hall Academy, we introduced providing every student in Years 7 to 11 with their own pouch. Phones are switched off and locked away on arrival, then unlocked at the end of the school day.

Since introducing the approach, we have seen students playing and talking together more, and staff have reported better engagement in lessons. Attendance has also improved, and we have seen fewer incidents of hurtful behaviour online. Those everyday moments of conversation and friendship are an important part of school life.

The new phone guidance comes as the government embarks on major reforms to ensure no child is left behind and make school unmissable. Based on all the latest evidence from PISA to Milburn, the reforms will strengthen reading, writing, speaking and listening, and numeracy, restore a full three-year Key Stage 3 and make more time for enrichment.

The Education Secretary’s commitment to give oracy equal status to reading and writing will strengthen every child’s ability to communicate and connect with confidence.

The new curriculum will also restore Key Stage 3 as a distinct three-year phase, giving pupils more time to master the fundamentals and experience a broad, engaging education. Schools will be expected not to start GCSE specifications early for large cohorts or routinely require pupils to narrow their options early.

The strengthened phone guidance and curriculum reforms are intended to work together to protect time and attention for learning, while giving children more opportunities to read, speak, listen, connect and develop the confidence and skills to thrive.

A new consultation on technology in the classroom launching today will build on this work, to ensure clear parameters are met to give teachers, parents and pupils confidence that any technology used to help children’s learning meets world-leading robust safety standards.

The consultation will explore independent safety certification for EdTech, giving parents and schools confidence that new technology is safe while allowing responsible innovation to thrive.

Emma Harrison, Business Specialist at the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), said:

Keeping children safe from harm is every school’s absolute priority. While education technology can provide many benefits, it is of paramount importance that it is safe and reliable.

Schools put a lot of work into ensuring the safety of any products they use, and a certification scheme has the potential to support schools in purchasing decisions and give them an additional layer of assurance when dealing with new forms of technology as they emerge.

We look forward to responding to the government’s consultation.

From distraction-free school days to safer technology and a stronger focus on the skills that make us human, this is about getting the balance right.

Together, the strengthened phone guidance, curriculum reforms and work on safer technology aim to help every child focus, connect and flourish at school, with technology enhancing skills and development rather than replacing them.

items.title: £90 million investment for new drones and sensors to protect undersea cables and hunt Russian submarines
items.summary: First phase of the Royal Navy’s Atlantic Bastion programme will deliver new drones, sensors and AI systems to protect undersea cables and energy networks. Known as Atlantic Net, the new tech will work alongside the Royal Navy’s crewed fleet
items.bodyHtml:
• First phase of the Royal Navy’s Atlantic Bastion programme will deliver new drones, sensors and AI systems to protect undersea cables and energy networks.
  • Known as Atlantic Net, the new tech will work alongside the Royal Navy’s crewed fleet to hunt Russian submarines, protect the nuclear deterrent and critical undersea infrastructure.
  • New agreement with Hampshire-based company Ocean Infinity Solutions will support almost 200 skilled new jobs, making defence an engine for growth.

The UK will be more secure from Russian undersea threats in the North Atlantic following a new £90 million investment in new drones, sensors and AI systems for the Royal Navy.

The new framework with British company Ocean Infinity Solutions, will strengthen the Royal Navy’s ability to protect crucial shipping routes and undersea infrastructure.

The advanced system, known as Atlantic Net will see the Navy equipped with a new network of autonomous systems operating across the North Atlantic.

These will include advanced sensors, which will help detect Russian submarines and nefarious activity and uncrewed systems, which will be able to patrol the depths of the seas, hunting down threats.

This high-tech net will create a single surveillance service that will provide submarine-hunting warships and Astute-class submarines with earlier warning of threats and a clearer picture of activity beneath the surface.

The framework that is due to be signed today is part of the Royal Navy’s wider Atlantic Bastion programme to create a hybrid naval force of crewed and uncrewed vessels’ - a key recommendation of the Strategic Defence Review - and was announced today at the International Sea Power Conference in Oslo, Norway.

Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, Luke Pollard MP said:

The threats beneath the North Atlantic are changing, and we are changing with them. This investment gives the Royal Navy new technology to find threats earlier and protect our critical infrastructure, while also backing British business.

It shows that we’re getting on with the job of investing in our Armed Forces and strengthening our deterrence under the sea, to support our ultimate, nuclear deterrent.

The framework with Hampshire-based company Ocean Infinity Solutions will pave the way for £90m of investment, supporting almost 200 new skilled jobs and its immediate supply chain, building on the 38,700 jobs in South East England directly supported by MOD spend with industry, while strengthening the Royal Navy’s ability to protect the UK’s undersea infrastructure.

Atlantic Bastion is the Royal Navy’s plan to create a hybrid naval force to hunt and track enemy submarines and protect the vast network of critical underwater infrastructure that connects and powers the UK and its allies, including communications cables and energy networks. Working alongside NATO and Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) allies, it will strengthen protection against interference, sabotage and hostile activity, with Atlantic Net increasing the scale, persistence and resilience of underwater surveillance.

The Royal Navy and Ocean Infinity Solutions will bring together maritime systems, underwater sensing, communications, remote operations and data services into a single capability directed by the Royal Navy.

items.title: UK Statement regarding conviction of Tanzanian Opposition Leader Tundu Lissu
items.summary: We are deeply concerned following the conviction of Tanzanian opposition leader, Mr Tundu Lissu, on charges of incitement. We recall the findings of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (opinion No. 74/2025), which concluded that Mr
items.bodyHtml:
We are deeply concerned following the conviction of Tanzanian opposition leader, Mr Tundu Lissu, on charges of incitement.  

We recall the findings of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (opinion No. 74/2025), which concluded that Mr Lissu’s detention was arbitrary, lacked sufficient legal basis, was accompanied by serious fair trial concerns and contravened protections contained in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which Tanzania is a State Party.  

We further recall Tanzania’s obligations under international human rights law, including to uphold the rights to a fair trial, freedom of expression, political participation and equal treatment before the law.  

We support the Presidential Commission of Inquiry’s view that political reconciliation is an important step to healing the wounds caused by the violence surrounding the October 2025 General Elections, and restoring peace, trust and solidarity.   

We urge the Tanzanian authorities to uphold this essential commitment to reconciliation, to a pluralist democracy, and to the principles of a fair trial, due process and the rule of law. 

Minister for Africa and International Development, Kirsty McNeill
items.bodyText:
We are deeply concerned following the conviction of Tanzanian opposition leader, Mr Tundu Lissu, on charges of incitement.  

We recall the findings of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (opinion No. 74/2025), which concluded that Mr Lissu’s detention was arbitrary, lacked sufficient legal basis, was accompanied by serious fair trial concerns and contravened protections contained in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which Tanzania is a State Party.  

We further recall Tanzania’s obligations under international human rights law, including to uphold the rights to a fair trial, freedom of expression, political participation and equal treatment before the law.  

We support the Presidential Commission of Inquiry’s view that political reconciliation is an important step to healing the wounds caused by the violence surrounding the October 2025 General Elections, and restoring peace, trust and solidarity.   

We urge the Tanzanian authorities to uphold this essential commitment to reconciliation, to a pluralist democracy, and to the principles of a fair trial, due process and the rule of law. 

Minister for Africa and International Development, Kirsty McNeill

items.title: Safety the focus as Maritime and Coastguard Agency seeks feedback on pleasure vessel definition
items.summary: The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) is asking for views on the definition of pleasure vessels to support its ongoing work to keep people safe on the water. A 12-week call-for-evidence launches today (Tuesday 10 November 2026) for marin
items.bodyHtml:
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) is asking for views on the definition of pleasure vessels to support its ongoing work to keep people safe on the water.

A 12-week call-for-evidence launches today (Tuesday 10 November 2026) for mariners, owners, operators and other stakeholders to provide their thoughts and experiences on how the current definition is understood and applied in practice.

Feedback requested includes whether there are situations where the distinction between pleasure and commercial use is unclear.

The MCA listening exercise was prompted by a Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) report into a fatal incident off Cowes, Isle of Wight, in October 2022, which recommended a review of the definition of pleasure vessels.

The definitions of pleasure and commercial vessels determine different regulatory safety requirements such as lifesaving equipment, training, inspections and certification.

The MCA’s Innovative Technologies Lead – Code Vessels, Esmé Flegg, said:

We want to hear from a range of groups and individuals about the pleasure vessel definition and how it is applied in practice, if there is ambiguity, and its influence on operations.

This is not a consultation on regulatory changes; this is a call for evidence, prompted by an important MAIB report.

The evidence gathered will help us to understand better how the current definition operates, aiding our ongoing work to ensure all sectors stay safe.

To find out more and respond to the call for evidence, visit Use and perceptions of the definition of ‘pleasure vessel’ - GOV.UK or email codes@mcga.gov.uk.

The deadline for responses is 1 February 2027.

Press office

Email public.relations@mcga.gov.uk

Press enquiries (Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm) 0203 817 2222

Outside these hours or on bank holidays and weekends, for media enquiries ONLY, please send an email outlining your query and putting #Urgent in the subject title.

items.title: Stay on top of your finances, start your Self Assessment today
items.summary: One in five people put off their financial admin because of lack of confidence. An HMRC survey revealed the majority of respondents turned to GOV.UK to better understand tax matters. Customers encouraged to start their Self Assessment tax r
items.bodyHtml:
• One in five people put off their financial admin because of lack of confidence.
  • An HMRC survey revealed the majority of respondents turned to GOV.UK to better understand tax matters.
  • Customers encouraged to start their Self Assessment tax return now as 31 January 2027 deadline approaches.

Millions of people risk putting off important financial admin because they lack confidence or find it overwhelming, new findings from HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has revealed.

HMRC is encouraging Self Assessment customers not to wait until January and to start their tax return now, giving themselves more time to check the information they need, get help if necessary and plan for any tax they owe.

Customers have until 31 January 2027 to file their online Self Assessment tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year and pay any tax owed.

Around 12 million people are expected to file a tax return each year, but around 5 million often leave completing the task until January.

Results from a recent HMRC-commissioned survey into the digital habits of more than 5,200 people showed that, while 35% of people said they are confident they stay on top of their financial admin, more than 18% said they put it off ahead of a deadline because they lack confidence and nearly a quarter said they put it off because it feels overwhelming.

But, more than half of the people who took part in the survey said GOV.UK is their go-to when they need help with tax matters.

Customers can visit GOV.UK to file their Self Assessment tax return online and access a wide range of help and guidance, including webinars and YouTube videos, to help them prepare and submit an accurate tax return.

Self Assessment guidance pages are among the most visited on GOV.UK. Between 1 October 2025 and the 31 January 2026 deadline, Self Assessment help and guidance pages were visited more than 34.2 million times with the most popular being the Personal Tax Account log-in page with 4.3 million visits.

Myrtle Lloyd, HMRC’s Chief Customer Officer, said:

There is still plenty of time to submit a Self Assessment tax return. By starting early, you have time to check your tax return thoroughly and spot any potential mistakes.

Help and support is available on GOV.UK, just search ‘Self Assessment’ on GOV.UK to find out more.

Customers who file their tax return now do not need to pay straight away. Instead, they have time to plan for any tax they owe ahead of the deadline.

The quickest and easiest way to pay is through the HMRC app although a list of available payment options are available on GOV.UK.

The HMRC app can also help Self Assessment customers find their Unique Taxpayer Reference, view previous years’ tax summaries, view payment history and set payment reminders, as well as accessing help and information about the tax return process.

If anyone is still unsure if they need to fill in a tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, they can use the Self Assessment checker tool on GOV.UK. They can also register online for Self Assessment if they need to complete a tax return for the last tax year. And, if they no longer need to complete a tax return, they can notify HMRC online.

Customers signed up to Making Tax Digital for Income Tax still need to submit their Self Assessment tax return for 2025 to 2026 in the usual way and pay any taxed owed by 31 January 2027.

Further Information

More information about Self Assessment.

Customers who received the 2025 Winter Fuel Payment, or Pension Age Winter Heating Payments in Scotland, and are in Self Assessment, will see the Winter Fuel Payment pre-populated in their 2025 to 2026 online tax return where possible, payment is due by 31 January 2027. Customers should check and add it manually if it is not shown. Customers with a total income over £35,000 will then pay the payment back through their Self Assessment tax bill.

Customers who pay their High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) through Self Assessment, will now have their or their partner’s Child Benefit payment details pre‑populated on their online Self Assessment tax return, making it easier for liable customers to complete an accurate tax return.

Some customers may be able to pay their HICBC via the PAYE digital service, a simple and easy way to pay the charge monthly via their salary, which amends their tax code. For more information on the HICBC PAYE digital service go to GOV.UK.

Self Assessment customers with a PAYE income who file online before 30 December may be able to have any tax owed collected via their tax code.

UK cryptoasset owners need to pay Capital Gains Tax on gains made from cryptoassets above the £3,000 tax-free allowance and declare it in their Self Assessment tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year. More information about paying tax when selling cryptoassets can be found on GOV.UK.

items.title: Appointment of Dean of Exeter: 10 November 2026
items.summary: The King has approved the nomination of The Reverend Arwen Caroline Folkes, Vicar of St Mary the Virgin, Eastbourne, in the Diocese of Chichester, as Dean of Exeter, in succession to The Very Reverend Jonathan Desmond Francis Greener, follo
items.bodyHtml:
The King has approved the nomination of The Reverend Arwen Caroline Folkes, Vicar of St Mary the Virgin, Eastbourne, in the Diocese of Chichester, as Dean of Exeter, in succession to The Very Reverend Jonathan Desmond Francis Greener, following his resignation.

Background

Arwen trained for ministry at Westcott House, Cambridge, gaining a BA (Hons) and MA from Durham University. She served her title at St. Just in Roseland and St. Mawes, in the Diocese of Truro, and was ordained priest in 2017.

In 2019, Arwen was appointed Rector of St. Peter’s East Blatchington and St. Andrew’s, Bishopstone, in the Diocese of Chichester, before taking up her current role as Vicar of St Mary the Virgin, Eastbourne, in 2024.

The King has approved the nomination of The Reverend Arwen Caroline Folkes, Vicar of St Mary the Virgin, Eastbourne, in the Diocese of Chichester, as Dean of Exeter, in succession to The Very Reverend Jonathan Desmond Francis Greener, following his resignation.

Background

Arwen trained for ministry at Westcott House, Cambridge, gaining a BA (Hons) and MA from Durham University. She served her title at St. Just in Roseland and St. Mawes, in the Diocese of Truro, and was ordained priest in 2017.

In 2019, Arwen was appointed Rector of St. Peter’s East Blatchington and St. Andrew’s, Bishopstone, in the Diocese of Chichester, before taking up her current role as Vicar of St Mary the Virgin, Eastbourne, in 2024.

items.title: Mine water heat network wins national award
items.summary: The Seaham Garden Village mine water heat network has won the Gamechanger Award at the 2026 Accelerate to Zero Awards. Judges chose the scheme from projects across the UK. It was recognised at a ceremony on Thursday 5 November 2026, held as
items.bodyHtml:
The Seaham Garden Village mine water heat network has won the Gamechanger Award at the 2026 Accelerate to Zero Awards.

Judges chose the scheme from projects across the UK. It was recognised at a ceremony on Thursday 5 November 2026, held as part of BE-ST Fest in Glasgow. The award celebrates innovative ways to support a just transition in the built environment.

Andrew Simpson, head of innovation, by-products and service delivery at the Mining Remediation Authority, said:

We’re delighted that Seaham Garden Village has won the Gamechanger Award.

The scheme shows what’s possible when we put a former coalfield’s mining legacy to work for the community. It uses warm water from our Dawdon mine water treatment scheme to provide clean, affordable and secure heat for hundreds of homes.

It’s a fantastic result for everyone involved. I’d like to thank everyone across the project and partnership for making it happen.

Project Manager, Stuart Bellwood, reflects on what the project means to him and to the former coalfield community it serves

How the scheme works

Our Dawdon mine water treatment scheme already pumps water from the flooded mine to the surface. This water is naturally between 18°C and 20°C.

A 733kW water source heat pump increases the temperature of the water. The heat then travels through a heat network to 750 affordable homes. The scheme is expected to save 505 tonnes of carbon emissions a year.

Kieran Walsh, regional manager for Vital Energi, said:

This is a really special project because it continues the story of the north-east’s mining heritage. It gives the infrastructure at Dawdon Colliery a new purpose, providing low-carbon heat for the surrounding area.

We’re also acting as the long-term energy services company. We’ll provide the heating and support customers, so this award is a fantastic way to begin that relationship.

Protecting the local water supply

Dawdon Colliery began producing coal in 1904 and operated for 85 years. After it closed, the mine workings gradually filled with groundwater, rainwater and seawater.

The Dawdon mine water treatment scheme pumps and treats this water to protect the local aquifer. The heat network does not change this safety role. It gives the same site a second use.

About the partnership

Durham County Council, the Mining Remediation Authority, Karbon Homes and Vital Energi developed the heat network together. Vital Energi designed and built the energy centre and network.

The network will supply affordable heat to 750 affordable homes at Seaham Garden Village. The village is part of a wider masterplan for 1,500 homes.

Other mine water treatment schemes

We operate more than 80 mine water treatment schemes across Great Britain. Seaham Garden Village shows how this existing infrastructure could also provide low-carbon heat.

For media enquiries contact the community response team

Email communityresponse@miningremediation.gov.uk

Telephone 0800 288 4211

For emergency media enquiries (out of hours) call: 0800 288 4242.
Only urgent media calls will be attended to.

items.title: Fair Work Agency recovers over £100,000 in unpaid mileage
items.summary: More than £107,000 has been secured for care workers after a Fair Work Agency investigation, prompted by information received by the contact centre, identified underpayments relating to business mileage. The investigation found that domicil
items.bodyHtml:
More than £107,000 has been secured for care workers after a Fair Work Agency investigation, prompted by information received by the contact centre, identified underpayments relating to business mileage. 

The investigation found that domiciliary care workers at a care provider were not receiving appropriate reimbursement for mileage incurred while carrying out their duties. 

Fair Work Agency colleagues worked with the employer to review its mileage arrangements. As a result the company recognised staff had been underpaid and sought to rectify this with affected workers, including former employees. The organisation also increased its mileage reimbursement rate from 5p per mile to 40p per mile for 2026.

The total amount identified for repayment is £107,935.96, including:

  • £61,343.93 for workers at the Mansfield branch
  • £46,592.03 for workers at the Northampton branch

A Fair Work Agency spokesperson said:

This outcome will make a significant difference to the workers affected and demonstrates the importance of ensuring employees receive the pay and entitlements they are owed.

We will continue to work with employers and workers to improve compliance, raise awareness of employment rights and help create fairer workplaces.

The Fair Work Agency continues to support workers and employers to improve compliance and ensure that workers receive the pay and employment rights they are entitled to.

items.title: PM call with President El-Sisi of Egypt: 9 November 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Egypt, Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, today. The Prime Minister began by offering his condolences to all those affected by the tragic train crash in Cairo yesterday. Turning to the Middle East, the Prime
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Egypt, Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, today.

The Prime Minister began by offering his condolences to all those affected by the tragic train crash in Cairo yesterday.

Turning to the Middle East, the Prime Minister thanked the President for Egypt’s support in facilitating UK defensive operations in the Gulf.

The leaders discussed the importance of a two-state solution between Israel and Palestine and agreed on the need to work with international partners to de-escalate conflict across the region.

The Prime Minister welcomed the recent signing of agreements on migration and green growth between the UK and Egypt and set out his ambition to build an even stronger relationship between the two nations.

The leaders looked forward to speaking again soon.

items.title: PM call with President Macron of France: 9 November 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister joined a call chaired by President Emmanuel Macron on artificial intelligence today. The Prime Minister began by thanking President Macron for his work to advance international cooperation on AI. The Prime Minister highli
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister joined a call chaired by President Emmanuel Macron on artificial intelligence today. The Prime Minister began by thanking President Macron for his work to advance international cooperation on AI.

The Prime Minister highlighted the importance of harnessing AI for good, including its potential to transform cancer and dementia treatment. He also stressed the need to remain clear eyed about the risks posed by AI and the importance of international cooperation, as well as the expertise the UK could offer via the AI Security Institute.

Looking ahead to the UK’s G20 Presidency in 2027, the Prime Minister outlined how AI would be at the top of the agenda. He also set out how the UK would look to advance work on international AI standards, while continuing to use the technology to tackle major global challenges.

items.title: Jocelyn Ledward KC appointed to lead Treasury Counsel
items.summary: Jocelyn Ledward KC will become the first woman to lead the Treasury Counsel team at the Central Criminal Court after being appointed First Senior Treasury Counsel to the Crown. The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, announced the appoint
items.bodyHtml:
Jocelyn Ledward KC will become the first woman to lead the Treasury Counsel team at the Central Criminal Court after being appointed First Senior Treasury Counsel to the Crown.

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, announced the appointment, which will take effect on 1 April 2027. Jocelyn Ledward KC will succeed Tom Little KC, who has served in the role since April 2024.

Treasury Counsel are based at the Old Bailey, where they take on many of the most demanding prosecutions in England and Wales. They also advise and appear on behalf of the Law Officers, government departments and principal prosecuting authorities.

As First Senior Treasury Counsel, Jocelyn Ledward KC will lead the team and oversee the operation of the Treasury Counsel system, while continuing to prosecute cases herself.

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, said:

Jocelyn Ledward KC will bring considerable experience, leadership and judgement to one of the most important roles in our criminal justice system.

Her appointment is also a significant moment. For the first time, a woman will lead the Treasury Counsel team.

I would like to thank Tom Little KC for his dedicated service as First Senior Treasury Counsel.

Jocelyn Ledward KC said:

I am honoured to be appointed First Senior Treasury Counsel. Treasury Counsel play a vital role in the criminal justice system, and I am proud to be the first woman to lead the team.

I look forward to working with colleagues across the system and continuing the high standards of those who have held this role before me.

Jocelyn Ledward KC was appointed Junior Treasury Counsel in 2014 and Senior Treasury Counsel in 2022. 

She has practised in serious and complex criminal law from QEB Hollis Whiteman Chambers since 1999. She was appointed as a Recorder of the Crown Court in 2022 and King’s Counsel in 2024.   

Notes to editors

  • Treasury Counsel are appointed by the Attorney General in consultation with the Director of Public Prosecutions. They are divided into Senior Treasury Counsel and Junior Treasury Counsel.
  • The First Senior Treasury Counsel leads the Treasury Counsel team and oversees the operation of the Treasury Counsel system. They work with the Law Officers, the Director of Public Prosecutions, the judiciary, HM Courts and Tribunals Service and other stakeholders. The appointment is for three years.
  • The title “Treasury Counsel” derives from the period when all Crown Counsel at the Central Criminal Court were instructed by the Treasury Solicitor. That procedure changed in 1908, after which the Director of Public Prosecutions instructed the permanent counsel based there.

items.title: New tools to support preparation for Martyn's Law
items.summary: The Security Industry Authority (SIA) is releasing new planning tools today to support premises and events in scope of Martyn’s Law as they prepare to comply with the new legislation. Martyn’s Law, which is expected to come into force in sp
items.bodyHtml:
The Security Industry Authority (SIA) is releasing new planning tools today to support premises and events in scope of Martyn’s Law as they prepare to comply with the new legislation. Martyn’s Law, which is expected to come into force in spring 2027, aims to keep people safe by ensuring that publicly accessible premises and events are better prepared against acts of terrorism. 

The SIA is urging all those in scope to use the new planning tools to start to prepare for the incoming legislation. 

Developed with the support of volunteers from premises and events and the SIA’s protective security partners, there is a new planning tool for those in the standard tier to work through what procedures they have or will put in place to comply and a template for the enhanced tier to use to start documenting their procedures.  

For those in the standard tier, the focus is on helping them think through how they will put in place appropriate procedures for evacuation, lockdown, communications and invacuation (moving people to safe areas within a premises) in the event of a terrorist attack.  

For the enhanced tier, the SIA has produced a template that can be used to document compliance when the new law comes in. The template is designed to help those in scope think through the procedures they will put in place and their impact on reducing harm in the event of an attack. It will also help them look at how they would assess any vulnerabilities to attack and how they will then use monitoring, movement of people, physical security and information security measures to reduce these.  

When Martyn’s Law comes into force, premises and events in scope will need to notify the SIA they are in scope. Those in the standard tier will not need to send any compliance documents at that point unless asked to do so. 

The SIA is inviting feedback on the tools released today and encouraging those in scope to test them out now and start to prepare. You can share feedback on these tools through this feedback form until 23 December.

Laura Gibb, Executive Director of Martyn’s Law at the SIA said:

We have talked to many people at events and in premises across the UK and heard their ask for practical tools. They have asked for help for those in scope of Martyn’s Law to work through their thinking, planning and preparation. These new materials are a first step. We will continue to work with those responsible for premises and events in scope to guide and support them in complying.

We cannot build an effective, workable system without the people and organisations who will be using it. We are encouraging everyone to get involved, help test the tools and templates and help us build something that works for premises and events of every size and type.

Henry Havis, Business Chair for the National Counter Terrorism Security Office (NaCTSO) Counter Terrorism Business Information Exchange said:

The Counter Terrorism Business Information Exchange has been delighted to work with the SIA in developing these practical tools. One of the consistent messages from industry has been the need for clear, proportionate and usable guidance that helps organisations translate the requirements of Martyn’s Law into practical action. These tools are an important step forward in doing exactly that.

For smaller standard tier premises, the planning tool provides a straightforward way to work through the public protection procedures and consider what is appropriate and reasonably practicable for their individual circumstances. For larger and more complex enhanced-tier premises and events, the template provides a welcome framework for documenting procedures, protective measures and the decisions that sit behind them.

Martyn’s Law is ultimately about protecting people. Use the period before Martyn’s Law comes into force to understand your responsibilities, review existing arrangements, identify gaps, engage your people, and make sure procedures and measures will work in practice, when they are needed. Ultimately, this is about making the places where people work, visit and gather safer.

The tools can be accessed on GOV.UK alongside further resources and information on Martyn’s Law. For anyone still unsure if Martyn’s Law applies to them, flowcharts are available to help with this on ProtectUK.

Media enquiries

For media enquiries only, please contact:

SIA press office

Email media.enquiries@sia.gov.uk

items.title: New cameras and sensors to help protect fish stocks & marine life in English waters
items.summary: Fish stocks and marine wildlife in English waters will benefit from greater protection, as new monitoring technology becomes a legal requirement for large pelagic fishing vessels from November 2028, subject to parliamentary timings. Remote
items.bodyHtml:
Fish stocks and marine wildlife in English waters will benefit from greater protection, as new monitoring technology becomes a legal requirement for large pelagic fishing vessels from November 2028, subject to parliamentary timings.

Remote Electronic Monitoring (REM) uses on-board cameras, sensors and GPS to give an ongoing picture of fishing activity at sea. This includes where vessels are fishing, what they’re catching, and whether marine mammals, seabirds or sharks are being accidentally caught.

A pelagic trawler is a large fishing boat designed to catch shoaling fish, like mackerel or herring from open water, using nets and on-board storage to handle large catches. Many of these boats already have REM systems installed, reflecting a wider shift across the industry towards greater transparency. 

This new requirement will bring the rest of the large pelagic trawl fleet in line, ensuring a level playing field for vessels doing the right thing.

Fisheries Minister Stephen Morgan said: 

This is a major step forward for protecting our seas, and the fact that most of the fleet is already on board speaks volumes.

For the first time, we will be able to fully monitor fishing activity at sea, ensuring a level playing field for everyone in the industry and helping scientists get the evidence they need to support our fish stocks and marine wildlife.

Evidence from REM will help scientists build a more accurate picture of fish stocks, as well as making it easier for regulators to spot and act proportionately on fishing practices that are harmful, or do not follow the rules. It will also support smarter decisions on how our fisheries are managed, meaning better protection for marine life and a more sustainable future for UK fishing.

The new requirement follows a successful trial, in which Defra worked with a volunteer pelagic trawl vessel to test how REM works in practice. The lessons learned from that project have shaped this policy.

items.title: Joint statement on the closure of Novaya Gazeta in Russia
items.summary: Today, after more than 30 years, the prominent independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta has ceased its operations inside the country. Its closure is a stark reminder of the sustained pressure facing independent journalism in Russia. For
items.bodyHtml:
Today, after more than 30 years, the prominent independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta has ceased its operations inside the country. Its closure is a stark reminder of the sustained pressure facing independent journalism in Russia. 

For decades, Novaya Gazeta and its journalists have reported on corruption, repression and human rights abuses, often at great personal risk. We remember those reporters whose work has cost them their lives, including Anna Politkovskaya. 

The Russian authorities continue to use repressive legislation to crack down on media freedom. Independent journalists face serious personal risks in carrying out their work, including arrest, detention, harassment and political imprisonment.  

As Co-Chairs of the Media Freedom Coalition, Finland and the UK stand in solidarity with independent journalists and media workers in Russia and in exile who continue their work despite these pressures. We call for the immediate and unconditional release of all political prisoners, including all the unlawfully imprisoned journalists.  

Independent media plays a vital role in ensuring people have access to reliable information and in holding those in power to account. We call on the Russian authorities to allow journalists and media workers to work freely and safely, end the repression of independent media and journalists, and uphold their international human rights obligations.

items.title: Report 12/2026: Collision between a passenger train and a van at Bax level crossing

items.bodyHtml:
R122026_261109_Bax UWC

PDF, 18.1 MB, 58 pages

This file may not be suitable for users of assistive technology.

Request an accessible format
If you use assistive technology (such as a screen reader) and need a version of this document in a more accessible format, please email enquiries@raib.gov.uk. Please tell us what format you need. It will help us if you say what assistive technology you use.

Summary

At around 12:42 on 13 July 2025, a passenger train travelling from Ramsgate to London Victoria collided with a stationary delivery van on Bax user worked crossing near Teynham in Kent. The train was travelling at approximately 71 mph (114 km/h) when the accident occurred. The driver of the van was fatally injured.

Bax user worked crossing has outward opening gates to either side of the railway and is fitted with an overlay miniature stop light system, which shows a green light if no trains are approaching. This will change to show a red light, and an audible warning will sound, once a train is detected approaching the crossing. The correct operation of the crossing is described by signs. These instruct users to check that a green light is showing before opening both gates, before crossing with a vehicle, and again before closing both gates.

RAIB’s investigation found that the van was stationary on the level crossing because the green light shown by the miniature stop light system when the delivery driver arrived almost certainly led them to believe that it was safe to enter the crossing once the entry gate had been opened, despite the exit gate still being closed. RAIB also found that the signage at the crossing and the lack of road markings did not effectively guide the delivery driver to use the correct crossing procedure.

Underlying factors were that a project to develop and implement new signage for use at private crossings, such as Bax, did not sufficiently consider how diverse information sources may influence crossing user behaviour. In addition, RAIB found that, once Network Rail had fitted miniature stop lights at a crossing, it became unlikely that further upgrades would take place, and reliance on signs being understood and obeyed remained essential for safe crossing usage. RAIB also found that the training and guidance provided to the delivery driver, who was self-employed but working on behalf of a logistics company, had not prepared them to use the crossing safely.

Although not linked to the accident on 13 July 2025, RAIB observed differing interpretations of the concept of an authorised user within railway processes for identifying and assessing risk at level crossings.

Recommendations

RAIB has made four recommendations. The first is addressed to Network Rail and asks for a review of the design of user worked crossings to reduce risk to users. This is supported by the second recommendation, which asks the Department for Transport, working in consultation with the Office of Rail and Road and relevant rail industry bodies in Great Britain, to update the framework of legal requirements, and guidance to road users relating to user worked level crossings. The third is addressed to the Health and Safety Executive, to review guidance to organisations employing people to drive or ride for work, or engaging self-employed people to do so, on the safe use of user worked crossings. The fourth asks Network Rail to review the concept of the role of authorised users in the guidance it provides to its staff.

Andrew Hall, Chief Inspector of Rail Accidents said:

“This report explains the factors that led to the death of a delivery van driver at Bax user worked level crossing in Kent in July 2025 and makes recommendations to reduce the chance of a similar accident happening again.  In August 2026, another delivery van driver was killed at a user worked crossing in Lancashire. These deaths are a tragedy, but as a train can be derailed by striking a delivery van, both accidents could also have had serious consequences for the people on board.

“Private user worked crossings are a 19th century concept operating in a 21st century world of more dense, faster rail services, more rural housing and abundant home deliveries. Most road users are unfamiliar with this type of crossing and with how to use them safely.

“A delivery van driver was also seriously injured in October 2017, at Frognal Farm user worked crossing in Kent. When RAIB published its report in August 2018, my predecessor wrote:

“I believe that the vital lesson from this investigation is how important it is that each user worked crossing is managed in a way that takes into account the context in which it is being used, and the needs and expectations of the people who may encounter it in the course of their everyday business. It is time for a fresh approach to this problem, for the sake of crossing users, train passengers and railway staff, who are all at risk.”

“Eight years later, I urge the rail industry duty holders, the domestic delivery industry, the Office of Rail and Road, and the Department for Transport to find effective ways to mitigate this obvious risk before there is further tragedy.”

Notes to editors

  1. The sole purpose of RAIB investigations is to prevent future accidents and incidents and improve railway safety. RAIB does not establish blame, liability or carry out prosecutions.

  2. RAIB operates, as far as possible, in an open and transparent manner. While our investigations are completely independent of the railway industry, we do maintain close liaison with railway companies and if we discover matters that may affect the safety of the railway, we make sure that information about them is circulated to the right people as soon as possible, and certainly long before publication of our final report.

  3. For media enquiries, please call 01932 440015.

Newsdate: 9 November 2026

items.title: Investigational treatments for lung cancer, Huntington’s disease and Alzheimer's gain Innovation Passports through the Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway
