items.bodyHtml:
This means they can access coordinated support throughout development through the UK’s Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP). This is the only end-to-end access pathway in the world where developers can work, from early stages of clinical development, with the national health system, the regulator and health technology assessment bodies. 

The ILAP is designed to de-risk product development and accelerate patient access to transformative new medicines and drug-device combinations, by providing a single integrated platform for collaboration. 

Following assessment by the ILAP Selection Panel, Innovation Passports have been awarded to:  

  • A chemical siRNA (small interfering RNA that can silence genes by cleaving mRNA) for the treatment of Huntington’s disease  

  • A chemical small molecule oncology therapy, with first-line Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) expected to be the lead indication. 

  • A chemical Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO) for the treatment of early Alzheimer’s disease 

Huntington’s disease is a rare, inherited and ultimately fatal neurodegenerative disease that places substantial burden on those affected and their families.  

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer, accounting for around 80–85% of cases. Around 50,200 people are diagnosed with lung cancer in the UK each year. 

Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. An estimated 982,000 people were living with dementia in the UK in 2024, with the number expected to rise.  

Professor Jacob George, Chief Medical and Scientific Officer of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency said: 

The Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway is a globally unique initiative designed to accelerate patient access to transformative new medicines and drug-device combinations. 

Today, we have issued Innovation Passports to three therapies that show real promise in addressing the unmet needs in Alzheimer’s, lung cancer and Huntington’s disease. 

John Spoors, Deputy Director of Medicines Evaluation at NICE said:   

We welcome the announcement that these medicines have been granted Innovation Passports through the Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway.  NICE welcomes the opportunity, through ILAP, to work with developers and partners across the health system to support evidence generation and early engagement on the issues that will shape future evaluation and patient access.

Dr Rob Peel, chair of the Scottish Medicines Consortium, said:  

We are pleased to support the Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway in recognising promising new therapies for Huntington’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease and lung cancer.  These conditions continue to place a substantial burden on patients, families and healthcare systems, and it is encouraging to see innovation being directed towards areas of important unmet need.

Dr Andrew Champion, AWTTC Programme Director, said:  

The award of Innovation Passports to these three investigational treatments is an encouraging step towards addressing unmet needs in lung cancer, Huntington’s disease and Alzheimer’s disease. AWTTC is pleased to work alongside our UK partners to support their development and assessment, bringing the needs of patients and NHS Wales into this collaborative process. Our shared ambition is to help promising medicines reach patients in Wales and across the UK, supported by robust evidence of safety, effectiveness and value.

Yvonne Greenstreet, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Alnylam, said:  

Huntington’s disease is a devastating condition with no therapies approved to slow its progression, underscoring the urgent need for new treatment options. We are honored that our investigational RNAi therapeutic brezosiran has received an Innovation Passport and welcome the opportunity to work closely with the MHRA and ILAP partners as we advance its development. We look forward to collaborating through this pathway to advance brezosiran efficiently, with the hope of meaningfully improving the lives of people living with Huntington’s disease.

James Harris, Interim General Manager, BeOne Medicines UK & Ireland Ltd., said:  

Despite advances in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer, significant unmet needs remain, particularly for patients with MTAP-deficient tumours, for whom no targeted therapies are currently available. The award of an Innovation Passport for BGB-58067 marks the second BeOne investigational medicine to enter the UK’s Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway in recent months, reflecting the strength of our oncology pipeline and our commitment to translating scientific innovation into potential new treatment options for patients who urgently need them. 

We welcome the opportunity to work closely with the MHRA and ILAP partners as we advance the development of this investigational PRMT5 inhibitor and its potential to bring an innovative new treatment option to patients with non-small cell lung cancer.

Dr Kylie Bromley, Managing Director, Biogen UK & Ireland said: 

Alzheimer’s disease remains one of the greatest health and social care challenges of our time and we welcome the MHRA’s Innovation Passport designation for diranersen. We now have an opportunity to collaborate with partners across the health system to ensure that innovations reach the patients who need them.  This achievement reinforces our optimism for the future of innovation in Alzheimer’s disease.

The products awarded an Innovation Passport are still in development, and any future availability will depend on the evidence of safety, effectiveness and value.  

Companies developing innovative medicines that address unmet patient needs across all therapeutic areas are encouraged to review the eligibility criteria and submit an application. Full guidance is available on the MHRA website.  

Applications for the next round of Innovation Passports open today (9 November) and remain open until 11 February 2027. 

Notes to editors:  

  1. The ILAP is delivered through a partnership between the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), NHS England, the UK Health Technology Assessment (HTA) bodies – the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), the Scottish Medicines Consortium (SMC) the All Wales Therapeutics and Toxicology Centre (AWTTC), and the Department of Health Northern Ireland.   

  2. Entry to ILAP is open to commercial and non-commercial developers worldwide. Applicants must submit medicines or drug-device combinations that have not yet entered their confirmatory trial, which will give more opportunity to benefit from the support offered within the pathway. More details can be found on the MHRA website.  

  3. The ILAP is a UK-wide initiative, comprising the following partners:  

  • The All Wales Therapeutics and Toxicology Centre (AWTTC) (on behalf of NHS Health boards and Trusts in Wales)  

  • The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)  

  • National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)  

  • NHS England  

  • Scottish Medicines Consortium (SMC) (on behalf of NHS boards in Scotland)  

  • Department of Health Northern Ireland  

  1. Supporting partners include:  

  • Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)  

  • National Institute for Health Research (NIHR)  

  • Office for Life Sciences (OLS)  

  • Scottish Government  

  • Welsh Government 

  1. Recently published articles that provide information on the benefit of the ILAP Target Development Profile and how the ILAP and the MHRA–NICE Aligned Pathway work together.  

  2. The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.   

  3. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care.   

  4. For media enquiries, please contact the newscentre@mhra.gov.uk, or call on 020 3080 7651.

items.title: £40 million for GPs to keep vulnerable patients out of hospital this winter
items.summary: Up to 300,000 vulnerable patients set to receive extra GP support this winter to help prevent serious illness and reduce avoidable hospital admissions £40 million will help GPs proactively support people with conditions including heart dise
items.bodyHtml:
• Up to 300,000 vulnerable patients set to receive extra GP support this winter to help prevent serious illness and reduce avoidable hospital admissions
  • £40 million will help GPs proactively support people with conditions including heart disease or frailty through health checks, home assessments and medication reviews
  • Builds on investment in NHS frontline ahead of winter to open more emergency care sites and bolster hospitals

Thousands of vulnerable patients will receive more proactive support from their GP this winter thanks to a £40 million government-funded programme, set out by the Prime Minister and the Health and Social Care Secretary today.

The programme will help keep people well at home and prevent avoidable hospital admissions as the government ramps up preparations to bolster the NHS for the winter pressures ahead.

Patients with conditions like heart disease, frailty or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) will get access to additional support from their GP, tailored to their needs and designed to help them avoid reaching a crisis point and needing to go to hospital.

Backing greater, easier access to care in the local community is a key part of the government’s work to rebuild the NHS and ensure people get the right treatment where and when they need it.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: 

If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E.

People deserve the right care in the right place. And our NHS staff, who work so hard, deserve the right tools to provide it.

I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.

Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, Yvette Cooper, said:

This practical plan helps GPs and local teams to provide more support for the frailest patients in the community to keep them well through the winter months. That is better for patients and means they are also less likely to need hospital care.

After such a heavy summer for our NHS as a result of the heat, everyone is working together to prepare for more challenging winter pressures. That includes the rollout of flu vaccinations, investing in extra urgent care capacity and strengthening partnerships with social care.

With thousands more GPs in post and millions more GP appointments this year, the £40 million programme to support vulnerable patients in the community is part of our plan to help patients, improve primary care and also to support our NHS through the heavier winter months.

Shifting care out of hospitals and into the community not only eases pressure on emergency departments so they can focus on patients in greatest need of urgent care, but also makes it possible for patients to receive care more conveniently in their local neighbourhood rather than having to make unnecessary and time-consuming hospital trips.

The ring-fenced funding will support GP practices to proactively identify and provide additional care for the patients they consider most at risk of becoming seriously unwell this winter. Primary care networks (PCNs) will be able to receive £126 for each eligible patient supported.

The extra support will be particularly targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty, emphysema and other types of COPD, and could include medication reviews, health checks and nurse-led respiratory clinics for up to 300,000 people across the country.

This will help general practice play an even greater role in preparing the NHS for winter by keeping vulnerable patients well and helping prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

The funding comes alongside greater flexibility for practices to increase GP capacity as pressures rise. Since October, practices can use GP reimbursement funding to bring in locum GPs, giving them greater freedom to respond to local demand.

There are now more than 2,800 additional GPs compared with July 2024, and more than 30,500 fully qualified full-time equivalent GPs are now working in general practice, the highest number in over a decade. As a result, patients are seeing improvements in GP access, with over 400 million appointments delivered over the past year, around 24 million more than in the equivalent 12-month period in the run-up to July 2024. 

According to the 2026 GP Patient Survey, more than three-quarters of patients say their overall experience of their local general practice is ‘good’. Patient satisfaction with ease of access to their local GP has also risen to 75.5%, up 15 percentage points from July 2024.

Dr Amanda Doyle, National Director for Primary Care and Community Services at NHS England, said: 

GPs and their teams are delivering record numbers of appointments this year, and with their role at the heart of communities, they are perfectly placed to spot patients at greatest risk of becoming very unwell.

By offering more support to our most vulnerable patients such as home assessments to prevent falls, we will help keep them well and prevent them ending up in hospital this winter.

Professor Andy Brooks, Clinical Chair, National Association of Primary Care (NAPC), said:

We welcome this investment, and the ambition here is right. Proactive, personalised care for the people most at risk is where general practice adds great value, and NAPC will be supporting practices to make the most of the opportunity that this scheme offers.

This is a valuable first step, and we’d like to see national policy go even further. We look forward to working with the government to learn from this scheme and build sustainable, lasting proactive care within neighbourhoods.

Ruth Rankine, Director of Primary Care, Community and Neighbourhood Health at the NHS Alliance, said: 

Practices know which of their patients are most at risk this winter. This funding gives them the capacity to act early, with medication reviews, health checks and support for people with frailty and long-term conditions, before problems turn into hospital admissions.

That’s better for patients and better for the NHS. It also moves care closer to home, where it should be. The next step is to make this kind of proactive care a permanent part of how neighbourhood health is funded and delivered.

The £40 million forms part of wider action to prepare the NHS for winter, alongside:

  • additional funding for urgent care
  • expanded Pharmacy First Services
  • the winter vaccination programme, which is giving people vital protection against winter illnesses

By 1 November 2026, more than 13.6 million people in England had received their flu vaccine. That is around 300,000 more than at the same point last year. Among school-aged children, 2.4 million had been vaccinated, almost half a million more than at the same point last year.

The government has also invested in upgrades for the ambulance fleet across England, with almost 2,000 new or replacement frontline ambulances delivered to services since July 2024. Thanks to investment in new scanners and cutting edge AI technology, a million more scans have also been delivered, with 125 additional CT and MRI scanners now operational across the NHS since March 2024.

The NHS received £190 million in the Budget to manage winter pressures, alongside £140 million for 14 new urgent care schemes. A further 25 new or expanded urgent care sites will be open this winter, including a £29 million same-day emergency care (SDEC) unit which opened on 20 October at William Harvey Hospital in Ashford, Kent. It is expected to accommodate an additional 60 patients a day, which will help to reduce the pressure on an emergency department that normally sees around 350 patients daily. 

East Kent Hospital Trust’s Chief Nursing and Midwifery Officer, Sarah Hayes, said: 

The SDEC units will help us to provide a faster and more convenient alternative for patients to see a team of experts immediately, and receive rapid assessment, diagnosis and treatment - allowing them to be home again the very same day.

This is also a positive milestone for our staff as it supports our work to reduce corridor care and relieve the pressure on our emergency departments.

This additional investment is a positive step, helping GPs identify and support those most at risk, reducing avoidable deterioration and hospital admissions.
items.bodyText:
Up to 300,000 vulnerable patients set to receive extra GP support this winter to help prevent serious illness and reduce avoidable hospital admissions
  £40 million will help GPs proactively support people with conditions including heart disease or frailty through health checks, home assessments and medication reviews
  Builds on investment in NHS frontline ahead of winter to open more emergency care sites and bolster hospitals


Thousands of vulnerable patients will receive more proactive support from their GP this winter thanks to a £40 million government-funded programme, set out by the Prime Minister and the Health and Social Care Secretary today.

The programme will help keep people well at home and prevent avoidable hospital admissions as the government ramps up preparations to bolster the NHS for the winter pressures ahead.

Patients with conditions like heart disease, frailty or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) will get access to additional support from their GP, tailored to their needs and designed to help them avoid reaching a crisis point and needing to go to hospital.

Backing greater, easier access to care in the local community is a key part of the government’s work to rebuild the NHS and ensure people get the right treatment where and when they need it.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: 


  If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E.

  People deserve the right care in the right place. And our NHS staff, who work so hard, deserve the right tools to provide it.

  I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.


Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, Yvette Cooper, said:


  This practical plan helps GPs and local teams to provide more support for the frailest patients in the community to keep them well through the winter months. That is better for patients and means they are also less likely to need hospital care.

  After such a heavy summer for our NHS as a result of the heat, everyone is working together to prepare for more challenging winter pressures. That includes the rollout of flu vaccinations, investing in extra urgent care capacity and strengthening partnerships with social care.

  With thousands more GPs in post and millions more GP appointments this year, the £40 million programme to support vulnerable patients in the community is part of our plan to help patients, improve primary care and also to support our NHS through the heavier winter months.


Shifting care out of hospitals and into the community not only eases pressure on emergency departments so they can focus on patients in greatest need of urgent care, but also makes it possible for patients to receive care more conveniently in their local neighbourhood rather than having to make unnecessary and time-consuming hospital trips.

The ring-fenced funding will support GP practices to proactively identify and provide additional care for the patients they consider most at risk of becoming seriously unwell this winter. Primary care networks (PCNs) will be able to receive £126 for each eligible patient supported.

The extra support will be particularly targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty, emphysema and other types of COPD, and could include medication reviews, health checks and nurse-led respiratory clinics for up to 300,000 people across the country.

This will help general practice play an even greater role in preparing the NHS for winter by keeping vulnerable patients well and helping prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

The funding comes alongside greater flexibility for practices to increase GP capacity as pressures rise. Since October, practices can use GP reimbursement funding to bring in locum GPs, giving them greater freedom to respond to local demand.

There are now more than 2,800 additional GPs compared with July 2024, and more than 30,500 fully qualified full-time equivalent GPs are now working in general practice, the highest number in over a decade. As a result, patients are seeing improvements in GP access, with over 400 million appointments delivered over the past year, around 24 million more than in the equivalent 12-month period in the run-up to July 2024. 

According to the 2026 GP Patient Survey, more than three-quarters of patients say their overall experience of their local general practice is ‘good’. Patient satisfaction with ease of access to their local GP has also risen to 75.5%, up 15 percentage points from July 2024.

Dr Amanda Doyle, National Director for Primary Care and Community Services at NHS England, said: 


  GPs and their teams are delivering record numbers of appointments this year, and with their role at the heart of communities, they are perfectly placed to spot patients at greatest risk of becoming very unwell.

  By offering more support to our most vulnerable patients such as home assessments to prevent falls, we will help keep them well and prevent them ending up in hospital this winter.


Professor Andy Brooks, Clinical Chair, National Association of Primary Care (NAPC), said:


  We welcome this investment, and the ambition here is right. Proactive, personalised care for the people most at risk is where general practice adds great value, and NAPC will be supporting practices to make the most of the opportunity that this scheme offers.

  This is a valuable first step, and we’d like to see national policy go even further. We look forward to working with the government to learn from this scheme and build sustainable, lasting proactive care within neighbourhoods.


Ruth Rankine, Director of Primary Care, Community and Neighbourhood Health at the NHS Alliance, said: 


  Practices know which of their patients are most at risk this winter. This funding gives them the capacity to act early, with medication reviews, health checks and support for people with frailty and long-term conditions, before problems turn into hospital admissions.

  That’s better for patients and better for the NHS. It also moves care closer to home, where it should be. The next step is to make this kind of proactive care a permanent part of how neighbourhood health is funded and delivered.


The £40 million forms part of wider action to prepare the NHS for winter, alongside:


  additional funding for urgent care
  expanded Pharmacy First Services
  the winter vaccination programme, which is giving people vital protection against winter illnesses


By 1 November 2026, more than 13.6 million people in England had received their flu vaccine. That is around 300,000 more than at the same point last year. Among school-aged children, 2.4 million had been vaccinated, almost half a million more than at the same point last year.

The government has also invested in upgrades for the ambulance fleet across England, with almost 2,000 new or replacement frontline ambulances delivered to services since July 2024. Thanks to investment in new scanners and cutting edge AI technology, a million more scans have also been delivered, with 125 additional CT and MRI scanners now operational across the NHS since March 2024.

The NHS received £190 million in the Budget to manage winter pressures, alongside £140 million for 14 new urgent care schemes. A further 25 new or expanded urgent care sites will be open this winter, including a £29 million same-day emergency care (SDEC) unit which opened on 20 October at William Harvey Hospital in Ashford, Kent. It is expected to accommodate an additional 60 patients a day, which will help to reduce the pressure on an emergency department that normally sees around 350 patients daily. 

East Kent Hospital Trust’s Chief Nursing and Midwifery Officer, Sarah Hayes, said: 


  The SDEC units will help us to provide a faster and more convenient alternative for patients to see a team of experts immediately, and receive rapid assessment, diagnosis and treatment - allowing them to be home again the very same day.

  This is also a positive milestone for our staff as it supports our work to reduce corridor care and relieve the pressure on our emergency departments.

This additional investment is a positive step, helping GPs identify and support those most at risk, reducing avoidable deterioration and hospital admissions.

items.title: NRS completes largest land remediation project at Harwell

items.bodyHtml:
Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) has completed its largest ever land remediation project, restoring 4.2 hectares of land at its Oxford-based site - following more than 60 years of liquid effluent treatment operations.

The completion of remediation at the former Liquid Effluent Treatment Plant (LETP) and neighbouring Sewage Farm Area at Harwell marks a major milestone in the environmental restoration of the historic nuclear research site.

LETP before decommissioning (circa 1999)

More than 97,000 tonnes of material have been removed during the project, which tackled an extensive network of buried tanks, pipelines, pumping stations, reinforced concrete structures and treatment infrastructure, some located up to 10 metres below ground.

The work represents the final major phase in the story of the LETP, which was constructed in 1948 to treat liquid waste generated by Harwell’s pioneering nuclear research programmes.

At its peak, active and trade drainage systems from across the site flowed to the facility, where waste was treated before being safely discharged through a dedicated pipeline to the River Thames. The plant also handled higher activity liquid waste, supporting decades of scientific research and innovation at Harwell.

Alongside the LETP, the former Sewage Farm Area had an even longer history. Originally constructed in the 1930s to serve RAF Harwell, it was later expanded as the site developed.

Following the end of LETP operations in 2013, attention turned to safely decommissioning the ageing facilities and restoring the land.

A comprehensive programme of research, testing and characterisation was undertaken before teams began the extensive task of locating, excavating and removing decades of buried infrastructure across the site.

The scale of the work makes it the largest land remediation project undertaken by NRS to date. To put the volume of material removed into perspective, the 97,000 tonnes excavated is greater than the fully loaded displacement of aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales.

Sustainability was also central to how the restored landscape was designed. A new Sustainable Drainage System (SuDS) pond has been created within the former Sewage Farm Area, providing a natural way to manage surface water while also creating new habitat for wildlife.

Material generated during construction of the pond was reused to reprofile the former LETP area. This avoided the need to import approximately 60,000 tonnes of material and prevented an estimated 2,700 vehicle movements, reducing both waste and the environmental impact of the work.

Public access has also been restored to Icknield Way, a designated public bridleway alongside the former LETP area which had been temporarily inaccessible while remediation was under way.

The transformation supports the wider Nuclear Decommissioning Authority (NDA) mission to safely and sustainably clean up the UK’s nuclear legacy while releasing land for reuse wherever possible.

Gary Reid, Harwell Site Director, said: “This is a hugely significant milestone for Harwell and one our teams should be incredibly proud of. Restoring an area that supported more than 60 years of pioneering nuclear research has been a complex undertaking, requiring years of careful planning, specialist expertise and collaboration across NRS, the NDA and our supply chain.

“But the real measure of success is what we leave behind. Returning this land for potential future use at Harwell Science and Innovation Campus means an area that once enabled pioneering nuclear research can continue to support science, innovation and wider economic benefit for generations to come. We are incredibly proud that NRS has played a part in enabling that next chapter.”

Clive Nixon, the NDA’s Chief Nuclear Strategy Officer, said: “This is a significant achievement, made possible by the expertise, commitment and collaboration of everyone involved. Transforming this historically important land into an asset for future use is a clear example of the lasting benefits we aim to deliver through the NDA mission.”

With physical remediation complete, work is now progressing through the final regulatory stages to delicence the land and surrender the environmental permit.

items.title: UK Government awards £1 million to Northern Ireland community group forum
items.summary: Co-operation Ireland, in partnership with Rural Action and NICVA, will receive up to £1 million over three years from the Northern Ireland Office’s (NIO) Community Partnership Fund to launch their ‘On the Radar: Pathways to Stronger Communi
items.bodyHtml:
Co-operation Ireland, in partnership with Rural Action and NICVA, will receive up to £1 million over three years from the Northern Ireland Office’s (NIO) Community Partnership Fund to launch their ‘On the Radar: Pathways to Stronger Communities’ project. The initiative will engage hundreds of grassroots groups across Northern Ireland, offering tailored support. By coming together, the three community organisations will draw on their extensive expertise in the community and voluntary sector to benefit smaller organisations. This will range from initial idea-generating workshops to intensive mentoring for 30 core organisations, followed by training on accessing funding for up to 500 groups. 

Speaking at the launch event in Cooperation Ireland’s Belfast Headquarters, NIO Parliamentary Under Secretary of State Baroness Ruth Anderson praised the role of Northern Ireland’s community and voluntary sector. 

She said:

“This £1 million grant award is great for Co-operation Ireland, Rural Action and NICVA, and for community and voluntary organisations across Northern Ireland.

“This grant will enable them to become a ‘single front door’ for Northern Ireland’s voluntary and community sector, sharing their considerable expertise in areas such as rural community development and cross-community peacebuilding to empower smaller local groups.
“The Community Partnership Fund will be key to building a network of skills, knowledge and support which will enable organisations across Northern Ireland to flourish, to the benefit of their communities.”

Co-operation Ireland Chief Executive Stephen Dallas said:

“Co-operation Ireland works with volunteers and groups at the heart of communities across Northern Ireland every day. 

“We are all too aware that often smaller grassroots groups can fall below the radar when it comes to access to funding and development opportunities. 

“The support and investment by the Community Partnership Fund is very much welcomed, and the On the Radar Programme will bring the important work of groups into view, will help them to access funding and will empower people through their ambitions and ideas.” 

Chief Executive of NICVA Celine McStravick said:

“NICVA is proud to be working with Co-operation Ireland and Rural Action, bringing together our extensive knowledge of the voluntary and community sector and our expertise in organisational development, governance, funding and sustainability. 

“Too many grassroots groups make an invaluable contribution to our communities, without having access to the skills, resources and opportunities needed to realise their full potential. 

“This programme is about changing that –meeting groups where they are, working alongside them to strengthen their foundations for the future.”

Chief Executive of Rural Action Teresa Canavan said:

“Our rural communities are sustained by the dedication, resilience and commitment of local volunteers and community organisations. 

“Yet too often, groups working tirelessly on the ground to improve the lives of others, can find themselves overlooked or can face barriers to accessing the funding,  development support, and other opportunities they need. 

“We strongly welcome the focus this programme places on engaging and supporting rural community groups, supporting them to build their capacity to deliver services in their local areas.”

ENDS

Notes to editors

  • For media queries contact the NIO press office: communications@nio.gov.uk

items.title: PM call with President Stubb of Finland: 8 November 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Finland, Alexander Stubb, this afternoon. The leaders began by discussing the latest on Ukraine, including the Brussels peace talks last week. It was vital that work towards a just and lasting pe
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Finland, Alexander Stubb, this afternoon.

The leaders began by discussing the latest on Ukraine, including the Brussels peace talks last week.

It was vital that work towards a just and lasting peace in Ukraine was prioritised and continued at pace, the leaders agreed, before a wider discussion on European security.

Putin had consistently failed to show he was serious about negotiations, underlining the importance of Ukraine’s partners piling on further pressure on Russia to force the Kremlin to engage seriously, the Prime Minister added.

Finally, both discussed the future of the UK-EU relationship. Leading up to the summit later this month, the Prime Minister said he was focused on a deal that delivered for all parties, and ensured a modern relationship that could be built on.

They looked forward to speaking again soon.

items.title: 畅通教育科技人才良性循环 为新质生产力蓄势赋能
items.summary: 编者按： 发展新质生产力是推动高质量发展的内在要求和重要着力点。近日，中共中央、国务院印发《关于发展新质生产力的意见》，为加快发展新质生产力作出系统部署。三里河推出权威专家系列解读，阐释政策内涵、洞察发展大势。今日刊发国家发展改革委国际合作中心处长、研究员鲍淑君的署名文章《得打好这三张牌》。 发展新质生产力，关键靠什么？近日，中共中央、国务院印发的《关于发展新质生产力的意见》（以下简称《意见》）给出了明确回答，其中一项重要部署就是“统筹推进教育科技人才体制机制一体改革”。

items.title: Scottish Secretary honours armed forces at Remembrance service
items.summary: Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander laid a wreath on behalf of the UK Government at the Annual Service of Remembrance in Edinburgh today (Sunday 8 November 2026). He joined the Edinburgh Lord Provost’s Wreath Laying Party from 11am at the
items.bodyHtml:
Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander laid a wreath on behalf of the UK Government at the Annual Service of Remembrance in Edinburgh today (Sunday 8 November 2026). 

He joined the Edinburgh Lord Provost’s Wreath Laying Party from 11am at the Stone of Remembrance, Edinburgh City Chambers, alongside members of the military, veterans and community leaders, to honour the service and sacrifice of British Armed Forces personnel, veterans and their families, past and present.

Speaking ahead of the service, Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander said:

Remembrance Sunday is a moment for the whole country to pause and remember the men and women who gave their lives for our freedoms, and to give thanks to our veterans, our serving personnel, and the families who stand behind them. 

In Edinburgh, I will be proud to stand alongside our veterans, members of our armed forces, and community leaders from across Scotland to honour their service and sacrifice.

We owe a debt to those who have served that can never be fully repaid, and we will continue to honour it, in Scotland and across the United Kingdom. The UK Government’s commitment to our armed forces is unwavering.

Following the wreath laying, Mr Alexander joined  the procession to St Giles’ Cathedral, piped by a pupil from George Heriot’s School, for a special Remembrance Sunday service. He gave a reading of Psalm 120, ‘A Song of Ascents,’ before attending a reception at Edinburgh City Chambers. 

Meanwhile, John Grady MP, Parliamentary Private Secretary to HM Treasury laid a wreath on behalf of the UK Government at Glasgow’s Remembrance Sunday service in George Square.

In London, the National Service of Remembrance was held at the Cenotaph on Whitehall, London, attended by the Prime Minister, senior members of the Cabinet and other political leaders.

items.summary: 近年来，资本市场虚假和误导性信息频繁扰乱市场秩序，损害资本市场参与主体合法权益，及时有力辟谣是快速对冲各类谣言负面影响，及时澄清市场误解误读，稳定市场预期的有效手段。为适应网络辟谣工作新形势，更好服务资本市场各类主体，维护资本市场信息传播秩序，在中国证监会办公厅、中央网信办违法和不良信息举报中心的指导下，由中国上市公司协会承办的“中国上市公司协会辟谣平台”现更名升级为“资本市场辟谣平台”，今日正式上线。

items.title: Curriculum overhaul to re-engage pupils in vital early secondary years
items.summary: In response to growing evidence, the Milburn Review, the White Working Class Education Inquiry and the Becky Francis Curriculum and Assessment Review, the government is announcing a distinct focus on the first years of secondary school, as
items.bodyHtml:
In response to growing evidence, the Milburn Review, the White Working Class Education Inquiry and the Becky Francis Curriculum and Assessment Review, the government is announcing a distinct focus on the first years of secondary school, as part of their major review of the National Curriculum.

Too many children are switching off from school in their early teens – affecting their attendance, attainment and life outcomes.  And many others are increasingly missing out on the rich and specialist education they should expect at secondary school or are being rushed through content before they have grasped the fundamentals.

As part of its wide-ranging plans to tackle disengagement, the disadvantage gap and the rising number of young people not in education, employment or training, the government will make the first three years of secondary school count, by restoring Key Stage 3 as a distinct three-year phase.

The new National Curriculum, due to be published in full later this year, which has been developed by subject experts, will see over-crowded content slimmed down and better sequenced across all school stages to create more space for deeper understanding and richer experiences that ignite a love of learning, ensure more children are stretched and make progress.

This will come with higher expectations on core knowledge and skills needed for the future, like oracy and confident speaking, reading fluently and reading for pleasure, and numeracy. There will also be a more engaging offer in subjects like drama, PE, music, and modern foreign languages, alongside technical and digital skills.

It also comes with new expectations on schools to stop the increasingly widespread practice of encroaching on Key Stage 3 with an ever earlier focus on GCSEs. Exams and assessments are a vital part of school life, but the pressure to prepare for GCSEs early is growing. Public First Global for the International Baccalaureate found that more than half of teachers say GCSE courses are dominating the first three years of secondary school, despite this content not being intended to begin until Year 10, with some schools starting GCSE teaching as early as Year 7.

The case for change is particularly important for white working-class pupils. The first Independent Inquiry into White Working-Class Educational Outcomes found that the transition into secondary school is a critical point, with disengagement in their early teens affecting their attendance, attainment and ultimately, their life chances.

Too many children are becoming disengaged at precisely the point when school should be opening new opportunities to them. The proportion of pupils persistently absent from school is almost doubling between Years 7 and 9 to one in four children. Persistent absence is one of the strongest predictors for a young person becoming NEET, and for white working-class children, persistent absence rates are 75% higher in secondary than in primary.

Lucy Powell, Education Secretary said:

The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning.

Instead, we’ve seen worrying trends of disengagement and high levels of persistent absence, with the disadvantage gap stubbornly large and too many leaving school without the knowledge and skills they need to thrive.  That’s what our exciting and engaging new National Curriculum aims to address as part of our wider education reforms.

What’s more, the pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding. I’m putting a stop to that.

The new curriculum and focus for these vital early teen years, will mean more children are excited to learn and more teachers are excited to teach. There will be more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions and prepare them better for the fast-changing world they will grow up in.

The new curriculum will say schools should not start GCSE specifications early for large cohorts or see children routinely required to narrow their options earlier or entered earlier for exams, teachers will still retain the flexibility to stretch high-achieving pupils or groups who are ready to go further without narrowing their options.

Sir Hamid Patel, co-chair of the Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes and chief executive of Star Academies, said: 

Throughout our research for the Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, we found huge challenges in KS3.

It is a time when a love of learning should be developed and when young people should experience a broad and balanced curriculum that exposes them to new ideas and new experiences - but instead too many white working class children are switching off and opting out. It is to be welcomed that the government is showing real commitment to renewing this important phase.

Baroness Estelle Morris, co-chair of the Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, said:

Our report highlighted the problems for children at points of transition, including the move from Primary to Secondary school - it also demonstrated how white working class young people and their families disengage from the education system through the Key Stage 3 years. This is why I welcome the government’s commitment to begin to address these issues.

The work of the inquiry is not yet over and we will soon come forward with fresh plans to drive change for white working class you people in the education system. Together, we should be relentless in our focus on changing the opportunities available for this group of children and families.

The renewed focus on Key Stage 3 goes alongside a new enrichment framework to help schools make more space for richer experiences that inspire young people – from practical experiments to debate.

This learning beyond the classroom is central to making school a place where all children want to be, helping tackle the sharp drop-off in engagement and attendance during the early secondary years.

Becks Boomer-Clark, chief executive of Lift Schools and co-chair of the KS3 Alliance, said:

The first three years of secondary school are a critical phase in their own right, yet for too long they have been treated as little more than a preparation ground for GCSEs.

The government’s commitment to protecting these years is a welcome move. This is not about lowering academic expectations, quite the opposite; it’s about giving young people the time to build really secure foundations in knowledge, while also having the space to explore, discover new interests and develop confidence in what they can achieve.

Getting this right has the potential to transform young people’s educational trajectories, particularly those who are at greatest risk of becoming disengaged from school.

items.title: The King to lead nation in silence on Remembrance Sunday
items.summary: Members of The Royal Family and senior politicians will lay wreaths at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph in London 10,000 veterans will pay tribute as part of The Royal British Legion’s March Past the Cenotaph His Majesty
items.bodyHtml:
• Members of The Royal Family and senior politicians will lay wreaths at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph in London
  • 10,000 veterans will pay tribute as part of The Royal British Legion’s March Past the Cenotaph

His Majesty The King will lead the UK in the annual two-minute silence to remember those who have fallen and suffered in conflict at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph. 

The King will be joined by members of The Royal Family, the Prime Minister, senior politicians and faith representatives to mark the Armistice of the First World War and all other conflicts involving British and Commonwealth forces. 

Approximately 10,000 veterans will take part in the Royal British Legion’s March Past, with over 300 different Armed Forces and civilian organisations represented. People of all ages will be among those marching – from bereaved children and military cadets, through to some of the last surviving veterans of the Second World War. There will be a huge range of participants, with the youngest person marching being aged only seven years old through to veterans aged over 100 years old. Veterans will also have travelled from far and wide to join the March Past, with some coming from as far as Canada and Australia to participate. Approximately 10,000 members of the public are expected to line Whitehall in London to watch the March Past and take part in the annual two-minute silence.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

I’m incredibly proud to be honouring those whose sacrifice continues to protect our way of life to this day. 

Remembrance Sunday gives us an opportunity, not only to mark that sacrifice and offer our gratitude, but also to reflect on its significance. To reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others.

I want to offer my personal thanks to those who served and those who continue to serve in our Armed Forces communities to this day.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said:

This Remembrance Sunday, we come together to reflect and honour the sacrifices that our Armed Forces made all those years ago in the First and Second World Wars and continue to make today. 

It is our duty to ensure that the immense courage of those who have served our country is never forgotten. They went to war to give us 80 years of peace. 

We are about to raise the first generation for whom fighting a war really is part of history. Our future generations must know the significance of those who served in our national story, that they forged a path for friendship and cooperation that meant no one in our country has had to fight a war since.

Today, we remember them, in grief and in gratitude, mindful that their legacy lives on in the freedom we enjoy today.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP said:

I grew up with my grandfather and great-grandfather’s war medals proudly on display in our living room. Defence runs in my blood and I feel intently the importance of Remembrance to those who have served and their families.

This weekend is a moment to pause and reflect on the enormous debt we owe to our Armed Forces, to pay tribute to those who made the ultimate sacrifice defending our freedoms, and to thank the personnel keeping us safe tonight.

We have a moral duty to stand by our veterans and the military families who sacrifice so much. They are the best of us, and we owe them our support as well as our gratitude and admiration.

Chief of the Defence Staff Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton said:

Today we honour the courage of all those who have served and died in conflict.

For the Armed Forces community, remembrance is a deeply personal time during which we reflect on the service of our predecessors and remember the colleagues we have lost.

That same spirit of service continues to drive the men and women who serve today.

Mark Atkinson, Director General, Royal British Legion:

As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today.

This year we have paid tribute to those who served in more recent conflicts, including the challenging operations in Bosnia, the Iraq War and the first Gulf War, and recognised the families who continue to live with the impact of that service.

From risking their lives in war zones, providing support during emergencies and humanitarian disasters, and spending time away from loved ones, we owe those who serve in the Armed Forces, and the families who stand alongside them, our gratitude. We encourage the nation to pause, reflect and remember their service and sacrifice.

As the 15th anniversary of the end of the Iraq War was marked earlier this year, many veterans will be reflecting on their experiences and the lasting impact of conflict. RAF veteran Steve Hooper, 43, served as a Mechanical Transport Driver during the Iraq War. He will be marching with the Invictus Games Alumni group. He said: 

I saw a lot of trauma in Iraq as an ambulance driver, and when I came back, I was struggling with sleep and having flashbacks. If it wasn’t for the support I received from the Royal British Legion through the Invictus Games, I don’t know where I’d be today.

I am proud to be marching alongside my fellow team members as we reflect on our recovery journeys and remember all those who weren’t as lucky. I’ll also be thinking about the families who still live with the impact of service and conflict. For me, it’s a time to pause, acknowledge and remember.

While the country gathers for Remembrance Sunday, 6,500 UK Armed Forces personnel will remain deployed on operations and at overseas bases. Personnel are currently supporting NATO allies in Eastern Europe, maintaining the continuous at-sea deterrent, and operating across the globe to deter aggression and defend our national interests. This year-round presence ensures the UK is ready to respond to emerging threats.

For those unable to travel to London for the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph or to their local Remembrance Sunday service, the national event will be broadcast live on the BBC, ITV and Sky News.  

ENDS

Notes to editors:

Full media commentary notes are available from the DCMS press office. 

How to watch: 

  • Sky News will broadcast the service live on TV, the Sky News App and website, and on YouTube. 
  • There will be live coverage of the service available on ITV News YouTube and the events of the day will be covered in the ITV News bulletins and throughout the day on ITVX.
  • On BBC television, coverage will be live on BBC One and iPlayer from 10:15. 
  • Additional live streams will also be available as follows from 1015:
    • A version with British Sign Language will be on the Red Button and iPlayer
    • Accessible audio-described commentary is available by selecting Audio Description on your TV or going to BBC iPlayer. 
    • Uninterrupted commentary-free coverage is  available on iPlayer
  • Highlights will be shown in the evening on BBC Two from 7.10pm
  • On radio there will be live coverage on Radio 4 and BBC Sounds.

Plan your journey using the Transport for London and National Rail Enquiries websites.

Check Transport for London status updates and National Rail Enquiries latest travel information before you travel.

Find up-to-date travel information by following National Rail Enquiries on Twitter or downloading the TfL Go app.

items.title: No one who has served our country should sleep rough on our streets
items.summary: No one who has served our country should sleep rough on our streets – Burnham Prime Minister to write personally to councils in England asking them to draw up specific plans to offer accommodation to any veterans sleeping rough ahead of the
items.bodyHtml:
No one who has served our country should sleep rough on our streets – Burnham

  • Prime Minister to write personally to councils in England asking them to draw up specific plans to offer accommodation to any veterans sleeping rough ahead of the Christmas period

  • PM says record funding linked to new drive against rough sleeping creates opportunity to prioritise giving every veteran specialist support to get off the street, consistent with commitments in the Armed Forces Covenant

  • PM urges any veterans who are sleeping on the streets, or those supporting them, to call the UK wide helpline on 0800 9520774 to receive immediate support

  • Commitment comes as government allocates nearly nine million pounds of funding to housing providers across the UK to provide targeted housing, employment and health support for veterans

  • The move is part of delivering the Prime Minister’s instruction on his first day in Downing Street to end rough sleeping in our country

The Prime Minister will say that, from now on, national government and local government should work together to the principle that no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep on the streets.

The Prime Minister’s overall commitment to end rough sleeping is backed by investing an additional £874m to make an overall record of £4.4bn funding.

He will ask councils to use part of this funding to draw up a specific plan to tackle homelessness amongst the ex-forces community, working with local organisations and charities supporting them.

To supplement the work of councils, £8.7 million is being allocated to eight organisations across the United Kingdom, including in Scotland, Liverpool and Kent, as part of the Reducing Veteran Homelessness programme. This funding will help local housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including health, addiction and employment services.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

No one who has served our country should be left to sleep rough on our streets. It is a simple principle and, from now on, I am setting it as an operating principle for the whole of government, national and local.

People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head. When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one.

Many councils are already doing a great job working with charities supporting the ex-forces community. With this new funding, they can take that to the next level and end the need for any veteran to sleep rough on any night.

This is what I meant when I spoke about putting the right standards back at the heart of the country when I walked up Downing Street for the first time.

To help deliver the new commitment, the Prime Minister is urging any veterans who are sleeping rough, or those supporting them, to call the UK-wide helpline on 0800 9520774. It will be able to connect them directly with housing and other specialist support.

The helpline has already supported more than 1,250 veterans into housing to date.

Notes to editors:

Organisations being allocated the £8.7 million of funding include:

The following organisations will receive a share of £8.7m funding as part of the Reducing Veteran Homelessness Programme:

  • Veteran Housing Scotland 
  • Launchpad 
  • Alabare 
  • The Riverside Group 
  • Wigan Council 
  • RBVE 
  • SSAFA, The Armed Forces Charity 
  • Tom Harrison House

items.title: 中国战机再次飞越世界地标性建筑，歼-10 拉出三色彩烟与“万里长城之缩影”惊艳同框
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，空军八一飞行表演队编队昨天低空飞越了天津黄崖关长城，央视新闻今日放出了现场视频。 画面显示，6 架歼-10 表演机保持密集队形，采取低空通场方式飞行，拉出了红、黄、蓝三色彩烟低空飞过长城。 IT之家注：黄崖关长城位于天津蓟州北部，是世界文化遗产 —— 万里长城的重要组成部分，素有“蓟北雄关”之称，也被誉为“万里长城之缩影”。此次飞越也是空军八一飞行表演队继 2018 年飞越黄崖关长城、2024 年飞越埃及金字塔上空后，再次飞越世界地标性建筑。

items.title: 立冬遇强雨雪，湿冷攻击上线，今年台风生成个数刷新本世纪以来纪录
items.summary: 立冬开场，下半年来强度最强、影响最南的冷空气强势上线，北方雨雪天气明显增多，且雨雪交杂。与此同时，南方大范围阴雨还在继续。今早，中央气象台暴雪预警和暴雨预警同时发布，这说明了此轮大范围强雨雪天气的强盛和少见；另外，这次河北和天津，同一个省市，同时出现在暴雪和暴雨预警里，很少见，也说明冷暖空气都很强。其中强降雪核心区域在河北东北部，由于强劲的南风遇上燕山山脉地形加持，个别点不排除特大暴雪的可能性。

items.title: 数字化保护中的权利边界与文化延续——读《非物质文化遗产的数字化保护及其与知识产权保护的冲突与协调》
items.summary: 数字化正在改变非遗被保存、传播和利用的方式。当传统技艺、民间艺术和仪式活动进入数据库、网络平台与商业开发的流程，文化的传播范围随之扩大，围绕它们的权利关系也变得复杂。谁能够决定资料的使用，谁应当分享开发收益，原有的传承群体又处于什么位置？这部著作抓住了这些相互关联的问题，将数字化的技术进展与知识产权保护的制度要求联系起来，考察二者如何发生冲突，又如何寻求协调。

items.summary: “过去谈到职业健康，人们往往更关心工作中的身体损伤和疾病预防。如今，随着人工智能等技术的发展和工作方式的变化，职业健康的内涵不断拓展。长期工作压力、职业倦怠、情绪耗竭以及心理负荷等问题，都值得给予更多重视。”在日前举办的2026年中国职业心理健康大会上，清华大学心理与认知科学系副主任张丹的一番话，道出了AI时代职业健康重心的变化。

items.title: Digital Veteran Card passes 23,000 downloads as veterans encouraged to discover its benefits
items.summary: Veterans encouraged to find out how the digital Veteran Card can help them access discounts and support More than 23,000 digital Veteran Cards downloaded since launch in October 2025 Veterans can apply for the digital version through the GO
items.bodyHtml:
• Veterans encouraged to find out how the digital Veteran Card can help them access discounts and support
  • More than 23,000 digital Veteran Cards downloaded since launch in October 2025
  • Veterans can apply for the digital version through the GOV.UK One Login app once their physical card has been fully processed and dispatched

As the nation prepares to remember and honour those who have served on Remembrance Sunday, veterans are being encouraged to discover the benefits of the digital Veteran Card.

More than 23,000 digital cards have been downloaded since the service launched last October, giving veterans a convenient way to keep proof of their service on their phone.

The digital card can help veterans access discounts at participating shops, restaurants and attractions. It can also help them demonstrate their veteran status when accessing services such as GP registration and relevant health support.

Stephanie Peacock, Minister for Digital Government, said:

Remembrance Sunday is when our whole country comes together to honour the courage, service and sacrifice of our Armed Forces community. We must never forget those who have served our country, or the debt of gratitude we owe them.

Our veterans deserve recognition not just on Remembrance Sunday, but throughout the year. The digital Veteran Card is a practical way to do that, making it easier for veterans to prove their service, keep their card close at hand and access discounts at participating shops, restaurants and attractions.

More than 23,000 digital Veteran Cards have now been downloaded. I want more veterans to know about the benefits their card can offer and have the choice to carry proof of their service wherever they go.

Veterans Minister Calvin Bailey MP, who served in the Royal Air Force and has a digital Veteran Card, said:

We’re determined to make it easier for veterans to access the support and entitlements they deserve. The digital Veteran Card makes it easy to get specialised health services or claim discounts on everyday shopping.

I’d encourage all my fellow veterans to sign up for their Veteran Card - either physical or digital - this remembrance time.

How to get a digital Veteran Card

Veterans must first apply for a physical Veteran Card. Once their application has been fully processed and their physical card dispatched, they can apply for and download the digital version through the GOV.UK One Login app.

The digital version is optional, and veterans can continue to use their physical card if they prefer. Offers and acceptance vary by organisation, so veterans should check before visiting.

Julie Kotecha, a British Army veteran said:

I always ask when I’m out shopping or using services whether there’s a discount for veterans. I’ve found my Veteran Card useful, and people are often impressed by it – it can be a good conversation starter, too.

I’m looking forward to using the digital version because it’ll be much easier to have it on my phone than carry extra cards around. I encourage other veterans to get their card, ask about discounts wherever you go, and make the most of what’s available to you. The team at the Veterans UK office are so helpful and are always happy to help.

Notes to editors

The digital Veteran Card launched in October 2025.

More than 23,000 digital Veteran Cards have been downloaded since launch.

The digital card is optional. Veterans must first apply for a physical Veteran Card and wait until it has been fully processed and dispatched before they can apply for the digital version.

Discounts and acceptance vary by organisation.

From the Tower of London, Andy explains how the Digital Veteran Card provides a simple way for veterans to access support and savings available in recognition of their military career.

Find out how to apply for a Veteran Card: HM Armed Forces Veteran Card: Get a digital version of your Veteran Card - GOV.UK

items.title: UK military satellite Titania launches into orbit following £3bn space investment into defence of space
items.summary: British-built satellite Titania has successfully launched and is in orbit, giving the Armed Forces a new pair of eyes in space. Titania launch comes as new advanced ground sensor trials to track movements and detect threats in space take pl
items.bodyHtml:
• British-built satellite Titania has successfully launched and is in orbit, giving the Armed Forces a new pair of eyes in space.

  • Titania launch comes as new advanced ground sensor trials to track movements and detect threats in space take place.

  • Part of more than £3 billion of defence investment over next four years to strengthen UK’s presence in space and protect satellites critical to daily life.

Britain has a new pair of eyes in space, with the successful launch of British-built military satellite Titania. 

The launch – completed last month – will further help the Armed Forces coordinate their efforts on and above Earth, by improving their ability to observe military activity on Earth from space.

Titania is the second satellite in the UK’s growing constellation of military satellites in orbit, following the successful launch of Tyche in October and will be operated by UK Space Command as part of the ISTARI programme.

Like Tyche, Titania weighs around 100kg – about the size of a washing machine – and orbits the Earth every ninety minutes, travelling at twenty-seven thousand kilometres per hour.  

The successful launch comes as the Ministry of Defence (MOD) also stands up Project Inaros, a new trial of an advanced network of sensors designed to monitor space from three sites around the world. 

Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting MP said: 

The new space age is here. Space underpins everything from weather forecasts and financial transactions to sat-navs and mobile phone connections, and it is critical for our national security and military operations.

Having Titania now in orbit and Project Inaros stepping up how we watch over our satellites means we can see threats sooner, making the UK safer.

Titania and Inaros are British-built and British-designed, backed by more than £3 billion of investment in space capabilities. That means highly skilled jobs across the UK, a stronger industrial base, and a more secure United Kingdom. 

Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth, the Chief of the Air Staff, said:  

The ability to observe the Earth from space is critical to both national resilience and military advantage. This will be demonstrated by Tyche and Titania, alongside Juno and Oberon in the years ahead. 

We will monitor these vital satellites using state-of-the-art technology around the world, including our Inaros sensors – to ensure our Armed Forces can fight and win wherever they are.

Under the ISTARI programme, MOD is delivering satellites and supporting ground systems to expand space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, giving British troops around the world an operational advantage. 

Titania was designed and built in Hampshire by the partnership of Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and BAE Systems as part of a £9.5 million contract, and will be followed by satellites Juno, with SSTL, and Oberon, with Airbus Defence and Space.  

Andrea Thompson, Managing Director, BAE Systems Digital Intelligence & Land, said: 

This programme highlights the strength of the UK’s sovereign space capability and the critical role it plays in protecting the nation. Building on our established heritage in space, we are proud to be investing in advanced technologies, strengthening specialist skills and supporting highly skilled jobs across the UK.  

As a trusted partner to Government, we remain committed to delivering innovative space solutions that enhance the nation’s resilience, security and prosperity for the long term. 

Dr Paul Hollinshead, Chief Executive Officer, Dstl, said: 

Dstl has been at the heart of Titania, from the original concept, through Science and Technology investment, technical development, programme delivery, and successful launch.  

The achievement reflects the expertise, resilience, and dedication of the Dstl team and showcases the value of long-term Defence Science and Technology investment, delivering mission success for our armed forces.

Project Inaros will trial three ground-based neuromorphic sensors, developed by British Australian company Optera in partnership with the National Security Strategic Investment Fund, to monitor movements in space from sites in the UK, Australia, and British facilities on the island of Cyprus.  

This cutting-edge technology, which mimics biological processes by detecting changes in light, could be developed to be an early warning system to spot unusual or threatening activity near UK satellites. Information gathered by Inaros will help UK Space Command units, like No. 1 Space Operations Squadron, No. 2 Space Warning Squadron, and the new No. 3 Space Effects Squadron, to safeguard the UK satellites which guide British ships, connect mobile phones and warn of missile attacks.  

Titania and Inaros will help deliver on the recognition in the Strategic Defence Review that space is increasingly vital to the UK’s national security and daily life. The work is part of the £3bn committed by the Defence Investment Plan for space-based capabilities to protect UK assets in space and strengthen deterrence on Earth. The DIP has committed £298 billion of spending over the next four years.

items.title: Better access to public services central to new Class Unit agenda
items.summary: Bridget Phillipson, Minister for Women and Equalities, hosted cross-sector voices on fixing class inequality Priorities of the new Class Unit set out to drive fairer outcomes in health services, access to jobs and community pride for workin
items.bodyHtml:
• Bridget Phillipson, Minister for Women and Equalities, hosted cross-sector voices on fixing class inequality

  • Priorities of the new Class Unit set out to drive fairer outcomes in health services, access to jobs and community pride for working-class Brits

  • Phillipson says “class stigma, stereotypes and disadvantages” must be confronted head on

Bridget Phillipson, the Minister for Women and Equalities, hosted the first roundtable of the government’s new Class Unit, bringing together experts, community leaders and people with lived experience to help shape its work.

The creation of the Class Unit in the heart of government marks a renewed drive to stamp out the inequalities and barriers that exist for working-class communities.

Initial priorities for the Class Unit discussed at the roundtable included:

  • tackling unequal outcomes in public services, including maternal health outcomes, community safety and opportunities for young people

  • fairer access to good jobs, addressing attainment and access gaps, class stigmas in the workplace and financial security

  • better life chances for every postcode, ending the vicious cycle of child poverty, focusing on intergenerational factors and geographic deprivation that cause deep-rooted disadvantage

Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson, said:

Class stigma, stereotypes and disadvantages are ever present in our lives, from classrooms, to careers or in healthcare.

We’ve taken big steps in the past 2 years to tackle child poverty and level the playing field across our communities, but there’s a long way to go, and the contributions of experts and those with lived experience will be invaluable as we work to shift deep-rooted inequalities.

After the roundtable, the minister spoke to youth participants from Mission 44, a charitable foundation set up by Sir Lewis Hamilton, to hear their perspectives on what practical changes could help them manage the leap from classroom to career.

The Unit will also be leading on the manifesto commitment to commence the socio-economic duty. This is a new legal requirement for public bodies to consider how to improve the lives of lower-income families when making decisions about public services.

Notes to editors

Attendees at the roundtable included:

  • Professor Lindsey Macmillan – Founding Director of the UCL Centre for Education Policy and Equalising Opportunities
  • Professor Fiona Devine – Vice-President and Dean of the Faculty of Humanities and Professor of Sociology, University of Manchester
  • Jason Arthur – CEO, Mission 44
  • Millie Light – Research Associate, Changing Realities Project
  • Katrin McEntee – Strategic Lead – Right to Health, Just Fair
  • Jenny Baskerville – Chief Executive, The Bridge Group
  • Graham Whitham – Chief Executive, Greater Manchester Poverty Action (Resolve Poverty)
  • Ben Plowden – Chief Executive, Campaign for Better Transport
  • Lord Victor Adebowale CBE – Chair of the NHS Alliance
  • Professor Sam Friedman – Professor of Sociology, London School of Economics
  • Priya Sahni Nicholas – Co-Executive Director, The Equality Trust
  • Carl Cullinane – Director of Research and Policy, The Sutton Trust
  • Chris Wellings – Director or Learning and Impact, Thrive at Five
  • Savannah Burney – Senior Policy Adviser, Barnado’s

Supporting statistics

  • Women in the most deprived areas are twice as likely to die in childbirth as those in the least deprived (Amos investigation, MBRRACE-UK)

  • 36% of people in top jobs were privately educated, against 7% of the population (Sutton Trust, Elitist Britain 2025)

  • 27% of children live in poverty after housing costs – 72% of them are in working families (Department for Work and Pensions, Households Below Average Income (HBAI) statistics 2024 to 2025)

items.title: Major boost for young people in Luton as Youth Hub opens to support them towards work
items.summary: New Youth Hub open from Monday to Friday will offer CV advice, skills training, mental health support, housing advice, and careers guidance under one roof. With almost a million young people not in education, employment or training Youth Hu
items.bodyHtml:
• New Youth Hub open from Monday to Friday will offer CV advice, skills training, mental health support, housing advice, and careers guidance under one roof. 

  • With almost a million young people not in education, employment or training Youth Hubs will open in every local area in Great Britain to give young people access to vital support on their doorstep. 

  • Opening comes as Government invests £2.5 billion to ensure all young people have the opportunity to earn or learn.

Young people in Luton are set to benefit from expanded employment support through a new Youth Hub in the area, as the government continues to deliver opportunity directly into the heart of the community. 

Youth Hubs are locations which bring together Jobcentre Plus, local authority services, employers and training providers under one roof to provide vital help to get young people aged 16 to 24 back on track. 

The Youth Hub for Luton will be based at Arndale House, 37 The Mall, Luton LU1 2LJ.  

Open from Monday to Friday the Hub is part of the Government’s commitment to deliver a Youth Hub in every local area of Great Britain, building a national network of support for the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training. 

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said:  

This new Youth Hub marks a major step forward for young people in Luton, delivering real support and opportunity right here in the community.

We are determined to bring opportunity to every corner of the country because no matter where you grow up, you deserve the chance to earn, to learn and to get on in life.

As part of the expansion, every Youth Hub will meet a set of minimum standards, ensuring young people can access on-site jobcentre support alongside mental health and housing support, skills and training opportunities, careers guidance and direct connections to employers with live job and apprenticeship opportunities.

The Luton Youth Hub will work with local partners including Luton Borough Council, The Culture Trust, Total Wellbeing Luton and LBC Housing team to deliver tailored support that reflects the needs of the local economy, helping to break down barriers to work and accelerate pathways into employment. 

Youth Hubs will be expanded to over 360 areas across Great Britain over the next three years, from Manchester and Salford to Dundee and Newport. 

The localised approach to employment support builds on the eight youth trailblazers across England, backed by £90 million, which are testing innovative ways to identify young people most at risk of falling out of education, employment or training and matching them up to local training or job opportunities. 

Together, these steps are transforming how support is delivered, moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach and delivering practical, personalised support that gets young people into jobs and drives opportunity in every community.

Additional information

  • Youth Hubs support young people aged 16–24. 

  • The programme brings together national and local partners to deliver integrated employment support. 

  • Further Youth Hubs will continue to roll out across Great Britain as part of the Government’s Youth Guarantee.

items.title: Flood risk reduced for Severn Stoke ahead of winter months
items.summary: Severn Stoke Flood Scheme finishes ahead of schedule Homes, businesses and infrastructure has flood risk reduced ahead of winter The government’s flood programme is helping grow the economy by investing a record £10.5 billion until 2036 The
items.bodyHtml:
• Severn Stoke Flood Scheme finishes ahead of schedule
  • Homes, businesses and infrastructure has flood risk reduced ahead of winter
  • The government’s flood programme is helping grow the economy by investing a record £10.5 billion until 2036

The scheme, which finished ahead of schedule, was delivered in partnership by the Environment Agency and Worcestershire County Council, working with contractors Alun Griffiths Construction Ltd.

Works included creating a new flood bank that runs to the west of the village. New drainage works to manage surface water and a section of raised road where it crosses over the flood bank.

Additional landscaping including tree planting, habitat creation and fencing will be completed over the coming months.

Construction of the Severn Stoke Flood Scheme.

Charlie Chandler, Area Flood Risk Manager for the West Midlands at the Environment Agency, said:

Across the country, the government is investing at least £10.5 billion up until 2036 into new and existing flood defence that will benefit nearly 900,000 properties.

As part of this, we are delighted to have delivered the Severn Stoke scheme ahead of schedule, helping to reduce flood risk for residents, businesses and visitors.

Councillor Josh Robinson, Cabinet Member for Environment and Communities at Worcestershire County Council, said:

Residents in Severn Stoke know better than most the disruption and worry that flooding can bring. That’s why it’s great to see this flood alleviation scheme operational ahead of winter, helping to protect homes, businesses and vital transport links.

Most importantly, it will give local people added reassurance and confidence as we head into the months when flood risk is often at its highest.

Part of the Severn Stoke flood scheme.

Severn Stoke has a long history of flooding from the River Severn, with the community severely impacted during recent winters. 18 properties, the local church, the local pub and the A38 have all been affected during periods of significant flooding. 

The Environment Agency has funded approximately £5 million of delivery costs, with Worcestershire County Council contributing a further £250,000. 

The government’s flood programme is also helping grow the economy, creating thousands of jobs,  protecting homes and businesses against billions of pounds of economic damage, and unlocking the building of new homes and businesses.  

Additional info: 

  • The war memorial will be accessible this weekend (Nov 7 and Nov 8) for the armistice day gatherings.
  • The Environment Agency has launched a ‘one stop shop’ for flooding guidance
  • This winter make sure you get flood warnings

items.title: 饶河口岸完成2026年明水期通关任务
items.summary: 中新网双鸭山11月6日电 (罗伟 张颖 田德雨)11月6日，随着“饶华渡631”轮渡船从俄方码头顺利返航停靠饶河口岸，饶河口岸2026年度明水期客货通关工作圆满收官，口岸正式进入季节性闭关模式。整个通航期间，口岸通关效能持续提升，跨境贸易与人流热度高涨，交出亮眼的跨境通关成绩单。饶河口岸作为国家一类客货口岸，是通往俄罗斯远东地区的重要门户，也是中俄海陆联运的桥梁和联结东北亚区域经济合作的纽带。

items.title: 2026年新疆消防宣传月活动启动

items.summary: 中新网海口11月6日电 (记者 王子谦)海南自贸港全岛封关运作以来，依托开放第五、第七航权优势，航空物流跑出“加速度”。记者6日从海南省交通运输厅获悉，今年前三季度，海南省航空货邮吞吐量26.6万吨，同比增长5.3%；其中境外货邮吞吐量3.7万吨，同比增长83.7%。
