items.title: New NHS blood test trial to help spot cancers earlier
items.summary: More than 20,000 NHS patients to take part in world-first cancer blood test trial Major research taking place in at least 200 GP practices in England targeted at wide range of abdominal cancers Government-funded programme aims to catch canc
items.bodyHtml:
• More than 20,000 NHS patients to take part in world-first cancer blood test trial
  • Major research taking place in at least 200 GP practices in England targeted at wide range of abdominal cancers
  • Government-funded programme aims to catch cancers before they develop

A world-leading new trial is being launched across at least 200 GP practices in England aimed at providing earlier diagnosis for a range of the most common cancers.

More than 20,000 NHS patients will take part in the trial to assess whether simple blood tests can spot prostate, ovarian, bowel, pancreatic, stomach, liver and other abdominal cancers.

Participating patients aged 45 and over who visit their GP with abdominal symptoms - such as persistent bloating or discomfort - will be offered the chance to take part in the trial. 

The cutting-edge blood tests aim to detect early markers of cancer before more severe symptoms develop, providing the potential to catch and treat major cancers before they can progress. 

Around 71,000 people are diagnosed with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer in England each year, and there are almost 35,000 deaths from these cancers.

Abdominal cancers are often found too late. Around 9 in 10 people diagnosed with bowel cancer at stage 1 survive at least 5 years, compared with around one in 10 at stage 4.

This new trial gives the chance for clinicians to catch these conditions earlier, when treatment is more effective, potentially saving lives.

Secretary of State for Health and Social Care Yvette Cooper said:

The earlier cancers are diagnosed, the more chance they can be successfully treated, and lives can be saved. This world-first trial will establish whether simple blood tests can help GPs identify much sooner the patients who need urgent support.

Innovations like these are a key part of our National Cancer Plan, which will provide faster diagnosis, more effective treatment, and better care for every patient, while also investing in the trials and technology that offer hope of curing cancer for good.

The blood tests patients will receive through the trial, called STRIDE-RCT, will look for signs of several cancers in a single sample and suggest where in the body they come from.

Most of the tests in the trial, developed by the University of Birmingham, will ask patients to have one or two tubes of blood taken at their GP practice, alongside routine blood tests.

The tests use a variety of the latest technology - including artificial intelligence and measuring proteins in the blood.

A positive result will help the GP and patient decide whether an urgent referral is needed but it is not by itself a confirmed cancer diagnosis.

Jonathan Reynolds, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, said:

Cancer affects all of us at some point in our lives, and millions of people up and down the country will know how it feels to face that awful uncertainty while they wait for a diagnosis. Finding cases early is key - giving patients a clear path to treatment and helping save lives.

The UK is a world leader in medical science research, and this trial shows how important that leadership is in bringing forward breakthroughs that can make a real difference to people.

The cancers covered by the trial will include:

  • bowel
  • small bowel
  • stomach
  • oesophageal
  • pancreatic
  • liver
  • bile duct and gallbladder
  • ovarian
  • endometrial
  • kidney
  • bladder
  • prostate

The trial will assess how well the tests work alongside GPs’ judgement before an assessment is made on rolling them out nationwide. 

Professor Peter Johnson, NHS National Clinical Director for Cancer and chair of the Office for Life Sciences (OLS) Cancer Healthcare Goals programme, said: 

Detecting abdomen cancer early is notoriously difficult because the symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions, but the NHS is determined to find a solution.

We are at the start of revolution in cancer diagnosis, and this trial will help us to find out whether blood tests can help GPs get the right patients to the right tests sooner, supporting earlier diagnosis when treatment is most likely to be successful.

It is vital that we gather the evidence about these new technologies and I am grateful to everyone taking part in this research.

Currently, just 2% to 6% of urgent referrals for cancer result in a diagnosis.

By giving GPs another tool to decide who needs further tests, the technology looks to reduce this figure and free up appointments for those with a genuinely urgent need.

Funded by the Office for Life Sciences through the government’s National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), the trial will receive up to £8.49 million of government funding and will cover a broad range of inner-city, rural, seaside and deprived communities.

This supports one of the main ambitions in the National Cancer Plan for England to identify cancers earlier, giving people the best chance of survival. It builds on progress already made, with 250,000 more people diagnosed on time or having cancer ruled out last year than in the year before the 2024 election.

This world-first trial underlines the UK’s leadership in life sciences, with companies from around the world looking to work with the NHS to evaluate these cutting-edge blood tests. It builds on the government’s Life Sciences Sector Plan and wider Industrial Strategy, backing research to bring new treatments to patients, create high-skilled jobs and become Europe’s leading life sciences economy by 2030.

The Chancellor recently announced £1 billion in public-private life sciences investment, supporting more than 1,000 jobs and the development of new treatments, bringing the total secured since the plan launched in July 2025 to more than £4 billion. The government has also met its target to set up at least 95% of commercial clinical trials within 150 days, helping patients access potentially life-changing treatments sooner. These efforts to boost the life sciences sector mean NHS patients will be at the forefront of the latest medical innovations with the potential to transform care.

Additional quotes

Professor Aneel Bhangu, consultant colorectal surgeon, Director of the Surgical Data and Policy Lab and Co-Chief Investigator, said:

Too many patients with cancer reach me after months of vague symptoms that were hard to pin down. At the same time, most people referred urgently do not have cancer, causing unnecessary worry and expense.

These blood tests might help GPs tell the 2 apart, but we need to know for certain before they are used across the NHS, and this trial is designed to give that answer quickly.

Dr Anisha Patel, NHS GP, author and bowel cancer survivor, said:

As a GP and someone diagnosed with stage 3 bowel cancer at a young age, I know how much earlier diagnosis matters.

The challenge in general practice is that cancer symptoms can be vague and overlap with many other conditions.

Cancers such as pancreatic, ovarian, bowel and stomach cancer can sometimes be difficult to recognise early, and a later diagnosis can mean fewer treatment options and poorer outcomes.

This trial offers real hope that blood tests could help us improve early diagnosis by identifying sooner who needs further investigation. 

Alongside this innovation, listening to patients, taking their concerns seriously, following up persistent symptoms and ensuring screening attendance must remain at the heart of our care.

Professor Lucy Chappell, NIHR CEO and Department of Health and Social Care Chief Scientific Adviser, said:

Abdominal cancers are frequently aggressive and difficult to detect. This is devastating for so many patients and their families and claims thousands of lives every year.

For the last 20 years, NIHR has invested in high quality research that transforms patient care. This NIHR and OLS-supported study will assess whether harnessing cutting-edge technologies and placing multi-cancer detection blood tests directly into routine GP consultations can provide earlier diagnosis for these cancers.

This could be game-changing, with potential to streamline urgent referrals, ease NHS pressures, and deliver earlier diagnoses when treatments are most effective.

Michelle Mitchell, Chief Executive of Cancer Research UK, said:

Symptoms such as bloating and stomach pain are common and could have many causes, making it difficult for GPs to know when to investigate for cancer. As a result, some cancers may go undetected until they are at a later stage, when they are harder to treat.

GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need. This trial exploring whether blood tests could help GPs identify people who need further tests and, ultimately, diagnose cancers earlier is welcome. The findings will be valuable in guiding further research, including whether these tests could be used in the NHS.

Jodie Moffat, Director of Charitable Impact at Bowel Cancer UK, said: 

We welcome this new trial, which will help to guide improvements in the diagnosis of bowel cancer.

Diagnosing bowel cancer can be tricky, particularly when the symptoms could be caused by a range of different diseases, so innovations which help health professionals to work out which patients need to be urgently referred would be a very positive step forward.

We look forward to seeing the results of the trial and are excited to see the positive difference it could make to the lives of many affected by bowel cancer.

Alfie Bailey-Bearfield, Head of Policy and Influencing at Pancreatic Cancer UK, said: 

We desperately need new tools to help doctors detect pancreatic cancer in time to save lives. Vague symptoms - like persistent tummy pain and indigestion - make it incredibly challenging to decide who should be urgently referred to hospital for tests.

It’s really encouraging to see the effectiveness of promising blood test technologies rigorously trialled at scale here in the UK. We are excited to see whether this new approach can help identify people at risk at an earlier stage, when pancreatic cancer is more treatable.

Currently, half of people with this devastating disease die within just 3 months of their diagnosis. Successful results from this study could guide the development of new tools and, in future, give many more people with pancreatic cancer the very best chance of survival.

 Associate Professor Dmitri Nepogodiev, consultant in public health at the University of Birmingham and Co-Chief Investigator, said:

Abdominal cancers are often found late, and people in our most deprived communities are more likely to be diagnosed in an emergency.

We have designed the trial to include practices in inner cities, coastal towns and rural areas, so the results apply to everyone the NHS serves.

items.title: Secretary of State hails PSNI anniversary as a 'major milestone'
items.summary: Acknowledging the 25th anniversary of the formation of the PSNI, Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant, said: The 25th anniversary of the establishment of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) marks a major milestone in the history of
items.bodyHtml:
Acknowledging the 25th anniversary of the formation of the PSNI, Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant, said:

The 25th anniversary of the establishment of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) marks a major milestone in the history of Northern Ireland.

A quarter of a century ago, Northern Ireland embarked on a path to deliver a modern, accountable, and representative police service capable of attracting and sustaining the support of the whole community. It was a core pillar of the vision set out in the Belfast Agreement.

Twenty-five years on, there has been a significant transformation in policing.

I pay tribute to all the men and women from across Northern Ireland who have stepped forward to serve their communities with courage, professionalism and integrity, and dedicated themselves to keeping the public safe.

I also pause to remember those officers who paid the ultimate price in the line of duty over the last 25 years, as well as those who served before them in the Royal Ulster Constabulary. Their sacrifice, and the sacrifice of their families, will never be forgotten.

Policing has faced profound challenges, but the fundamental principle of policing by consent remains the bedrock of a peaceful and prosperous Northern Ireland.

To all who serve and have served in the PSNI, thank you for your unwavering commitment to public service.
items.bodyText:
Acknowledging the 25th anniversary of the formation of the PSNI, Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant, said:


  The 25th anniversary of the establishment of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) marks a major milestone in the history of Northern Ireland.

  A quarter of a century ago, Northern Ireland embarked on a path to deliver a modern, accountable, and representative police service capable of attracting and sustaining the support of the whole community. It was a core pillar of the vision set out in the Belfast Agreement.

  Twenty-five years on, there has been a significant transformation in policing.

  I pay tribute to all the men and women from across Northern Ireland who have stepped forward to serve their communities with courage, professionalism and integrity, and dedicated themselves to keeping the public safe.

  I also pause to remember those officers who paid the ultimate price in the line of duty over the last 25 years, as well as those who served before them in the Royal Ulster Constabulary. Their sacrifice, and the sacrifice of their families, will never be forgotten.

  Policing has faced profound challenges, but the fundamental principle of policing by consent remains the bedrock of a peaceful and prosperous Northern Ireland.

  To all who serve and have served in the PSNI, thank you for your unwavering commitment to public service.

items.title: 北京队主场大胜宁波队 豪取CBA常规赛八连胜
items.summary: 中新社北京11月4日电 （记者 国璇）11月3日晚在北京首钢冰球馆举行的2026-2027赛季中国男子篮球职业联赛（CBA）常规赛第8轮较量中，北京首钢队（简称“北京队”）主场以120:88大胜宁波町渥队（简称“宁波队”），豪取八连胜，以全胜战绩稳居积分榜头名。

items.title: 菲律宾央行：货币政策仍处紧缩周期 通胀预计数月后见顶
items.summary: 中新社马尼拉11月4日电 (记者 周璟)菲律宾央行行长雷莫洛纳3日表示，鉴于通胀仍处高位，菲律宾央行目前处于货币紧缩周期，预计通胀将在未来数月达到峰值。

items.title: 旅俄侨界举行纪念孙中山先生诞辰160周年座谈会
items.summary: 中新社莫斯科11月3日电 (记者 田冰)由俄罗斯中国和平统一促进会、俄罗斯华侨华人联合总会主办的纪念孙中山先生诞辰160周年座谈会3日在莫斯科举行。中国驻俄罗斯大使馆临时代办张伟、旅俄主要侨团负责人、留学生和侨胞代表等出席活动。

items.title: 中国微短剧何以全球“圈粉”
items.summary: 近年来，凭借独特内容优势与成熟产业体系，中国微短剧迅速走红全球，成为数字时代中华文化出海的鲜活载体与传播力量。法国、美国、加拿大等多国影视从业者的创作实践与行业观察表明，中国微短剧立足人类共通情感、深耕本土化创作，为中外文明交流互鉴、全球文化产业创新发展注入了新动能。

items.bodyHtml:
• Professor Dapo Akande elected as judge to the International Court of Justice following crunch UN vote 
  • Leading international lawyer and academic received support from majority of UN Member States
  • Election underlines the UK’s commitment to the international rule of law as UK judge returns to Court after 9 years

A new UK judge, Professor Dapo Akande, has today been elected as a judge to the International Court of Justice (ICJ).

In an ever more challenging world, Professor Akande will play a key, independent role in ensuring the Court continues to uphold the international rule of law. 

For almost a decade the UK has not had a judge in the International Court of Justice, but following a campaign backed by the Prime Minister, UK ministers and diplomats across the world, Professor Akande will now be a judge at the ICJ for the next 9 years.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

This election is a clear signal to our partners that the UK is back on the world stage and ready to play our part in ensuring global stability and upholding the rule of law.

Professor Akande will bring integrity, legal rigour and independent expertise to the International Court of Justice and I am incredibly proud that he is representing the UK.

Professor Dapo Akande said: 

I am deeply honoured to be elected to the International Court of Justice. 

I am incredibly grateful to all the states that have put their faith in me. I pledge to serve with independence and to deciding cases on the basis of a faithful and impartial application of the law. I look forward to contributing to the ICJ’s vital work in helping to resolve disputes by peaceful means, alongside the other colleagues elected today.” 

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: 

Everywhere I go around the world, people tell me how impressive Professor Akande is and we have been proud to support his campaign. I am confident that his legal expertise, independence and commitment to international law will make him an asset to the Court and the international community.” 

This is a victory for the UK’s commitment to the rule of law and our ability to stand up for our values on the world stage.

A Professor of Public International Law and a Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, Professor Akande is also an elected member of the UN International Law Commission.

Originally qualified as a lawyer in Nigeria, and now one of the UK’s foremost international lawyers, with nearly three decades of experience as a scholar and practitioner, Professor Akande has built a career of global reach.

He has acted as counsel, adviser and expert in cases before international courts and tribunals, including the ICJ.

As an independent practitioner, he has advised governments from States across all five UN regional groups, as well as international organisations including the UN and the African Union.

Telephone 020 7008 3100

Email the FCDO Newsdesk (monitored 24 hours a day) in the first instance, and we will respond as soon as possible.

items.title: Child Trust Fund injustice to end under Government plans
items.summary: Easier access to savings for thousands of young adults lacking the mental capacity to make financial decisions Families spared complex and lengthy court process under new reforms Part of Government’s plan to create a fairer Britain for ever
items.bodyHtml:
• Easier access to savings for thousands of young adults lacking the mental capacity to make financial decisions

  • Families spared complex and lengthy court process under new reforms

  • Part of Government’s plan to create a fairer Britain for everyone

Young people lacking the mental capacity to make financial decisions will finally have easier access to their savings, ending a long-standing injustice that has created unnecessary barriers for families. 

Following years of campaigning and legal difficulties faced by families, new legislation will be introduced by the Government to allow simpler access to Child Trust Funds, replacing the complex and often costly Court of Protection process.  

The reforms are expected to allow parents and carers to go directly to Child Trust Fund providers to access savings, solving years of unnecessary anguish for an estimated 63,000 to 126,000 young adults. 

Child Trust Funds were introduced in 2005 to provide children a financial boost as they start adulthood, but the scheme made no provision for 18-year-olds who lacked the mental capacity to manage their finances without a straightforward way to access their savings.  

Campaigners, disability charities, and the financial services sector will help shape the new process, protecting young people while pulling down barriers that have frustrated families for years. 

Justice Minister, Jake Richards said: 

Young people who lack the mental capacity to make financial decisions should be able to access their savings as easily as possible – especially when this money was put aside by loved ones to help them take their first steps into adulthood. 

This is simply an injustice that we’re finally putting right and as campaigners have argued for years, change is long overdue. This legislation will ensure this group of young adults no longer face difficulty from accessing money that is rightfully theirs.

Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Rt Hon Lucy Rigby KC MP, said:

The changes that we’re introducing will help tens of thousands more young people to connect with their Child Trust Funds – worth on average £2,600 each.

I’m so pleased that we will finally ending this long-standing injustice and I’m grateful to everyone who has worked with us to make this happen.

The Government will work with various stakeholders to explore how the new process is designed, including who can access funds, what evidence is required and what proportionate safeguards are necessary to protect young people who lack mental capacity without creating unnecessary and costly red tape. 

The scheme won’t replace the important work of the Court of Protection, which will remain available as an alternative route to protect the financial interests of adults lacking the mental capacity to make financial decisions. 

The Government will bring forward an amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill to enable the new scheme, with the details to be set out in secondary legislation following Parliamentary approval. 

Anna Bird, CEO of Contact says:

We warmly welcome the government’s commitment to legislate for a simpler way for young disabled people to access savings in Child Trust Funds. For too long, tens of thousands of young disabled people and their families have faced a complicated and costly process to access money that rightfully belongs to them.

This marks a significant breakthrough after six years of determined campaigning led by parent carer Andrew Turner, whom Contact has proudly supported. We congratulate Andrew and all the parent carers who have campaigned to bring about this change.

We thank the Minister, Jake Richards MP for listening and committing to act. We look forward to working with families, the government and financial providers to turn this commitment into a straightforward scheme with appropriate safeguards.

Andrew Turner, parent campaigner, said:

This bold move from the government is extremely positive news for tens of thousands of young people who have been locked out of their Child Trust Fund savings.

By removing the barriers that make it hard for people to invest in child savings schemes for disabled children, you also create the opportunity to build a stronger financial foundation for their future. 

A simpler process for accessing these savings will release millions of pounds of benefit and help reduce the administrative burden on parents supporting a disabled child.

I am extremely grateful to Minister Richards and the government for their commitment to solving this long-running issue and look forward to working with them to deliver a much-needed solution.

items.title: Charity regulator appoints interim managers to Wirral community transport charity amidst ongoing investigation
items.summary: The charity was placed under statutory inquiry in June 2026 to investigate governance and financial concerns including allegations of having too few trustees, being in breach of its governing document, and that it has not complied with stat
items.bodyHtml:
The charity was placed under statutory inquiry in June 2026 to investigate governance and financial concerns including allegations of having too few trustees, being in breach of its governing document, and that it has not complied with statutory accounting requirements and has expenditure that does not seem to align with its objects. 

Gareth Harris and James Dowers of RSM have now been appointed as interim managers of the charity to the exclusion of the charity’s trustees. The Interim Managers will: 

  1. Protect the charity’s assets and review its finances and financial controls.
  2. Examine its governance and operational arrangements and assess whether changes are needed to safeguard the charity and its beneficiaries.
  3. Consider the charity’s longer-term viability and report regularly to the Commission.

The appointment, which took effect on 12 October 2026, will remain in place until the Commission varies or ends the order. The Commission’s inquiry into the charity remains ongoing.  

ENDS  

Notes to editors:  

  1. The Charity Commission is the independent, non-ministerial government department that registers and regulates charities in England and Wales. Its ambition is to be an expert regulator that is fair, balanced, and independent so that charity can thrive. This ambition will help to create and sustain an environment where charities further build public trust and ultimately fulfil their essential role in enhancing lives and strengthening society.    

  2. Merseycare Transport Services Ltd is now known as Merseycare Community Transport Ltd under the same registered charity number (1133408).

  3. More information on the scope of the inquiry into Merseycare Transport Services Ltd can be found here: Charity Commission investigates Wirral community transport charity - GOV.UK

  4. On 12 October 2026, the inquiry exercised the Commission’s power to appoint an Interim Manager by Order under section 76(3)(g) of the Charities Act 2011 to the exclusion of any trustees.    

  5. Information about the Charity Commission’s appointment of Interim Managers can be found on GOV.UK: When and how the Charity Commission appoints Interim Managers - GOV.UK 

  6. Merseycare Transport Services Ltd is an independent charity and community transport provider based in Wirral. It has no corporate connection to Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust, which is a separate NHS healthcare organisation.

Contact the press office

Email pressenquiries@charitycommission.gov.uk

items.title: Supply chain Adjudicator urges farmers to speak up over unfair supply contracts
items.summary: Farmers are being encouraged to raise concerns about their supply contracts, as the Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator continues his work to promote fairer trading practices and improve relationships between farmers and purchasers. The A
items.bodyHtml:
Farmers are being encouraged to raise concerns about their supply contracts, as the Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator continues his work to promote fairer trading practices and improve relationships between farmers and purchasers. 

The Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator Richard Thompson published his second annual report today (Tuesday 3 November), highlighting progress in promoting fairer trading practices across the dairy and pig sectors. 

The Adjudicator has been working closely with farmers and businesses across the UK’s milk and pig sectors to promote fair dealing, improve understanding of supply contract obligations and encourage better trading practices. 

In one case, the ASCA helped a dairy farmer secure clearer contract terms after concerns they could be prevented from selling surplus milk to other buyers. By raising the issue with the processor while protecting the farmer’s identity, the office helped secure changes confirming farmers could sell surplus milk elsewhere. 

Richard Thompson, Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator, said: 

Fairer supply chains start with clear contracts, honest communication and a shared understanding of rights and responsibilities. 

We’ve seen how raising concerns early can lead to better contracts and resolve problems before they escalate. Producers don’t need to make a formal complaint to contact us. They can seek advice and raise concerns in confidence. 

With our work now covering milk and pigs, we’ll continue helping producers and purchasers tackle concerns, improve practices and build stronger trading relationships. 

Farming Minister Stephen Morgan said: 

Farmers deserve a fair deal, clear contracts and a level playing field to help their businesses thrive. 

Richard and his team are helping deliver this by working with farmers and processors to resolve concerns and build fairer trading relationships. 

We’re also strengthening protections for dairy farmers, with fair contracts and transparent supply chains vital to a productive, profitable and sustainable sector. 

The report also highlights work with producers, processors and industry representatives to improve understanding of the Fair Dealing Obligations Regulations, identify emerging concerns and encourage better practice across agricultural supply chains.

items.bodyText:
Farmers are being encouraged to raise concerns about their supply contracts, as the Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator continues his work to promote fairer trading practices and improve relationships between farmers and purchasers. 

The Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator Richard Thompson published his second annual report today (Tuesday 3 November), highlighting progress in promoting fairer trading practices across the dairy and pig sectors. 

The Adjudicator has been working closely with farmers and businesses across the UK’s milk and pig sectors to promote fair dealing, improve understanding of supply contract obligations and encourage better trading practices. 

In one case, the ASCA helped a dairy farmer secure clearer contract terms after concerns they could be prevented from selling surplus milk to other buyers. By raising the issue with the processor while protecting the farmer’s identity, the office helped secure changes confirming farmers could sell surplus milk elsewhere. 

Richard Thompson, Agricultural Supply Chain Adjudicator, said: 


  Fairer supply chains start with clear contracts, honest communication and a shared understanding of rights and responsibilities. 

  We’ve seen how raising concerns early can lead to better contracts and resolve problems before they escalate. Producers don’t need to make a formal complaint to contact us. They can seek advice and raise concerns in confidence. 

  With our work now covering milk and pigs, we’ll continue helping producers and purchasers tackle concerns, improve practices and build stronger trading relationships. 


Farming Minister Stephen Morgan said: 


  Farmers deserve a fair deal, clear contracts and a level playing field to help their businesses thrive. 

  Richard and his team are helping deliver this by working with farmers and processors to resolve concerns and build fairer trading relationships. 

  We’re also strengthening protections for dairy farmers, with fair contracts and transparent supply chains vital to a productive, profitable and sustainable sector. 


The report also highlights work with producers, processors and industry representatives to improve understanding of the Fair Dealing Obligations Regulations, identify emerging concerns and encourage better practice across agricultural supply chains. 

Over the coming year, the Adjudicator will continue working with the dairy and pig sectors, while preparing to support the development and potential implementation of fair dealing regulations in the egg sector.

items.title: RSH launches independent inquiry into social housing landlord
items.summary: RSH has the power to hold an inquiry if it suspects that the affairs of a landlord may have been mismanaged, if it has failed to meet a regulatory standard or there is a risk that, if no action is taken by the regulator or the landlord, it
items.bodyHtml:
RSH has the power to hold an inquiry if it suspects that the affairs of a landlord may have been mismanaged, if it has failed to meet a regulatory standard or there is a risk that, if no action is taken by the regulator or the landlord, it will fail to meet a standard.     

RSH Chief Executive Jonathan Walters said:

“A statutory inquiry is a serious regulatory tool that we only use very rarely. This reflects the severity of our concerns with ASHA  and its longstanding failure to put things right. We will use the independent findings to inform our next steps.” 

ASHA is a London-based landlord providing social housing in London and supported exempt accommodation in Birmingham. It is a Community Benefit Society and is designated as a not-for-profit provider.

RSH has notified ASHA and relevant stakeholders of the inquiry.

Scope of the inquiry   

The inquirer is independent from RSH. However, RSH specifies the matters on which the  inquirer is to report.

The inquirer is required to examine the following matters and make findings on whether: 

  • There are or have been any actual, potential, or perceived conflicts of interest within ASHA’s executive team or board.

  • The Board and Executive have the necessary degree of skills, independence and effectiveness to manage ASHA’s affairs.

  • There is any evidence that ASHA, its officers, employees or agents have entered into any arrangements or transactions, made payments, or conferred other benefits for the purpose of advancing the interests of any third parties

  • There have been any instances of ASHA’s social housing assets being used in a way that may be inconsistent with applicable policies, procedures, regulatory requirements and any relevant law.

  • Any officer, employee or agent of ASHA, has contributed to any mismanagement or failure to comply with a standard, and if so to identify such individuals

  • Any matters referred to above, or any other matters uncovered by the inquirer in the course of the inquiry, individually or collectively, constitute mismanagement a failure to meet any of the applicable standards.

The scope of the inquiry may be amended or extended during the course of the inquiry if necessary. 

Certain enforcement powers are only available to RSH following the commencement of an inquiry where specific conditions are satisfied. RSH will consider the findings of the inquiry and determine whether any further regulatory action is appropriate. RSH will publish the outcome of the inquiry following its conclusion.

Ends

Note for editors

  1. A registered provider is responsible for ensuring that it manages itself effectively, achieves the standards set by the regulator, and engages positively with the regulator’s regulatory framework. Where a failing in delivering the outcomes of the standards has been identified, the regulator expects providers to respond in a prompt and effective manner. It may be necessary for the regulator to step in and exercise its powers under the Housing and Regeneration Act 2008 as amended (the Act) when a provider fails to do so. The regulator has published guidance on how the regulator uses and intends to use its statutory regulatory and enforcement powers.

  2. Section 206(1) of the Act sets out the grounds under which the regulator can hold an inquiry. Further guidance on the use of an inquiry can be found on the RSH website.

  3. RSH published a regulatory notice in July 2021 concluding that Ash-Shahada Housing Association Limited is non-compliant with the governance elements of the Governance and Financial Viability Standard. It failed to ensure that it had effective governance arrangements in place that deliver its aims, objectives and intended outcomes for tenants in an effective, transparent and accountable manner; failed to demonstrate that it had an appropriate, robust and prudent risk and control framework in place; and had not been able to demonstrate that it managed its affairs with an appropriate degree of skill, independence, diligence, effectiveness, prudence and foresight.

  4. ASHA has fewer than 1,000 units of social housing and is therefore classed as a small provider. RSH does not issue grades to small providers and only publishes or updates regulatory judgements (previously known as ‘regulatory notices’ for small providers) where we consider there to be serious weaknesses or failings in a landlord’s delivery of the outcomes of our standards.

  5. RSH previously made statutory appointments to ASHA’s board in 2025.

  6. For media enquiries please see our Media enquiries page. For general enquiries email enquiries@rsh.gov.uk.

items.title: Giant 12-tonne box lowered into place for fusion upgrade
items.summary: Engineers at the UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) have achieved a technological milestone, having manoeuvred a massive 12-tonne component into position for the UK’s flagship fusion machine, MAST Upgrade, at UKAEA’s Culham Campus. The doub
items.bodyHtml:
Engineers at the UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) have achieved a technological milestone, having manoeuvred a massive 12-tonne component into position for the UK’s flagship fusion machine, MAST Upgrade, at UKAEA’s Culham Campus.

The double beam box features a double-decker layout designed to house two neutral beam injectors (NBIs). A neutral beam injector plays a vital role in fusion research by firing high-energy neutral atoms into the plasma, raising its temperature to more than 30 million degrees Celsius.

By adding two more injectors to MAST Upgrade’s existing setup, the new double beam box will double the machine’s neutral beam heating power from 4.4 megawatts (MW) to 8.8 MW.

The hotter plasma conditions – expected to double from 30 million to 60 million degrees Celsius – will enable researchers to investigate the technologies and physics needed for future fusion power plants, including the UK’s prototype fusion power plant, STEP.

Andrew Thornton, Head of MAST Upgrade Operations at UKAEA, said:

The lift of the double beam box is a huge step forward for MAST Upgrade. By doubling our heating power, we will explore plasma conditions we simply couldn’t reach before. We will be able to study the stability of higher-pressure plasmas while testing how the MAST Upgrade exhaust system copes with these hotter, higher-performance plasmas.

These are crucial questions for STEP and future fusion power plants. It’s also a great example of the engineering skill and collaboration across UKAEA’s science and engineering teams.

Giant 12-tonne box lowered into place for fusion upgrade

The double beam box lift took place as part of wider MAST Upgrade engineering work, currently underway, including the installation of a new electron Bernstein wave (EBW) microwave heating system. Other engineering upgrades underway include:

  • the transfer and repurposing of power supply equipment from the Joint European Torus (JET)
  • fabrication and installation of the beam line module, which will allow the neutral beam to be formed and injected into the plasma
  • manufacture and assembly of a cryopump, shortly to be installed inside the double beam box vessel, which will control the pressure in the double beam box
  • installation of the positive ion neutral injectors (PINIs)

About the double beam box vessel

The completed double beam box vessel, including its lid, will weigh around 15 tonnes, roughly equivalent to two and a half African elephants. It has a volume of 20 cubic metres, about the same as 130 bathtubs, and is made from 316L stainless steel, a grade widely used in offshore infrastructure and medical implants for its strength, durability and resistance to corrosion. The material also offers good vacuum compatibility, essential for the ultra-high vacuum conditions required inside the vessel.

All major hardware is expected to be manufactured and fitted inside the double beam box vessel by the end of autumn 2027. The vacuum-tight vessel will then be commissioned for use in scientific experiments due to begin in 2028.

items.title: New plans “resurrect” genuine pensions for millions of private sector workers
items.summary: Private sector workers to enjoy a pension that lasts throughout retirement, something public sector workers take for granted. Automatic enrolment got private sector workers saving, now the next step in rebuilding workplace pensions is a def
items.bodyHtml:
• Private sector workers to enjoy a pension that lasts throughout retirement, something public sector workers take for granted.
  • Automatic enrolment got private sector workers saving, now the next step in rebuilding workplace pensions is a default pension for life.
  • DC savers to be given a new option, offering many of the benefits of DB pensions, with introduction of retirement collective pensions.

Over the last 30 years, the vast majority of private sector Defined Benefit (DB) pension schemes, that once provided an inflation protected income for life in retirement, have closed.

The introduction of Automatic Enrolment means nine in 10 eligible private sector workers are now saving, up from four in 10 in 2012. But the vast majority are saving into Defined Contribution (DC) pensions and are left entering retirement with a savings pot rather than a route to a genuine pension that provides a secure income that lasts throughout their later life.

The Government is now acting to resurrect the option of genuine pensions for all private sector workers. Guided Retirement will bring back pensions that pay an income, often inflation protected, for the entirety of your retirement without the need for complex financial decisions.

This is the latest part of the Government’s agenda to fundamentally reform the UK’s offer to today’s workers who are tomorrow’s pensioners. It combines a sustainable State Pension that is the foundation of later-life income, real pensions that all workers pay into during their working lives to enjoy in retirement, and a new National Care Service that will be there for people when they need it.

Minister for Pensions Torsten Bell said:

Private sector workers deserve a much better deal when it comes to pensions. They are doing the right thing and saving for retirement, but when they get there too many are left without a genuine pension.

We are resurrecting proper pensions for private sectors workers, guaranteeing them the option of an income that last throughout retirement and in many cases protection against the rising cost of living - things public sector workers take for granted.

We are going to give pensions back to the people who are working hard and saving for their retirement.

Speaking at the Association of British Insurers (ABI) Long-Term Savings Conference, Minister for Pensions Torsten Bell announced two consultations:

  • Guided Retirement, published jointly with the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and the Pensions Regulator, on how default pensions should work in practice.
  • Retirement Collective Pension Schemes, on draft regulations so these schemes can be used as a default pension under Guided Retirement.

Guided Retirement will require pension schemes to provide a default pension for savers approaching retirement. After years of saving into a DC pension, savers will have the option of a stable income for the rest of their lives, without having to become investment experts overnight.

The need for this is clear. In 2025/26, around 46% of first-time pension pot accesses involved the pot being fully withdrawn and this is not just a UK challenge, with many countries, including Australia leaving individuals facing risk and fear in retirement. Guided Retirement will close that gap by requiring pension providers to offer a genuine pension that protects people from the risk of outliving their savings.

Pensions schemes will do more of the heavy lifting for their members, with, for example, Retirement Collective Pension Schemes (RCPS) pooling risk to deliver stability and growth and providing a fully managed pension people can rely on for life.

The Government is publishing its response to the policy consultation on RCPS today, alongside draft regulations to enable providers to offer them as a default pension.

Choice remains at the heart of the approach. For those savers who want a different option, they will always be free to choose. But for those who do not want to navigate complex decisions alone, Guided Retirement will ensure they get a good deal and a reliable income for the whole of their retirement.

The consultations sets out how default pensions, including Retirement Collective Pension Schemes, should be designed and delivered, how schemes should support members approaching retirement, and how to keep the framework practical. It seeks views on these plans.

Therese Chambers, executive director at the Financial Conduct Authority, said:

People should not have to navigate complex pension decisions alone. Guided retirement will offer a simpler way to turn savings into income, regardless of which workplace pension people have.

The Government is publishing its response to the policy consultation on RCPS today, alongside draft regulations to enable providers to offer them as a default pension.

TPR Executive Director of Strategy, Policy and Analysis, Richard Knox, said:

People need more help to turn a pension pot into a sustainable retirement income, and well-designed default options at retirement will help people navigate these complex and important financial decisions.

Schemes should engage with DWP’s consultation on guided retirement and help make these reforms a success.

Additional information

  • Developed by DWP, HMT, FCA and TPR, the Guided Retirement consultation sets out initial proposals for secondary legislation under the Pension Schemes Act 2026. It will run from 3 November 2026 to 22 December 2026.
items.bodyText:
Private sector workers to enjoy a pension that lasts throughout retirement, something public sector workers take for granted.
    Automatic enrolment got private sector workers saving, now the next step in rebuilding workplace pensions is a default pension for life.
    
DC savers to be given a new option, offering many of the benefits of DB pensions, with introduction of retirement collective pensions.
  


Over the last 30 years, the vast majority of private sector Defined Benefit (DB) pension schemes, that once provided an inflation protected income for life in retirement, have closed.

The introduction of Automatic Enrolment means nine in 10 eligible private sector workers are now saving, up from four in 10 in 2012. But the vast majority are saving into Defined Contribution (DC) pensions and are left entering retirement with a savings pot rather than a route to a genuine pension that provides a secure income that lasts throughout their later life.

The Government is now acting to resurrect the option of genuine pensions for all private sector workers. Guided Retirement will bring back pensions that pay an income, often inflation protected, for the entirety of your retirement without the need for complex financial decisions.

This is the latest part of the Government’s agenda to fundamentally reform the UK’s offer to today’s workers who are tomorrow’s pensioners. It combines a sustainable State Pension that is the foundation of later-life income, real pensions that all workers pay into during their working lives to enjoy in retirement, and a new National Care Service that will be there for people when they need it.

Minister for Pensions Torsten Bell said:


  Private sector workers deserve a much better deal when it comes to pensions. They are doing the right thing and saving for retirement, but when they get there too many are left without a genuine pension.

  We are resurrecting proper pensions for private sectors workers, guaranteeing them the option of an income that last throughout retirement and in many cases protection against the rising cost of living - things public sector workers take for granted.

  We are going to give pensions back to the people who are working hard and saving for their retirement.


Speaking at the Association of British Insurers (ABI) Long-Term Savings Conference, Minister for Pensions Torsten Bell announced two consultations:


  Guided Retirement, published jointly with the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and the Pensions Regulator, on how default pensions should work in practice.
  Retirement Collective Pension Schemes, on draft regulations so these schemes can be used as a default pension under Guided Retirement.


Guided Retirement will require pension schemes to provide a default pension for savers approaching retirement. After years of saving into a DC pension, savers will have the option of a stable income for the rest of their lives, without having to become investment experts overnight.

The need for this is clear. In 2025/26, around 46% of first-time pension pot accesses involved the pot being fully withdrawn and this is not just a UK challenge, with many countries, including Australia leaving individuals facing risk and fear in retirement. Guided Retirement will close that gap by requiring pension providers to offer a genuine pension that protects people from the risk of outliving their savings.

Pensions schemes will do more of the heavy lifting for their members, with, for example, Retirement Collective Pension Schemes (RCPS) pooling risk to deliver stability and growth and providing a fully managed pension people can rely on for life.

The Government is publishing its response to the policy consultation on RCPS today, alongside draft regulations to enable providers to offer them as a default pension.

Choice remains at the heart of the approach. For those savers who want a different option, they will always be free to choose. But for those who do not want to navigate complex decisions alone, Guided Retirement will ensure they get a good deal and a reliable income for the whole of their retirement.

The consultations sets out how default pensions, including Retirement Collective Pension Schemes, should be designed and delivered, how schemes should support members approaching retirement, and how to keep the framework practical. It seeks views on these plans.

Therese Chambers, executive director at the Financial Conduct Authority, said:


  People should not have to navigate complex pension decisions alone. Guided retirement will offer a simpler way to turn savings into income, regardless of which workplace pension people have.


The Government is publishing its response to the policy consultation on RCPS today, alongside draft regulations to enable providers to offer them as a default pension.

TPR Executive Director of Strategy, Policy and Analysis, Richard Knox, said:


  People need more help to turn a pension pot into a sustainable retirement income, and well-designed default options at retirement will help people navigate these complex and important financial decisions.

  Schemes should engage with DWP’s consultation on guided retirement and help make these reforms a success.


Additional information


  Developed by DWP, HMT, FCA and TPR, the Guided Retirement consultation sets out initial proposals for secondary legislation under the Pension Schemes Act 2026. It will run from 3 November 2026 to 22 December 2026.

items.title: PM meeting with Prime Minister Mottley of Barbados: 2 November 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister met the Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Mottley ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua. Setting out his vision for the UK, the Prime Minister said he was focused on building strong friendships abr
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister met the Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Mottley ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua.

Setting out his vision for the UK, the Prime Minister said he was focused on building strong friendships abroad with partners to navigate major global challenges. 

That included on climate, where countries like Barbados were on the front line of rising sea levels, extreme temperatures and significant environmental changes, the Prime Minister. 

It was vital that Commonwealth partners continued to shine a light on the major impacts climate change was causing, the leaders agreed, paying tribute to Prime Minister Mottley’s leadership in this space. 

The Prime Minister then set out how the UK wanted to reset international financial frameworks for debt through the UK-hosted G20 next year. 

Turning to the Prime Minister’s announcement outlining how the UK was offering a structured dialogue for communities impacted by the transatlantic slave trade, the leaders discussed next steps and the Prime Minister thanked Prime Minister Mottley for her ongoing support. 

The leaders looked forward to speaking further during the summit.

items.title: PM meeting with Prime Minister Albanese of Australia: 2 November 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister met Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua. The leaders discussed the increasingly uncertain global landscape and agreed that strong partnerships betwee
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister met Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua. 

The leaders discussed the increasingly uncertain global landscape and agreed that strong partnerships between close allies like the UK and Australia are more important than ever. 

Turning to the AUKUS partnership, the leaders agreed the build programme was making strong progress, and the submarines would play vital role in the defence and security of all three nations. 

The Prime Minister reflected on the UK’s decision to sanction West Bank settlements, and the leaders agreed on the need to stand by the two state solution. 

Both reflected on the impact of the Israel-Palestine conflict on community cohesion and agreed there was no place for anti-semitism in the UK or Australia. 

The leaders also underlined their unwavering support for Ukraine. 

Turning to the close relationship between the UK and Australia, the leaders underlined the importance of ensuring opportunities for young people both at home and abroad. 

On broader migration, the Prime Minister updated on the new rules being rolled out for migrants looking to settle in the UK, and the leaders discussed how best to drive down illegal migration. 

They both looked forward to continuing their discussions during CHOGM and staying in close contact.

items.title: New Government-backed cyber security protections could save UK businesses thousands
items.summary: Government launches cyber security offer for small and medium-sized businesses as part of national response to enhance resilience against cyber threats Thousands of businesses can get a 75% discount on Government’s certification, with thous
items.bodyHtml:
• Government launches cyber security offer for small and medium-sized businesses as part of national response to enhance resilience against cyber threats
  • Thousands of businesses can get a 75% discount on Government’s certification, with thousands more part of key supply chains to benefit for free
  • Organisations including Thales, Capgemini and SANS sign on as software security ambassadors to drive better software security practices and seal shut software vulnerabilities

Thousands of small and medium-sized business owners across the UK can now take advantage of a new Government-backed 75% discount for its Cyber Essentials certification programme – a scheme helping businesses put essential protections in place to safeguard their systems from cyber threats and attacks.

Recent estimates suggest a significant cyber-attack on a UK business or organisation could cost on average £195,0001. The cost of these attacks means money coming out of UK businesses and the people they employ, preventing them from re-investing and growing their business and our economy.

In a speech at the National Cyber Security Centre’s Annual Review today, Cyber Security Minister, Baroness Lloyd will announce how Government is fully backing UK businesses to protect themselves in the cyber race.

The Cyber Essentials certification will be discounted by 75% for micro, small and medium sized businesses – meaning they could pay as little as £80 and no more than £125 (plus VAT) to get peace of mind that their organisation is protected against the most common online threats.

Government is also working with over 230 businesses across industry, who have signed up to the Cyber Resilience Pledge, to help them safeguard their supply chains and ensure they have the essential protections in place.

Pledged organisations will be able to refer groups of SMEs within their supply chains to undertake Cyber Essentials certification completely free of charge. This will include access to a free cyber security advisor for select businesses, who may have limited in-house cyber expertise, to be supported through the process.

This combined package of support is designed to make it easier for micro, small and medium-sized businesses to take practical action on cyber security, while helping strengthen the supply chains of some of Britain’s biggest brands in food, banking and essential services we rely on every day.

Cyber Security Minister, Liz Lloyd said:

Small and medium-sized businesses employ millions of people across our nation, and should not be left vulnerable in the age of rising cyber threats.. We are not going to sit back and let malicious actors take advantage – we will back our SMEs and help them be protected and secure.

We are making it easier and cheaper to access expert cyber support, identify and plug vulnerabilities in their digital systems, and achieve certification through our Cyber Essentials scheme.

It doesn’t matter whether you’re sitting at the head of the table in the boardroom, or working from the kitchen counter at home - if you run a business, no matter the size, securing your digital systems must be a top priority and we’re equipping businesses for the evolving digital future.

This comes alongside a major push to make the software underpinning Britain’s economy more secure. 14 new organisations are joining as the UK’s second cohort of Software Security Ambassadors: Fortinet, Thales, Capgemini, SANS, Risk Ledger, Zscaler, Acubed IT Solutions Ltd, CloudPeek, Dot On, Hippo Digital, Investec, IoT M2M Council, Nine23, and QinetiQ.

Joining the existing ambassadors the companies will work with Government to champion secure software development and encourage the adoption of the Software Security Code of Practice across their supply chains and the wider economy.

The scheme aims to encourage more software developers to build their products aligned to the code of practice – safeguarding their systems from common cyber threats. Ambassadors will also encourage companies in their networks, and in their own supply chains, to meet the expectations of this code of practice. The end goal is securing the software backbone of businesses millions of people rely on every day.

Today’s measures build on the wider package announced as part of the Budget last week, to strengthen the UK’s ability to defend itself as artificial intelligence transforms both the cyber threat and the tools available to tackle it, which included:

  • £70 million for a new National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre within the NCSC to build and maintain a national picture of vulnerabilities across critical national infrastructure and the wider economy.
  • Investing £60 million into a national Cyber Shield, using agentic AI to strengthen the UK’s cyber defences, including a £25 million Challenge Fund supporting UK AI and cyber security innovators.
  • A new NCSC AI Cyber Security Centre of Excellence in Manchester, focused on training and developing the next generation of government cyber and AI experts.
  • £40 million for a National Agentic Security Unit to develop capabilities to monitor and respond to uncontrolled bots and strengthen resilience against agentic incidents.
  • £24 million to enhance public-sector cyber defences, putting advanced AI technology to work protecting our vital public services.

Together with the new support for businesses and collaboration with the software industry, the measures all form part of the government’s concerted drive to strengthen cyber resilience across the UK economy.

Notes to editors:

Cyber Essentials scheme

Cyber Essentials is the minimum standard of cyber security recommended by the Government for organisations of all sizes. Developed by the experts at the NCSC, the certification scheme is aligned to five technical controls designed to prevent the most common internet based cyber security threats.

On top of increasing cyber resilience, organisations with Cyber Essentials which have a turnover of less than £20m, also receive up to £25,000 of cyber liability insurance.

  • See here for further details on the Cyber Essentials Funding Package.

  • The Cyber Essentials First Step Fund, will provide eligible micro, small and medium-sized UK businesses a 75% discount on the cost of a new Cyber Essentials certification. This discount, covered by £2.4m of Government funding, will be on a first comes first served basis to micro, small and medium businesses who have not been certified in the last four years . It will be available until March 2027, or until the allocated funding runs out. Government estimates approximately 6,000 new businesses could benefit from this funding. Businesses can start their certification here Link to offer active from 3 November: firststep.iasme.co.uk
  • The Cyber Essentials for suppliers grant, worth up to £7m until March 2029, will offer eligible UK-based SME suppliers of Cyber Resilience Pledge signatories, fully Government funded first-time certification and tailored Cyber Advisor support through Cyber Essentials. SME businesses nominated for this offer will be contacted by their Cyber Resilience Pledge signatory organisation and guided to apply through the Cyber Essentials process. Government estimates approximately 8000 businesses could benefit from this funding.

Cyber Resilience Pledge

  • The Cyber Resilience Pledge is a voluntary government initiative through which organisations publicly commit to make cyber security a board-level responsibility, sign up to the NCSC Early Warning service and take a risk-based approach to requiring Cyber Essentials across their supply chains. More than 230 organisations have signed the Pledge so far – a full list of signatories available on GOV.UK.

Software Security Code of Practice

  • The Software Security Code of Practice sets out expectations for the security and resilience of software. The Software Security Ambassadors scheme brings together organisations committed to championing secure software development and supporting a resilient cyber ecosystem.

Software Security Ambassadors list:

  • Accenture
  • Acubed IT Solutions Ltd
  • Capgemini
  • Cisco
  • CloudPeek
  • Dot On
  • Fortinet
  • Hexiosec
  • Hippo Digital
  • Investec
  • IoT M2M Council
  • ISACA
  • ISC2Lloyds Banking Group
  • NCC Group
  • Nexor
  • Nine23
  • Palo Alto Networks
  • QinetiQ
  • Risk Ledger
  • Sage
  • Salus
  • SANS
  • Santander
  • Thales
  • Zaizi
  • Zscaler

Sources: [1] Due to lack of available UK-based cost data, the estimate is based on data from primarily US disclosures. The underlying assumption is that average costs for US-based organisations can be compared to the average costs in the UK. The average cost per organisation is scaled up by the estimated number of firms affected by cyber attacks obtained from the CSBS. Please note that for medium and large firms this estimate is based on a limited sample size of 18 and should therefore be interpreted as indicative only.

items.summary: 中新网11月3日电 11月3日，中国气象局今日召开的新闻发布会，国家气象中心副主任黄卓表示，预计11月北方大部气温偏高，冬麦区大部降水偏多，利于冬小麦播种出苗和冬前生长；东北地区大部气温正常或略偏低，降水接近常年，对粮食收晒和储运有利。南方大部气温偏高，降水偏多，其中江淮南部、江汉东南部、江南北部等地降水偏多5至8成，不利秋收扫尾，部分地区可能土壤过湿，易导致冬小麦播种、油菜播栽缓慢；华南南部气温偏高、降水偏少，利于晚稻收获晾晒；西南地区西部气温偏高，降水偏少，农业干旱风险较…

items.title: 靠维生素“续命”？长期猛补更伤身！
items.summary: 维生素常被译为“维他命”，取“维持生命”之意，足见其对人体健康的关键价值。由于人体自身几乎无法合成维生素，只能通过日常饮食获取补充。如今随着年龄增长，不少人总担忧自己维生素摄入不足，将每日补充维生素当成了固定的日常习惯。可补充越多就越好吗？是否会带来负面效果？

items.title: One million more scans to help catch cancer sooner
items.summary: 125 more CT and MRI scanners added since March 2024, helping enable an extra one million scans a year AI-powered MRI technology is helping the NHS see more patients and cut scan times New Manchester and Trafford Community Diagnostic Centre
items.bodyHtml:
• 125 more CT and MRI scanners added since March 2024, helping enable an extra one million scans a year
  • AI-powered MRI technology is helping the NHS see more patients and cut scan times
  • New Manchester and Trafford Community Diagnostic Centre (CDC) showcases how the NHS is bringing tests closer to home

Patients across England are benefiting from faster cancer diagnoses, after one million more scans were delivered thanks to new scanners and cutting-edge AI technology.

NHS England data published on 3 November 2026 shows that, from March 2024 to March 2026, the number of CT and MRI scanners in the NHS has increased by 125, giving doctors greater capacity to diagnose cancer and other serious conditions earlier and get patients into treatment sooner.

The expansion comes as each month in 2026 so far has set an NHS monthly record for diagnostic activity, with the diagnostic waiting list having fallen in 3 of the 5 months since April.

Cancer waiting times are better than last year, and the overall waiting list for elective care is down by over 250,000 since July 2024.

CT and MRI scanners are a vital part of diagnosing cancers including lung, brain, breast and prostate cancer. More scanners mean more patients can get the tests they need sooner, reducing waits and helping speed up diagnosis and treatment. 

Minister of State for Health, Karin Smyth, said:

Getting the right diagnosis and treatment as quickly as possible can make all the difference, particularly for patients with cancer and other serious conditions.

That’s why, in the face of record demand, we are expanding NHS capacity and using new technology to help more people get the tests and care they need.

The 125 new scanners and rollout of AI technology are helping deliver around a million extra scans every year, while the new Manchester and Trafford CDC with its modern facilities and cutting-edge equipment will allow people to get checked quickly and conveniently in the community.

Alongside the expansion in scanning capacity, AI-powered MRI technology is being introduced across the NHS, helping services carry out on average 14% more scans while maintaining image quality. The technology is helping hospitals create thousands of extra appointments and allowing patients to spend less time in scanners.

The new £19.2 million Manchester and Trafford CDC, which officially opened on Thursday 29 October, will further expand access to vital tests and scans, giving patients quicker and more convenient care closer to home.

Professor Peter Johnson, NHS England’s National Clinical Director for Cancer, said: 

Waiting for test results can be an anxious time for anyone worried about cancer, so receiving answers sooner can make a real difference.

By increasing access to scans and using technology to help clinicians see patients faster, the NHS is making it easier for people to get checked quickly and closer to home at a time that suits them.

The earlier cancer is diagnosed, the more treatment options there are and the better the chance of a successful outcome for patients.

Most of the new machines added since March 2024 (107 of 125) have gone into community diagnostic centres, which carried out nearly 2.2 million CT and MRI scans in the 12 months up to March 2026 - an extra million compared with the 12 months up to March 2024.

AI acceleration software has already been installed in more than half (54%) of compatible NHS MRI scanners. The software speeds up scan times as it needs less data to achieve a high-quality image. The saved time can be used to get more patients through each machine per day, meaning at a national level the NHS can increase the number of MRI appointments it undertakes.

Every NHS trust in the country will be given the opportunity to upgrade compatible MRI scanners by 2029. A full rollout would enable existing equipment to deliver up to 162,000 more checks per year.

Dr Stephen Harden, President of the Royal College of Radiologists, said:

Demand for diagnostic scans is rising, so it is vital we have the equipment and workforce to scan, diagnose and treat patients efficiently and safely. We are pleased to see the government continue to roll out newer and AI-enabled scanners that are helping to scan more patients and providing the images radiologists analyse.

Background information

The national figures on the number of scanners come from NHS England’s 2025 to 2026 National Imaging Data Collection (to be published on the morning of 3 November 2026), which shows continued growth in diagnostic scanner capacity.

The NHS estimates that an MRI scan currently takes between 15 minutes and one hour. This depends on what part of the body is being scanned.

Each month in 2026 so far has set an NHS monthly record for diagnostic activity, and the diagnostic waiting list has fallen in 3 of the 5 months since April.

items.title: Care workers, women returning to employment and builders to gain practical AI skills
items.summary: Four Barnsley training projects will share over £800,000 to bring practical artificial intelligence skills into everyday workplaces. The AI Upskilling Challenge Fund targets support where it is needed most, from frontline healthcare to loca
items.bodyHtml:
• Four Barnsley training projects will share over £800,000 to bring practical artificial intelligence skills into everyday workplaces.
  • The AI Upskilling Challenge Fund targets support where it is needed most, from frontline healthcare to local construction and small businesses.
  • Successful solutions from this Tech Town pilot could set a national blueprint for equipping a generation across Britain.

Frontline care staff, builders, and mothers returning to work across Barnsley will gain practical AI skills through four new training projects being awarded funding today (Tuesday 3 November).

Backed by more than £800,000 from the AI Upskilling Challenge Fund, these local initiatives will bring practical, problem-solving tools directly to hospital wards, construction sites, and small businesses.

Four organisations will deliver this hands-on training, focusing on practical outcomes that save time, boost confidence and improve employability:

  • Barnsley College is taking mobile AI training units directly to hospital and social care staff and the wider community, offering practical taster sessions that build confidence and support career progression.
  • Atheni will help 140 people, most aged 40 or over, across six manufacturing, engineering and construction firms in Barnsley. They’ll use AI shaped around each company’s documents and shared trade context, to help with quotes, tenders and safety paperwork.
  • Fossu (Ignite AI), with Barnsley YMCA, Postnatal Minds and Barnsley & Rotherham Chamber of Commerce, will run challenge-led programmes and buildathons for 100 residents, helping women returning to work and young people use AI to solve real problems facing local businesses and communities.
  • Optimise Cyber Solutions, in partnership with Abbeydale Training, will support twenty small businesses across Barnsley to adopt AI safely, confidently and effectively. Combining their expertise in training, digital skills and responsible AI adoption, the partnership will help businesses move beyond basic AI awareness to practical workplace implementation, improving productivity while prioritising  the development of the next generation of female AI leaders.

The pilots form part of the Barnsley Tech Town initiative, demonstrating the government’s commitment to rewiring how public services and skills are delivered. By bringing central and local government together, it returns power to local communities and ensures AI training is designed directly around Barnsley’s unique economic needs.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said:

I know people are worried about what AI could mean for their careers. As this technology changes workplaces, the government will not leave people to navigate this new era alone. 

The schemes we are backing in Barnsley will help set the standard for how we equip people from all walks of life with the skills and confidence they need. By working in partnership with businesses and communities, we are ensuring AI empowers workers, is shaped around local economic opportunities, and builds a future where everyone shares in the rewards.

Minister for the Future of Work, Kate Dearden, said: 

AI is already changing the way we work, and successful adoption depends on workers having the skills and confidence to be part of that change.

Whether you’re a care worker, a builder or a small business owner, it’s important that people understand how AI could change their work and have the skills to help shape how it is used.

That’s why we’re backing projects like this pilot in Barnsley, which will provide practical training shaped around local businesses, their workforces and the needs of the local economy.

Barnsley was named the UK’s first Tech Town in February, as an example of  how AI can improve everyday life through better public services, stronger local businesses and new opportunities for jobs and skills. Working with local schools, colleges, employers, and the NHS, the programme will identify successful approaches that could be rolled out nationwide, helping ensure communities across Britain share in the benefits of AI.

Councillor Luke Wheat, Barnsley Council’s Cabinet spokesperson for Regeneration and Assets, said: 

Tech Town is about making new technology work for Barnsley people and businesses. This funding means practical AI support will be taken directly into workplaces and communities across the borough.

These four projects will help people build confidence and learn skills they can use in their jobs, both now and in the future. It’s about making sure new technology brings real benefits to people’s working lives.

We’ll learn from what works here in Barnsley and share that with others. At the same time, we’ll keep working towards our ambition to become the UK’s leading digital town, making sure our communities across the borough share in the opportunities that growth brings.

Other Tech Town projects are helping Barnsley residents prepare for work and exploring ways to improve local healthcare. The AI Career Launchpad will offer six months of training and paid work placements through Barnsley College. The Getting Job Ready with AI pilot helps jobseekers find roles, improve applications and prepare for interviews. At Barnsley Hospital, another pilot is testing how AI could improve patient care, reduce missed appointments and cut paperwork for staff.

Across the country, more workers and young people will have opportunities to build their skills and enter the tech sector. The government’s AI Skills Boost initiative aims to equip 10 million UK workers with key AI skills by 2030. A further 10,000 work experience placements will help young people take their first steps into the digital and tech sector over the next three years.

Local communities will also get more support to make AI work for them. Building on the experience of Barnsley, the Budget announced a £30 million investment for three of Yorkshire’s regional Mayors, to roll out AI in the service of their communities.

The government is also backing research into what AI means for people’s jobs and living standards. An additional £23 million over three years will support the AI Economics Institute, the world’s first government-backed research institution dedicated to studying AI’s impact on productivity, growth and the wider economy.

Notes to Editors

David Akeroyd, Principal and CEO of Barnsley College, said:

Health and social care staff do vital work, and Barnsley College is making it easier for them to develop AI skills around the demands of their roles.

By offering flexible, practical training in workplaces and out in the community, we’ll help people build confidence in how AI could support their everyday work and progression – wherever they are in both their careers, and their understanding of AI.

Barnsley’s Tech Town ambitions should create opportunities for people across our community. This funding will help us reach staff who might otherwise struggle to access training and give them an accessible starting point for developing new skills.

Chris Annetts, Founder and CEO, Optimise Cyber Solutions said:

Artificial intelligence presents a tremendous opportunity for small businesses, but many lack the confidence, skills or knowledge to use it effectively and safely.

By working in partnership with Abbeydale Training, we’re bringing together our expertise to help local businesses turn AI into a practical tool that improves productivity, saves time and creates opportunities.

I am particularly proud to be supporting this initiative and contributing to Barnsley’s ambition to become a national leader in digital innovation.

Imelda Fossu, CEO, Ignite AI (Fossu Ltd) said:

The best way to learn AI is to build something with it. That’s why we’re delighted to be delivering Build Barnsley. It puts practical, hands-on AI skills in the hands of women returning to work and young people, who’ll work on real challenges set by local employers and community partners.

Louise Ballard, co-founder of Atheni said:

Nobody goes to work to copy and paste. AI can help with the repetitive parts of almost any role, and the people who know the job, whether they’re in the office or on site, bring the judgement and experience to make it useful. Put those together and the combination is formidable. We’re delighted to be working with teams in Barnsley, and what we learn together here could help firms like these right across the country.

Over £800,000 has been awarded across the four successful delivery partners as follows:

  • Atheni Strategy Limited: £231,000
  • Optimise Cyber Solutions Limited: £200,000
  • Fossu Limited: £195,188
  • Barnsley College: £184,403

The AI Upskilling Challenge Fund was announced in July to identify and back innovative organisations capable of delivering practical AI training to underserved groups in Barnsley. 

The Fund forms part of the Barnsley Tech Town initiative, which was announced on 3 February 2026, positioning Barnsley as the UK’s first government-backed Tech Town.

Tech Town supports Barnsley 2030: Barnsley Council’s long-term plan to build a prosperous, better, fairer and more inclusive borough.

For further information see: www.optimisecyber.com/, www.weareignite.ai/build-barnsley or contact barnsley@atheni.ai

About Atheni: Atheni helps people make AI part of their everyday work. Its own AI-powered platform tailors training to each person, their role and their organisation, so whole teams change the way they work across whatever tools they already have. Founded in 2023 by Mackenzie Howe and Louise Ballard, Atheni works across sectors including manufacturing, financial and professional services, and further education. More about its work in Barnsley: atheni.ai/barnsley/

ENDS
