  I am particularly proud to be supporting this initiative and contributing to Barnsley’s ambition to become a national leader in digital innovation.


Imelda Fossu, CEO, Ignite AI (Fossu Ltd) said:


  The best way to learn AI is to build something with it. That’s why we’re delighted to be delivering Build Barnsley. It puts practical, hands-on AI skills in the hands of women returning to work and young people, who’ll work on real challenges set by local employers and community partners.


Louise Ballard, co-founder of Atheni said:


  Nobody goes to work to copy and paste. AI can help with the repetitive parts of almost any role, and the people who know the job, whether they’re in the office or on site, bring the judgement and experience to make it useful. Put those together and the combination is formidable. We’re delighted to be working with teams in Barnsley, and what we learn together here could help firms like these right across the country.


Over £800,000 has been awarded across the four successful delivery partners as follows:


  Atheni Strategy Limited: £231,000
  Optimise Cyber Solutions Limited: £200,000
  Fossu Limited: £195,188
  Barnsley College: £184,403


The AI Upskilling Challenge Fund was announced in July to identify and back innovative organisations capable of delivering practical AI training to underserved groups in Barnsley. 

The Fund forms part of the Barnsley Tech Town initiative, which was announced on 3 February 2026, positioning Barnsley as the UK’s first government-backed Tech Town.

Tech Town supports Barnsley 2030: Barnsley Council’s long-term plan to build a prosperous, better, fairer and more inclusive borough.

For further information see: www.optimisecyber.com/, www.weareignite.ai/build-barnsley or contact barnsley@atheni.ai

About Atheni:
Atheni helps people make AI part of their everyday work. Its own AI-powered platform tailors training to each person, their role and their organisation, so whole teams change the way they work across whatever tools they already have. Founded in 2023 by Mackenzie Howe and Louise Ballard, Atheni works across sectors including manufacturing, financial and professional services, and further education. More about its work in Barnsley: atheni.ai/barnsley/

items.title: UK to lead multinational military training exercise to prepare for peace in Ukraine
items.summary: UK and France to jointly lead thousands of troops from 11 nations in Exercise Koalicja in Poland. Major exercise will test Allies’ readiness to support Ukraine and rebuild their Armed Forces once the conflict ends. 300 UK troops, RAF Typhoo
items.bodyHtml:
• UK and France to jointly lead thousands of troops from 11 nations in Exercise Koalicja in Poland.
  • Major exercise will test Allies’ readiness to support Ukraine and rebuild their Armed Forces once the conflict ends.
  • 300 UK troops, RAF Typhoons and Voyager aircraft will take part, demonstrating the UK’s commitment to Ukraine’s security.

Hundreds of British troops, RAF jets and forces from 11 nations will rehearse how to secure lasting peace in Ukraine when the fighting ends in a major exercise in Poland this month.

The UK and France will jointly lead Exercise Koalicja, the first major exercise run by the Multinational Force Ukraine (MNF-U). MNF-U is the military arm of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of nations who have pledged strengthened military, economic and diplomatic support to Ukraine.

The exercise runs from 9 November to 22 November and will test how to move, protect and supply a force that would help rebuild Ukraine’s Armed Forces once the fighting ends.

300 UK personnel are among the 2,800 troops taking part on land, in the air and at sea. Soldiers from the British Army’s 7 Brigade (the ‘Desert Rats’) will rehearse crucial logistical movements, while RAF Typhoons and a Voyager refuelling aircraft will fly sorties overhead. The jets will simulate how they would reassure commercial air travel once Ukraine’s skies reopen.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP said:

This exercise shows the UK is stepping up, alongside France and our allies, to prepare for the day peace comes to Ukraine. This isn’t a hypothetical plan, it’s a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops.

By leading this work with our allies, we are protecting the UK and Europe for the long term and delivering on our commitment to keep the country safe. Ukraine’s security is our security, and we will stand with them for as long as it takes.

In the event of peace, the MNF-U will help underpin Ukraine’s future security by enabling safer Ukrainian skies and seas and regenerating Ukrainian forces. It would only move into Ukraine once fighting has ceased and at the request of Ukraine’s government. It would not carry out peacekeeping or ceasefire-monitoring duties.

The MNF-U is commanded by British three-star general Lieutenant General Tom Bateman. The UK jointly leads the MNF-U with France, with the force’s headquarters set to move from Paris to London this year.

Commander of the Multinational Force-Ukraine Lieutenant General Tom Bateman said:

This exercise will show that the Multinational Force-Ukraine is a real, capable, readily deployable force that represents a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine’s long-term stability and security.

The MNF-U will be more ready every day to support Ukraine when the fighting ends, ensuring the Armed Forces of Ukraine are in the strongest possible position to deter future aggression.

The 11 nations participating in the exercise are Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Türkiye and the UK.

The exercise will involve testing command-and-control arrangements for the force, rehearsing the movement of personnel, equipment and supplies and assessing how different components can integrate and operate effectively as one multinational force.

As well as the exercise’s land and air components, Turkish forces will stand up the MNF-U’s maritime element in Istanbul, testing arrangements for maritime mine clearance to allow commercial shipping to safely return to Ukraine’s ports.

Ukraine’s security is central to the UK’s own security. The Russian state chose to invade Ukraine, undermining European security and the principle that international borders cannot be changed by force. A stable, secure Ukraine helps protect the UK, Europe and the wider rules-based international order.

Britain continues to strengthen Ukraine’s ability to defend itself by providing military aid and training to Ukrainian forces, while working with allies to maintain economic and diplomatic pressure on the Russian state against a backdrop of continuing barbaric Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine.

The UK has never sought confrontation with Russia and has no quarrel with the Russian people. But not seeking confrontation does not mean failing to defend ourselves and our Allies. The UK will continue to support Ukraine’s right to defend itself, protect UK and European security and work with Allies to deter future threats.

The UK is stepping up defence spending in the biggest sustained increase since the Cold War, reaching 2.7% of GDP from 2027-2028and with nearly £300 billion over four years.

items.title: Government announces new commissioner and interim chair to the Social Mobility Commission
items.summary: Baroness Alison Garnham appointed as Commissioner to the Social Mobility Commission (SMC) Baroness Garnham will also serve as Interim Chair while a new chair is selected The government’s new Class Unit will have a renewed focus on reducing
items.bodyHtml:
• Baroness Alison Garnham appointed as Commissioner to the Social Mobility Commission (SMC)
  • Baroness Garnham will also serve as Interim Chair while a new chair is selected
  • The government’s new Class Unit will have a renewed focus on reducing class inequalities and stamping out child poverty 

The Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson, has announced Baroness Alison Garnham as the new commissioner and interim chair to the SMC.

Last month, the Minister for Women and Equalities announced a drive to improve the life chances of working class people, reduce inequalities faced by lower-income families and open up opportunities through the creation of a Class Unit.

Baroness Garnham will ensure SMC is fulfilling its legal duty until its closure and use her lifetime of expertise as an external advisor to the Class Unit.

The new unit will bring tackling the causes of deprivation to the forefront of the government agenda, sitting alongside other equality units on race, women, LGBT+ and disability.

Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson said:

Tackling the deep rooted inequalities faced by working class families is crucial. From education to health care, your background should not dictate your opportunities.

Our Class Unit will ensure the Commission’s purpose continues right at the heart of government, with ministers rightly accountable for driving action and delivering real change to people’s lives.

I want to thank Alun Francis for his commitment to this agenda over the past 5 years, and look forward to working with Alison with her wealth of experience and expertise, as the SMC goes through this transitional period.

Alison Garnham is currently the Chief Executive of the Child Poverty Action Group (CPAG) and a life peer in the House of Lords. She previously served as CEO of the Daycare Trust and the Director of Policy at One Parent Families (now Gingerbread).

The current chair, Alun Francis, ended his term on 31 October 2026. The government is grateful for the work he and the board of commissioners have completed.

Notes to editors 

Once the government announces the preferred candidate for the permanent role of chair, the candidate will be subject to a pre-appointment hearing from the Women and Equalities Committee.

Alison Garnham was announced as a Labour life peer in the House of Lords in 2026, an elected Fellow of the Academy of Social Sciences, and spent 9 years on the Social Security Advisory Committee.

The Social Mobility Commission is an independent non-departmental public body. It is sponsored by the OEO in the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

Read more about the closure of the Social Mobility Commission.

items.title: HM Land Registry publishes new avoidable requisitions data to help cut delays
items.summary: At a glance Third dataset gives conveyancers fresh information to help improve application quality and reduce preventable registration delays. Wider analysis shows around 400,000 fewer avoidable requisition points were raised in 2025 than i
items.bodyHtml:
At a glance

  • Third dataset gives conveyancers fresh information to help improve application quality and reduce preventable registration delays.
  • Wider analysis shows around 400,000 fewer avoidable requisition points were raised in 2025 than in 2022 - a reduction of 47.7%.
  • HM Land Registry urges firms to use their data alongside free guidance and training to tackle recurring issues.

HM Land Registry has today published its third avoidable requisitions dataset, giving conveyancers and law firms updated information to help prevent errors and omissions in applications that often delay registration and create extra work for them.

The release covers the period 1 April to 30 September 2026 and is intended to help firms review their application quality and focus their checks, training and quality assurance where they can make the most difference. It comes as wider HM Land Registry analysis shows sustained progress in reducing avoidable requisition points since 2022.

A requisition is a request for more information or action before an application can be completed. Avoidable points relate to errors or omissions that could usually have been prevented before submission, such as missing identity evidence, discrepancies in names, unclear plans or missing supporting documents. A single requisition can contain more than one point.

Annual avoidable requisition points fell overall from around 839,000 in 2022 to 439,000 in 2025 - a reduction of 47.7%. After adjusting for application volumes, the rate fell by 39.1%, showing that the improvement was not just the result of fewer applications.

The positive trend continued between January and September 2026, with around 94 avoidable points raised per 1,000 applications - an 11% reduction in the rate compared with 2025. This progress reflects the shared efforts of conveyancers, post-completion teams, industry bodies and HM Land Registry. Read more here: Avoidable requisitions continue to fall as we work together.

Andrew Robertson, Head of Customer Policy at HM Land Registry, said:

Reducing avoidable requisitions is a shared achievement. Conveyancers, post-completion teams and industry bodies have worked with us to improve application quality, helping to reduce unnecessary work and delays for everyone involved.

Our third dataset is an opportunity to build on that progress. We encourage firms to use their data to identify recurring issues and focus their checks and training where they will have the most impact. We will keep improving our guidance, services and the consistency of the requisitions we raise.

Despite the progress, preventable issues still cause unnecessary work. Missing or unclear information is now the most common broad category of avoidable requisition, while identity evidence not being supplied is the most common individual avoidable point.

HM Land Registry is encouraging firms to examine the specific reasons behind their requisitions and use that insight to strengthen pre-submission checks. Free guidance, workshops and training resources are available to help, alongside continuing work within HM Land Registry to improve the accuracy and consistency of requisitions. For more information, see Avoidable requisitions are falling. What’s next?

View the third avoidable requisitions dataset

Notes to editors

  1. The 2022-2026 trend figures are drawn from HM Land Registry’s wider analysis published in its October 2026 blogs (see point 5 below). They should not be described as a comparison of the three published datasets or as findings specific to the third release.
  2. The figures count avoidable requisition points, not individual applications or requisition letters. More than one point can be raised in a single requisition. A rate of 94 points per 1,000 applications does not mean that 9.4% of applications received an avoidable requisition.
  3. Figures are rounded as presented in the source blog. The reported reductions of 47.7% and 39.1% use the source analysis; the latter adjusts for application volumes.
  4. We have emailed each firm’s Responsible Person - the person overseeing its HM Land Registry online account - with more detailed information about the requisition points the firm has received.
  5. Background: Avoidable requisitions continue to fall as we work together, published 12 October 2026, and Avoidable requisitions are falling. What’s next?, published 19 October 2026.
  6. Practical support is available through HM Land Registry’s training hub, including a dedicated resource: Tackling avoidable requisitions.

items.title: New COOs appointed by government agency
items.summary: The Government Property Agency (GPA) has today (Monday, November 2) appointed a duo of highly experienced leaders as its joint Chief Operating Officers (COOs). Erin Robinson and Helen Mills will establish a co-leadership model at the GPA, u
items.bodyHtml:
The Government Property Agency (GPA) has today (Monday, November 2) appointed a duo of highly experienced leaders as its joint Chief Operating Officers (COOs).

Erin Robinson and Helen Mills will establish a co-leadership model at the GPA, under a job-share arrangement, to lead the agency’s corporate services and operational delivery.

The pair established the success of this working model at the former Department for Science, Innovation and Trade (DSIT) where they previously worked together as People and Transformation Directors.

Find out more about this joint appointment on the GPA website.

items.title: 决不能让企业诉求“石沉大海” 重庆荣昌以法治护航民营经济发展
items.summary: 中新网重庆11月2日电 (梁钦卿)重庆市荣昌区2日召开《重庆市民营经济促进条例》(下称《条例》)专项解读暨“政企同心·共解难题”营商环境恳谈会。荣昌区人民政府区长廖传锦在会上表示，对于受客观条件限制一时难以解决的问题，要向企业讲清政策边界、说明制约原因，并拿出阶段性整改方案和时间表，确保事事有回音、件件有着落，决不能让企业诉求“石沉大海”。

items.title: 印尼制造业PMI创31个月新高 出口订单增长强劲

items.title: 年接待游客突破600万人次 九寨沟精细管护守护山水魅力

items.title: 云南三季度以工代赈带动近30万人就业 发放劳务报酬超73亿元
items.summary: 中新网昆明11月2日电 (陆希成)云南省发展和改革委员会2日消息，2026年三季度，云南实施以工代赈项目4991个，带动29.87万名民众就业，发放劳务报酬73.82亿元(人民币，下同)，较今年一季度分别增长47%、71%和429%。当季参与项目的民众人均增收2万余元，各地开展劳动技能培训28.99万人次。

items.title: 宁夏落地首笔小时级绿电交易

items.title: Prime Minister meets Welsh First Minister at National Economic Council
items.summary: Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock said Today the Prime Minister put a positive offer on the table for how the UK Government and Welsh Government can work together to empower Welsh communities and drive growth in every postcode. I
items.bodyHtml:
Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock said

Today the Prime Minister put a positive offer on the table for how the UK Government and Welsh Government can work together to empower Welsh communities and drive growth in every postcode.

I’m delighted that we can now move forward with discussions on where power, responsibilities and decision-making should sit to best serve the people of Wales.

Devolution was never intended to stop at Cardiff Bay. While we recognise it is for the Welsh Government to determine how local government works in Wales, we are offering to work in partnership to unlock Wales’s potential.
items.bodyText:
Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock said


  Today the Prime Minister put a positive offer on the table for how the UK Government and Welsh Government can work together to empower Welsh communities and drive growth in every postcode.

  I’m delighted that we can now move forward with discussions on where power, responsibilities and decision-making should sit to best serve the people of Wales.

  Devolution was never intended to stop at Cardiff Bay. While we recognise it is for the Welsh Government to determine how local government works in Wales, we are offering to work in partnership to unlock Wales’s potential.

items.title: New Belfast fabrication hall to support shipbuilding for decades
items.summary: New fabrication hall opens today at Navantia UK’s Harland & Wolff site in Belfast, the centrepiece of a £157 million investment programme across their four UK shipyards. The hall will support construction of three new Fleet Solid Suppor
items.bodyHtml:
• New fabrication hall opens today at Navantia UK’s Harland & Wolff site in Belfast, the centrepiece of a £157 million investment programme across their four UK shipyards.
  • The hall will support construction of three new Fleet Solid Support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary, and 900 skilled jobs and apprenticeships in Belfast.
  • Follows record-breaking defence investment in Northern Ireland’s industry, which rose by 63% in real terms in 2025/26 to £464 million.

Belfast welders, fabricators, and crane operators are set to benefit from a record-breaking year of defence investment in Northern Ireland, as Navantia UK opened the new Resurgent Hall at the iconic Harland & Wolff site in Belfast today.

The opening marks a major milestone in the construction of three new support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary (RFA), cementing Belfast’s role at the heart of the UK’s shipbuilding renewal.

During the site opening today, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard officially opened the fabrication hall, the new centrepiece of Navantia UK’s £157 million investment programme across its four UK shipyards. Around £100 million is being invested in Belfast alone.

Supporting over 900 skilled jobs and apprenticeships, the newly extended hall adds 5,000 square metres of fabrication space, fitted with new cranes, robotic plasma-cutting technology and a new mechanised panel line. Navantia UK’s Harland and Wolff site will now be able to deliver the Fleet Solid Support (FSS) programme.

Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard MP said:

Few sights in the UK are more evocative of our industrial heritage than the Samson and Goliath cranes, and it’s fitting that this new hall sits on the shoulders of these iconic giants.

Belfast continues with its proud shipbuilding history by building the modern shipbuilding capability the country needs today, with this new fabrication hall at the heart of it.

Navantia’s £157 million investment across its UK yards shows what sustained investment in shipbuilding delivers: good jobs, growing skills, and the support ships our Navy needs.

Minister for Northern Ireland Sarah Owen said:

Standing in Navantia’s state-of-the-art fabrication hall is a great reminder of the scale of UK Government defence investment in Northern Ireland, with £460 million spent here by the Ministry of Defence in the last year - equivalent to £240 per person.

This impressive facility is a key milestone in the UK Government’s Fleet Solid Support (FSS) programme, which has invested around £100 million in Belfast alone.

Navantia is building on Belfast’s historic shipbuilding legacy while supporting hundreds of skilled jobs and apprenticeships, ensuring that it remains at the heart of the UK’s defence industry while boosting economic growth.

Alongside investment in the new hall, Navantia UK is refurbishing Samson & Goliath – the two yellow cranes that dominate the skyline of Belfast’s docks – rounding off a programme of modernisation that will expand the yard’s capacity and increase its capability to deliver complex builds.

Navantia UK is prime contractor for the FSS programme and is leading on fabrication and final assembly of the three FSS ships, RFA Resurgent, Reliant and Resourceful, backed by £1.6 billion of Ministry of Defence (MOD) funding. The ships will replenish Royal Navy task groups at sea, directly linking today’s investment in Belfast to the operational capability of the fleet. Work is progressing on schedule and within budget, with all three ships due to enter service in the early 2030s.

Since completing its acquisition of Harland & Wolff, Appledore, Methil and Arnish sites in January 2025, Navantia has grown into one of the UK’s leading shipbuilding employers, now supporting more than 1,300 jobs and over 340 apprentices across Northern Ireland, England and Scotland, and has committed to creating 750 apprenticeships by 2030.

Navantia UK CEO, Donato Martinez, said:

Shipbuilding is returning to Belfast. We are turning Harland & Wolff into one of the most advanced shipyards in Europe. Our new fabrication hall will be equipped to build state-of-the-art ships to serve and defend the UK for generations to come.

We’ve named it Resurgent for a reason. Jobs, investment and activity are resurgent in shipbuilding. Belfast is at heart of that revival, and the fleet solid support programme is the first of many projects we aim to deliver here for the Ministry of Defence.

The opening comes as recent figures show MOD investment in Northern Ireland’s defence sector rose by 63% in real terms in 2025/26, to £464 million, the highest level since records began. That investment, equivalent to £240 for every person living in Northern Ireland, is helping give people in Northern Ireland breathing room day-to-day, while fuelling the growth and reindustrialisation of communities across the country.

Keith Bethell, NAD Group Maritime Director, said:

The opening of the Resurgent Fabrication Hall is a clear sign that growth in UK shipbuilding is happening right now, in Belfast. This investment is renewing our industrial capability, creating skilled jobs and apprenticeships, and strengthening the supply chains that underpin our national resilience. It gives us the modern capability we need to deliver the Fleet Solid Support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary and lays the foundations for Belfast to compete for future UK naval and maritime programmes.

UK naval shipbuilding is backed by the Defence Investment Plan, which commits £298 billion of UK defence investment over the next four years.

items.title: New Chair appointed of the Leasehold Advisory Service
items.summary: Professor Nick Hopkins has today (2 November 2026) been announced as the new Chair of the Leasehold Advisory Service (LEASE), where he will strengthen the organisation’s role in championing the rights of leaseholders and park home owners. L
items.bodyHtml:
Professor Nick Hopkins has today (2 November 2026) been announced as the new Chair of the Leasehold Advisory Service (LEASE), where he will strengthen the organisation’s role in championing the rights of leaseholders and park home owners.

LEASE is a government-funded body which provides free advice and information to leaseholders and park homeowners in England and Wales, including on commonhold and building safety issues.

As Chair, Professor Hopkins will provide strategic direction for LEASE as it continues to modernise its services and support leaseholders and park home owners in understanding their rights.

He brings a wealth of experience in land and property law, following a decade as the Law Commissioner for Property, Family and Trust Law in England and Wales, which included leading the Commission’s work on residential leasehold and commonhold reform, as well as his current position as Professor of Land Law at University College London.

Professor Hopkins has been a prominent advocate for reforming the leasehold and commonhold system, and through his work with the Law Commission, helped develop proposals intended to give homeowners greater control over their buildings.

Professor Hopkins takes over from Martin Boyd who has led LEASE since 2023 and provided strong leadership throughout a significant transformation and modernisation of the organisation’s services. 

Minister for Housing and Planning, Matthew Pennycook MP said:

I warmly congratulate Professor Nick Hopkins on his appointment as LEASE’s Chair, and I very much look forward to working with him through this critical period as we both provide leaseholders with relief and progress the reforms necessary to end the feudal leasehold system for good.

I am extremely grateful to Martin Boyd for the service and leadership he has provided over the past three years. As a result of his considerable energy, expertise and commitment, LEASE has improved materially to the benefit of leaseholders and homeowners alike.

Professor Nick Hopkins said:

I am delighted to have been appointed Chair of LEASE at this significant period of reform of the sector. I look forward to working with LEASE’s Board and staff to support leasehold homeowners and owners of park homes in England and Wales and promote their rights. Alongside this vital work, I welcome the opportunity to help prepare current and future homeowners for the transition to commonhold as the default tenure for flat ownership so that they can fully benefit from the advantages that it will bring.

Martin Boyd, outgoing Chair of LEASE said:

I am very pleased to hand on the baton of chairing LEASE to Professor Nick Hopkins at the end of my 3 years term. Radically transforming LEASE was my original brief. That transition is now almost complete, but it now becomes a stepping stone for Nick to take forward. At this critical time of legislative reform Nick’s knowledge will help ensure consumers get the help they need. I thank all the team at LEASE and the Department for their support over the last three years.

LEASE Chief Executive Kion Ahadi said:

I’m delighted that Professor Nick Hopkins is joining LEASE as our new Chair. His experience and expertise in leasehold and commonhold reform will be a real strength as we prepare LEASE for the changes ahead. I look forward to working with Nick to deliver more personalised advice and strengthen our digital services, making it easier for people to get the help they need.

I’d also like to thank Martin for his leadership over the past three years and his commitment to leaseholders and park home owners.

Professor Nick Hopkins is now in-post and the appointment is expected to run for three years.

The government remains committed to improving the experience of leaseholders and the Prime Minister has confirmed the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill will be introduced to Parliament before the end of this year.

items.title: National Housing Bank invests up to £70 million in Fiera Real Estate and Packaged Living
items.summary: National Housing Bank, a Homes England company, has committed up to £70 million to the Fiera Real Estate Single Family Housing (FRESH) fund, a new open-ended fund targeting a portfolio in excess of £1 billion of professionally managed famil
items.bodyHtml:
National Housing Bank, a Homes England company, has committed up to £70 million to the Fiera Real Estate Single Family Housing (FRESH) fund, a new open-ended fund targeting a portfolio in excess of £1 billion of professionally managed family rental homes. 

Backed by the Bank’s £51 million cornerstone investment and capital from private institutional partners, FRESH has now reached £200 million of investment capacity. This includes a further £19 million commitment from the Bank, which will become available as the fund scales, supporting early platform growth and attracting additional institutional investment into the residential sector. 

FRESH, established by Fiera Real Estate UK Limited and Packaged Living Limited, Fiera Real Estate’s rental living platform, will invest through forward-funding and forward-commitment agreements with developers and housebuilders. Working alongside institutional investors and delivery partners, the fund will unlock housing developments and accelerate the delivery of new homes in supply constrained locations to deliver a diversified portfolio of newly built family rental homes across the UK. 

The investment reflects the National Housing Bank’s role in supporting housing sectors with the potential to increase supply and unlock significant private investment. 

Angela Rayner, Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government said: 

The housing crisis is putting pressure on families across the country, which is why we’re determined to get better quality homes built. 

This £70 million investment will get new family homes for rent off the ground and unlock private investment to build the housing our communities desperately need.

Simon Century, Chief Executive Officer for the National Housing Bank, said: 

This investment demonstrates the role the National Housing Bank can play in attracting institutional capital into housing delivery. By partnering with Fiera and Packaged Living, we are supporting the creation of a pipeline of family rental homes at scale, helping to address undersupply in key markets and deliver lasting benefits for communities.

Charles Allen, Head of European Real Estate at Fiera Real Estate, commented: 

Securing this commitment is a strong validation of our investment thesis and joint track record with Packaged Living in delivering high-quality rental housing. The strategy provides institutional investors with targeted exposure to an established asset class that can be scaled effectively, marking another major step in our growth journey. 

Living represents one of Fiera’s three conviction sectors alongside real estate debt and logistics, all of which are driven by strong structural tailwinds, long-term supply-demand imbalances, and defensive, inflation-resilient income streams.

Ed Ellerington, CEO of Packaged Living, added: 

This is a further example of how effective collaboration between private and public capital can accelerate housing delivery across multiple tenures and at scale. Packaged Living has been a pioneering force in the institutionalisation of UK single-family rental housing, which is now a mature asset class with demonstrable benefits across sustainability and socio-economic impact. 

We will leverage our full lifecycle expertise and proven track record to deliver high-quality, sustainable homes that offer the potential for downside protection, growth prospects and measurable benefits for our investors.

The National Housing Bank’s investment demonstrates how public and private capital can work together to accelerate housing delivery. By investing in scalable platforms such as FRESH, the Bank is helping to unlock new sources of institutional investment into housing, support the delivery of high-quality homes and increase housing supply in areas where new homes are needed most. 

ENDS 

About the National Housing Bank: 

We are the National Housing Bank, a Homes England company and government-backed public finance institution providing purpose-led finance to accelerate housing delivery and regeneration across England. 

Over the next decade, we will invest up to £16 billion through debt, equity and guarantee products, stepping in where the market cannot. We aim to attract more than £50 billion of private capital to enable more homes, stronger places and thriving, sustainable communities. 

We offer partners tailored and blended finance solutions alongside the full range of Homes England support. Our delegations and flexible approach mean we can respond with agility to changing market conditions, bringing long-term investment to transform places and boost economic growth across England. 

Learn more about us:  

https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/national-housing-bank/about  

https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/homes-england/about

Email: homesenglandnews@communities.gov.uk

items.title: Five things you need to know ahead of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax quarterly deadline
items.summary: Sole traders and landlords earning more than £50,000 must send their second quarterly update for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax by Saturday 7 November 2026. HMRC busts common myths to help customers prepare for the second quarterly updat
items.bodyHtml:
• Sole traders and landlords earning more than £50,000 must send their second quarterly update for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax by Saturday 7 November 2026.
  • HMRC busts common myths to help customers prepare for the second quarterly update with confidence.

HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) is helping sole traders and landlords earning more than £50,000 prepare for their second Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax quarterly update by answering some of the most common questions raised since the first quarterly update in August.

Customers must submit their second quarterly update to HMRC by 7 November 2026.

Myth 1: “A quarterly update is the same as a tax return”

Fact: An MTD quarterly update is not a tax return. It’s a short summary of self-employment and property income and expenses, which is sent through compatible software. There’s no tax calculation involved and no payment is due when you send it.

Customers’ overall tax position is only calculated when they submit their tax return for the 2026 to 2027 tax year.

Myth 2: “I need to contact HMRC to see if they have received my quarterly update”

Fact: If a customer successfully completed their first quarterly update in August, there’s no need to recheck their status or contact HMRC for reassurance. They can check their submission history at any time by logging into their HMRC online account or through MTD software, without needing to call or use webchat.

Myth 3: “I can only use specialist accounting software”

Fact: There are a variety of HMRC-recognised software options to suit different needs and circumstances. Some customers use software designed specifically for sole traders and landlords, while others use more advanced accounting packages. Some free software options are also available. Customers can also use spreadsheets linked to bridging software. There is guidance on GOV.UK to help people choose MTD compatible software that is right for them.

Myth 4: “If I spot a mistake in my last update period, I need to resend the last update”

Fact: MTD allows customers to keep their information up-to-date throughout the year. If a customer spots a mistake with a digital record, then they should correct it as soon as possible. The correction will then be reflected in the next quarterly update they send – so there’s no need to resend quarterly updates.

Myth 5: “Because the deadline falls on a Saturday, I need to find a way to send before the weekend”

Fact: Customers can send their second quarterly update before or on 7 November. HMRC is encouraging people to send it as early as possible following the end of the update period.

Customers that need support should contact HMRC during the week when the full phone service is available. However, phone support will be available through the Self Assessment helpline on Saturday 7 November (from 9am to 3pm) for customers who need assistance with sending their quarterly update.

Craig Ogilvie, HMRC’s Director of Making Tax Digital, said:

Thousands of sole traders and landlords have already successfully sent their first quarterly update, and we want the second to be just as straightforward.

As the next deadline approaches, we’re helping customers prepare with confidence by answering common questions about MTD and highlighting the support available.

Customers can send their update any time before 7 November and I would encourage them to do so as early as possible to ensure they have everything in place before the deadline.

Quarterly updates are not tax returns, no tax is due when they’re sent, and customers can keep their information up to date throughout the year.

For more information about MTD for Income Tax, visit GOV.UK.

Further information

MTD for Income Tax became mandatory for sole traders and landlords earning more than £50,000 from 6 April 2026.

Quarterly updates must be sent through HMRC-recognised software, including bridging software for those using spreadsheets.

Agent Dedicated Line (ADL) will not be available on Saturday 7 November, however agents can contact the Self Assessment helpline on 0300 200 3310 for support. Business-as-usual webchat services will be available from 8am to 4pm.

There are certain exemptions from MTD for Income Tax, including for those who are digitally excluded. Visit GOV.UK for details.

MTD for Income Tax will extend to sole traders and landlords earning more than £30,000 from 6 April 2027, and to those earning more than £20,000 from 6 April 2028.

items.title: MHRA launches patient safety essay competition for MedSafetyWeek
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is urging everyone to help protect patients by reporting all types of safety concerns from medicines and healthcare products, including medical devices, using the Yellow Card sc
items.bodyHtml:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is urging everyone to help protect patients by reporting all types of safety concerns from medicines and healthcare products, including medical devices, using the Yellow Card scheme, as part of the eleventh annual #MedSafetyWeek (2-8 November 2026) campaign. 

This year’s global campaign message is clear: “Don’t ignore suspected side effects, report them.” More than 130 organisations from over 120 countries will share medicines-safety messages in more than 60 languages.  

You can support the campaign to raise awareness of the Yellow Card scheme by using the new campaign materials on the Yellow Card website, including posters, digital screens, waiting room materials and social media assets, to raise awareness and promote Yellow Card reporting and by following MHRA social media channels and sharing content using #MHRAYellowCard, #MedSafetyWeek, #ReportSideEffects and #patientsafety to raise awareness of reporting. 

To coincide with #MedSafetyWeek, the MHRA has also launched its 2026 national patient safety essay competition on the detection and reporting of AI-related adverse events.  This year the competition also invites pharmacy students to take place alongside UK medical students.  

Essay competition widens to pharmacy students following strong demand 

The MHRA Patient Safety Essay Competition launched last year to a strong response, with 68 entries received from more than 30 medical schools across the UK. Following queries from pharmacists keen to get involved, the MHRA has expanded the 2026 competition to include pharmacy students, reflecting the vital role pharmacy professionals play in medicine safety.  

Entrants are invited to submit an essay of up to 2,000 words on the topic: “Artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to play a transformative role in healthcare over the next 5 years. Using examples, explain how the Yellow Card scheme can enable the identification of risks associated with the adoption of AI as a medical device. Consider practical ways to improve the detection and reporting of AI-related adverse events by patients and healthcare professionals using the Yellow Card scheme. Discuss how improved reporting could support the safe use of AI-enabled medical devices.” 

Entries close on Monday 11 January 2027. Six prizes are available. First prize winners receive £500 and an invitation to present their essay at a national meeting of the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM), the independent advisory body on medicine safety, and the Interim Devices Working Group (IDWG). Second and third prizes of £300 and £200 are also available in each category. 

Professor Anthony Harnden, MHRA Chair and professor of primary care at the University of Oxford, said: 

“Last year’s essay competition showed just how engaged medical students and foundation doctors are with the challenge of making medicines safer. The theme of AI in healthcare could not be more timely. As these technologies become part of everyday clinical practice, we need the next generation of healthcare professionals thinking now about how we identify and report the risks they bring. This year we’ve widened the competition to pharmacy students too, recognising the vital role they play in medicine safety. I’d encourage every eligible student to take part, whether studying medicine or pharmacy; your insight could genuinely help shape how we monitor the safety of AI-enabled medical devices across the country.” 

A call to action – report safety concerns from all healthcare products 

Medicines, vaccines, blood products and medical devices save lives and improve health, but problems can occur. Side effects may appear suddenly or develop gradually, while device problems may involve faults, failures or unexpected results. 

You do not need to prove that a product caused the problem before submitting a Yellow Card. Reports are particularly important when a reaction is serious, affects day-to-day life, is not listed in the product or user information, or follows a change in medicine, dose or combination of treatments. 

Alison Cave, Chief Safety Officer at the MHRA, said: 

“Every Yellow Card report matters. It gives us real-world evidence about how medicines and medical devices are being used and helps us identify possible safety issues that may not have been seen before. 

If you suspect a side effect, experience a problem with a medical device, find a medicine may be defective, or think a medical product could be fake, please do not ignore it. You do not need to be certain, and your report could help us connect the dots and protect others from harm. 

“I’d particularly encourage healthcare professionals to report problems with medical devices, including AI-enabled devices, where we know reporting rates are currently low. As these technologies become more common in clinical practice, this kind of first-hand reporting is vital to help us spot and act on safety issues early. “ 

Please submit a Yellow Card for: 

  • Suspected side effects from medicines, vaccines, herbal remedies, homeopathic products or e-cigarette products 

  • Medical device incidents, including faults, failures or unexpected behaviour 

  • Suspected defective medicines or concerns about product quality 

  • Suspected fake or unlicensed medical products, particularly those obtained online or through social media 

Anyone can report, including patients, parents, carers and healthcare professionals. A report should include as much information as possible, but it is still valuable if every detail is not available. 

How to report 

Report online at yellowcard.mhra.gov.uk or through the Yellow Card app. Reporting usually takes only a few minutes. If you are worried about your health, contact a healthcare professional; the Yellow Card scheme cannot provide medical advice. 

Enter the 2026 essay competition at Patient safety essay competition. 

Stay informed and help spread the message 

Read the patient information leaflet or instructions supplied with a product, discuss known side effects with a healthcare professional, and consider whether new or changing symptoms could be linked to the healthcare product.  

Don’t ignore suspected side effects or other safety concerns – report them through the Yellow Card scheme. 

Notes to Editors 

The full terms and conditions for the essay competition are available at: Patient safety essay competition  

#MedSafetyWeek is an international campaign led by Uppsala Monitoring Centre, the World Health Organization Collaborating Centre for International Drug Monitoring. The campaign is supported by the World Health Organization, members of the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities and other national and international organisations with an interest in medicine safety. MHRA is part of the planning team for #MedSafetyWeek since its inception. 

The 2026 campaign runs from 2-8 November. More than 130 organisations from over 120 countries are expected to share campaign messages in more than 60 languages. 

The MHRA is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care. 

People should contact a healthcare professional if they are worried about their health. The MHRA cannot provide individual medical advice. 

For media enquiries, contact newscentre@mhra.gov.uk or call 020 3080 7651.

items.title: IPO campaign launched as toxins found in counterfeit beauty products
items.summary: The ‘Face the Fakes’ campaign highlights that: beauty products are an increasing target for counterfeiters in the UK, with cosmetics, skincare and perfumes now among Trading Standards’ ten most commonly investigated fakes four in ten seized
items.bodyHtml:
The ‘Face the Fakes’ campaign highlights that:

  • beauty products are an increasing target for counterfeiters in the UK, with cosmetics, skincare and perfumes now among Trading Standards’ ten most commonly investigated fakes
  • four in ten seized counterfeit cosmetics tested contained potentially harmful substances – from mercury and excessive lead to methanol and even nicotine
  • tests found 13,200 parts per million of mercury in one skincare product, high levels of lead in lipstick, eyeshadow and contour products, and nicotine in perfume. A counterfeit fragrance contained around 80% methanol
  • legitimate cosmetics sold in the UK must meet strict safety requirements. Counterfeit products are highly unlikely to have undergone the same rigorous safety checks. People therefore have no assurance about what ingredients they contain or how they have been made
  • one in five (20%) young adults aged 18 to 24 who bought beauty products in 2025 admitted knowingly buying fakes. This is more than three times the proportion recorded in 2023 (6%)
  • nearly three in four people who bought counterfeit cosmetics and toiletries purchased them online. This highlights the importance of checking sellers and knowing what to look out for when shopping for beauty products

Counterfeit beauty products are putting people’s health at risk, prompting warnings from the Intellectual Property Office, Trading Standards and beauty industry experts about the dangers of fake cosmetics. They are urging people to buy from trusted sources.

Testing of products seized in the UK found four in ten (40%) contained potentially harmful substances. These include mercury, high levels of lead, methanol and nicotine.

The Intellectual Property Office’s (IPO) new Face the Fakes campaign is highlighting the hidden risks identified through testing of seized counterfeit products. These include a skincare product containing 13,200 parts per million of mercury and high levels of lead in make-up. A counterfeit fragrance contained around 80% methanol, a toxic alcohol that can cause serious poisoning.

Beauty products are a major target for counterfeiters in the UK. Cosmetics, skincare and perfumes are among Trading Standards’ ten most commonly investigated counterfeit goods.

In July, the Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit and Greater Manchester Police seized 1,666 counterfeit hair products from a warehouse in Manchester. These included hair extensions, shampoo and conditioners.

This follows a raid in Bolton, where Trading Standards officers seized £2 million worth of counterfeit goods, including perfume, cosmetics, clothing and vapes.

The findings come as the latest IPO data counterfeit beauty buying is rising sharply among younger consumers. The latest IPO Counterfeit Goods Tracker (September 2026) found that 20% of 18 to 24-year-olds who bought beauty products in 2025 knowingly purchased counterfeits. This is more than three times the proportion recorded in 2023 (6%).

The growing role of online and social media shopping is adding to concerns. Nearly three in four (71%) people who bought counterfeit cosmetics and toiletries purchased them online, where convincing product listings, familiar branding and positive reviews can make fakes difficult to identify.

The real impact of counterfeit beauty

Giorgia Aloi is supporting the campaign after her mother suffered an allergic reaction to a counterfeit foundation purchased through a social media marketplace. What appeared to be a genuine beauty product left her mother with a painful reaction on her face. The experience brought home the potential dangers of counterfeit cosmetics.

The experience prompted Giorgia to establish SafeGlam, a platform raising awareness of the harms of counterfeit beauty products. She is now sharing her family’s experience as part of the IPO’s Face the Fakes campaign to warn others about the risks.

What’s really inside counterfeit beauty products?

Trading Standards has tested a cross-section of 50 seized counterfeit cosmetic products and identified potentially harmful substances across skincare, make-up and fragrance.

  • mercury in skincare: one counterfeit skin-lightening cream contained 1.32% mercury, equivalent to 13,200 parts per million. Mercury is prohibited in cosmetics of this type and repeated exposure through the skin can damage the kidneys and nervous system, with effects that may not be immediately visible
  • lead in make-up: high levels of lead were found in multiple counterfeit lipsticks, eyeshadows and contour products, including 40 mg/kg in one contour kit. Lead can build up in the body over time, potentially damaging the brain, nervous system and kidneys. There are particular risks for children and during pregnancy
  • nicotine in perfume: testing also detected nicotine in a counterfeit perfume, despite it being prohibited in cosmetics
  • methanol in fragrance: one counterfeit fragrance tested contained around 80% methanol, a toxic alcohol that can be absorbed through the skin or inhaled. Methanol can cause serious poisoning, including damage to the nervous system and eyesight. This can potentially result in permanent blindness
  • hydroquinone in skincare: one counterfeit skin-lightening cream contained 8.1% hydroquinone, a chemical prohibited in cosmetic skin-lightening products in the UK. It can cause skin irritation and, with repeated use, pigmentation changes including patchy skin lightening and ochronosis. Ochronosis is a potentially permanent blue-black discolouration of the skin. Unlike legitimate cosmetics, which must meet strict UK safety requirements, counterfeit products can bypass these safeguards. They can also be made in unhygienic conditions, increasing the risk of contamination. This means people cannot be sure what’s inside them or whether they’re safe to use

Helen Barnham, Head of Enforcement Engagement at the Intellectual Property Office, said:

These findings show why counterfeit beauty products can pose such serious risks to consumers. Products can look remarkably convincing but behind the packaging they can contain dangerous substances that have no place in the cosmetics people use every day, and can be made in appalling, unhygienic conditions.

Counterfeiters exploit the names and reputations of brands that consumers know and trust, while bypassing the rigorous safety standards that legitimate businesses work hard to meet. With our latest research showing a sharp rise in counterfeit beauty buying among young adults, we want to make sure people understand the potential risks and know how to protect themselves. Our Face the Fakes campaign is giving consumers practical advice to shop more safely, including checking who is actually selling a product and choosing trusted sources.

Rani Ghosh, an independent toxicologist, said:

When you hear that mercury has been found in face cream, lead in make-up or nicotine in perfume, it raises serious questions about what is going into these products and how they are being made.

Some reactions to unsafe cosmetics may be visible, such as irritation, swelling or changes to the skin. But what concerns me as a toxicologist is what you might not see. Substances such as mercury and lead can affect the body internally, and those effects may not be immediately obvious.

Counterfeit beauty products can look incredibly convincing. You cannot tell from the packaging what chemicals are inside, how the product has been made, or what risk it might pose. That is why knowing where your beauty products come from matters.

Helping consumers Face the Fakes

The IPO’s Face the Fakes campaign is working with content creators and the beauty industry to highlight the potential harms of counterfeit beauty products using visual content, expert evidence and practical consumer advice. The IPO is also working with industry organisations to help beauty businesses protect their customers and supply chains. New guidance for salons, beauty professionals and smaller businesses is being shared through trade bodies. It provides practical advice on identifying warning signs and sourcing products from trusted suppliers.

Dr Emma Meredith, Director-General of the Cosmetic, Toiletry and Perfumery Association (CTPA), said:

There is a rigorous safety framework behind every legitimate cosmetic product sold in the UK. Ingredients are carefully controlled, products have to be made in clean and hygienic conditions, and they must undergo a safety assessment. Companies have clear legal responsibilities for the products they place on the market.

A huge amount of work happens behind the scenes to make sure people can use their cosmetics with confidence. Counterfeit products can bypass those safeguards, which is why knowing who you are buying from and choosing trusted sources really matters.

Millie Kendall, CEO of the British Beauty Council, said:

The UK beauty industry puts enormous care, creativity and expertise into creating products that people love and can use with confidence. Safety and trust run right through our industry, from the brands developing products to the retailers and professionals bringing them to consumers.

Counterfeiters trade on the reputation and creativity that brilliant beauty businesses have worked hard to build, without putting in the same care or meeting the same standards.

We are proud to support Face the Fakes and stand alongside businesses across our industry to help consumers buy beauty with confidence and keep fakes out of their beauty bags.

Face the Fakes: five ways to shop safe

  1. Check who you’re buying from. Look beyond the marketplace or social platform and check the seller behind the listing. Where possible, buy from trusted retailers, official brand websites or authorised sellers.
  2. Question the deal, and don’t be rushed. A discount doesn’t mean something is fake, but an unusually low price can be a warning sign. Be wary of deals or sales tactics that pressure you to buy quickly – pause and think twice before you purchase.
  3. Look beyond the shiny stuff. Don’t rely on convincing imagery or five-star reviews alone. Check the product information, ingredients, company or contact details and other information you’d expect to see. Look beyond the listing for information about the seller.
  4. Pay attention if something feels off. When your product arrives, check the packaging for an ingredients list, batch number, company name and address and any relevant safety warnings. Missing details, blurry print, spelling mistakes or something that looks, smells or feels different from what you expect can be warning signs.
  5. Think it could be fake? Don’t use it – report it. Don’t try it and see. Keep the product, packaging, receipt and seller details, and report your concerns to Trading Standards. Find out more about Face the Fakes and how to shop safe on the Safeglam website.

Notes to editors

  • to coincide with the launch of the IPO’s Face the Fakes campaign, special-effects make-up artist EllaDoesFX has recreated examples of visible reactions reported in real-world cases involving counterfeit or unsafe cosmetics. These include irritation, swelling and blistering. The recreations illustrate reported reactions and are separate from the findings of the Trading Standards testing
  • meanwhile, toxicologist Rani Ghosh is helping consumers by explaining the potential health effects associated with substances found in testing. These include effects that consumers cannot necessarily see
  • trading Standards tested a cross-section of 50 seized counterfeit cosmetic products, including skincare, make-up and fragrance. 20 products failed on safety grounds
  • IPO Counterfeit Goods Tracker Wave 5: Research conducted on behalf of the Intellectual Property Office (IPO), with fieldwork undertaken in 2025 and findings published on 17 September 2026. The research examines UK consumers’ attitudes towards and purchasing of counterfeit goods, including cosmetics, toiletries and hygiene products. Comparisons are made with the 2023 survey

items.title: 助力母婴营养提升 菲仕兰支持《乳品与孕妇乳母营养健康专家共识》发布
items.summary: 11月1日，荷兰皇家菲仕兰支持《乳品与孕妇乳母营养健康专家共识》(以下简称《共识》)正式发布。《共识》汇聚食品科学、妇幼营养及临床营养学等多领域权威专家，通过文献检索分析与专题研讨的方式开展共识研究，系统梳理了孕产期营养对母婴健康的近远期影响、我国孕妇乳母群体的营养现状与认知误区、乳品(含强化乳制品)在孕产期营养管理中的核心价值，以及多方协同的落地路径。《共识》为我国孕妇乳母营养的改善提出方向性建议，为相关标准法规的完善提供科学依据，为乳品行业的创新与发展提供了指导意见。

items.title: Mayors and local leaders work with No10 North to drive search for 'top 10' biggest strategic investment sites across country
items.summary: Mayors and local leaders will help identify opportunities as government works to unlock up to 10 major industrial and commercial sites across the UK. The Strategic Sites Accelerator will deploy around £700 million, alongside expert support
items.bodyHtml:
• Mayors and local leaders will help identify opportunities as government works to unlock up to 10 major industrial and commercial sites across the UK.
  • The Strategic Sites Accelerator will deploy around £700 million, alongside expert support to tackle barriers including planning, grid connections and access to finance.
  • Programme aims to crowd in up to £2 billion in private investment and could support tens of thousands of jobs over time.

Tens of thousands of jobs and up to £2 billion in private investment over time will be targeted across the UK, as our regions are backed with a £700 million package of support to help drive reindustrialisation.

Starting today [Monday 2 November], the Strategic Sites Accelerator will deploy around £700 million alongside expert support to help unlock up to 10 major industrial and commercial sites across the country, helping some of the UK’s most promising investment opportunities get off the ground.

The Accelerator will focus on commercially viable sites with strong investor demand, where government backing can help overcome the barriers stopping development from moving ahead.

It will tackle the key barriers holding back high-potential sites that could support Britain’s reindustrialisation. That includes everything from access to finance, grid connections, and planning constraints, removing the blockers that can cool would-be investors.

The Accelerator will support sites in a range of ways, from loans and equity and targeted grant funding to technical expertise, bringing government, local partners and developers together to tackle specific barriers.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:

Local leaders know their communities best. Only by trusting them with real power and resources will we see change.

This £700 million package is helping break down the barriers to local growth, so people can feel the benefits of a growing economy and love where they live.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said:

Britain’s potential is everywhere, but we hear the same old arguments all too often – outdated infrastructure, insufficient access to finance, and problems with planning.

These are barriers that hold back investment, block new jobs, and shackle our potential, and we need to do more to empower our local leaders and help drive the growth their communities deserve and expect.

This programme will get the ball rolling for up to 10 of the UK’s most important potential sites, attract billions in investment, unlock tens of thousands of good-quality jobs in the years ahead, and bring good growth to every postcode.

The Accelerator is already engaging on potential sites in Glasgow, Burgess Hill and Sheffield with technical support and expertise, and will back our Mayors and local authorities with blended finance across the country.

This includes exploring investment opportunities in Greater Manchester, West Yorkshire, West Midlands, South Yorkshire, Liverpool City Region, the North East, Glasgow City Region and Cardiff Capital Region – building on the National Wealth Fund’s strategic partnerships in these regions.

The Accelerator will also be open to sites across every nation and region of the UK, from science parks and manufacturing sites to innovation districts held back by viability constraints.

Bringing together the Office for Investment and the National Wealth Fund, with CBRE as its National Delivery Partner, the Accelerator will work with investors, developers and regional partners on commercially credible sites where there is genuine market demand, using finance and technical support to tackle the specific barriers preventing investment or development from going ahead.

No10 North will work alongside the programme and local leaders to support the government’s wider drive to identify investment opportunities across the country. This includes working closely with the Accelerator to exchange pipelines of priority projects in support of the National Economic Council.

Marking a major step forward for the Government’s Industrial Strategy, the scheme aims to unlock up to 10 strategic sites across the UK’s high-growth sectors like advanced manufacturing, digital and tech, defence, and life sciences.

Jobs in tech and digital in particular can attract salaries upwards of £45,000 – well above the UK national average. That means secure, good paying jobs that will put homegrown talent at the heart of the industries driving growth and create new opportunities for business and communities for decades to come.

The Accelerator marks the latest step in government’s drive to see good growth in every postcode following the Chancellor’s Budget last week, alongside new powers and resources for mayors and local leaders to attract game-changing investment into their communities.

It will also help drive the growth of sectors which are already transforming our economy. In Life Sciences for example, £4 billion of investment has flooded into the sector since July 2025, while our technology sector is currently valued at more than £1 trillion.

Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester said:

Powered by our trailblazing Good Growth Fund, Greater Manchester’s integrated pipeline will turbocharge £10billion of investment over the next decade in sites that will support new investment across the whole city-region, create high-quality jobs and drive long-term economic growth. But too often viable developments are held back by complex infrastructure, remediation or delivery challenges.

The Strategic Sites Accelerator is a welcome step in helping to address those barriers and support places across the UK to bring forward nationally significant opportunities more quickly. We look forward to continuing to work with government and partners to identify sites that can unlock growth and benefits for communities and businesses.

Paul Bristow, Mayor of Cambridgeshire & Peterborough said:

Delivering growth in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough means tackling the viability challenges that can prevent major developments from going ahead. Viability remains one of the most pressing concerns in the market, and the Strategic Sites Accelerator, alongside the Government’s commitment to working in partnership with regional mayors and local leaders, is a welcome step towards unlocking strategic sites with significant economic potential.

By removing barriers, accelerating development and attracting investment, we can bring forward projects sooner, create jobs and ensure Cambridgeshire and Peterborough realises its full economic potential.

Claire Ward, Mayor of the East Midlands said:

Sites with strong development potential need flexible support to bring them into productive use. As Mayors, we are always looking for ways to deploy that support in a way that works for our business, places, and economies – and the Strategic Sites Accelerator meets that mark.

It will help us to bring forward strategic sites, create jobs, and support a more resilient, green industrial future. I look forward to working with the Office for Investment to unlock opportunities across the EMCCA region.

Oliver Coppard, Mayor of South Yorkshire said:

South Yorkshire is a place where we make things happen. I’m proud we’re already trailblazing a new approach, working alongside Government to unlock opportunities across the Don Valley Corridor, including at Runway Park.

We know what long-term investment and partnerships can achieve. We’ve built a world-leading advanced manufacturing cluster around the AMRC, which is celebrating its 25th birthday this year. It’s already home to companies like Boeing, Rolls-Royce and McLaren, who are all growing their presence in South Yorkshire.

Now we have an opportunity to build on our success, bringing the public and private sectors together to attract investment and create new opportunities.

Government backing through the Strategic Sites Accelerator, alongside our new strategic partnership with the National Wealth Fund, will help us unlock the potential of Runway Park.

We can grow the industries of the future and create more good jobs, giving people across South Yorkshire the chance to stay near and go far.

Richard Parker, Mayor of the West Midlands, said:

Our West Midlands Growth Plan and new Reindustrialisation Blueprint set out how we intend to create economic growth in our region. We want to take the great ideas being developed here, turn them into successful businesses and make sure the jobs that follow stay here.

We have the right ingredients. But too often major investment opportunities are held back by practical barriers, whether that’s infrastructure, access to finance or getting sites ready for development.

This Strategic Sites Accelerator is exactly the kind of partnership we need with Government to remove those barriers. We can then attract private investment and turn our ambitions into good, well-paid jobs for local people.

Helen Godwin, Mayor of the West of England, said:

Building on brownfield land can bring real challenges, but strategic investment develops enormous opportunities – worth tens of billions in the West of England. Regional funding is already enabling the regeneration of an old diesel depot in Bristol and a former gasworks in Bath.

The national Strategic Sites Accelerator and our new Future Places Fund can together transform the future of what is already the country’s fastest-growing regional economy. With the right support from government, working for the West Country, we can go even further to create more jobs, get more homes built, and drive good growth.

Tracy Brabin, Mayor of West Yorkshire said:

Our West Yorkshire Local Growth Plan is unlocking sites for new homes and commercial development across the region, backed by a £450 million capital fund made possible by devolution.

The new Strategic Sites Accelerator will help turbocharge our ambitions, and provide space for businesses to grow and create high-quality jobs for local people.

Using innovative funding approaches to unlock development, we will give businesses across our region the support they need to continue to succeed.

Iain Jenkinson, Head of UK Public-Private Capital at CBRE said:

This is the first time in a generation that a UK Government has backed an industrial strategy with the funding and support needed to unlock strategic sites, especially those with prevailing viability challenges. A fit-for-purpose real estate proposition is essential to drive productivity and support high-value business investment.

The Office for Investment deserves great credit for launching the Strategic Site Accelerator. Working alongside the Office for Investment and the National Wealth Fund, CBRE is delighted to support this initiative as the programme’s National Delivery Partner.

Background

  • The Strategic Sites Accelerator is designed to unlock strategically important commercial and industrial sites where credible market demand exists but barriers are preventing development.
  • Around £700 million will be available through equity, debt and targeted grant funding, alongside technical and advisory support. The ambition is to crowd in up to £2 billion of private investment.
  • The Government’s public ambition is to support six to 10 sites. Individual investments will be subject to the necessary commercial assessment, due diligence and approvals.
  • Employment will depend on the sites and investments ultimately brought forward. The agreed formulation is that, if sites address their viability constraints, tens of thousands of jobs could be created directly and through the wider economy over time.
  • Government is also giving mayors a greater stake in the growth they generate, with a share of business rates from 2027 and an assignment of income tax from 2028.
  • A further £285 million will support areas moving towards devolution deals or Strategic Authority status, including £120 million of capital funding to help places develop and deliver investment opportunities.

That means secure, good paying jobs that will put homegrown talent at the heart of the industries driving growth and create new opportunities for business and communities for decades to come.

The Accelerator marks the latest step in government’s drive to see good growth in every postcode following the Chancellor’s Budget last week, alongside new powers and resources for mayors and local leaders to attract game-changing investment into their communities.

It will also help drive the growth of sectors which are already transforming our economy. In Life Sciences for example, £4 billion of investment has flooded into the sector since July 2025, while our technology sector is currently valued at more than £1 trillion.

Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester said:


  Powered by our trailblazing Good Growth Fund, Greater Manchester’s integrated pipeline will turbocharge £10billion of investment over the next decade in sites that will support new investment across the whole city-region, create high-quality jobs and drive long-term economic growth. But too often viable developments are held back by complex infrastructure, remediation or delivery challenges.

  The Strategic Sites Accelerator is a welcome step in helping to address those barriers and support places across the UK to bring forward nationally significant opportunities more quickly. We look forward to continuing to work with government and partners to identify sites that can unlock growth and benefits for communities and businesses.


Paul Bristow, Mayor of Cambridgeshire & Peterborough said:


  Delivering growth in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough means tackling the viability challenges that can prevent major developments from going ahead. Viability remains one of the most pressing concerns in the market, and the Strategic Sites Accelerator, alongside the Government’s commitment to working in partnership with regional mayors and local leaders, is a welcome step towards unlocking strategic sites with significant economic potential.

  By removing barriers, accelerating development and attracting investment, we can bring forward projects sooner, create jobs and ensure Cambridgeshire and Peterborough realises its full economic potential.


Claire Ward, Mayor of the East Midlands said:


  Sites with strong development potential need flexible support to bring them into productive use. As Mayors, we are always looking for ways to deploy that support in a way that works for our business, places, and economies – and the Strategic Sites Accelerator meets that mark.

  It will help us to bring forward strategic sites, create jobs, and support a more resilient, green industrial future. I look forward to working with the Office for Investment to unlock opportunities across the EMCCA region.


Oliver Coppard, Mayor of South Yorkshire said:


  South Yorkshire is a place where we make things happen. I’m proud we’re already trailblazing a new approach, working alongside Government to unlock opportunities across the Don Valley Corridor, including at Runway Park.

  We know what long-term investment and partnerships can achieve. We’ve built a world-leading advanced manufacturing cluster around the AMRC, which is celebrating its 25th birthday this year. It’s already home to companies like Boeing, Rolls-Royce and McLaren, who are all growing their presence in South Yorkshire.

  Now we have an opportunity to build on our success, bringing the public and private sectors together to attract investment and create new opportunities.

  Government backing through the Strategic Sites Accelerator, alongside our new strategic partnership with the National Wealth Fund, will help us unlock the potential of Runway Park.

  We can grow the industries of the future and create more good jobs, giving people across South Yorkshire the chance to stay near and go far.


Richard Parker, Mayor of the West Midlands, said:


  Our West Midlands Growth Plan and new Reindustrialisation Blueprint set out how we intend to create economic growth in our region. We want to take the great ideas being developed here, turn them into successful businesses and make sure the jobs that follow stay here.

  We have the right ingredients. But too often major investment opportunities are held back by practical barriers, whether that’s infrastructure, access to finance or getting sites ready for development.

  This Strategic Sites Accelerator is exactly the kind of partnership we need with Government to remove those barriers. We can then attract private investment and turn our ambitions into good, well-paid jobs for local people.


Helen Godwin, Mayor of the West of England, said:


  Building on brownfield land can bring real challenges, but strategic investment develops enormous opportunities – worth tens of billions in the West of England. Regional funding is already enabling the regeneration of an old diesel depot in Bristol and a former gasworks in Bath.

  The national Strategic Sites Accelerator and our new Future Places Fund can together transform the future of what is already the country’s fastest-growing regional economy. With the right support from government, working for the West Country, we can go even further to create more jobs, get more homes built, and drive good growth.


Tracy Brabin, Mayor of West Yorkshire said:


  Our West Yorkshire Local Growth Plan is unlocking sites for new homes and commercial development across the region, backed by a £450 million capital fund made possible by devolution.

  The new Strategic Sites Accelerator will help turbocharge our ambitions, and provide space for businesses to grow and create high-quality jobs for local people.

  Using innovative funding approaches to unlock development, we will give businesses across our region the support they need to continue to succeed.


Iain Jenkinson, Head of UK Public-Private Capital at CBRE said:


  This is the first time in a generation that a UK Government has backed an industrial strategy with the funding and support needed to unlock strategic sites, especially those with prevailing viability challenges. A fit-for-purpose real estate proposition is essential to drive productivity and support high-value business investment.

  The Office for Investment deserves great credit for launching the Strategic Site Accelerator. Working alongside the Office for Investment and the National Wealth Fund, CBRE is delighted to support this initiative as the programme’s National Delivery Partner.


Background


  The Strategic Sites Accelerator is designed to unlock strategically important commercial and industrial sites where credible market demand exists but barriers are preventing development.
  Around £700 million will be available through equity, debt and targeted grant funding, alongside technical and advisory support. The ambition is to crowd in up to £2 billion of private investment.
  The Government’s public ambition is to support six to 10 sites. Individual investments will be subject to the necessary commercial assessment, due diligence and approvals.
  Employment will depend on the sites and investments ultimately brought forward. The agreed formulation is that, if sites address their viability constraints, tens of thousands of jobs could be created directly and through the wider economy over time.
  Government is also giving mayors a greater stake in the growth they generate, with a share of business rates from 2027 and an assignment of income tax from 2028.
  A further £285 million will support areas moving towards devolution deals or Strategic Authority status, including £120 million of capital funding to help places develop and deliver investment opportunities.
