items.title: ‘No Place for Knives’ campaign launches in London hotspots
items.summary: Criminals in two London hotspots are being warned of a step-up in police action in a new Home Office knife crime campaign launching today. The ‘No Place for Knives’ campaign will be piloted in parts of Westminster and Croydon, with adverts
items.bodyHtml:
Criminals in two London hotspots are being warned of a step-up in police action in a new Home Office knife crime campaign launching today. 

The ‘No Place for Knives’ campaign will be piloted in parts of Westminster and Croydon, with adverts appearing at tube stations, bus stops and on social media – as well as a mural at Boxpark Croydon.  

They will raise awareness of increased police activity, including, smarter metal detection, rapid response e-bikes, extra foot patrols and live facial recognition. The campaign is also being piloted in Birmingham city centre. 

Developed by the Home Office with police and local authorities, the campaign targets those most at risk of committing knife crime.  

These areas, along with 16 other boroughs in Greater London, have received over £8.1 million of funding through the Home Office’s Knife Crime Concentrations Fund to roll out targeted interventions to tackle knife crime. As well as the enforcement measures featured in the campaign adverts, it also covers prevention approaches such as youth outreach and visible local safety patrols in busy night-time economy areas. 

Recent figures show knife crime has fallen 11% since the General Election, while knife-related homicides have fallen by 25% and knife-enabled robbery is down by 18%. In London, knife crime has fallen by 14% over the same period, while knife-related homicides have fallen by 34% and knife-enabled robbery is down by 19%.   

Policing and Crime Minister Sarah Jones said: 

Everyone in Westminster and Croydon deserves to feel safe on their streets. We know that hearing of knife crime incidents happening in your city can have the opposite effect and we want to stop that. We’re working with police to target knife crime where it causes the greatest harm, using intelligence and cutting-edge technology to make our communities safer.  

‘No Place for Knives’ sends a clear message: action is being taken and we will not accept people putting young lives and our communities at risk.

The campaign forms part of the Government’s wider mission to halve knife crime in a decade, combining tougher enforcement with prevention and early intervention to protect young people and make communities safer.  

 Commander Pete Stevens of the Metropolitan Police said: 

We know the devastating impact knife crime has – not just on families who have lost loved ones but on entire communities. Our officers work tirelessly to combat this senseless violence, proactively directing our resources towards the people who pose the most risk.  

These tactics are working. In the last financial year knife-enabled crime fell by 14.9 per cent across London and over the last five years the number of people hospitalised after being attacked with a sharp weapon has fallen by 29 per cent.  

We will continue to target violent criminals who threaten our communities. Every knife removed and every suspect arrested has the potential to prevent serious harm or save a life.” 

 Mick Duthie, Director of Operations at the charity Crimestoppers, said:  

We know that knife crime can have devastating consequences for individuals, families and communities.  

If someone has information about knife carrying violence but is worried about being identified, our charity provides a way to speak up completely anonymously.  

By sharing information, communities can help prevent harm, protect young people and contribute to safer neighbourhoods.” 

Patrick Green, CEO of Hackney-based Ben Kinsella Trust said: 

Every young person deserves to feel safe without feeling the need to carry a knife. We therefore welcome the Home Office’s ‘No Place for Knives’ campaign and its contribution to the wider effort to reduce knife crime and protect young lives.

A particular strength of ‘No Place for Knives’ is that it has drawn on young people’s input during its development. Young people understand better than anyone the pressures, anxieties and misconceptions that can lead to knife carrying.

By listening to young people and reflecting their experiences in the campaign, the Home Office has created a stronger and more authentic platform for encouraging safer choices and preventing violence.

items.title: 施劲松：史前治水是长江文明鲜明特征 彰显史前先民生存智慧
items.summary: 中新网湖北荆门11月1日电 (记者 孙自法)中国社会科学院考古研究所所长施劲松研究员11月1日表示，开展中华文明探源研究，离不开长江文明的溯源研究。考古发现和研究表明，史前治水是长江文明的鲜明特征，对于水资源的利用和管理，集中彰显史前先民顺应自然、改造自然的生存智慧，也深刻影响早期聚落形态的演变、社会组织的发展乃至区域文明化的进程。

items.title: 'See it. Say it. Sorted.' marks a decade of keeping Britain's railways safe
items.summary: ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ campaign marks 10 years, having helped prompt over 1.5 million texts to British Transport Police, leading to almost 83,000 crimes recorded passengers using 61016 led to 175,000 police deployments over the past deca
items.bodyHtml:
• ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ campaign marks 10 years, having helped prompt over 1.5 million texts to British Transport Police, leading to almost 83,000 crimes recorded
  • passengers using 61016 led to 175,000 police deployments over the past decade, showing how a single text can lead to an arrest, investigation and conviction
  • government work under nationalisation puts passengers at the heart of transport, with £17 million to improve CCTV at stations, and the British Transport Police receiving a £63 million boost over 3 years - funding over 200 additional officers

Passengers have helped the British Transport Police record almost 83,000 crimes over the past decade by texting 61016, according to new figures released today, as the ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ campaign reaches its tenth anniversary.

Since its launch in 2016, the campaign has become one of the most recognised public safety messages in the country, encouraging passengers to trust their instincts and report anything that doesn’t feel right to the British Transport Police.

This has led to real action – more than 200,000 texts are now sent to the British Transport Police each year using 61016, and last year saw an almost tenfold increase since the campaign was launched in 2016. These texts alone – more than 1.5 million exchanged over the last 10 years – have led to more than 175,000 police deployments across the rail network.

Rail Minister Lord Hendy said:

We’re committed to making our railways safe, and for a decade, ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ has played a vital role in doing this, supporting the British Transport Police, transforming how people report crimes and issues across the network.

Almost 83,000 crimes have been recorded through the 61016 number – proof that reporting leads to real action, showing the difference passengers can make simply by speaking up.

Over 60% of people say they feel safer because of visible security measures when travelling and ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ is mandated across every train operator and station in England, Scotland and Wales, making it one of the most visible and widely deployed public safety campaigns in the country.

While the campaign is primarily a counter-terrorism campaign, it has evolved as a way of promoting the 61016 number, giving people another way to report a wide range of other crimes and safety issues to the British Transport Police.

This includes an incident in March 2025, where a passenger on a train to London Euston witnessed a man viewing graphic child abuse material on his phone and discreetly reported it by texting 61016.

Officers intercepted the train, arrested the man and he was sentenced to over 2 years in prison – showing the difference a single text can make to bring offenders to justice.

British Transport Police Chief Constable, Lucy D’Orsi, said:

For 10 years, ‘See it. Say it. Sorted.’ has encouraged passengers to report anything that doesn’t feel right, helping raise awareness of British Transport Police’s 61016 text service, which now receives more than 25,000 messages each month.

The free, discreet service allows passengers to report crime, suspicious behaviour and sexual harassment directly to us, enabling swift action to keep people safe and bring offenders to justice. The public are our eyes and ears on the railway and their vigilance continues to play a vital role in helping keep the network safe.

The government is committed to making sure our railways are safe, and the British Transport Police are receiving an extra £63 million in funding over 3 years for 200 more officers, including 36 officers as part of a new team dedicated specifically to reducing violence and intimidation against women and girls.

This is alongside a £17 million investment to improve CCTV at stations, and for the first time rail operators are being assessed on their commitments to tackle violence against women and girls.

items.title: Asbestos compensation injustice ended for bereaved families
items.summary: Government ends system that penalised bereaved families during their most difficult times. Around 300 families a year to benefit from full compensation rate for workers who have died from asbestos related diseases. Families to receive signi
items.bodyHtml:
• Government ends system that penalised bereaved families during their most difficult times.
  • Around 300 families a year to benefit from full compensation rate for workers who have died from asbestos related diseases.
  • Families to receive significantly more following decades of campaigning

In 2025, workers who developed asbestos-related or dust-related diseases, such as mesothelioma and pneumoconiosis, received average payments of around £17,700 through the Government’s compensation schemes where compensation had not otherwise been secured from an employer.

Before today’s change, where an eligible person died before making a claim, their loved ones received average payments of around £10,700 in 2025, around £7,000 less than the average payment made to sufferers. For a 60-year-old claimant, a dependant could now receive £56,656 instead of £24,526.

While no amount of money can make up for their loss, this additional compensation can help families with day-to-day expenses and provide support as they navigate life without their loved one.

Minister for Social Security and Disability, Sir Stephen Timms said:

Losing a loved one to an asbestos-related disease is devastating. Families should not then face a financial penalty because of that loss.

From today, bereaved families will receive the full compensation their loved ones would have been entitled to, ending a longstanding unfairness in the system.

This is a long-overdue change that will provide greater support for families at a difficult time.

After decades of campaigning from groups including the Asbestos Victims Support Group Forum UK and parliamentarians, the legislation now rights a historic wrong, ensuring bereaved families receive the same compensation entitlement as sufferers, at an estimated cost of between £2 million and £6 million per year.

UK Government Minister for Scotland Melanie Ward said:

For far too long, the families of workers who have suffered from the devastating effects of asbestos and dust-related diseases have been short-changed by outdated compensation rules.

I’m glad that from today, the UK Government is putting an end to this injustice - including for victims in Scotland - by scrapping reduced payments for dependants. Across the UK, this long-awaited reform will increase compensation payments for grieving families

I pay tribute to the campaigners who have fought for many years to make this change happen.

Jane Lassey, Director of Regulation at the Health and Safety Executive said:

Asbestos-related diseases continue to cause great suffering, and the effects of past exposure are still being felt by workers and their families. This change means bereaved families will receive the support their loved ones would have been entitled to.

HSE’s priority remains preventing future harm. We will keep working with employers, workers and partners to make sure the risks from asbestos are understood and managed, so that fewer families have to go through this loss.

The corresponding scheme in Northern Ireland, run by the Department for Communities, is expected to introduce similar changes in due course. 

This announcement comes following the laying of the legislation in September, as part of the Government’s effort to support bereaved families.

Additional Information:

  • The new law applies to new dependant claims made from 31 October 2026; this is not eligible for retrospective claims.

  • The Pneumoconiosis etc. (Workers’ Compensation) Act 1979 scheme and the 2008 Diffuse Mesothelioma Scheme provide lump-sum compensation to people who have contracted a dust-related disease through their work, or to their dependants, where they have been unable to claim damages from an employer, often because the employer no longer exists.

  •  Under the 2008 Scheme. a 60-year-old claimant would receive £56,656, while an eligible dependant currently receives £24,526 if no claim was made before death. Under the new law, the dependant would receive the full £56,656.

  • The same principle applies on the 1979 scheme. A 60-year-old diagnosed with an asbestos-related disease who makes a successful claim under the 1979 Scheme would receive a lump sum payment of £34,062 (2026/27 rate for an individual aged 60 with a disablement assessment of 31-40%). If they die before making a claim, an eligible dependant can currently receive £21,011. Under the new law, the dependant would instead receive £34,062, matching the amount that would have been paid to the individual.

  • The changes follow an independent legal review of the schemes, which recommended a range of updates to reduce legal and reputational risk, including the changes to dependant payments and the introduction of a clear “relevant date” for award calculations.

    The new law applies to new dependant claims made from 31 October 2026; this is not eligible for retrospective claims.
  
  
    The Pneumoconiosis etc. (Workers’ Compensation) Act 1979 scheme and the 2008 Diffuse Mesothelioma Scheme provide lump-sum compensation to people who have contracted a dust-related disease through their work, or to their dependants, where they have been unable to claim damages from an employer, often because the employer no longer exists.
  
  
     Under the 2008 Scheme. a 60-year-old claimant would receive £56,656, while an eligible dependant currently receives £24,526 if no claim was made before death. Under the new law, the dependant would receive the full £56,656.
  
  
    The same principle applies on the 1979 scheme. A 60-year-old diagnosed with an asbestos-related disease who makes a successful claim under the 1979 Scheme would receive a lump sum payment of £34,062 (2026/27 rate for an individual aged 60 with a disablement assessment of 31-40%). If they die before making a claim, an eligible dependant can currently receive £21,011. Under the new law, the dependant would instead receive £34,062, matching the amount that would have been paid to the individual.
  
  
    The changes follow an independent legal review of the schemes, which recommended a range of updates to reduce legal and reputational risk, including the changes to dependant payments and the introduction of a clear “relevant date” for award calculations.

items.title: Faster planning decisions as new rules and AI tackle delays
items.summary: Homeowners and small businesses to get quicker answers as new rules put expert officers in charge of straightforward applications New AI planning tool cuts time spent on key tasks by 58%, halving processing times for routine householder app
items.bodyHtml:
• Homeowners and small businesses to get quicker answers as new rules put expert officers in charge of straightforward applications  
  • New AI planning tool cuts time spent on key tasks by 58%, halving processing times for routine householder applications  
  • Over 400 planners recruited through government-backed schemes, exceeding manifesto commitment of 300  

Homeowners looking to extend or convert their loft, and small businesses improving their premises, could get faster planning decisions under new rules to cut unnecessary delays.  

From today (Saturday 31 October) straightforward applications will be decided by expert planning officers rather than waiting for a planning committee slot, helping families, shopkeepers and pub landlords get decisions sooner.  

The new National Scheme of Delegation will give greater certainty for applicants, while freeing up councillors to focus on the most significant developments.  

Families and businesses could also get quicker decisions thanks to 420 newly recruited planners through government-backed programmes, surpassing the government’s 2024 manifesto commitment to recruit 300 additional planners more than two years before the end of this Parliament.

New AI technology designed to take time-consuming admin off planners’ desks will also help homeowners get quicker decisions on their applications, like getting permission for a house extension or a conservatory. Developed with Google DeepMind, Google Cloud, Faculty and local authorities, PlanAssist brings together applications, policies and site constraints into one place for trained officers to review. Early testing cut time spent on key planning tasks by 58% - helping us halve processing times for routine householder applications from eight weeks to four.  

Following a successful trial in Camden, Barnet and Dorset Councils, the tool will now expand to 15 councils for 12 months, with the government intending to make it available to every council in England by the end of 2027.

With householder applications accounting for nearly 70% of applications each year, the changes will get more everyday applications moving, delivering a faster, more efficient planning service for residents and businesses and giving planners more time to tackle complex cases. 

 Housing Secretary Angela Rayner said:  

“Families wanting more space and businesses looking to grow shouldn’t be left waiting unnecessarily for straightforward planning decisions.  

“We’re giving councils the people, tools and reforms they need to get applications moving faster, while freeing up planners and councillors to focus on the developments that will deliver the homes and infrastructure communities need.  

“We’ve already beaten our manifesto commitment to recruit 300 planners, and we’re going further with 1,400 new recruits across the planning system by the end of this Parliament.” 

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said:

“Whether it’s building an extension or converting a loft, families shouldn’t face unnecessary delays getting the go-ahead to improve their homes.

“This is what putting AI to work for the public looks like in practice. By slashing the time spent on routine planning tasks by more than half, we’re helping families get quicker answers while freeing up skilled planners to focus on the major developments that will get Britain building.”

Owen Larter, Senior Director, Frontier AI Policy & Global Affairs at Google DeepMind said:

“PlanAssist puts AI to work by freeing planning officers to spend more time deciding on applications and less time on administrative paperwork

“Providing the tool to more councils is the natural next step, and we’ll continue supporting the government and local councils as they seek to build more homes and unlock economic growth.”

Maureen Costello, Vice President, UK, Ireland and Sub-Saharan Africa, Google Cloud said:

“We aren’t just helping local councils digitise paperwork; with Google’s frontier AI and secure cloud infrastructure, we are building a system of intelligence that tackles real operational backlogs. Building on encouraging early testing with local authorities, expanding PlanAssist across 15 councils will help speed up everyday household applications like kitchen and loft extensions, while freeing up vital capacity for planning officers to help the UK reach its national homebuilding targets.”

Paul Maltby, Director of Public Services, Faculty:

“AI has the potential to rid the state of backlogs. To do that, it must be trustworthy and built with those who use it in mind. We have worked with planning officers in Camden, Dorset and Barnet to shape the system around them. It shows it’s working in a way that they can follow, and is tailored to tackle the challenges they face.

“That’s why this system halves the time it takes to review applications, and it is how the same technology will go on to help unclog the planning system and get homes built more quickly.” 

Through the Incubator for AI, the government’s applied AI team, this project forms part of the Prime Minister’s AI Taskforce’s drive to put AI to work across government, cutting bureaucracy, improving public services and delivering real benefits for working people.

Together, these changes form part of the government’s planning reforms to speed up decisions, strengthen local planning services and support the delivery of the homes and infrastructure the country needs. 

Further information

PlanAssist brings together planning applications, local policies and site constraints in one place, helping officers identify key information more quickly and efficiently. Planning officers remain responsible for reviewing applications and making decisions. 

The tool compiles the information officers need and gives an evidence-backed initial assessment, speeding up routine householder applications which make up 70% of planning officers’ workload.

Following successful initial testing with the London Borough of Camden, London Borough of Barnet and Dorset Council, the government has now expanded testing to a further 12 councils, bringing the total number involved to 15. The 12 additional councils are: Ashford Borough Council, London Borough of Lambeth, Newcastle City Council, Nottingham City Council, Bristol City Council, Cumberland Council, North Lincolnshire Council, Rochdale Borough Council, London Borough of Redbridge, South Gloucestershire Council, Stoke-on-Trent City Council and Westminster City Council. 

Officers will use PlanAssist alongside their normal process, to test its performance at scale

PlanAssist will not be mandated software and the government is removing blockers to AI adoption by mandating the digitisation and publication of key planning documents as open data by the end of 2027, which will support all property technology tools with better quality data.  

In 2026/27, the Department is investing over £14 million in two major routes into the profession: the Pathways to Planning graduate scheme and Public Practice.  

  • Pathways to Planning, delivered by the LGA, provides a structured two-year placement and fully supported master’s-level training for graduates working in local planning authorities. Over £12 million has been allocated this financial year, including £8.5 million for salary bursaries. 

  • Public Practice, a social enterprise specialising in placing mid-career built-environment professionals into the public sector, is receiving over £2 million this year, including £1.6 million in targeted salary support for eligible councils. Alongside direct placements, Public Practice is helping authorities strengthen recruitment processes, address organisational barriers and promote more inclusive hiring practices. 

PlanAssist is the name now given to the AI prototype announced in June 2026: AI tool to slash planning decision times as government accelerates push to build 1.5 million homes - GOV.UK

items.title: More than two thirds of new Civil Service roles created in Places for Growth locations
items.summary: Over two thirds (c 67%) of all new full-time Civil Service positions in key regional locations. Places for Growth drives economic growth by transferring Civil Service roles to regional hubs across the UK. The government is undertaking a dev
items.bodyHtml:
• Over two thirds (c 67%) of all new full-time Civil Service positions in key regional locations.
  • Places for Growth drives economic growth by transferring Civil Service roles to regional hubs across the UK.
  • The government is undertaking a devolution revolution as Whitehall officials to be posted into mayors’ offices.

Local communities across the UK are benefiting from Civil Service jobs coming closer to home, with four in five civil servants based outside London.  

Upon taking office, the Prime Minister promised a clear break from centralisation, pledging to shift power away from Westminster and return decision-making to communities where people live, work, and invest. In the first month of No.10 North he announced a major package of measures to put more Whitehall capacity behind local leaders and help unlock good growth in every postcode.

The foundations for the Prime Minister’s ambitions are already being built through the Places for Growth programme, which brings the Civil Service closer to the communities it serves.  New data shows that since the programme launched to March 2025, 24,621 roles have now moved outside London. This means that the programme has exceeded its 22,000 target three years early.

Additionally, progress is being made to move half of Civil Service senior leadership into regions and nations, with 36.6% of UK-based Senior Civil Servants now based out of London as of March 2026. This is crucial for embedding senior leaders into regional communities, to build strong relationships in these places across government and industry.  

Cabinet Office Minister, Mark Ferguson said:

We are shifting power and decision making to local communities to ensure that we have a truly UK-wide Civil Service.

Policy and decision makers must reflect the country we live in, so those making decisions understand how these are felt in the communities they impact.

This is devolution by design and devolution by default, and we will unlock talent across the country to ensure the inner workings of government move with the times.

With these building blocks in place to deliver devolution, embedding leaders in the English regions and the Nations ensures relationships become established to enable partnership across central government, with regional and local authorities, as well as industry.  The programme supports good jobs and growth in every postcode, spreading opportunity across the country gives people across the country the opportunity to have rewarding careers and serve the public in the Civil Service.

Today’s news follows the Prime Minister’s announcement in August for Whitehall officials to be posted into mayors’ offices. In a package aimed to support the devolution revolution, high-performing civil servants will be seconded into mayoral authorities to build capability and capacity and accelerate the transfer of power to local areas.

In addition to this, a new Civil Service Fast Stream pilot in Yorkshire and Humber was announced, to ensure young people can build successful careers without having to leave the places they call home by relocating to London.

The creation of No.10 North is the beating heart of the principle behind these policies, as it has brought together departments behind a shared mission to devolve power and unlock growth across the country.

The transition of power outside of London will further strengthen these local ties and bring government functions closer to the communities they serve.  Bringing officials closer to the communities they serve to ensure that national policy reflects local realities, drives community investment and establishes a modern public service.

By building thriving Civil Service communities nationwide, the Government aims to unlock talent across the country and partner effectively with local leaders to deliver a modern, world-class public service.

items.title: Major undersea power cable given green light
items.summary: Sea Link approved between Suffolk and Kent - a major electricity network upgrade capable of carrying 2 GW of power, helping more homegrown, secure, clean electricity reach homes and businesses The UK government community benefits scheme wil
items.bodyHtml:
• Sea Link approved between Suffolk and Kent - a major electricity network upgrade capable of carrying 2 GW of power, helping more homegrown, secure, clean electricity reach homes and businesses
  • The UK government community benefits scheme will be delivered by National Grid with over a £1 million each for community funds in Kent and Suffolk, which could support local priorities such as improving community facilities, enhancing green spaces and developing local skills
  • Decisions back more clean power and the grid Britain needs to reduce exposure to volatile fossil fuel prices

Families and businesses could benefit from more clean, homegrown power as the government today (Friday 30 October) approves Sea Link, a major undersea power connection between Suffolk and Kent.

Developed by National Grid, the 2 GW link will be capable of carrying enough electricity to power the equivalent of 2 million homes, helping move more power from where it is generated to where it is needed. By easing pressure on the grid, it will help reduce the need to pay generators to switch off when the network cannot carry their electricity.

The project will help strengthen Britain’s energy security, making the electricity network more resilient and reducing wasted energy, helping to bring down costs for consumers.

The approval builds on the Prime Minister’s announcement of the Great British Grid, a publicly owned body within Great British Energy that will bring together public and private investment to speed up network upgrades. 

The government is also bringing forward reforms to let developers and businesses build their own grid connections where appropriate, reducing delays and costs and supporting growth.

Energy Minister Michael Shanks said: 

Britain’s future rests on rebuilding the national grid so renewable energy and businesses can connect, driving economic growth and reducing our exposure to volatile global fossil fuel markets which are driving up all our bills.

By rewiring Britain we get homegrown power to where it’s needed, we make sure the grid is resilient for the future and we bring bills down for good.

The decision comes after the approval of 2 major solar farms in Nottinghamshire and Cheshire, backing both the homegrown power Britain needs and the infrastructure to deliver it.

Great North Road Solar and Biodiversity Park, near Newark in Nottinghamshire, will have a generating capacity of 800 MW - enough to power the equivalent of around 400,000 homes a year, according to the developer.

The project will be the joint biggest solar farm in the country by generating capacity, alongside Springwell Solar Farm, which was approved earlier this year.

Almost 4,000 sheep are expected to graze beneath and between the panels, potentially rising to 9,000 during lambing - keeping the grass down while allowing farming to continue alongside electricity generation.

Frodsham Solar, north of Frodsham in Cheshire, will combine solar panels with battery storage, allowing some of the electricity generated to be stored for use when it is needed.

Notes to editors

Today’s decisions bring the number of nationally significant clean energy projects approved by the government since July 2024 to 39.

See the Sea Link decision.

Sea Link is a 2 GW electricity transmission connection between Suffolk and Kent, running primarily offshore.

Great North Road’s developer, Element Green, estimates that the project has the potential to provide enough clean, affordable energy to meet the power needs of approximately 400,000 homes.

Elements Green’s plans include planting 64,500 new trees, over 50 km of hedgerows and providing 34.8 km of new walking and riding routes.

The developer behind Frodsham says it could generate enough electricity for 40,000 homes.

Sea Link is a 2 GW electricity transmission connection between Suffolk and Kent, running primarily offshore.

Great North Road’s developer, Element Green, estimates that the project has the potential to provide enough clean, affordable energy to meet the power needs of approximately 400,000 homes.

Elements Green’s plans include planting 64,500 new trees, over 50 km of hedgerows and providing 34.8 km of new walking and riding routes.

The developer behind Frodsham says it could generate enough electricity for 40,000 homes.

items.title: Major boost for young people in West Dunbartonshire as Youth Hub opens to support them towards work
items.summary: New Youth Hub, open from Tuesday to Friday, will offer CV advice, skills training, mental health support, housing advice, and careers guidance under one roof. With almost a million young people not in education, employment or training Youth
items.bodyHtml:
• New Youth Hub, open from Tuesday to Friday, will offer CV advice, skills training, mental health support, housing advice, and careers guidance under one roof. 

  • With almost a million young people not in education, employment or training Youth Hubs will open in every local area in Great Britain to give young people access to vital support on their doorstep. 

  • Opening comes as Government invests £2.5 billion to ensure all young people have the opportunity to earn or learn.

Young people in West Dunbartonshire are set to benefit from expanded employment support through a new Youth Hub in the area, as the government continues to deliver opportunity directly into the heart of the community.

Youth Hubs are locations which bring together Jobcentre Plus, local authority services, employers and training providers under one roof to provide vital help to get young people aged 16 to 24 back on track.

The Youth Hub for West Dunbartonshire will be based in Tullochan, 9 Poplar Street, Dumbarton, G82 2RD.

Open from Tuesdays to Friday, the Hub is part of the Government’s commitment to deliver a Youth Hub in every local area of Great Britain, building a national network of support for the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said: 

This new Youth Hub marks a major step forward for young people in West Dunbartonshire, delivering real support and opportunity right here in the community.

We are determined to bring opportunity to every corner of the country because no matter where you grow up, you deserve the chance to earn, to learn and to get on in life.

As part of the expansion, every Youth Hub will meet a set of minimum standards, ensuring young people can access on-site jobcentre support alongside mental health and housing support, skills and training opportunities, careers guidance and direct connections to employers with live job and apprenticeship opportunities.

The West Dunbartonshire Youth Hub will work with local partners including Working4U, Skills Development Scotland and Scottish Action for Mental Health to deliver tailored support that reflects the needs of the local economy, helping to break down barriers to work and accelerate pathways into employment.

Youth Hubs will be expanded to over 360 areas across Great Britain over the next three years, from Manchester and Salford to Dundee and Newport.

The localised approach to employment support builds on the eight youth trailblazers across England, backed by £90 million, which are testing innovative ways to identify young people most at risk of falling out of education, employment or training and matching them up to local training or job opportunities.

Together, these steps are transforming how support is delivered, moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach and delivering practical, personalised support that gets young people into jobs and drives opportunity in every community.

Additional information

  • Youth Hubs support young people aged 16–24. 

  • The programme brings together national and local partners to deliver integrated employment support. 

  • Further Youth Hubs will continue to roll out across Great Britain as part of the Government’s Youth Guarantee.

items.title: MOD and Trail Riders Fellowship collaborate to promote safe access to Salisbury Plain Training Area
items.summary: The department has collaborated with The Trail Riders Fellowship (TRF) to promote safe access to Salisbury Plain Training Area (SPTA), one of the UK’s most important military training environments. The campaign features a series of social m
items.bodyHtml:
The department has collaborated with The Trail Riders Fellowship (TRF) to promote safe access to Salisbury Plain Training Area (SPTA), one of the UK’s most important military training environments.

The campaign features a series of social media videos highlighting the importance of military training, environmental protection and public safety.

The videos focus on the primary purpose of Salisbury Plain Training Area as a military training estate, demonstrating the scale, intensity and complexity of the activity undertaken to prepare Armed Forces personnel for operations. It also highlights the impact that interruptions from members of the public can have on military readiness and training delivery.

Through the collaboration, the TRF provides a great example of how parts of the estate can be accessed responsibly, showcasing how its members engage with the training area safely and underlining the importance of safety awareness, compliance and personal responsibility.

In addition, the videos highlight the nationally important ecology of Salisbury Plain Training Area, including protected habitats and wildlife that are negatively impacted by irresponsible access, often resulting in irreversible damage to flora and fauna.

Lt Col Jamie Powell, Senior Training Safety Officer SPTA, said:

Salisbury Plain Training Area plays a vital role in preparing our Armed Forces for operations and deployment; training that can be many months in the planning. Every time training is interrupted it creates delay, additional costs and potentially results in vital training being missed.

By working with responsible user groups such as the Trail Riders Fellowship, we’re able to demonstrate that safe and responsible public access can be achieved whilst respecting the land’s primary military use.

Graeme Collins, Chair of the Trail Riders Fellowship, said:

Our members value continued access to Salisbury Plain Training Area and recognise the importance of respecting its military purpose. We’re pleased to support this campaign and help promote safe, responsible use of the training estate.

When accessing SPTA, the public is reminded to always:

  • Follow all signs and safety information including red flags and adhere to instructions from military safety staff
  • Check firing times and local access information online before visiting
  • Stick to public rights of way, do not enter restricted areas
  • Keep dogs under control, in sight and always pick up after them
  • Not touch any military debris and report it for safe removal.

items.title: Sea Link development consent decision announced
items.summary: The Sea Link Project comprises construction of a new converter station within 5km of the proposed Friston substation to be connected via High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC) underground cables between the new converter station and the pr
items.bodyHtml:
The Sea Link Project comprises construction of a new converter station within 5km of the proposed Friston substation to be connected via High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC) underground cables between the new converter station and the proposed Friston substation.

The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate for consideration by National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) Plc on 27 March 2025 and accepted for examination on 23 April 2025.

Following an examination during which the public, statutory consultees and interested parties were given the opportunity to give evidence to the Examining Authority, recommendations were made to the Secretary of State on 30 July 2026.  

This is the 118th energy application out of 186 applications examined to date and was again completed by the Planning Inspectorate within the statutory timescale laid down in the Planning Act 2008.  

Local communities continue to be given the opportunity of being involved in the examination of projects that may affect them. Local people, the local authority and other interested parties were able to participate in this six-month examination.  

The Examining Authority listened and gave full consideration to all local views and the evidence gathered during the examination before making its recommendation to the Secretary of State. 

The decision, the recommendation made by the Examining Authority to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero and the evidence considered by the Examining Authority in reaching its recommendation are publicly available on the project pages of the National Infrastructure Planning website. 

This decision was made by Baroness Curran on behalf of the Energy Secretary’s legal authority.

Journalists wanting further information should contact the Planning Inspectorate Press Office, on 0303 444 5004 or 0303 444 5005 or email:  

Press.office@planninginspectorate.gov.uk

items.title: PM meeting with the First Minister of Wales: 30 October 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister met with the First Minister of Wales, Rhun Ap Iorwerth, in Glasgow following a meeting of the National Economic Council today (Friday 30 October). The Prime Minister welcomed the positive discussions at the NEC, where the
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister met with the First Minister of Wales, Rhun Ap Iorwerth, in Glasgow following a meeting of the National Economic Council today (Friday 30 October).

The Prime Minister welcomed the positive discussions at the NEC, where the First Minister of Wales agreed to start a process to explore how each government could contribute to regional empowerment, reindustrialisation and achieving good growth in every postcode.

This would be a policy sprint led by No10 North, involving officials from each government, to take this agenda forward.

The Prime Minister said he looked forward to Cardiff hosting the next meeting of the National Economic Council in spring 2027.
items.bodyText:
The Prime Minister met with the First Minister of Wales, Rhun Ap Iorwerth, in Glasgow following a meeting of the National Economic Council today (Friday 30 October).

The Prime Minister welcomed the positive discussions at the NEC, where the First Minister of Wales agreed to start a process to explore how each government could contribute to regional empowerment, reindustrialisation and achieving good growth in every postcode.

This would be a policy sprint led by No10 North, involving officials from each government, to take this agenda forward.

The Prime Minister said he looked forward to Cardiff hosting the next meeting of the National Economic Council in spring 2027.

items.title: PM meeting with First Minister of Scotland: 30 October 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister met with the First Minister of Scotland in Glasgow following a meeting of the National Economic Council today (Friday 30 October). The Prime Minister and First Minister agreed the meeting at the NEC had been extremely pos
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister met with the First Minister of Scotland in Glasgow following a meeting of the National Economic Council today (Friday 30 October). 

The Prime Minister and First Minister agreed the meeting at the NEC had been extremely positive. They said it had been a valuable exercise in starting the process of exploring how each government could contribute to regional empowerment, reindustrialisation and achieving good growth in every postcode.

They agreed that now there would be a policy sprint led by No10 North, involving officials from both governments, to take this agenda forward.

Outside that process, the Prime Minister said the UK Government would review and respond to a range of issues raised by the First Minister.

This would not include a second independence referendum in Scotland, which the Prime Minister has repeatedly made clear, is off the table.

items.title: Triheptanoin (Dojolvi) approved to treat adults and children with a group of rare inherited disorders
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has today, 30 October 2026, approved an oral liquid form of triheptanoin (Dojolvi) to treat adult and paediatric patients with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD
items.bodyHtml:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has today, 30 October 2026, approved an oral liquid form of triheptanoin (Dojolvi) to treat adult and paediatric patients with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD). The product has a conditional marketing authorisation because further evidence of its efficacy and safety from an ongoing paediatric study is required for a full marketing authorisation.  

LC-FAOD is a group of rare inherited disorders in adults and children of all ages.  

Patients with LC-FAOD may have difficulty producing enough energy because of their body’s inability to use long-chain fatty acids as an energy source. This puts them at risk of major clinical events resulting in frequent hospitalisations. 

Julian Beach, MHRA Executive Director, Operations, said:  

“Enabling patient access to high quality, safe and effective medical products is important to us.  

“Patients living with rare diseases often face significant barriers in accessing effective treatments and we’re assured that the appropriate regulatory standards for the approval of this medicine have been met. 

“As with all products, we will keep the safety of triheptanoin under close review.” 

Triheptanoin is a liquid that is taken daily by mouth, as part of a carefully controlled diet. It can only be obtained with a prescription, and patients should always take this medicine exactly as directed by their healthcare professional. 

The medicine works by helping to prevent energy crises in the cells that can cause muscle breakdown, damage to the heart muscle and low blood sugar. 

The most common side effects of the medicine (which may affect more than 1 in 10 people) include stomach pain, diarrhoea, and vomiting.  

Anyone who suspects they are having a side effect from this medicine are encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme.

Notes to editors   

  • The new marketing authorisation was granted on 30 October 2026 to Ultragenyx Netherlands. 

  • More information can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristics and Patient Information leaflets which will be published on the MHRA Products website within 7 days of approval.   

  • The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe.  All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.   

  • The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care.   

  • For media enquiries, please contact the newscentre@mhra.gov.uk, or call on 020 3080 7651.

items.title: Cornwall's first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair moves hundreds of young people closer to employment
items.summary: More than 250 young people secured jobs opportunities on the day, as employers connected with young people to showcase jobs, apprenticeships and training opportunities in the region. The fair was hosted at the Eden Project, and highlighted
items.bodyHtml:
• More than 250 young people secured jobs opportunities on the day, as employers connected with young people to showcase jobs, apprenticeships and training opportunities in the region. 

  • The fair was hosted at the Eden Project, and highlighted opportunities for young people in local high growth sectors including renewable energy, engineering and critical minerals. 

  • Jobs fair is part of the government’s wider youth employment support, backed by £2.5 billion investment to help young people build a strong career path.

Employers and vacancies available on the day reflected the growing investment in clean energy, critical minerals and engineering sectors in Cornwall.  

Over 500 young people attended the event, with many receiving advice on looking for job opportunities, completing applications, and preparing for interviews, giving them the confidence and skills they need to take the first step towards employment.  

Workshops were held to ensure young people are able to make the most of the opportunities available to them, with one session seeing Google help jobseekers understand how to effectively use AI to enhance their CV, prepare for interviews and plan their career goals. 

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said: 

Every young person deserves the chance to fulfil their potential, which is why we’re bringing jobs, training and support directly into communities. 

I’m delighted to see businesses and local partners opening doors for hundreds of young people, offering not just interviews, but also mentorship and career advice. 

Through the Youth Guarantee, we’re determined to give every young person the chance to earn or learn.

The Youth Guarantee is the Government’s package of support aimed at giving every young person the chance to earn or learn, and the Jobs Fairs have become a key part of this, taking place across the country from Blackpool, Glasgow, and Cardiff to Leeds. These events have resulted in over 1,000 young people already moving into jobs, work experiences or training opportunities. 

The event reinforced the Government’s commitment that all young people under 25 should be offered one of the following high-quality pathways:  

  • Employment  

  • Continued education  

  • An apprenticeship  

  • A traineeship, a work experience placement or Sector-Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP) 

Cornwall Jobs Fair is the latest example of the Government’s work to support young people into employment or training. The youth employment support package, backed by £2.5 billion investment, will support almost one million young people, and create 500,000 opportunities.  

 As part of the government’s ongoing commitment to young people, at least one Youth Guarantee jobs fair will be held in every region of Great Britain. giving young people across the country direct access to opportunities near them. 

Additional Information: 

Over 45 employers and providers from across Nottingham attended the jobs fair, including:

items.title: CMA opens investigation into Meta’s commercial terms
items.summary: The CMA will examine whether Meta is abusing a dominant position by imposing exploitative terms on publishers and advertisers The terms allow Meta to access and use content from news publishers’ websites to develop and provide its own produ
items.bodyHtml:
• The CMA will examine whether Meta is abusing a dominant position by imposing exploitative terms on publishers and advertisers
  • The terms allow Meta to access and use content from news publishers’ websites to develop and provide its own products and services

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has launched an investigation into whether Meta’s commercial terms for businesses using its platforms and services breach competition law.

The terms, which Meta planned to revise on 20 November but has since put on hold, could allow it to collect content from the websites of businesses and publishers that use its services and then use it to develop and provide its own products and services, including its AI features – without those businesses getting a choice on if or how their content is used.

The CMA is concerned that Meta requiring news publishers and other content businesses to accept these terms could amount to an unlawful imposition of unfair trading conditions for thousands of UK businesses that rely on its services to reach customers and audiences.

The CMA is using its Competition Act 1998 (CA98) powers so it can urgently investigate the concerns it has heard from stakeholders including the News Media Association and Movement for an Open Web (MOW).

The investigation will assess whether Meta holds a dominant position in a relevant market in the UK and, if so, whether its terms amount to an abuse of that position under the CA98.

Meta had originally planned to introduce changes to its commercial terms on 30 October but, following active engagement with the CMA, announced that implementation would be delayed until 20 November. Meta has since announced, on 28 October, a pause to the roll out of its commercial terms, pending a consultation with industry groups.

Sarah Cardell, Chief Executive of the CMA, said:

Digital platforms play an important role in helping UK businesses reach millions of customers around the world. But where a company holds a dominant position, it must not use that position to impose unfair terms.

We’ve heard concerns from news publishers and other businesses and are acting swiftly to investigate whether Meta’s proposed changes may breach competition law, using the most appropriate powers available to us to examine these issues in detail. We will be working to reach a swift and satisfactory resolution to this case.

As this is only the start of the CMA’s investigation, no decision has yet been made on whether Meta has broken the law. The CMA will now gather and assess evidence, including from Meta and affected third parties.

Separately, the CMA is seeking information from Meta on its new Meta One business subscription service and the concerns raised by the Federation of Small Businesses about the potential impact on small businesses of posting external links on Facebook and Instagram without paying a subscription fee. No decision has yet been taken on whether the CMA will take formal action in this area and these issues fall outside the scope of the CA98 investigation launched today.

Further information and updates will be published on the CMA’s case page.

Notes to editors:

  1. At this stage, no assumptions should be made about whether competition law has been broken. Further detail of the CMA’s procedures in competition cases is available in its guidance.
  2. The relevant legislation is the Competition Act 1998. The Chapter II prohibition prohibits conduct by one or more undertakings that amounts to an abuse of a dominant position in a market and may affect trade within the United Kingdom.
  3. The Competition Act 1998 also allows for the CMA to impose interim measures where temporary action is needed to prevent significant damage or protect the public interest.
  4. The CMA may launch an investigation under the Competition Act 1998 where it has reasonable grounds to suspect an infringement of competition law.
  5. The CMA has limited powers to take action under the digital markets competition regime (DMCR) for businesses that have not been designated with strategic market status. To date, Meta has not been designated with this status under the DMCR. The CMA continues to keep potential candidates for SMS designation under active review, with the next set of proposals due to be considered by the CMA Board in spring 2027.

For media enquiries, contact the CMA press office.

items.title: New action to tackle harassment at work
items.summary: Crackdown on sexual harassment in the workplace, with employers required to take all reasonable steps to prevent it Staff to be better protected from all forms of harassment by clients and customers Changes come as part of the Employment Ri
items.bodyHtml:
• Crackdown on sexual harassment in the workplace, with employers required to take all reasonable steps to prevent it
  • Staff to be better protected from all forms of harassment by clients and customers
  • Changes come as part of the Employment Rights Act, which will benefit over 18 million workers.

Millions of people are set to get stronger protections from sexual harassment at work from today (Friday 30 October).

With nearly a quarter of adults who experience sexual harassment reporting it takes place in the workplace, these changes will ensure employers think seriously about the risks their staff face.

Harassment can leave someone dreading their next shift, questioning whether they will be believed or feeling like they have no choice but to tolerate unacceptable behaviour to keep their job. These changes send a clear message: feeling intimidated, humiliated or unsafe should never be part of anyone’s working day.

Minister for the Future of Work, Kate Dearden said:

No one should have to put up with sexual harassment. From today, employers must start taking stronger action to protect their staff, listening when people speak up and acting before problems emerge.

I pay tribute to the campaigners whose tireless work today delivers the raise in standards to make sure everyone, whatever their job, can go to work and feel safe.

Employers must now take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of their staff before it occurs. This could include practical measures like having a clear reporting policy or training staff on handling difficult situations. 

Protections have also been strengthened for workers facing all forms of harassment from third parties. Going beyond protections for harassment between colleagues, this will now apply to clients and customers too. 

Whether that is a passenger harassing a bus driver, a waiter being intimidated by diners, or a shop worker dealing with abuse from customers, reforms will ensure that unacceptable behaviour is not treated as part of the job.

Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson said:

Too many women are being forced to live smaller lives because of the scourge of misogyny, and that includes in the workplace.

Strengthening the law to better protect women at work is an essential step as we work to shift attitudes and build a society where women can live freely not cowed by harassment and abuse.

We’re working hand-in-hand with businesses to stamp out misogyny, with our new Misogyny Prevention Fund driving further action through programmes like youth mentoring, workplace training, and nationwide campaigns.

New measures to support workplace dialogue also start from today, with trade unions gaining strengthened rights for their representatives, as well as stronger rights to access workplaces and secure recognition.

These form part of the Government ‘resetting’ industrial relations and will allow trade unions to educate people about their rights, support conversations between employers and workers, resolve issues before they escalate, and facilitate the conditions for a satisfied workforce. In fact, evidence suggests that more satisfied workers are more productive ones.

Notes to Editors

  • Cases in this area are complex and depend upon specific circumstances which may differ in different workplaces or employer. In this context, these changes give victims much stronger legal protections, with more specific guidance due to be published in due course by the Equality and Human Rights Commission.

  • Nearly a quarter of adults experiencing sexual harassment report that it occurs in the workplace. Source: Impact assessment: Require employers to take “all reasonable steps” to prevent sexual harassment of their employees, drawing on Experiences of harassment in England and Wales - Office for National Statistics

  • Evidence on the link between job satisfaction and productivity: Bosworth D and others. ‘Does good work have a positive effect on productivity? Research findings’. 2021. Does good work have a positive effect on productivity? Research findings - Carnegie UK

  • Guidance on changes to the law on prevention of sexual harassment can be found here: https://www.acas.org.uk/employment-rights-act-2025/harassment-law-changes/sexual-harassment

  • Further details about the changes to workplace rights as part of the Employment Rights Act can be found here:https://www.business.gov.uk/campaign/employment-changes/  

  • Further details on the Misogyny Fund can be found here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-launches-first-ever-misogyny-prevention-fund

items.title: MHRA approves gene-editing treatment for children aged five and over with serious inherited blood disorders
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved an extension to the use of Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel), allowing children aged five and over with severe sickle-cell disease and transfusion-dependent β-thal
items.bodyHtml:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved an extension to the use of Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel), allowing children aged five and over with severe sickle-cell disease and transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia to receive the gene editing treatment. 

The treatment was previously authorised in the UK for patients 12 and over with these serious inherited blood disorders. The latest approval extends its use to younger children who meet the eligibility criteria. 

Both severe sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia are genetic conditions caused by errors in the genes for haemoglobin, which is used by red blood cells to carry oxygen around the body.  

In people with severe sickle cell disease, this genetic error can lead to attacks of very severe pain, serious and life-threatening infections, and anaemia (whereby your body has difficulty carrying oxygen).  

In people with β-thalassaemia, it can lead to severe anaemia. Patients often need a blood transfusion every 3 to 5 weeks, and injections and medicines throughout their lives.  

Casgevy works by editing a faulty gene in a patient’s bone marrow stem cells so that the body produces functioning haemoglobin. The stem cells are collected from the patient, edited in a laboratory and then infused back into the body following conditioning treatment.  

Julian Beach, MHRA Executive Director Operations, said:    

“Severe sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia are serious, lifelong conditions that in some cases can be fatal.  

“This approval means this innovative gene-editing treatment can now be used in eligible children from the age of five, extending this treatment option to younger patients. It is based on careful assessment of the available evidence on the treatment’s safety, quality and effectiveness. 

“As with all medicines, we will continue to closely monitor the safety and effectiveness of Casgevy.”  

Side effects associated with this treatment include nausea, fatigue, fever and increased risk of infection. 

Before treatment with Casgevy, patients undergo conditioning treatment to prepare the bone marrow for the modified stem cells. Following the infusion, patients may need to remain in hospital while the treated cells establish themselves in the bone marrow and begin producing red blood cells with functioning haemoglobin. 

Notes to Editors   

  • The marketing authorisation extension was granted on 29 October 2026 to Vertex Pharmaceuticals (Europe) Ltd.   

  • Approximately 15,000 people in the UK have sickle cell disorder. 

  • More information can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristics and Patient Information leaflets which will be published on the MHRA Products website within 7 days of approval.   

  • The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe.  All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.   

  • The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care.   

  • For media enquiries, please contact the newscentre@mhra.gov.uk, or call on 020 3080 7651.

items.title: Government steps up action on breast cancer
items.summary: Ashley Dalton MP will advise on improving cancer care through the National Cancer Plan Action on earlier diagnosis, better treatment and patient support aims to improve survival and quality of life Women with breast cancer could be spared 1
items.bodyHtml:
• Ashley Dalton MP will advise on improving cancer care through the National Cancer Plan
  • Action on earlier diagnosis, better treatment and patient support aims to improve survival and quality of life

Women with breast cancer could be spared 10 hospital visits during radiotherapy through government-backed research, as well as benefit from action to diagnose cancer earlier and strengthen patient support.

More than 1,000 people have joined a government-funded trial, testing whether breast cancer radiotherapy can be safely cut from 3 weeks to just 5 days.

The FAST-Forward Boost trial is running at 39 hospitals across the UK and will test a shorter course of radiotherapy with an additional targeted dose, known as a boost, to help prevent breast cancer returning. 

The milestone comes as Ashley Dalton MP, who is living with metastatic breast cancer, is appointed as an adviser on delivery of the National Cancer Plan for England to help ensure patients’ experiences shape decisions on cancer care. Ms Dalton stepped down from her role as Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Public Health and Prevention on 2 March 2026 to manage her health and treatment side effects.

As Breast Cancer Awareness Month draws to a close, figures show more women are taking up their first breast screening invitation than at any point in the past decade, with uptake reaching 63.6%. However, around 4 in 10 women invited for the first time do not attend.

Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper is urging women who receive an invitation to take up the potentially life-saving offer.  

Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said: 

This trial shows how the UK is using our world-beating research capabilities to pursue huge improvements and transformations in cancer treatment for patients in our NHS.

This programme is aiming to radically shorten the treatment times for breast cancer - to support patients and save more lives. The UK is home to some of the best medical research and clinical expertise in the world, and this trial is the latest example of what we can achieve when we bring them together.

Better cancer care also means listening to those who know what it means to live with it.

That’s why Ashley Dalton’s appointment as adviser on the National Cancer Plan is so important. Her personal experience of cancer, alongside her previous experience at the Department of Health and Social Care, will help ensure the plan reflects the realities of people living with cancer.

Ashley Dalton MP said:

It’s a real honour to be appointed the government’s Cancer Adviser. Publishing the National Cancer Plan was a huge professional and personal achievement of mine and I have been determined to ensure that the commitments in it are driven forward.

Now I can do this in a more formal way, working directly with the responsible minister, James Frith.

My time as health minister taught me so much, and so has living with metastatic breast cancer. I want to use my experiences in the best way I can, to support the commitment in the National Cancer Plan that by 2035, 3 out of 4 people diagnosed with cancer will be cancer free or living well with cancer after 5 years.

Professor Lucy Chappell, National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) CEO and Department of Health and Social Care Chief Scientific Adviser, said:

Playing a major role in tackling some of the biggest killers, including breast cancer, is at the very heart of what we do. For 20 years, NIHR has invested in studies like the FAST-Forward Boost trial - funding high-quality research that transforms patient care in the NHS.

We know the impact breast cancer treatment can have on patients and their families, and how the side effects of radiotherapy can affect people’s quality of life, even long after treatment has ended. Studies like this are crucial, as they aim to not only identify new treatment options which can be delivered swiftly and safely - but also minimise side effects, giving patients more time away from hospitals and with the people that they love.

The trial is led by the Institute of Cancer Research, London and funded through NIHR. 

If successful, the approach could reduce travel costs and time away from work and family, while freeing up NHS capacity to treat more people. 

The government, in partnership with NIHR and NHS England, is also delivering trials of AI to support the analysis of mammograms and working with Breast Cancer Now over the next 3 years to help women recognise signs of cancer and access trusted information and support after treatment. 

The National Cancer Plan sets out action to find cancer earlier, improve treatment and ensure people living with cancer receive the best possible care and support. 

Professor Anna Kirby, Chief Investigator of the FAST-Forward Boost trial, consultant medical oncologist at The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust and professor in radiotherapy for breast cancer at the Institute of Cancer Research, London, said:

Reaching 1,000 participants is a fantastic milestone. It reflects the commitment of patients and clinical teams across the UK to answering an important question about how we can improve breast radiotherapy for patients.

It is particularly heartening to see so many women, at a challenging time in their own lives, choosing to take part in research that could help improve treatment for women with breast cancer in the future. We are incredibly grateful to every one of them.

Rachael Franklin, Deputy Chief Executive at Breast Cancer Now, said:

In England, around 30% of female breast cancers are diagnosed via screening, most at an early stage making it a vital part of early detection.

Maximising early diagnosis is essential as the earlier breast cancer is found the more likely treatment is to be successful. When diagnosed at stage 1 almost 100% of people survive for 5 years or more, compared with just 32% at stage 4.

As the first partner of the Renewed Women’s Health Strategy, we’re pleased to see the government today committing to step up action against breast cancer and we look forward to seeing the results of this new radiotherapy trial.

Background information

The FAST-Forward Boost trial aims to recruit 4,830 people by 2028. Participants will be followed up for 5 years, with results expected in 2033.

The partnership with Breast Cancer Now was announced earlier this month and supports the Renewed Women’s Health Strategy for England.

Ashley Dalton, the Labour MP for West Lancashire, is living with incurable metastatic breast cancer. She was originally diagnosed with primary breast cancer in 2013. She revealed a secondary (metastatic) breast cancer diagnosis in January 2025. She will advise on improving cancer care through the National Cancer Plan for England.

This will include:

  • highlighting where delivery is off track and further intervention may be needed
  • assessing whether the plan is delivering improvements in quality of life and patient experience for people affected by cancer

The latest breast screening statistics are available from NHS England: Breast Screening Programme, England, 2024 to 2025.

Hospitals taking part in the trial

The 39 hospitals taking part are:

  • Addenbrooke’s Hospital, Cambridge

items.title: Defence contracts to prioritise British jobs and skills
items.summary: Major changes will require overseas defence contractors to invest benefits back into the UK up to the same contract value, such as jobs, skills and industry. Government backs British business by prioritising buying British defence contracts
items.bodyHtml:
• Major changes will require overseas defence contractors to invest benefits back into the UK up to the same contract value, such as jobs, skills and industry.
  • Government backs British business by prioritising buying British defence contracts wherever possible, as part of changes outlined in the Budget.
  • Comes after the government set a target of 3% GDP spend on defence in 2030, on the path to the NATO commitment of 3.5% in 2035.

British workers, businesses and apprentices will benefit from major changes which will see more defence work carried out in the UK thanks to the launch of a world-leading Offsets policy. 

Under the new rules, overseas companies that win significant UK defence contracts will be required to invest back into Britain, through new British jobs and apprenticeships, opening UK factories, investing in domestic suppliers, transferring technology and innovation know-how.  

This means contracts worth over £50 million will be considered for offsets. The contractors will be required to deliver such benefits to the UK that could reach the same value as the contract, for example a £100m contract could see new jobs, facilities, or skills training up to the same £100m value in the UK.

The government is prioritising buying British defence contracts wherever possible. Where it must buy defence equipment from overseas, this new approach will ensure British workers and businesses still benefit.  

The move will encourage overseas defence suppliers to build enduring partnerships with UK industry, helping UK SMEs to access global supply chains and create new opportunities for growth. 

Announced today by the Chancellor and Defence Secretary on a visit to BAE Systems Scotstoun, Glasgow, the policy applies to overseas defence contracts worth £50 million or more, delivered through the government’s Back British approach set out in the Budget. 

Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey MP said:  

We are putting British jobs and British businesses at the heart of how Government spends taxpayers’ money.

When a big contract goes overseas, these changes will ensure 100% of the value creates new opportunities for workers and businesses here at home, strengthening our industrial base and supporting growth across Britain.  

The defence economy in Scotland is worth £2.5 billion and directly supports 12,200 jobs, backed by the recent £10 billion Norway export deal for Type 26 Frigates supporting 2,000 local jobs and the £453 million Typhoon radar system supporting 300 roles in Edinburgh.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP said: 

Every pound we invest in defence should be judged by what it does for Britain. That’s why we are backing British by buying British wherever we can.  

Even when that is not possible, we are acting to ensure that any investment brings jobs, skills and investment back home, strengthening our national security by boosting our domestic industry. 

Since 2016, over £35.2 billion has been spent on defence contracts and services with industry overseas, representing 11 per cent of total MOD direct expenditure with industry and commerce between 2016/17 and 2025/26. 

The new policy means future spending of this kind will also support jobs, skills and growth at home. 

Companies that win qualifying contracts will be able to meet their commitment in several ways, including: 

  • creating British jobs and apprenticeships 

  • opening or expanding factories in the UK 

  • investing in British suppliers 

  • transferring technology and know-how to UK firms 

  • using more UK-made components 

The UK joins allies who already use similar offset type polices to boost the economic benefit from defence procurement, such as Poland, Norway and the Netherlands. 

Under the policy, overseas contracts worth over £50 million will be considered for offset. A new central Offset Authority will agree, value and monitor delivery through dedicated Offset Agreements, ensuring consistency across the lifetime of each arrangement. 

Where the UK must buy defence equipment from overseas, this policy ensures Britain gets something back. The approach will be applied on a case-by-case basis by the MOD.  

Last year alone, the MOD’s defence investment supported 274,000 jobs in UK industry, up 10 per cent on the year before, with £34.1 billion going to businesses based in the UK - and 85% of MOD expenditure already goes to UK firms.

The government’s fully funded Defence Investment Plan - backed by £298 billion over the next four years - will deliver stronger front-line military capability, supporting jobs, businesses and economic growth across the UK. 

The policy delivers key commitments from the Defence Investment Plan and Defence Industrial Strategy, and forms part of the Government’s wider Back British approach through the Budget.  

It follows the Chancellor’s announcements on Wednesday confirming a new commitment for the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank to deploy up to £5 billion over the next 4 years into defence, dual use and other sectors that support our national security alongside the commencing of treaty negotiations with the Netherlands, Poland, and Finland on the Multilateral Defence Mechanism to procure at scale and stockpile vital equipment which the UK has access to. 

The Offset Policy is published today (30 October) and will apply to a select number of procurements from April 2027, with suppliers notified early and clearly where offset requirements will apply.

Under the policy, overseas contracts worth over £50 million will be considered for offset. A new central Offset Authority will agree, value and monitor delivery through dedicated Offset Agreements, ensuring consistency across the lifetime of each arrangement. 

Where the UK must buy defence equipment from overseas, this policy ensures Britain gets something back. The approach will be applied on a case-by-case basis by the MOD.  

Last year alone, the MOD’s defence investment supported 274,000 jobs in UK industry, up 10 per cent on the year before, with £34.1 billion going to businesses based in the UK - and 85% of MOD expenditure already goes to UK firms.

The government’s fully funded Defence Investment Plan - backed by £298 billion over the next four years - will deliver stronger front-line military capability, supporting jobs, businesses and economic growth across the UK. 

The policy delivers key commitments from the Defence Investment Plan and Defence Industrial Strategy, and forms part of the Government’s wider Back British approach through the Budget.  

It follows the Chancellor’s announcements on Wednesday confirming a new commitment for the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank to deploy up to £5 billion over the next 4 years into defence, dual use and other sectors that support our national security alongside the commencing of treaty negotiations with the Netherlands, Poland, and Finland on the Multilateral Defence Mechanism to procure at scale and stockpile vital equipment which the UK has access to. 

The Offset Policy is published today (30 October) and will apply to a select number of procurements from April 2027, with suppliers notified early and clearly where offset requirements will apply.
