items.title: PM’s message to Devolved Governments: “Work with me to empower every single part of the UK”
items.summary: PM offers to work together for everyone across the UK in meetings with Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland today Opportunities for young people, reindustrialisation and regional empowerment on the agenda at the first National Economic Coun
items.bodyHtml:
• PM offers to work together for everyone across the UK in meetings with Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland today
  • Opportunities for young people, reindustrialisation and regional empowerment on the agenda at the first National Economic Council for the nations in Glasgow
  • No10 North offer to work collaboratively to support growth in every postcode

Prime Minister Andy Burnham makes new offer to work with each nation to place more decision-making in the hands of regions and cities at a meeting with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales in Glasgow today.

At the first National Economic Council for the nations, the Prime Minister will say that devolution by default shouldn’t be about the transfer of powers from one Parliament to another but should go deeper within nations to empower all places and communities who know best what they need to grow and access opportunities.

The Prime Minister said he would do politics differently when he took office. He is clear that when we share common challenges and the common goal of achieving better outcomes for people across the United Kingdom, we should work together.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

“Through No10 North, we are rewiring the state. I want to make sure every city and region in the United Kingdom is part of that.

“Today I’ll be making an offer to the governments of each nation. Put politics aside and work in partnership with the UK Government to develop models of regional empowerment that ensure communities can use their own strengths to unlock their potential. 

“This is the next stage of devolution. Together, there is no limit to what we can achieve.”

Devolution works best when it is built from grass roots up, putting control into the hands of the people and the places who know their communities best. The Prime Minister wants to explore closer working with the Devolved Governments through No10 North to drive reindustrialisation, while removing existing barriers to growth.

Today’s meeting follows the Prime Minister announcing that £1 billion will be invested across the UK over the next four years in innovation clusters to help high potential regions build world-leading industries.

And it comes after the Chancellor this week gave families more breathing space and investment for businesses at the Budget, with action on the cost of living, fuel prices and local jobs – alongside continued funding for the Devolved Governments to provide public services.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is convening the first meeting of the National Economic Council (NEC) dedicated to the nations with the First Minister of Scotland John Swinney, the First Minister of Wales Rhun ap Iorwerth and representation from Northern Ireland.

items.title: Secretary of State announces appointment of a new Civil Service Commissioner for Northern Ireland
items.summary: The Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, the Right Honourable Sir Chris Bryant MP, has today announced the appointment of Dr Cathy Gormley-Heenan OBE as a Civil Service Commissioner for Northern Ireland with effect from 1 November 2026.
items.bodyHtml:
The Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, the Right Honourable Sir Chris Bryant MP, has today announced the appointment of Dr Cathy Gormley-Heenan OBE as a Civil Service Commissioner for Northern Ireland with effect from 1 November 2026.

Background

Civil Service Commissioners are appointed under the Northern Ireland Constitution Act 1973 by the King, on recommendation from the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland. Their function is to regulate appointments to the Northern Ireland Civil Service and under the terms of the Civil Service Commissioners (Northern Ireland) Order 1999, the Commissioners also have the power to consider, and determine, appeals to them by civil servants under the Northern Ireland Civil Service Code of Ethics.  

Further information on the work of the Commissioners is available at:

https://www.nicscommissioners.org/

Terms of appointment

  • This position is part-time for a period of five years ending on 31 October 2031.  
  • The position receives a daily fee of £300.
  • The position is not pensionable.

Biographies

Professor Cathy Gormley-Heenan OBE is the University Provost at Ulster University, a Trustee of the British-Irish Association, and a Board member of the NI Chamber of Commerce, and Maze Long Kesh Development Corporation (MLKDC), and a former Commissioner for the Independent Fiscal Commission for Northern Ireland, alongside various other board level roles and responsibilities.

Political Activity

All appointments are made on merit and with regards to the statutory requirements. Political activity plays no part in the selection process. However, in accordance with the original Nolan recommendations, there is a requirement for appointees’ political activity in defined categories to be made public. 

Dr Cathy Gormley-Heenan OBE declared that she has not been politically active in the last five years. 

Regulation

Appointments to the Civil Service Commissioners for Northern Ireland are not regulated by the Commissioner for Public Appointments.  

Statutory Requirements

Appointments to the Civil Service Commissioners for Northern Ireland are made under the provisions of section 36 (1) of the Northern Ireland Constitution Act 1973.

items.title: Appointment of Regius Professorship of Greek in the University of Oxford: 29 October 2026
items.summary: The King has approved that Professor Laura Swift, Professor of Greek at the University of Oxford and Fellow and Tutor in Classics at Magdalen College, be appointed to the Regius Professorship of Greek at the University of Oxford in successi
items.bodyHtml:
The King has approved that Professor Laura Swift, Professor of Greek at the University of Oxford and Fellow and Tutor in Classics at Magdalen College, be appointed to the Regius Professorship of Greek at the University of Oxford in succession to Professor Gregory Hutchinson. The Regius Professorship of Greek was established by Henry VIII in 1541.

Professor Laura Swift

Professor Swift took her BA in Literae Humaniores at Magdalen College, Oxford in 2002, followed by an MSt and DPhil at Oxford, completing her doctorate in 2007. She subsequently held academic and research positions at Oxford and University College London before taking up a Lectureship at the Open University in 2012. She returned to Oxford in 2022 as Tutorial Fellow in Classics at Magdalen College and Associate Professor of Greek in the Faculty of Classics, and was awarded the title of Professor in 2024. The Regius Professorship is held in association with an Ordinary Studentship (professorial fellowship) at Christ Church.

Professor Swift is a literary critic of ancient Greece, specialising in Greek tragedy and lyric poetry. Her doctoral thesis received the Hellenic Foundation Thesis Prize and her subsequent research has received international recognition including an Alexander von Humboldt postdoctoral fellowship and a Philip Leverhulme Prize. She is known particularly for her work on the relationship between Greek tragedy and other forms of choral poetry, including her book The Hidden Chorus, and for her work on fragmentary texts from antiquity. She wrote the first complete commentary on the seventh-century BC poet Archilochus.

Professor Swift also works with contemporary theatre-makers and other creative practitioners, exploring how fragmentary ancient texts can inspire new creative work. She is an active advocate for making Classics accessible to wider audiences and has contributed to the development of the Classical Civilisation A level curriculum, as well as working across radio, podcasts, theatre and literary festivals.

items.title: 中国科学家揭示日冕纳耀斑磁重联加热机制
items.summary: 中新网北京10月29日电 (记者 陈溯)太阳的最外层大气——日冕，长久以来藏着一道困扰科学界的难题：日冕的温度远高于太阳表面，它究竟是如何被加热到百万摄氏度的？近日，中国原子能科学研究院联合北京师范大学等高校及科研院所，首次完整演示了纳耀斑通过磁重联加热日冕的物理过程，为“日冕加热”这一长期未解的重大科学问题提供了首个实验室定量基准，对理解恒星大气中的能量释放机制及其对行星空间环境的影响具有重要的科学意义。

items.title: Local Government Reorganisation moves forward in five counties
items.summary: Five areas have moved closer to streamlined local government in their area as the government announced the next steps in its review of Local Government Reorganisation. Following the announcement of a review last month, Ministers have confir
items.bodyHtml:
Five areas have moved closer to streamlined local government in their area as the government announced the next steps in its review of Local Government Reorganisation.  

Following the announcement of a review last month, Ministers have confirmed that the programme is continuing and remains aligned with the wider plans to shift power out of Westminster and back to local communities, including those announced at this week’s Budget.

The government is now minded-to go ahead with reorganisation in five areas. There will be a period of three weeks minimum for further representations before final decisions are taken.

The five areas where the government is minded to proceed are:

  • In East Sussex and Brighton and Hove, the two unitary proposal including boundary changes requested by Brighton and Hove City Council, except for the parish of Falmer.  
  • The one unitary proposal in Gloucestershire;  
  • The three unitary proposal in Oxfordshire, including boundary changes.  
  • The two unitary proposal in Warwickshire; 
  • The two unitary proposal in Worcestershire;

The Government remains committed to the reorganisation programme. Ministers will consider the best way forward for all remaining areas in the programme – 15 in total, including the nine areas which had reorganisation paused in September and which now have their decisions withdrawn.

Withdrawing these decisions does not mean reorganisation has been cancelled in these areas. All options and proposals remain under consideration in these areas and every area will have an outcome by early next year.

Local elections in these areas will go ahead in May 2027 on existing council boundaries, providing certainty for local leaders and communities.  New councils will be established for 2029, with elections to shadow councils in May 2028.

All areas with previous decisions will receive £450,000 per the number of previously announced new unitary authorities from the £63 million capacity fund, to cover costs incurred in implementing reorganisation. Cambridgeshire and Peterborough and West Sussex will each receive £500,000 as decisions have yet to be made there.  This funding will be paid in the coming weeks. The remaining balance will be paid after final decisions. 

Minister for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth Jim McMahon OBE told Parliament today:

Yesterday’s budget showed that we are committed to giving local leaders, local councils and local communities the tools to shape their own future. 

No areas want to see a return to two-tiers once strong unitary councils are in place… The decisions that we take now will be the building blocks for how this country is governed for generations to come.

Reorganisation in Surrey will remain unaffected with two new unitary authorities – East and West Surrey – going live in April 2027.   

The government has heard concerns from places about retaining their city status and has committed to making it a priority to protect them and will consider all available options – including bringing in new legislation if necessary. 

For more information:

Areas where government is minded to proceed:

  • East Sussex and Brighton and Hove: Two unitary proposal submitted by East Sussex County Council, Eastbourne Borough Council, Hastings Borough Council, Lewes District Council and Rother District Council - with the boundary change requested by Brighton and Hove City Council, with the exception of Falmer parish.
  • Gloucestershire: One unitary proposal submitted by Cotswold District Council, Gloucestershire County Council, Stroud District Council, and Tewkesbury Borough Council.
  • Oxfordshire: Three unitary proposal submitted by Oxford City Council, including the adjoining area of West Berkshire Council - with the boundary change Oxford City Council requested alongside the proposal.
  • Warwickshire: Two unitary proposal submitted by North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton & Bedworth Borough Council, Stratford-on-Avon District Council and Warwick District Council.
  • Worcestershire: Two unitary proposal submitted by Bromsgrove District Council, Malvern Hills District Council, Redditch Borough Council, Worcester City Council and Wychavon District Council.

15 areas remaining under review:

Nine areas where decisions are now withdrawn and will be reconsidered:

  • Derbyshire and Derby 
  • Devon, Plymouth and Torbay  
  • Hertfordshire 
  • Kent and Medway 
  • Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool 
  • Leicestershire, Leicester, and Rutland 
  • Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire
  • Nottinghamshire and Nottingham 
  • Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent 

Four areas where decisions were withdrawn in September:

  • Essex, Southend on Sea and Thurrock 
  • Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton 
  • Norfolk 
  • Suffolk

Two areas which are awaiting decisions:

  • Cambridgeshire and Peterborough 
  • West Sussex

items.title: Britain’s ambitious scale-ups backed to keep growing in the UK
items.summary: Scale UK Connect pilot will give 200 high-growth UK firms expert advice, connections and international opportunities to help them grow. Businesses can apply now to access support from a network of partners covering the UK, from London, Grea
items.bodyHtml:
• Scale UK Connect pilot will give 200 high-growth UK firms expert advice, connections and international opportunities to help them grow. 
  • Businesses can apply now to access support from a network of partners covering the UK, from London, Greater Manchester and the West Midlands, to the South West, Yorkshire, Scotland and beyond. 
  • Home-grown companies will get the support they need to attract international investment and reach new customers – creating good jobs and growth in communities across the UK.

Ambitious scale-ups across Britain will get the expert support they need to scale up and stay in the UK, meaning more talented innovators can build their businesses at home and benefit people all over the country.  

The UK is one of the best places in the world to start a company - UK tech start ups raised $17bn in the first half of 2026 – which is more than France, Germany and Sweden combined. But too many promising businesses stall as they try to grow, in part because they lack the advice, capital or connections to reach the next level.  

A new pilot scheme, Scale UK Connect, will tackle this head-on with 200 scale-ups across the UK getting expert account management and tailored advice on how to expand. It will also include new ways to network with fellow founders, investors and major funds, opening up new trade opportunities at home and abroad.  

The pilot, which will offer a 12-month programme of sustained support, aims to develop a pipeline of high growth companies to follow in the footsteps of UK success stories like Quantexa and Synthesia, bringing benefits to Brits and boosting economic growth. 

UK Science Minister Chris McDonald said: 

Britain is brimming with entrepreneurial talent that can benefit us all. But those who put their neck on the line to start the businesses behind jobs and growth need to know we’ve got their backs to take their ambitions further. 

Scale UK Connect will do exactly that. We’re giving 200 companies, from all over the country, the expert advice, investor connections and global opportunities they need to grow here, stay here, and create good jobs and growth in every postcode.”  

This announcement is one piece in a major package of support for entrepreneurs announced in Chancellor John Healey’s Budget yesterday, including cementing the UK’s world leading tax offer for founders and their companies, and a step change in how procurement will support UK industry and innovation. 

Building on work over the past 12-months, the package addresses practical barriers founders and high-growth firms continue to face: finding customers, accessing capital, attracting exceptional talent and navigating government. Together, these measures take the Chancellor closer to his ambition to make the UK the best place in the world for business to start, scale and stay. 

The Scale UK Connect pilot will be led by growth agency London & Partners, in partnership with organisations in Manchester, the West Midlands, Yorkshire, the South West and Scotland.  

This means businesses from all over the UK will benefit, with an emphasis on building connections between scale-ups, investors and corporates at home and around the world. 

The Scale UK Connect pilot builds on an approach with a proven track record: 

Intelligent Lab on Fiber (iLoF) is a digital health company using an AI platform to understand a patient’s individual biology so they can get a quicker diagnosis or avoid unnecessary treatment for diseases like lung cancer and Alzheimer’s. 

iLoF joined a London & Partners’ trade mission to Japan through the Grow London Global programme, and attended major health tech fair BioJapan. This gave the team practical insight into the business culture of a key market, with iLoF going on to secure a partnership with Japanese investor Hamamatsu. 

It’s a key part of the Government’s wider Scale UK mission announced at the Budget; championing high-growth businesses, listening to their concerns, and taking action to support them. 

Janet Coyle CBE, Managing Director at London & Partners, said:  

Scale UK Connect will help ambitious businesses find new customers, attract investors, and break into markets around the world. We’ll connect UK entrepreneurs with the right people and opportunities, helping them win overseas business in months rather than years.” 

Neil Rami, Chief Executive of the West Midlands Growth Company, said:  

Supporting high-growth businesses to scale up is critical to delivering the ambitions of our West Midlands Growth Plan. These firms drive innovation, boost productivity, and create skilled jobs, helping to strengthen our regional and national economies. Through the support available from the West Midlands Growth Company and Growth Hub, businesses will be able to accelerate their growth, reach the next stage of their journey, and contribute to the long-term prosperity of our region.

Ambitious businesses are already signalling their enthusiasm. They include Glasgow’s Raven Controls, whose software helps major venues and events respond more quickly to safety incidents; Newcastle-based GeoPura, which replaces polluting generators with portable hydrogen power; and Birmingham’s CyberQ Group, which provides round-the-clock protection against cyber threats. 

Applications are open to companies until January 2027. The cohort will formally launch in February 2027, followed by 12 months of tailored support. High-growth businesses can find out more and apply at Scale Up Connect. 

Notes to editors 

  • Scale UK Connect is an 18-month national pilot worth £3.4 million, run by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade with London & Partners and regional delivery partners aligned with Mayoral Strategic Authorities including the Manchester Growth Company and the West Midlands Growth Company.  
  • Additionally, TechSPARK in the South West, Tech SY in Yorkshire and Pathways Forward in Scotland form an integral part of this partnership to ensure broad coverage across the UK. 
  • Recruitment for the pilot runs from now until January 2027. The cohort launches in February 2027, firms get 12 months of support, and a final report is due in April 2028. 
  • In 2025-26, London & Partners’ ‘Grow London Global’ programme supported 265 scale up businesses to export internationally, generating £595 million in GVA and with more than 6,600 jobs expected. The programme, which expanded beyond the capital in January 2024, has supported 41 businesses outside London to date, while 85% of its 2025-26 graduates reported an increase in turnover between starting and completing the programme. 
  • Further information on new support for founders and innovative businesses is set out in the Entrepreneurship in the UK prospectus on GOV.UK.

items.title: Under-18 sales ban extended to nicotine products and all vapes
items.summary: Ban on sale of nicotine-free vapes and addictive products such as nicotine pouches to children comes into effect from today Government ends promotional giveaways, substantial discounts and vending-machine sales of vaping and nicotine produc
items.bodyHtml:
• Ban on sale of nicotine-free vapes and addictive products such as nicotine pouches to children comes into effect from today
  • Government ends promotional giveaways, substantial discounts and vending-machine sales of vaping and nicotine products
  • New enforcement powers to crack down on rogue traders, including £200 fixed penalty notices

Children will be better protected from respiratory illnesses and nicotine addiction from today (29 October 2026), as new restrictions on the sale and promotion of vapes and nicotine products come into force across the UK.

More than a million children are estimated to have tried vaping, with more than 370,000 vaping regularly, putting them at a higher risk of developing respiratory illnesses.

Selling nicotine-containing vapes to under 18s was already illegal. But from today, products that were not previously covered by existing age-of-sales rules, such as nicotine-free vapes and nicotine pouches, strips and pearls, will become illegal. 

For the first time, adults aged 18 or over will also commit an offence if they buy, or attempt to buy, a vaping or nicotine product on behalf of someone under 18.

The measures also prohibit promotional giveaways and substantial promotional discounts in shops and online, alongside vending machines that either sell or dispense vapes or nicotine products. Local authority stop smoking services can continue providing products to help adult smokers to quit.

Trading Standards will lead retail enforcement in England, supported by new fixed penalty powers which will enable swifter action against rogue retailers. Enforcement agencies are receiving up to £30 million a year until 2028 to 2029. This includes up to £10 million a year for Trading Standards and the recruitment of 120 specialist apprentices to strengthen the workforce tackling illicit and underage tobacco and vape sales.

Dame Diana Johnson, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety, said:

Our landmark Tobacco and Vapes Act was the greatest piece of public health legislation in a generation.

Six months to the day since the act became law, we’re extending protections for young people and stopping businesses from cashing in on our children’s health.

Chief Medical Officer, Professor Chris Whitty, said:

Addicting children to nicotine or encouraging them to vape could lead to the risk of serious health harms - it is completely unacceptable.

These measures will help protect children from marketing of nicotine products and attempts to encourage them to vape.

The public health advice remains clear: vaping is less harmful than smoking and can help adult smokers quit, but it is not risk-free. Children and adult non-smokers should never vape. 

Today’s measures form part of the phased implementation of the Tobacco and Vapes Act, which became law on 29 April 2026. They support the government’s ambition for a smoke-free UK and the shift from sickness to prevention set out in the 10 Year Health Plan for England.

Scotland Public Health Minister, Maree Todd, said:

We want to protect future generations from nicotine addiction and we know that nicotine products, particularly pouches, are starting to gain popularity among young people.

By banning the sale of these products to under 18s, the Scottish Government is taking a crucial step in protecting people’s health. This in turn is helping people across Scotland to live longer, healthier lives.

Welsh Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health, Nerys Evans, said:

We all want to see our children grow up happy and healthy, free from the risk of nicotine addiction. Vapes and nicotine products have been marketed towards young people, drawing far too many in. The new restrictions mean that all vaping and nicotine products cannot be sold to under 18s and the tactics used to tempt them will no longer be allowed.

These changes are giving our young people and children a better chance to grow up healthier, now and for years to come.

Northern Ireland’s Health Minister, Robbie Butler, said:

The Tobacco and Vapes Act is a landmark public health milestone, creating a smoke-free generation for our children and young people.

The rise in the use of vapes and nicotine products among young people is very concerning and the changes today will protect future generations from the serious harm caused by nicotine addiction.

Dr Ian Walker, Cancer Research UK’s Executive Director of Policy and Information, said: 

These new measures are a welcome step to strengthening regulation and restricting the promotion of nicotine products to young people. Although evidence so far shows that legal vapes are far less harmful than tobacco and can help people stop smoking, we don’t know their long-term health effects, so they shouldn’t be used by young people and adults who have never smoked. 

Governments in every UK nation must ensure that the world-leading Tobacco and Vapes Act is fully implemented and properly enforced alongside increasing support for people trying to quit smoking. With landmark measures to raise the age of sale for tobacco products starting in January, we’re firmly on the path to ending cancers caused by smoking in the UK and protecting young people from the devastating harms of tobacco.

Hazel Cheeseman, Chief Executive of Action on Smoking and Health, said: 

Nicotine products have been promoted indiscriminately in recent years through giveaways at festivals, shopping centres and railway stations. With no age of sale for nicotine pouches or limits on free handouts, children have been exposed to potentially harmful marketing. Today’s regulation brings the law up to date and will protect children. 

However, striking a balance is important with regulations, these nicotine products are less harmful than smoking and may have a role in helping people to quit. It is welcome to see carve outs for stop smoking services to continue to provide free nicotine alternatives for those who need them.

John Herriman, Chief Executive, Chartered Trading Standards Institute (CTSI), said: 

Trading Standards officers see first hand how easily children have been able to get hold of vapes and nicotine products, and the harm this causes. That is why CTSI strongly supports these measures, which close loopholes the profession has long urged the government to address and marks a significant step forward in protecting young people from nicotine addiction. 

The introduction of fixed penalty notices is particularly welcome, giving Trading Standards a swifter, more practical way to tackle retailers who fail to comply. Our members stand ready to enforce the new rules and to help businesses get it right.

Andrew McCracken, Director of External Affairs at Asthma + Lung UK, said: 

Today’s restrictions tighten the net on vape manufacturers who for too long have profited from harming kids’ lungs.  

Children are especially vulnerable to the dangerous effects of vaping as their lungs are still developing. Yet, vape manufacturers have spent years designing products that look and taste like sweets, and too many young people are growing up addicted to nicotine.

These restrictions are an important step towards protecting the lung health of the next generation, but they are not the final step. Next we need to look at further restricting vape product packaging, flavours and displays.

Peter Roderick, Addictions Spokesperson at the Association of Directors of Public Health and Director of Public Health for City of York Council, said:  

Today’s announcement brings another health-promoting measure in the Tobacco and Vapes Act into effect, helping to protect our children and young people from ever becoming addicted to nicotine.

Coupled with stronger restrictions on promotion, including stopping free product giveaways and large discounts in shops and online, these changes will help reduce the appeal, accessibility and affordability of these highly addictive products, and help create a future where everyone has a chance to live a healthier life for longer, free from the harms of smoking, while still ensuring vapes are available to support adults who need them to quit smoking.

Mr Tim Lane, President of the Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCS England), said:

Today’s new restrictions are an important step towards protecting children from nicotine addiction and the potential harms of vaping. 

As surgeons, we see every day the devastating effects of smoking, including increased risks of surgical complications, delayed recovery and death.

Preventing young people from becoming dependent on nicotine, while continuing to help adults stop smoking, will reduce avoidable harm and strengthen the nation’s long-term health.

Professor Sanjay Agrawal, Special Adviser on Tobacco at the Royal College of Physicians, said:  

The Tobacco and Vapes Act is landmark legislation that will protect future generations from the harms of smoking and help stop children and non-smokers being drawn into vaping. Today’s measures close loopholes and clamp down on the industry tactics that encourage young people to try these products and keep using them. 

Vaping can play an important role in helping adults quit smoking, which is far more harmful, but children and people who have never smoked should not start vaping. We strongly welcome these measures and the wider action to create the first smoke-free generation.

Professor Tracy Daszkiewicz, President of the UK Faculty of Public Health, said: 

The Faculty of Public Health strongly welcomes these measures to protect children and young people from nicotine addiction. Nicotine dependence is a significant public health concern, and no child should be exposed to products that risk lifelong addiction and harm to their health. Extending age-of-sale restrictions to all vaping and nicotine products, alongside tighter controls on promotions and stronger enforcement, delivers greater protection and puts the health of young people first.

This is a vital step towards creating a nicotine-free generation and reducing future health inequalities.

Alexa Knight, Director of Policy and Influencing at the Mental Health Foundation, said:  

Research across many countries consistently finds that young people who vape are more likely to experience depression, anxiety and suicidal thoughts. In one large US survey, over 40% of young people who vape reported moderate-to-severe symptoms of depression or anxiety - twice the rate among those who don’t currently vape.

Many young people who are struggling turn to vaping to cope, and emerging evidence suggests nicotine dependence may make things worse. Restricting children’s access to vaping products is not just a tobacco control measure - it is a mental health intervention.

Further measures will follow, including: 

  • from 1 January 2027, it will be illegal to sell tobacco products, herbal smoking products or cigarette papers to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009. Anyone born after this date will never be legally sold tobacco
  • the comprehensive advertising and sponsorship ban, which we intend to be in force from 1 June 2027
  • proposals to restrict product packaging, flavours, displays and on widening smoke-free and introducing vape-free places. Consultations have already taken place and the responses are being considered with further information in due course

Today’s measures close loopholes and clamp down on the industry tactics that encourage young people to try these products and keep using them. 

  Vaping can play an important role in helping adults quit smoking, which is far more harmful, but children and people who have never smoked should not start vaping. We strongly welcome these measures and the wider action to create the first smoke-free generation.


Professor Tracy Daszkiewicz, President of the UK Faculty of Public Health, said: 


  The Faculty of Public Health strongly welcomes these measures to protect children and young people from nicotine addiction. Nicotine dependence is a significant public health concern, and no child should be exposed to products that risk lifelong addiction and harm to their health. Extending age-of-sale restrictions to all vaping and nicotine products, alongside tighter controls on promotions and stronger enforcement, delivers greater protection and puts the health of young people first.

  This is a vital step towards creating a nicotine-free generation and reducing future health inequalities.


Alexa Knight, Director of Policy and Influencing at the Mental Health Foundation, said:  


  Research across many countries consistently finds that young people who vape are more likely to experience depression, anxiety and suicidal thoughts. In one large US survey, over 40% of young people who vape reported moderate-to-severe symptoms of depression or anxiety - twice the rate among those who don’t currently vape.

  Many young people who are struggling turn to vaping to cope, and emerging evidence suggests nicotine dependence may make things worse. Restricting children’s access to vaping products is not just a tobacco control measure - it is a mental health intervention.


Further measures will follow, including: 


  from 1 January 2027, it will be illegal to sell tobacco products, herbal smoking products or cigarette papers to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009. Anyone born after this date will never be legally sold tobacco
  the comprehensive advertising and sponsorship ban, which we intend to be in force from 1 June 2027
  proposals to restrict product packaging, flavours, displays and on widening smoke-free and introducing vape-free places. Consultations have already taken place and the responses are being considered with further information in due course

items.title: Environment Secretary commits to take further action against water bosses over pollution
items.summary: The Environment Secretary is set to take further action against failing water companies, with tougher consequences for executives at persistently underperforming firms, and demanding action on the worst pollution incidents. Intending to shi
items.bodyHtml:
The Environment Secretary is set to take further action against failing water companies, with tougher consequences for executives at persistently underperforming firms, and demanding action on the worst pollution incidents. 

Intending to shine a harsh light on these serious incidents, Ministers will visit a number of sites to interrogate companies’ responses. Dame Angela Eagle will also be looking at options to strengthen the ban on executives’ bonuses.

It follows the first ever joint report from the Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales, the Drinking Water Inspectorate and Ofwat, which leaves nowhere for underperforming companies to hide.

The watchdogs have pooled their data for the first time, closing loopholes that let failing firms point to a good score from one regulator while falling short with another. It marks another significant step towards a more integrated, joined-up approach to water regulation, ahead of the creation of a single new water regulator for England and Wales.

The joint report is published alongside the Environment Agency’s Environmental Performance Assessment Report, which starkly demonstrates that pollution incidents remain far too high, with only one company achieving the top four-star rating.

There were six Category 1 incidents during 2025, each representing an unacceptable failure by water companies to protect people and the environment. These sites will be prioritised for visits by the Environment Secretary.

In addition, the Environment Secretary will set out a clear set of improvement actions for each water company. These will include tackling leakage from pipes, delivering sustained reductions in pollution incidents, and improving customer satisfaction scores.

One-star ratings automatically mean that bonuses will be blocked for executives at Southern Water, Thames Water, South West Water and Yorkshire Water – thanks to new rules which took effect in 2025.

The same applies to any water company with a Category 1 pollution incident – these are incidents which have a major, serious, persistent and/or extensive impact or effect on the environment, people and/or property.

While these shocking failures will automatically trigger bonus bans for six Chief Executives under the existing rules, the Environment Secretary recognises that executives are continuing to be rewarded in spite of persistent underperformance. Further details on strengthening the bonus ban are expected to be set out in the coming weeks.

This comes after the Environment Secretary took the unprecedented step of clearly setting expectations for the next Price Review, warning companies they must deliver better value for money for struggling households.

Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle said:

Water companies have let the public down time and time again, and today’s report is further proof that root-and-branch reform cannot wait.

People are sick of excuses. They want clean rivers, lakes and seas, and the certainty that every pound they pay is being invested wisely, not wasted.

I am demanding answers from the companies that are failing, and I’ll be shining a spotlight on the worst offences around the country. We are getting on with the job of building a water system that finally works for the people who pay for it.

By pooling their data, the regulators are closing the gaps between environmental and financial regulation, giving the public a fuller and more transparent picture of how water companies are performing than ever before, and making it harder for failing companies to point to a good score from one regulator while falling short with the other. The aim is simple – greater transparency, tougher collective scrutiny, and restored public trust in an industry that has tested it badly.

Ministers will meet the chief executives of underperforming companies to demand answers to both performance and updates the delivery of key infrastructure improvements.

The government has made clear that nothing is off the table when it comes to holding underperforming companies to account. Where companies fail to deliver, regulators will not hesitate to use the full range of enforcement powers available, including fines and prosecutions.

Government has already delivered the biggest increase in regulators’ powers in a decade through the Water (Special Measures) Act 2025, the introduction of rapid automatic penalties and is going further and faster to strengthen powers through the strengthened Water Bill to build on this to ensure persistent failure carries more consequences.

items.title: 《绝地求生》电竞 2027 年启用四阶段赛制，印度成为独立赛区
items.summary: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，《绝地求生》官方昨日公布了 2027 年竞赛体系改革方案，将全年赛事调整为四个独立阶段，并重新划分地区赛区。 其中，印度将成为新的独立竞赛区域，原有的 EMEA 赛区将拆分为欧洲、欧亚和中东北非（MENA）三个赛区，美洲赛区则拆分为北美和南美。官方表示，此次调整旨在为更多战队提供参与全球赛事、展现竞技实力的机会。 根据官方公布的方案，2027 年《绝地求生》电竞将采用四阶段赛制，每个阶段均由地区联赛和对应的绝地求生全球系列赛（PGS）组成。 …

items.title: Regulators publish first joint report on water industry performance, giving the public a clearer picture of company performance
items.summary: The Drinking Water Inspectorate, Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat have today published the first Water Industry Performance Insights report. The four regulators have brought their evidence together, giving the public, g
items.bodyHtml:
The Drinking Water Inspectorate, Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat have today published the first Water Industry Performance Insights report. The four regulators have brought their evidence together, giving the public, governments and industry a single, clear view of how the water industry is performing.

The report reflects a shared commitment by regulators to transparency, accountability and driving improvements across the sector for consumers and the environment. It marks a step towards a more integrated, joined-up approach to water regulation, as signalled by the UK and Welsh Governments, who have outlined a once-in-a-generation programme to transform the water system, including the Water Bill.

Water touches every part of daily life. People expect clean, safe drinking water. They expect services to keep working during drought and that their rivers and coastlines are protected. Regulators exist to hold companies to account for that and to ensure the protection of public health and the environment.

Designed to give an overview of individual water companies’ performance, the joint report sits alongside the regulators’ individual annual performance reports. EA, NRW and Ofwat have published these more in-depth reports today - with DWI publishing their report back in July - and together they provide a data driven insight into the performance of the water industry.

The joint report shows a mixed picture, but with strengths to build on:

  • Drinking water quality remains among the best in the world, with 99.97% of tests meeting the required standards.
  • Companies have reduced internal sewer flooding in homes and local businesses, a particularly distressing customer failure, by 43% in recent years.
  • Leakage has reduced over the long term, but with all companies facing growing pressure on water resources, particularly during drought, further reductions are needed.
  • Household consumption remains similar to the previous year, at 137.3 litres per person per day.
  • Water supply interruptions performance across the sector has improved, though some customers continue to experience long-duration interruptions.
  • Pollution incidents remain one of the main areas of concern, with 2,991 incidents across England and Wales in 2025, including 84 classed as serious.
  • Just 93.7% of required environmental improvement actions were completed on time, with 142 of 2,254 planned actions not delivered.

The Environment Agency’s Environmental Performance Assessment (EPA) continues to expose the scale of environmental underperformance by water and sewerage companies with a further decline in EPA star ratings to 16 stars out of a possible 36. Where performance falls short, the EA will not hesitate to take enforcement action, including prosecutions and financial penalties, against the worst-performing companies.

Marcus Rink, Chief Inspector of the Drinking Water Inspectorate said: 

Consumers in England and Wales can have continued confidence that their drinking water remains among the highest quality in the world, with 99.97% of tests meeting the strict standards that protect public health. That is a record the industry should be proud of. 

This report marks a significant first step, bringing four regulators together for the first time to give a more transparent and collaborative picture of the water sector. It is a foundation we intend to build on, working ever more closely to ensure clean and resilient drinking water supply now and for the future.

Philip Duffy, Chief Executive at the Environment Agency, said:

People expect two simple things: safe water from their taps and clean, healthy rivers. Today’s report shows good performance on drinking water quality, but on wastewater and pollution the sector is still falling short.

We are stepping up inspections and enforcement and will use our powers to hold water companies to account and drive the improvements people and the environment deserve.

Helen Campbell, Interim Executive Director for Delivery at Ofwat, said:

Customers rightly expect the record investment approved by Ofwat to deliver tangible improvements in their daily lives and for the environment.

Over the past year we have seen some step up to this challenge, but this is inconsistent and poor performance continues in too many places.

The responsibility sits with water companies to deliver on what they have agreed to, and we will continue to work across regulators to drive stronger outcomes.

Ceri Davies, Chief Executive of Natural Resources Wales, said:

Improving water quality is one of the most significant environmental challenges we face. This joint insights report provides a clearer picture of water company performance by bringing together evidence from across the regulatory systems.

While progress has been made in some areas, there is more to do. We will continue to work with partners across the sector to drive improvements that benefit people, nature and the resilience of our water environment.

Today’s figures reflect greater scrutiny as much as they do underlying performance. Where performance falls short, regulators will act, using the full range of tools available, including fines, enforcement action and requirements for companies to fix problems. Regulators will support companies where they are improving and continue to challenge them where standards aren’t met.

Water companies have committed record levels of investment for 2025 to 2030, with over £104 billion to upgrade water and sewage networks. Regulators are committed to ensuring this investment is well spent and delivers for customers, communities and the environment.

Notes to editors

EA Water and Sewerage Companies in England: environmental performance report

The EA’s Environmental Performance Assessment (EPA) rates water and sewerage companies in England and Wales from 1 to 4 stars, based on measures including pollution incidents, compliance with permits, and self-reporting.

The EPA report covers performance across the 2025 calendar year.

Since 2015, the Environment Agency has concluded 73 prosecutions against water and sewerage companies, securing fines totalling over £172 million.

Ofwat Water Company Operational Performance

Ofwat set stretching targets for water companies in the 2024 price review, to drive real improvements for customers, communities and the environment.

Ofwat’s new Water Company Operational Performance report tracks every company against these targets from the start of the new investment period, and shows which companies are improving and which are falling short. It also monitors companies’ performance over longer timeframes.

In this first year, we’re already seeing progress in some areas, but others still need urgent attention.

Ofwat’s data-driven approach to assessing company performance has been expanded this year to provide a broader view of company performance - both individually, and in comparison to other companies. The new ‘improving’ tag shows the direction the company is travelling in.

In the categorisation for 2025-26, ten companies are categorised as good or on-track, while seven are categorised as off-track and we expect them to improve. Eight companies also received an Improving tag, recognising improvements the company has made over time.

  • South West Water (Bristol region) and South West Water (South West region) are categorised separately, so there are 17 categorisation assessments across 16 companies.

Published today:

  • EA Water and sewerage companies in England: environmental performance report 2025
  • EA Water Only Companies in England: Environmental performance report 2025
  • EA Water resources 2025-2026: analysis of the water industry’s annual water resources performance
  • Ofwat’s Water Company Operational Performance Report, previously the Water Company Performance Report
  • NRW’s Annual performance report for Dŵr Cymru (Welsh Water)
  • NRW’s Annual performance reports for Hafren Dyfrdwy
  • NRW Storm Overflow spill report

Published in July: Drinking Water Inspectorate Chief Inspector Report for both England and Wales.

items.title: Lord Chancellor visits United Nations to promote British candidate to UN court
items.summary: Campaigning on behalf of Professor Dapo Akande to win seat on International Court of Justice Justice Secretary Alex Norris to give speech at UN General Assembly setting out Britain’s commitment to the rule of law and its support for Profess
items.bodyHtml:
• Campaigning on behalf of Professor Dapo Akande to win seat on International Court of Justice
  • Justice Secretary Alex Norris to give speech at UN General Assembly setting out Britain’s commitment to the rule of law and its support for Professor Akande’s candidacy
  • The visit comes ahead of the election on November 3rd

In a speech to UN member states the Lord Chancellor Alex Norris will set out his support for the election of Professor Dapo Akande as a judge to the ICJ.  

The ICJ plays a vital role helping states peacefully resolve disputes by law, supporting international stability, and upholding principles on which all states rely.  The UK’s support of the ICJ is part of its commitment to strengthen justice, human rights and the rule of law around the world.    

The Lord Chancellor will set out to the UN General Assembly the benefits of having Professor Akande on the court. He will say: 

At a moment when international law is under pressure, Professor Akande brings the independence, legal rigour, judgement and breadth of perspective that the Court needs.   

He would make a formidable contribution to its work. 

The intervention from the Lord Chancellor and Chris Elmore, the Minister for the UN, comes ahead of a regular election to the court on 3 November. This year also marks the 80th anniversary of the ICJ’s inaugural sitting in the aftermath of the Second World War.  

During the speech the Justice Secretary will also set out the United Kingdom’s opposition to the sanctions brought against the International Criminal Court. He will say: 

The International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court have distinct jurisdictions and mandates.  

However, the principle at stake is common. Judicial institutions must be able to act independently, impartially and with integrity.   

Attempts to impede their work weaken not only the institutions targeted, but the wider international legal order on which all States rely. 

The United Kingdom will continue to support the ICC and uphold the rules-based international system.

items.title: Government and industry to take on investment bias and workplace culture to support more women in tech
items.summary: Better workplace culture, improved reporting routes to tackle harassment, and fairer investment practices are expected to inform new voluntary standards announced as part of the Chancellor’s Budget Government to launch a scale-up women’s pr
items.bodyHtml:
• Better workplace culture, improved reporting routes to tackle harassment, and fairer investment practices are expected to inform new voluntary standards announced as part of the Chancellor’s Budget
  • Government to launch a scale-up women’s programme, with enhanced support to help women-led businesses scale and grow
  • Creating a fairer sector and investment culture where women are empowered to start and scale businesses at the same rate as men could unlock £310 billion for the UK economy2
  • Early industry ambassadors including BT, Revolut, Sage, Balderton Capital and Octopus Ventures, will co-create the standards with the Women in Tech Taskforce

As announced at the Budget yesterday, a major new push to back women in technology will help tackle barriers facing female founders and workers while boosting growth across the UK economy.

Government will work with industry through its Women in Tech Taskforce to develop two new voluntary standards on workplace culture and on investment practices, alongside launching a new scale-up women’s programme to help more women start, grow and scale technology businesses.

The UK is home to one of the world’s leading tech sectors, but women continue to face barriers to entering, progressing and securing investment. Women make up just 22% of the IT workforce3, despite evidence showing that closing participation gaps could add up to £4 billion a year to UK GDP.

While enabling women to found and grow businesses at the same rate as men could unlock £310 billion for the economy2.

Government’s recent call for evidence found that 74% of respondents believe a better workplace culture would support women’s progression and leadership in tech1,2.

To help break down some of these barriers and encourage more inclusive behaviour, the government is committing to a new “Tech Forward Standard”. Commitments are intended to improve workplace culture and could include measures such as developing trusted harassment reporting routes so workers feel safe to come forward.

Women founders face additional challenges in raising investment. Only 2p of every £1 invested in venture capital funding in the UK goes to women founded businesses5. A new “Inclusive Investment Standard” the taskforce are progressing, could include commitments around broadening deal sourcing channels, and tracking women-led businesses progress from pitch to funding decisions, so it’s clear where founders drop out and where change is needed.

The result: a fairer, more transparent route to funding, helping more great ideas get the financial backing they deserve. 

Alongside these voluntary standards, in 2027 government will launch a new scale-up women’s programme. This will help women founders of high-potential, high-growth UK businesses to secure investment and scale.

The programme will help address the barriers that lead to persistent funding gaps for women-founded companies, providing support that could include workshops, peer learning, networking and introductions to investors. The programme will be run jointly between DCMS and BIST.

Digital Inclusion Minister and Women in Tech Taskforce co-chair Vicky Foxcroft said:

Too many talented women are leaving tech or never getting the chance to build a career in it in the first place.

That’s not just unfair, it’s a waste of talent our economy can’t afford. These initiatives are about working with industry to create opportunities for all, so that tech becomes a place where women can thrive, from the classroom right through to the boardroom.

Chief Executive and co-founder of Stemettes and Women in Tech Envoy Anne-Marie Imafidon said:

Too many women have told us about facing misconduct like harassment and discrimination in tech. That is unacceptable and a key driver of poor participation in the sector. This launch is about working with industry to ensure we have a future that works for everyone, by creating the cultural change women and their allies have long been calling for.   

With 74% of respondents to our Call for Evidence advocating for better workplace culture, we now have a clear mandate to work with industry and make tech somewhere women stay, thrive and lead.

Both standards will now enter a period of co-creation with industry, investors and the Taskforce, ahead of their formal launch in the coming months. The Women in Tech Taskforce will reconvene in November to take forward this next phase of work, helping ensure the standards deliver meaningful change for women across the technology sector.

These initiatives come alongside wider work to build more opportunities for women and girls in tech.

TechFirst Girls Competition

Government has launched registration for the first ever TechFirst Girls Competition, giving girls across the UK the chance to build tech skills and confidence, and to see what a future career in technology could look like for them.

Get Tech Certified

Government has also kicked off digital upskilling across the public sector through its Get Tech Certified programme, which is open to all public servants, not just those in technical roles. This year sees the launch of a dedicated Women in Tech strand, bringing together events, mentoring and career stories to help more women in the public sector build confidence and progress their digital careers.   

TechFirst Women’s Programme

Government will also support women at all career stages, from early-career professionals to career changers and returners, to move into paid jobs in artificial intelligence, cyber security and other high-growth technology sectors. Through the TechFirst Women’s Programme, 300 women across the UK will receive mentoring, skills development and matching with live vacancies, with the aim of securing paid roles lasting at least six months by March 2027.

NOTES TO EDITORS

  • 1 DSIT (2026) The Economic Impact of Equal Opportunities in the Digital Economy
  • 2 HMT (2019) The Alison Rose review of female entrepreneurship; original estimate of £250 bn adjusted for inflation to £310 bn
  • 3 BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, Women in Tech Report 2026 (key findings): There were 433,000 female IT specialists in the UK in 2025 – 22% of all IT specialists in the UK at that time. These figures come from BCS analysis of the ONS Labour Force Survey.
  • 4 Master, A., Meltzoff, A. N., Cheryan, S. (2021) Gender stereotypes about interests start early and cause gender disparities in computer science and engineering Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 118(48), e2100030118.
  • 5 Investing in Women Code Annual Report 2026 - GOV.UK

Ambassadors of the Standards include:

Tech Forward Standard

  • Arm
  • British Science Association
  • BT Group
  • Cellnex
  • Code First Girls
  • Coding Black Females
  • Colt
  • East Midlands Cyber Security Cluster
  • Founders4Schools
  • FDM Group
  • Global Tech Advocates
  • GTA Black Women in Tech
  • Ivee
  • Openreach
  • Marsh
  • Niyo
  • Olio
  • Revolut
  • Sage
  • Startup Coalition
  • Stemettes
  • techUK
  • Tech London Advocates
  • Tech North Advocates
  • Technology Scotland
  • Tramshed Tech
  • TUC
  • Virgin Media O2
  • Vorboss

Inclusive Investment Standard

  • Ada Ventures
  • Alma Angels
  • Balderton Capital
  • BlankPage Capital
  • British Chambers of Commerce
  • ClimbUK
  • Impact X Capital
  • Innovate Finance
  • Octopus Ventures
  • Phoenix Court

  • ScaleUp Institute

  • Full ambassador cohorts and both Standards are expected to be published in the coming months.

  • The Get Tech Certified campaign itself runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026, and is delivered by Government Digital Service and Government Digital and Data in partnership with technology providers covering AI, cloud computing, cyber security, data, software engineering, architecture, FinOps and quantum computing. More information on the Women in Tech strand can be found here: Women in Tech - Government Digital and Data Hub

items.title: LPC recommendations take the National Living Wage to £13.21

items.bodyHtml:
The Government has today announced increases to minimum wage rates from April 2027. The National Living Wage (NLW), the minimum wage rate for all workers aged 21 and over, will rise by 3.9 per cent to £13.21. The minimum wage for 18-20 year olds will increase to £11.27 and the rates for 16-17 year olds and apprentices will increase to £8.31, all of which are 3.9 per cent increases in line with that for the NLW.

In announcing these increases, the Government has accepted in full the recommendations made by the Low Pay Commission.

Although our recommendation for the NLW will not reach the two thirds of median earnings reference point set out in our remit, it still makes progress towards it. Commissioners remain committed to reaching the remit’s key reference point of two thirds of median earnings when economic conditions allow.

While the rate recommended is below that needed to reach the reference point, it is above the range of inflation forecasts from April 2027 to March 2028, with additional allowance made for some upside risk. Therefore, we judge that it will protect the rate in real terms over the period specified in our remit.

The rates announced today are:

NMW rate from April 2027 Increase (£) Increase (%)
National Living Wage (21 and over) £13.21 50p 3.9
18-20 Year Old Rate £11.27 42p 3.9
16-17 Year Old Rate £8.31 31p 3.9
Apprentice Rate £8.31 31p 3.9
Accommodation Offset £11.53 43p 3.9

Baroness Philippa Stroud, LPC Chair, said:

“Discussions with workers and employers alike this year reflected the tough economic headwinds being faced across the economy. It has been challenging to come to a recommended increase that is both fair to workers and gives employers the resilience they need to grow their businesses.

“We have based our recommendations on a careful marshalling of all the available economic evidence, alongside intense reflection and negotiation between our Commissioners. The advice presented is line with the ambition to protect the economy and labour market, giving fair and realistic rates for the year ahead.

“The wider economic picture has been critical in helping decide the increase for 2027. Economic growth has been better than expected this year, but this growth is not leading to hiring. Furthermore, our stakeholders are worried about the risks of a further energy price shock to the economy.“

The remit for younger workers continues to state the Government’s desire to lower the age of eligibility for the NLW to 18. Over the last 4 years we have made good progress on this aim and increased the 18–20 year old rate substantially, reducing the gap between it and the adult rate.

While there is still potential to lower the age limit, especially for 20 year olds, demand for young workers has slowed and the risks associated with ambitious rises have increased. Therefore, we recommend pausing on alignment by recommending a percentage increase in line with that for the NLW, which we believe is consistent with the remit’s aim of prioritising youth employment. We recommend a 3.9 per cent increase or 42p to £11.27 for 18-20 year olds.

For 16-17 year olds, the vast majority of whom are in full-time education, the recommended increase is 31p to £8.31. Employment for this age group has deteriorated over recent years. The evidence does not point to this being the result of minimum wage increase, however this decline is difficult to ignore so future increases are not risk free.

Apprentices of all ages are entitled to the Apprentice Rate in the first year of their apprenticeship. Although vacancy numbers have declined faster than for all vacancies in the economy, we don’t think that the Apprentice Rate is the key factor here either. In light of this, alongside some concern from employers about the cost of employing apprentices, we are recommending an increase of 31p to £8.31 (3.9 per cent).

The Low Pay Commission today publishes its advice to the Government and a short report summarising the evidence used in reaching these recommendations.

NOTES FOR EDITORS

  • The LPC’s recommendations were submitted to the Government on 23 October 2026. The Government has today announced acceptance of those recommendations.
  • The LPC has now published its letter of recommendations to the Government and a short report summarising the main evidence Commissioners relied on to make those recommendations. The LPC’s full annual report will be laid before Parliament and published in the new year.
  • The Government’s remit to the LPC, which determines the Commission’s work through the year, was published in March and is available here.
  • The LPC expects its recommended rate to represent a real-terms increase across the whole of the period to April 2027, using a range of inflation measures, thereby protecting low-paid workers’ living standards.
  • Our assessment of and projections for median earnings rely on the ONS’s Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) and Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) series. These are supplemented by HMRC’s Real Time Information (RTI) data and wage forecasts from the Bank of England and HM Treasury’s Independent Panel of Economic Forecasts.
  • The National Living Wage (NLW) is currently the statutory minimum wage for workers aged 21 and over. This age threshold came down from 25 to 23 in April 2021 and from 23 to 21 in April 2024.
  • Different minimum wage rates continue to apply to 18-20 year olds, 16-17 year olds and apprentices aged under 19 or in the first year of an apprenticeship. The Government has stated its ambition to reduce the NLW age threshold from 21 to 18; this follows the LPC’s advice, as set out in the publication “The National Minimum Wage Beyond 2024”.
  • Rates for workers aged under 21, and apprentices, are currently lower than the NLW to reflect lower average earnings and higher unemployment rates. International evidence also suggests that younger workers are more exposed to employment risks arising from the pay floor than older workers. , the LPC’s remit requires us to set the rates for younger workers that prioritise employment.
  • The National Living Wage is different from the UK Living Wage and the London Living Wage calculated by the Living Wage Foundation. Differences include that: the UK Living Wage and the London Living Wage are voluntary pay benchmarks that employers can sign up to if they wish, not legally binding requirements; the hourly rate of the UK Living Wage and London Living Wage is based on an attempt to measure need, whereas the National Living Wage is based on a target relationship between its level and average pay; the UK Living Wage and London Living Wage apply to workers aged 18 and over, the National Living Wage to workers aged 21 and over. The Low Pay Commission has no role in the UK Living Wage or the London Living Wage.
  • The Accommodation Offset is an allowable deduction from wages for accommodation, applicable for each day of the week. In April 2027 it will increase to £11.53 per day.
  • The Low Pay Commission is an independent body made up of employers, trade unions and experts whose role is to advise the Government on the minimum wage. The rate recommendations introduced today were agreed unanimously by the Commission.
  • The current Low Pay Commissioners are: Baroness Philippa Stroud (Chair), Matthew Fell, Andrew Goodacre, Louise Fisher, Dr Patricia Rice, Simon Sapper, Professor Jonathan Wadsworth and Janet Williamson.
  • Baroness Philippa Stroud can be contacted via the Low Pay Commission’s press office on 07920 531 878.

items.title: Leeds station set for biggest transformation in a generation as government backs city’s growth with a £303 million upgrade
items.summary: budget confirms a further £200 million investment to transform Leeds station by 2030, taking total investment in one of the North’s busiest stations to over £300 million more space, better infrastructure and improved passenger facilities wi
items.bodyHtml:
• budget confirms a further £200 million investment to transform Leeds station by 2030, taking total investment in one of the North’s busiest stations to over £300 million
  • more space, better infrastructure and improved passenger facilities will cut congestion and boost capacity for the almost 12 million extra passengers expected at the station annually by 2043
  • upgrade paves the way for the Transpennine Route Upgrade and Northern Powerhouse Rail, delivering a turn-up-and-go network that drives economic growth across the region

Passengers travelling through Leeds station are set to see major improvements, from shorter queues to reduced crowding and improved accessibility, as the government injects a further £200 million to transform one of the North’s busiest transport hubs.

With additional funding announced at the budget today (28 October 2026), the upgrades are set to be delivered by 2030 and will include the construction of a new central overbridge, 3 new entrances, more space on the concourses and a longer platform 14 to transform the UK’s third busiest station outside of London.

Passengers will benefit from more direct routes through the station and less crowding thanks to nearly 40% more ticket barriers and boosted lift capacity to make journeys quicker and easier.

Three new entrances will strengthen links between the station and the city centre, improving access to the South Bank, the Dark Arches and Princes Square, supporting regeneration, jobs and commercial opportunities across Leeds.

These renovations also pave the way for the Transpennine Route Upgrade, an £11 billion investment which will boost passenger capacity by 30% and electrify key routes across the North, supporting economic growth, new jobs and homes in West Yorkshire.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said:

Leeds station is the gateway to West Yorkshire, and this extra £200 million investment will turn it into a station this city can be proud of: modern, welcoming and built for the people who rely on it every single day.

The great cities of the North deserve better transport and that’s exactly what we’re delivering. We’re paving the way for Northern Powerhouse Rail, forging stronger connections across the region and backing the infrastructure that creates jobs, builds homes and puts passengers first as we work to set up Great British Railways.

The announcement comes just one week after the Transport Secretary confirmed a brand-new station at Bradford Interchange, which, in tandem with the proposed West Yorkshire Mass Transit, would support thousands of new homes, jobs and up to £1 billion in economic benefits.

Currently, Leeds station handles more than 27 million passengers a year, with 8 in 10 services in West Yorkshire starting or ending there. With annual passenger numbers forecast to grow by almost 12 million by 2043, this £300 million investment will future-proof the station, ensuring Leeds has the right infrastructure in place to seize opportunities for economic growth.

A new station in the heart of Bradford city centre and upgrades to Leeds station will provide better connections, faster journeys and improved facilities for passengers as the government kick-starts Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR), which will unlock the North’s potential by transforming travel across the region.

NPR will deliver a turn-up-and-go railway for passengers, meaning multiple trains an hour will run frequently enough between major cities across the North that passengers won’t need to check a timetable before going to the station.

After decades of frustration, the government is building a railway that works for passengers. From bringing operators back into public ownership to investing in new and better stations, fleets and technology, real improvements are underway ahead of the establishment of Great British Railways.

Mayor of West Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin, said:

Leeds Station is the beating heart of our region’s transport network, connecting millions of people to jobs, education and opportunity every year – and it’s only going to get busier.

This investment will benefit passengers and businesses, help to unlock the capacity we need for future growth and create a gateway to West Yorkshire that reflects our ambition.

Together with our wider plans for West Yorkshire’s Weaver Network, we’re building a better-connected region which works for all.

Switchboard 0300 330 3000

NPR will deliver a turn-up-and-go railway for passengers, meaning multiple trains an hour will run frequently enough between major cities across the North that passengers won’t need to check a timetable before going to the station.

After decades of frustration, the government is building a railway that works for passengers. From bringing operators back into public ownership to investing in new and better stations, fleets and technology, real improvements are underway ahead of the establishment of Great British Railways.

Mayor of West Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin, said:


  Leeds Station is the beating heart of our region’s transport network, connecting millions of people to jobs, education and opportunity every year – and it’s only going to get busier.

  This investment will benefit passengers and businesses, help to unlock the capacity we need for future growth and create a gateway to West Yorkshire that reflects our ambition.

  Together with our wider plans for West Yorkshire’s Weaver Network, we’re building a better-connected region which works for all.
