items.title: Government and Rolls-Royce agree £2.5bn to build jet engines in the UK and create tens of thousands of jobs
items.summary: Government agreement with Rolls-Royce will keep UK at forefront of aerospace innovation and could see jet engines built in the UK for decades to come. Multi-decade co-operation includes joint 10-year £2.5bn programme for next-generation jet
items.bodyHtml:
• Government agreement with Rolls-Royce will keep UK at forefront of aerospace innovation and could see jet engines built in the UK for decades to come.
  • Multi-decade co-operation includes joint 10-year £2.5bn programme for next-generation jet engines for passenger and military planes.
  • Agreement expected to support 3,300 jobs by end of 2029 with tens of thousands more in the decades ahead.

Tens of thousands of new jobs are expected to be created from a new government agreement with Rolls-Royce to help turbocharge Britain’s reindustrialisation, including a £2.5 billion programme for cutting-edge cleaner and more efficient jet engines, jointly funded over 10 years.

Announced by the Chancellor as he delivers his first Budget today (28 October), the multi-decade cooperation will develop new jet engines for single-aisle aircraft – the planes taking Brits on their summer holidays in Europe – with only a handful of nations and companies able to build them.

Rolls-Royce estimates that securing a UK engine on these planes could lead to billions more being invested in the UK in the coming decades, which could add £120 billion to the economy over the lifetime of the programme.

Identified by the Industrial Strategy as the UK aerospace sector’s biggest opportunity over the next 50 years, the agreement will put Britain ahead in the race to power the planes carrying millions of passengers around the world for decades to come.

The agreement could help support British industry to take advantage of huge market opportunities, delivering on the Government’s drive to reindustrialisation so that all parts of the UK benefit.

The investment is expected to support for 3,300 existing jobs over the next few years, with the potential for tens of thousands of new roles beyond that.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

Britain has always been an industrial powerhouse. But that strength isn’t just part of our past, it should be a core part of our future too.

That’s why we’re driving forward reindustrialisation and this agreement shows what that looks like in practice.

It gives businesses the certainty to invest, creates jobs people can build a future on, and keeps British industry where it belongs, at the forefront of innovation.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said:

Reindustrialisation isn’t just a soundbite – it’s a cast iron commitment to deliver good jobs and growth for people all over the country. That’s exactly what this agreement does.

It makes sure Britain will win the race to power the next generation of passenger planes, keeping jet engine manufacturing in the UK and creating tens of thousands of jobs in the long term.

It’s also a real vote of confidence in the economic plan we’re delivering – giving businesses the certainty they need to grow and invest here on our shores.

New jobs are expected to cover a range of areas from engineering and research to manufacturing – creating roles which run from the design stage all the way through to the factory floor.

The vast majority of these will also be created outside London and the South East – tapping into the numerous sites and supply chains Rolls-Royce maintains across the country.

It represents a big step forward in the Prime Minister’s plan to reindustrialise Britain, showing how the Industrial Strategy is creating the right conditions for companies to invest, create good jobs and build their future in the UK, while helping secure future military air capability.

Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO, Rolls-Royce, said:

This is a landmark moment for the UK’s aerospace industry. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to lay the foundations for decades of sustainable economic growth across the UK, creating high-value jobs and transforming the country’s advanced manufacturing supply chain.

Aerospace is a growing and globally attractive market and this programme with Government is vital to enable the UK to compete. Working together, we can also sustain the nation’s capability to power military aircraft and secure its position as one of only two countries that can design, develop, make and service the jet engines that power the world’s commercial airliners.

The technology, engineering skills and industrial capabilities developed through this agreement could be used in both passenger and military plane engines, boosting the UK’s national security at a time of global uncertainty.

It will develop technologies including advanced materials, electronic systems, advanced manufacturing and the use of robotics and AI. It also comes alongside a jobs and skills plan that will help build the workforce we need for the future.

That means new opportunities for companies to start up, scale up, and grow, and new avenues of British expertise that can be exported all over the world. 

A key part of the agreement is a commitment to work closely with Rolls-Royce, the wider aerospace sector, regional and local expertise to ensure UK-based suppliers directly benefit from the decades of sustained investment being delivered.

Later this year the Government will publish its plan for Britain and set out how, over 10 years, it will make this country work for people and businesses again. This means more control of the basics to make the country more functional, more power in the hands of people and places to set their own ambitions, and from there good growth in every postcode.

Background

  • The cooperation agreement provides the framework under which future government support will be provided.
  • No new grants have been awarded through the agreement at this stage, and any future government support will remain subject to appropriate legal, value-for-money, affordability and government approval processes.
  • It is also subject to agreement on terms and conditions with Rolls-Royce, and must pass checks on value for money, affordability and compliance with subsidy control rules.
  • Jet engines are some of the most complex and valuable parts of aircraft, with the UK one of only a small number of countries able to design, manufacture and support advanced aerospace engines.
  • This agreement will help take a sector which employs around 113,000 people and brings over £46 billion per year into our economy to the next level. *Single-aisle aircraft are expected to account for the largest share of the global civil aerospace market. ATI analysis indicates that by 2050 they could represent around $164 billion of a $278 billion annual global market. For the UK, the opportunity is to grow its share of the single-aisle market from $5.3 billion today to $24 billion a year by 2050.
  • According to Rolls-Royce, its UK supply chain spend was over £3 billion in 2025.
  • The agreement builds on the £100 million Aerospace Supply Chain fund backed by the British Business Bank and industry announced this summer. This will help ambitious suppliers across the country to grow and meet increasing demand for UK aerospace products and services.

Key sources

  • Rolls-Royce narrowbody aircraft production estimates: The next evolution of aviation.
  • ADS Group UK aerospace sector employment and economic contribution figures: Value of aerospace, defence, security and space to the UK grew two thirds since 2015, ADS finds - ADS Group.
  • Aerospace Technology Institute estimates of the value of the global market for commercial aircraft by 2050: Engineering Growth

items.title: Budget 2026: Breathing space for Welsh families and businesses
items.summary: Energy costs lowered as home heating oil tariffs removed and 0% VAT on household electricity extended. Growth backed with new investment in Cardiff Parkway station, north Wales and Port Talbot. The Welsh Government will have an additional £
items.bodyHtml:
• Energy costs lowered as home heating oil tariffs removed and 0% VAT on household electricity extended. 
  • Growth backed with new investment in Cardiff Parkway station, north Wales and Port Talbot. 
  • The Welsh Government will have an additional £450 million for public services.

Families and businesses in Wales will get breathing space from action announced in Budget 2026. 

Against a backdrop of global uncertainty, rising energy costs and pressure on household finances, Chancellor John Healey has taken action on the cost of living, fuel prices, and local jobs — alongside continued funding for the Welsh Government to deliver public services. 

In the Budget, John Healey announced: 

  • Energy costs: The removal of the 4% tariff on Kerosene will support the 105,000 Welsh households that rely on heating oil to heat their homes. The UK government will extend 0% VAT on household electricity bills for three months, to 30 June 2027., while a Debt Relief Scheme will write off crisis-era debt for eligible households. 

  • Fuel: The extension of the 5p cut to fuel duty for a further six months until 30 June 2027. The 3.7p cut to red diesel duty continues, which matters for farmers, rural hauliers and other fuel-heavy users across Wales. He also announced a permanent increase to the generosity of mileage rates to support those who drive for work.    

  • Food prices: Tariffs axed on over 100 food products, including chocolate and fruit juice. Combined with tariff suspensions earlier this year, this will save households up to £21 annually.  

  • Pensions: By the end of this Parliament, roughly 64,000 low-income pensioners in Wales will pay less tax or none at all on their income, as a result of reducing the disproportionate administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax  

  • Wages: Increasing the National Living Wage by 3.9% to £13.21 per hour and the National Minimum Wage by 3.9% to £11.27 per hour for 18 to 20-year-olds and by 3.9% to £8.31 per hour for 16 to 17-year-olds and eligible apprentices. The last minimum wage increase helped 170,000 people in Wales. 

Backing growth in Wales

  • £30 million will fund the next stage of Cardiff Parkway railway station, driving growth along the M4 corridor  
  • £2.5 million to expand the M-SParc science park in Anglesey, subject to business case, delivering additional space and support for SMEs.  
  • £11 million of new funding to replace the Port Talbot Aberavon Bridge – part of the town’s regeneration – subject to business case.    
  • Extending duty suspensions for 350 goods to help businesses in the chemicals, plastics, hydrogen, automotive and food and drinks sectors.  
  • The Budget strengthens Britain’s national security by fully funding the £15 billion Defence Investment Plan, including £4.7 billion that was previously unfunded. Defence spending supports 7,800 jobs in Wales, including 4,900 industrial jobs, up 26% from 2025. 

Secretary of State for Wales, Stephen Kinnock, said: 

We are taking action by providing households in Wales with much needed breathing space, through reducing the cost of food and energy and putting more money in the pockets of lower income pensioners and workers. 

Having previously secured a £6.5 billion uplift to increase Wales’ budget to record levels, we are now making an additional £450 million available to the Welsh Government to fund public services such as the NHS. And in these uncertain times, I am also enormously proud of our new defence investment which will underpin our collective security and support thousands of jobs in Wales. 

This UK government has already committed generational investment across Wales – from new nuclear, to defence and rail – and today’s Budget will help us turn numbers into reality.” 

Extra funding for public services

Wales gets money for public services through the block grant. This is money collected from taxpayers across the UK, including people in Wales, which the Welsh Government can then spend on devolved services like health, education and housing. 

This Budget means the Welsh Government has at least 20% more funding per person than equivalent spending in the rest of the UK. For each £1 of equivalent UK government spending in the rest of the UK, the Welsh Government has at least £1.20 to spend per person in Wales. The higher amount reflects that providing services across Wales genuinely costs more, and ensures the Welsh Government is funded above what experts say Wales needs, considering factors like geography. 

The Welsh Government will have an additional £450 million for public services, on top of the additional £1 billion from Budget 2025 and Spring Forecast 2026, meaning Wales continues to receive funding well above its assessed level of need.

And in these uncertain times, I am also enormously proud of our new defence investment which will underpin our collective security and support thousands of jobs in Wales. 

  This UK government has already committed generational investment across Wales – from new nuclear, to defence and rail – and today’s Budget will help us turn numbers into reality.” 


Extra funding for public services

Wales gets money for public services through the block grant. This is money collected from taxpayers across the UK, including people in Wales, which the Welsh Government can then spend on devolved services like health, education and housing. 

This Budget means the Welsh Government has at least 20% more funding per person than equivalent spending in the rest of the UK. For each £1 of equivalent UK government spending in the rest of the UK, the Welsh Government has at least £1.20 to spend per person in Wales. The higher amount reflects that providing services across Wales genuinely costs more, and ensures the Welsh Government is funded above what experts say Wales needs, considering factors like geography. 

The Welsh Government will have an additional £450 million for public services, on top of the additional £1 billion from Budget 2025 and Spring Forecast 2026, meaning Wales continues to receive funding well above its assessed level of need.

items.title: Prime Minister and Chancellor’s call with the President of Ukraine: 28 October 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister and Chancellor spoke to the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, this morning ahead of Cabinet. They began by setting out how what was happening in Ukraine was central to UK and European security. Outlining the UK’s
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister and Chancellor spoke to the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, this morning ahead of Cabinet.

They began by setting out how what was happening in Ukraine was central to UK and European security.

Outlining the UK’s unflinching support, the Prime Minister said he was delighted to be able to update the President this morning, on behalf of the Ukrainian people, how the UK would increase its financial support to Ukraine by £10 billion in today’s Budget. 

That included £500 million additional military support from the Ministry of Defence to plug urgent gaps in Ukraine’s air defences this winter, £7 billion of economic support being made available over three years, and a further £3 billion in UK Export Finance (UKEF) capacity for Ukraine, prioritised for military support, the Prime Minister said.

It was the biggest financial package ever committed to Ukraine by the UK and was a symbol of this government’s commitment to ensuring Ukraine had the means to continue its courageous fight against Russia’s illegal invasion, the Prime Minister added.

The UK would also continue to increase its pressure on Putin, to force him to the negotiating table, by continuing to step up its sanctions, the Chancellor said.

The leaders also discussed the upcoming European Political Community meeting and agreed on the need to use the meeting to drive forward further support from partners for Ukraine.

The Prime Minister and Chancellor finished the call by telling President Zelenskyy that all of the Ukrainian people were in their thoughts as they continued to face such barbaric attacks.

They looked forward to speaking again soon.

items.summary: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，据界面新闻报道，菲尔兹奖得主、芝加哥大学教授邓煜近日在一场论坛上阐述了他对 AI 时代数学研究的思考。 邓煜引用帕斯卡“人是一根会思考的芦苇”的名言指出，如果人类因为有了 AI，就放弃了自主思考能力的话，真的就和动物没什么区别了。邓煜提醒，切莫过度依赖工具、放弃独立思辨，如果甘愿把思考的权利完全交给 AI，给 AI 做狗，人也就丢掉了自身最核心的特质。 他进一步表示，数学是检验和体现人类自主思考、自主探索能力最纯粹的学科。无论是在 AI 时代…

items.title: RSH warns council to make fundamental changes for tenants
items.summary: Haringey London Borough Council must make fundamental changes to deliver improved outcomes for its tenants, the Regulator of Social Housing has warned. The north London local authority was given a C4 consumer grade today after RSH’s inspect
items.bodyHtml:
Haringey London Borough Council must make fundamental changes to deliver improved outcomes for its tenants, the Regulator of Social Housing has warned.

The north London local authority was given a C4 consumer grade today after RSH’s inspection found very serious failings.

Although Haringey LBC had indicated a willingness to address issues and taken some action, RSH has not yet seen sufficient evidence that it understands the potential risk to tenants and is able to put matters right.

Issues included:

  • A substantial backlog of overdue repairs including damp and mould cases, poor tenant satisfaction, and weaknesses in performance, oversight and assurance.
  • Only around half of non-emergency repairs reported were completed on time in 2025/26.
  • Despite improvement activity over several years, outcomes remain poor and tenants continue to experience delays, missed appointments and communication failures.
  • Almost 4,000 remedial fire safety actions are overdue – including more than 1,400 actions categorised as high risk.
  • Not providing timely responses or demonstrating learning from complaints.
  • A failure to inform the RSH about significant issues which had emerged.

RSH Deputy Chief Executive Kate Dodsworth said: “A C4 judgement sends a clear signal that tenants have been let down and that urgent and sustained improvement is needed.

“We will maintain intensive engagement and close oversight, set clear expectations for improvement and, if necessary, use our powers to make sure change happens.

“We expect landlords in this position to take urgent action to address and fix the issues identified and improve outcomes for tenants.”

Two other local authorities received a C3 consumer grade in today’s regulatory judgements.

RSH found serious failings in how Tamworth Borough Council in Staffordshire is meeting the outcomes of the regulatory standards. It has not shown that all actions arising from health and safety assessments are carried out within appropriate timescales.

There were issues around its reporting of hazards including a lack of detail on the number of overdue hazards and the timeliness of remedial actions, and the reporting and oversight of anti-social behaviour. RSH saw limited evidence of meaningful opportunities for tenants to scrutinise their landlord’s performance and influence how its services are delivered. 

Tamworth has engaged constructively with RSH during the inspection. It is improving its understanding of tenants’ homes and strengthening its repairs process, and taking action to address the other issues RSH found in the inspection.

RSH also found serious failings in how Woking Borough Council in Surrey is meeting the outcomes of the regulatory standards. RSH identified some weaknesses in the council’s completion of overdue fire, water and asbestos remedial actions. The council needs to improve its disrepair reporting and improve communication with tenants on this issue.

RSH also found serious failings in Woking’s delivery of the outcomes of the Tenancy Standard and the Neighbourhood and Community Standard, notably around the management of anti-social behaviour and hate incidents, and tenancy oversight.

Woking is largely meeting its health and safety obligations and targets for repairs. It has engaged constructively with us throughout the inspection process and is taking action to address these weaknesses.

Two landlords – Irwell Valley Housing Association in Greater Manchester and The Pioneer Housing and Community Group Limited based in Birmingham – received a C1 today for their first grading following inspection.

And three landlords – Karbon Homes Limited in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, South Holland District Council in Lincolnshire and Tuntum Housing Association Limited in Nottingham – received consumer upgrades to C1.

Home Group Limited based in Newcastle-upon-Tyne received a C2 for its first consumer grading and a G2 downgrade. RSH said it needs to improve some aspects of its board reporting to enable effective oversight of consumer and compliance risk areas. It also needs to strengthen board oversight of assurance findings and reviews to enable timely delivery of improvements.  

The Housing Plus Group and Trent and Dove Housing Limited, both based in Staffordshire, received a C2 for their first consumer gradings. Both have G1/V2 grades that were assessed and unchanged.

ReSi Homes Group received its first gradings of C2, G2 and V1* following inspection. The for-profit landlord owns around 1,400 shared ownership homes, the majority of which are in the south west, south east and London, managed by third party property managers.

The first of this year’s stability checks were also published today - RSH’s annual review of a landlord’s financial information, business plan and risk profile to assess whether its financial viability gradings remain appropriate.

Among those was G15 landlord Notting Hill Genesis (NHG), which currently has C3, G3 and V2 grades. RSH continues to engage intensively with NHG as it delivers the required improvements and is monitoring their progress closely. RSH is considering alternative resolution options should they be needed and could take regulatory action if required.

ENDS

Notes to editors

The full list of judgements published today is provided in the table below.

  1. On 1 April 2024 RSH introduced revised consumer standards for social housing landlords, designed to drive long-term improvements in the sector. It also began a programme of landlord inspections. The changes are a result of the Social Housing Regulation Act 2023 and include stronger powers to hold landlords to account. More information about RSH’s approach is available in its document Reshaping Consumer Regulation.
  2. RSH does not give grades to small landlords (under 1,000 homes) and only publishes regulatory judgements where it considers there to be serious weaknesses or failings in a landlord’s delivery of the outcomes of the standards.
  3. Grades marked with an asterisk indicate a for-profit registered provider.
  4. More information about RSH’s responsive engagement, programmed inspections and consumer gradings is also available on its website.
  5. RSH promotes a viable, efficient and well-governed social housing sector able to deliver more and better social homes. It does this by setting standards and carrying out robust regulation focusing on driving improvement in social landlords, including local authorities, and ensuring that housing associations are well-governed, financially viable and offer value for money. It takes appropriate action if the outcomes of the standards are not being delivered.
  6. RSH publishes gradings for consumer, governance and viability. Local authorities only receive consumer gradings. More information can be found on our How we approach regulatory judgements and gradings page.

items.bodyText:
Haringey London Borough Council must make fundamental changes to deliver improved outcomes for its tenants, the Regulator of Social Housing has warned.

The north London local authority was given a C4 consumer grade today after RSH’s inspection found very serious failings.

Although Haringey LBC had indicated a willingness to address issues and taken some action, RSH has not yet seen sufficient evidence that it understands the potential risk to tenants and is able to put matters right.

Issues included:


  A substantial backlog of overdue repairs including damp and mould cases, poor tenant satisfaction, and weaknesses in performance, oversight and assurance.
  Only around half of non-emergency repairs reported were completed on time in 2025/26.
  Despite improvement activity over several years, outcomes remain poor and tenants continue to experience delays, missed appointments and communication failures.
  Almost 4,000 remedial fire safety actions are overdue – including more than 1,400 actions categorised as high risk.
  Not providing timely responses or demonstrating learning from complaints.
  A failure to inform the RSH about significant issues which had emerged.


RSH Deputy Chief Executive Kate Dodsworth said: “A C4 judgement sends a clear signal that tenants have been let down and that urgent and sustained improvement is needed.

“We will maintain intensive engagement and close oversight, set clear expectations for improvement and, if necessary, use our powers to make sure change happens.

“We expect landlords in this position to take urgent action to address and fix the issues identified and improve outcomes for tenants.”

Two other local authorities received a C3 consumer grade in today’s regulatory judgements.

RSH found serious failings in how Tamworth Borough Council in Staffordshire is meeting the outcomes of the regulatory standards. It has not shown that all actions arising from health and safety assessments are carried out within appropriate timescales.

There were issues around its reporting of hazards including a lack of detail on the number of overdue hazards and the timeliness of remedial actions, and the reporting and oversight of anti-social behaviour. RSH saw limited evidence of meaningful opportunities for tenants to scrutinise their landlord’s performance and influence how its services are delivered. 

Tamworth has engaged constructively with RSH during the inspection. It is improving its understanding of tenants’ homes and strengthening its repairs process, and taking action to address the other issues RSH found in the inspection.

RSH also found serious failings in how Woking Borough Council in Surrey is meeting the outcomes of the regulatory standards. RSH identified some weaknesses in the council’s completion of overdue fire, water and asbestos remedial actions. The council needs to improve its disrepair reporting and improve communication with tenants on this issue.

RSH also found serious failings in Woking’s delivery of the outcomes of the Tenancy Standard and the Neighbourhood and Community Standard, notably around the management of anti-social behaviour and hate incidents, and tenancy oversight.

Woking is largely meeting its health and safety obligations and targets for repairs. It has engaged constructively with us throughout the inspection process and is taking action to address these weaknesses.

Two landlords – Irwell Valley Housing Association in Greater Manchester and The Pioneer Housing and Community Group Limited based in Birmingham – received a C1 today for their first grading following inspection.

And three landlords – Karbon Homes Limited in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, South Holland District Council in Lincolnshire and Tuntum Housing Association Limited in Nottingham – received consumer upgrades to C1.

Home Group Limited based in Newcastle-upon-Tyne received a C2 for its first consumer grading and a G2 downgrade. RSH said it needs to improve some aspects of its board reporting to enable effective oversight of consumer and compliance risk areas. It also needs to strengthen board oversight of assurance findings and reviews to enable timely delivery of improvements.  

The Housing Plus Group and Trent and Dove Housing Limited, both based in Staffordshire, received a C2 for their first consumer gradings. Both have G1/V2 grades that were assessed and unchanged.

ReSi Homes Group received its first gradings of C2, G2 and V1* following inspection. The for-profit landlord owns around 1,400 shared ownership homes, the majority of which are in the south west, south east and London, managed by third party property managers.

The first of this year’s stability checks were also published today - RSH’s annual review of a landlord’s financial information, business plan and risk profile to assess whether its financial viability gradings remain appropriate.

Among those was G15 landlord Notting Hill Genesis (NHG), which currently has C3, G3 and V2 grades. RSH continues to engage intensively with NHG as it delivers the required improvements and is monitoring their progress closely. RSH is considering alternative resolution options should they be needed and could take regulatory action if required.

The changes are a result of the Social Housing Regulation Act 2023 and include stronger powers to hold landlords to account. More information about RSH’s approach is available in its document Reshaping Consumer Regulation.
  
RSH does not give grades to small landlords (under 1,000 homes) and only publishes regulatory judgements where it considers there to be serious weaknesses or failings in a landlord’s delivery of the outcomes of the standards.

items.title: UK engineering firm appointed to deliver major decommissioning project at Dungeness A
items.summary: Worth up to £190 million, the contract will help accelerate the safe decommissioning of the site, reduce long-term national risk and support British industry, skills and economic opportunities for local communities. The project will remove
items.bodyHtml:
Worth up to £190 million, the contract will help accelerate the safe decommissioning of the site, reduce long-term national risk and support British industry, skills and economic opportunities for local communities.

The project will remove eight boiler units, each weighing around 800 tonnes, together with associated plant and infrastructure. It follows four years of enabling work to prepare the site for this complex phase of delivery.

Dungeness A first boiler arrived on site in 1962

Rob Fletcher, Chief Executive Officer of NRS, said: “This is a landmark project for NRS and a major engineering challenge. By working closely with Aureos, our supply chain and regulators, we will explore new approaches in line with the recommendations of the Nuclear Regulatory Review to safely decommission our sites, deliver better value for taxpayer and maintain our unwavering commitment to safety.”

The boilers will be moved using a specialist jack and slide system, allowing some of the station’s largest remaining structures to be removed safely, efficiently and with precision. Their removal will mark visible progress in transforming the site and reducing future care demands.

Vicki Baxter, Senior Project Manager, added: “Reaching this point is a real achievement for everyone involved. It reflects exceptional teamwork, careful planning and close collaboration in completing the demolition and site preparation work safely.”

Aureos was selected through a competitive procurement process that assessed technical capability, project certainty, innovation, social value and cost.

Dave Evans, Dungeness A Site Director, said: “This contract marks the beginning of one of the most significant stages in Dungeness A’s decommissioning journey. It is the result of years of planning and preparation and moves us significantly closer to achieving our decommissioning mission for the site.”

Darren James, Chief Executive Officer of Aureos, said: “On behalf of Aureos, I am delighted that we have received this award following a procurement process that placed significant emphasis on innovation. We look forward to working with NRS to deliver the project and recognise its importance to the Dungeness A site and surrounding area.”

The supplier will work closely with local communities and stakeholders throughout the project, including schools, universities, community groups and local businesses. Activities will include engagement events, supply chain opportunities, volunteering initiatives and regular updates to ensure the project delivers lasting benefits for the region.

Dungeness A Boilers and Ancillary Plant Removal Project Team

Once complete, the project will have removed around a third of Dungeness A’s above-ground structures, significantly reducing the site’s footprint and long-term maintenance requirements while supporting NRS’s progress towards completing the site’s decommissioning mission and ultimately making land available for future beneficial use.

See the story unfold in our latest YouTube video

items.title: More people protected as government acts to make more homes safe
items.summary: Support to be extended to more leaseholders including those in collectively owned and enfranchised buildings who currently risk facing bills for serious building and fire-safety defects A new scheme will make construction product manufactur
items.bodyHtml:
• Support to be extended to more leaseholders including those in collectively owned and enfranchised buildings who currently risk facing bills for serious building and fire-safety defects
  • A new scheme will make construction product manufacturers contribute towards the cost of putting unsafe buildings right
  • Comes alongside wider reforms to give millions of leaseholders stronger rights, protections and control over their homes

More homeowners who have been facing significant bills to make their homes safe will be given better protection from those high costs, under new measures announced today (27 October 2026).

Existing rules already protect many leaseholders from footing the bill for fixing historic building safety defects, but some people still fall through gaps in the system due to different forms of ownership not covered by the law, leaving them at risk of paying for problems they did not cause.

The government will now go further to narrow these gaps and give more people financial support.

Construction product manufacturers connected to historic unsafe cladding and insulation products will also be made to contribute more towards putting affected buildings right. For the first time, government will have powers it needs to recover contributions from manufacturers - and at scale.

These new proposals were unveiled in Parliament during the second reading of the Remediation of Unsafe Cladding Bill – a drive to get unsafe buildings fixed faster and make sure those responsible for fixing unsafe buildings will face tougher consequences if they fail to act.

Building Safety Minister Baroness Blake said:

We are going further to protect more homeowners from unfair costs and make construction product manufacturers contribute towards putting things right.

Alongside new powers to force those responsible to fix unsafe buildings, these measures will help give residents the safety and security they deserve.

The new measures will intend to help:

Leaseholders who buy a flat as their only home but miss out on costs protections because of the previous owners’ circumstances.

  • Under current rules, whether someone is protected from some building safety bills can depend on the circumstances of the person who owned the flat on 14 February 2022. This means someone can buy a flat later as their only or main home and still miss out, because a previous owner was ineligible. The government is exploring how to narrow this gap, to help more leaseholders feel confident in the safety of their home.

Leaseholders in collectively owned and enfranchised buildings who can face some of the biggest bills for fixing fire-safety problems.

  • Because there is no separate freeholder, residents are not covered by the leaseholder protections of the Building Safety Act, putting them at risk of paying a lot. New government funding will help towards remediation of internal high risk and high-cost fire-safety defects.

Leaseholders with multiple properties that have non-cladding building safety problems they did not cause and are not currently protected under the Building Safety Act.

  • At the moment, protections generally cover people who owned no more than three properties on 14 February 2022. The government plans to raise this limit to six, so more people who owned four to six properties and did not qualify on this date will be protected from having these costs passed on to them. This will support individuals at risk of high bills through no fault of their own and in many cases need to make their properties safe for the people that live in them.

The Bill will speed up action by placing a legal duty on those responsible to fix unsafe buildings, with those failing to act facing criminal penalties and fines of up to £500,000. It will also allow authorities to step in and get work done where those responsible consistently refuse to do so.

ENDS

Notes to editors

  • See more information here about the Bill’s introduction to Parliament.

  • Existing leaseholder protections are based on circumstances on 14 February 2022, when the protections were first published. Among other conditions, a lease can qualify where the flat was the owner’s only or main home at that point, or they owned no more than three UK properties. The lease’s protected or unprotected status passes to future buyers, meaning someone buying the flat later as their only home can still miss out. The date was fixed to prevent the rules being gamed once the protections were known. See more information here.

  • Further details on eligibility and funding for the new protections, as well as how the construction product manufacturer scheme will operate, will be introduced into the Bill later as it passes through Parliament or published alongside it in due course.

items.title: Great North Road Solar and Biodiversity Park development consent decision announced
items.summary: The application is for a Solar photovoltaic array generating station, battery energy storage system and grid connection infrastructure, with a maximum generation capacity of 800MW. The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate
items.bodyHtml:
The application is for a Solar photovoltaic array generating station, battery energy storage system and grid connection infrastructure, with a maximum generation capacity of 800MW.

The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate for consideration by Elements Green Trent Limited on 27 June 2025 and accepted for examination on 22 July 2025.

Following an examination during which the public, statutory consultees and interested parties were given the opportunity to give evidence to the Examining Authority, recommendations were made to the Secretary of State on 28 July 2026.  

This is the 117th energy application out of 185 applications examined to date and was again completed by the Planning Inspectorate within the statutory timescale laid down in the Planning Act 2008.  

Local communities continue to be given the opportunity of being involved in the examination of projects that may affect them. Local people, the local authority and other interested parties were able to participate in this six-month examination.  

The Examining Authority listened and gave full consideration to all local views and the evidence gathered during the examination before making its recommendation to the Secretary of State. 

The decision, the recommendation made by the Examining Authority to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero and the evidence considered by the Examining Authority in reaching its recommendation are publicly available on the project pages of the National Infrastructure Planning website. 

This decision was made by Baroness Curran on behalf of the Energy Secretary’s legal authority.

Journalists wanting further information should contact the Planning Inspectorate Press Office, on 0303 444 5004 or 0303 444 5005 or email:  

Press.office@planninginspectorate.gov.uk

items.title: 全国短池游泳锦标赛：张雨霏、张展硕创新纪录 徐嘉余率队破纪录
items.summary: 中新社北京10月27日电 (刘梦青)2026年全国游泳锦标赛(25米)27日在北京国家游泳中心“水立方”继续进行。张雨霏、张展硕分别斩获女子100米蝶泳、男子800米自由泳冠军，并刷新短池亚洲纪录；在男女4×100米混合泳接力决赛中，徐嘉余仰泳开棒游出48秒54的成绩、打破短池亚洲纪录，率浙江寿仙谷队夺冠，并破亚洲纪录。

items.title: UK sets pace on new undersea sensors to detect threats, as AUKUS partners test advanced kit in San Diego
items.summary: UK to lead development of three pioneering payloads for uncrewed underwater vehicles, as part of AUKUS security partnership Announcement wraps up Maritime Big Play exercise in San Diego, enhancing integration of uncrewed systems across AUKU
items.bodyHtml:
• UK to lead development of three pioneering payloads for uncrewed underwater vehicles, as part of AUKUS security partnership

  • Announcement wraps up Maritime Big Play exercise in San Diego, enhancing integration of uncrewed systems across AUKUS fleets in another step towards a UK Hybrid Navy

  • Work builds on AUKUS Pillar II framework, strengthening security and deterrence across Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific

The UK will lead the next stage of delivery of cutting-edge undersea sensing technologies which will be deployed from uncrewed underwater vessels as part of the AUKUS security partnership.

The announcement rounds off a week of testing and demonstrations at the Maritime Big Play exercise in San Diego.

This advances the first signature project under AUKUS Pillar 2 - announced in May as part of the trilateral security partnership between Australia, the UK and the United States - seeks to pool the innovation of each nations’ defence sector to develop advanced military capabilities to strengthen deterrence and security around the world.

The UK will lead development and delivery of three pioneering sensor payloads for uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs): a Synthetic Aperture Sonar, a Deployable Anti-Submarine Warfare Sensor, and a Deployable Non-Kinetic Effector.

These capabilities will collect detailed underwater information, deploy sensors to detect and classify underwater threats, and generate underwater effects. The payloads will help UUVs provide surveillance of large ocean areas and protect underwater infrastructure.

The payloads will be available across the three nations’ UUV fleets from 2027, enhancing the reach and effectiveness of those fleets and reinforcing strategic deterrence across the Euro-Atlantic, High North and Indo-Pacific.

The project positions AUKUS at the forefront of autonomy and uncrewed systems in the maritime domain and wraps up the latest series of exercises conducted last week at the Maritime Big Play (MBP) exercise in San Diego, a proving ground where autonomous marine capabilities are integrated and tested before wider adoption across the AUKUS partnership.

Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard said:

The UK is all in on AUKUS, and this cutting-edge technology shows why. By leading development of these sensor payloads, we’re putting British innovation at the heart of AUKUS and strengthening our collective undersea capability.

In places like Frome, Basingstoke and Dorchester, British companies large and small are driving this work forward, creating skilled jobs and backing our plan to deliver a modern, Hybrid Navy fit for the threats we face.

Sir Stephen Lovegrove, the Prime Minister’s Special Representative on AUKUS, said:

AUKUS is a uniquely powerful partnership, and the depth and breadth of our cutting-edge capability and strength in the maritime domain has been demonstrated this week in San Diego.

The UK is now stepping forward to lead development of three of the most advanced undersea sensor payloads any of our three nations have fielded, sharpening our collective edge and reinforcing security across the Euro-Atlantic and the Indo-Pacific.

The AUKUS partnership is backed by the Defence Investment Plan, which set out £298 billion of UK defence spending over the next four years, marking the largest sustained increase since the end of the Cold War.

The Maritime Big Play exercise aims to shorten the path from innovation to capability by testing new maritime technologies in realistic operational environments. Exercises at MBP-Pacific tested how Australian, UK and US crewed and uncrewed systems operate together across four strands: anti-submarine warfare, lethality, contested resupply, and subsea and seabed warfare.

The UK led the anti-submarine warfare (ASW) strand, contributing thirteen uncrewed surface vehicles, two ASW targets and four underwater gliders from six industry partners. The testing supports the transition to a Hybrid Navy: a more flexible, modern force blending crewed and uncrewed platforms, able to detect underwater threats to the UK and allies’ critical undersea infrastructure.

Royal Navy Captain Keith Taylor said

Maritime Big Play-Pacific gives AUKUS a unique opportunity to turn autonomy into operational advantage. By bringing scientists, industry and warfighters together, and developing the common control solutions that allow diverse autonomous systems to operate and fight as one, we can rapidly build an integrated allied force with greater scale, combat effectiveness and deterrent effect.

The event also showcased two of the four UK winners from the AUKUS Maritime Innovation Challenge – SEA Ltd, based in Frome, and Decision Analysis Services Ltd, based in Basingstoke – demonstrating their cutting-edge technology to trilateral partners and media at MBP-P. 

The two companies, along with A2i (based in Dorchester) and US company MSI Transducers, make up the four suppliers that won the Maritime Innovation Challenge, and a share in £3 million of funding to develop innovative capabilities enabling the command, control and cooperation of undersea systems.

The winners show the breadth and diversity across AUKUS innovation, with one SME, two large suppliers, and one micro-consultancy. MBP featured 12 UK industry partners showcasing their role at the forefront of development in the maritime domain, demonstrating how the AUKUS partnership is driving economic growth across the UK, creating skilled jobs and opportunities for companies of all sizes.

Maritime Big Play and the announcement on delivery progress for the first signature project follows a strong month for UK delivery against AUKUS Pillar 2. This includes the successful test firing of a US-Australian heavyweight torpedo from a UK extra-large uncrewed underwater vehicle, XV Excalibur, a historic first for an uncrewed submarine and an important milestone in enhancing interoperability and delivering the signature project.

This includes the successful test firing of a US-Australian heavyweight torpedo from a UK extra-large uncrewed underwater vehicle, XV Excalibur, a historic first for an uncrewed submarine and an important milestone in enhancing interoperability and delivering the signature project.

items.title: Frodsham Solar development consent decision announced
items.summary: The application is for a Solar photovoltaic array with an electrical generating capacity of over 50MW comprising solar PV modules and related mounting structures, inverters, transformers, switch gear and control equipment, a substation, and
items.bodyHtml:
The application is for a Solar photovoltaic array with an electrical generating capacity of over 50MW comprising solar PV modules and related mounting structures, inverters, transformers, switch gear and control equipment, a substation, and underground on and off-site cabling, as well as associated energy storage equipment.

The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate for consideration by Frodsham Solar Ltd on 30 May 2025 and accepted for examination on 27 June 2025.

Following an examination during which the public, statutory consultees and interested parties were given the opportunity to give evidence to the Examining Authority, recommendations were made to the Secretary of State on 29 July 2026.  

This is the 116th energy application out of 184 applications examined to date and was again completed by the Planning Inspectorate within the statutory timescale laid down in the Planning Act 2008.  

Local communities continue to be given the opportunity of being involved in the examination of projects that may affect them. Local people, the local authority and other interested parties were able to participate in this six-month examination.  

The Examining Authority listened and gave full consideration to all local views and the evidence gathered during the examination before making its recommendation to the Secretary of State. 

The decision, the recommendation made by the Examining Authority to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero and the evidence considered by the Examining Authority in reaching its recommendation are publicly available on the project pages of the National Infrastructure Planning website. 

This decision was made by Baroness Curran on behalf of the Energy Secretary’s legal authority.

Journalists wanting further information should contact the Planning Inspectorate Press Office, on 0303 444 5004 or 0303 444 5005 or email:  

Press.office@planninginspectorate.gov.uk

items.title: Government launches first ever misogyny prevention fund
items.summary: A new, multi-million-pound misogyny prevention fund will aim to root out misogynistic attitudes and support women and girls The Chancellor is providing £15 million to act as basis to unlock further philanthropic and corporate funding Minist
items.bodyHtml:
• A new, multi-million-pound misogyny prevention fund will aim to root out misogynistic attitudes and support women and girls

  • The Chancellor is providing £15 million to act as basis to unlock further philanthropic and corporate funding

  • Minister for Women Bridget Phillipson hails “critical step” as government works to “confine misogyny to history books”

A new drive to support women and girls and tackle misogyny is in line for government investment, as the Chancellor, John Healey, and Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson, announce the first misogyny prevention fund.

The Chancellor will provide a £15 million injection to the Office for the Impact Economy (OIE) to be invested in schemes over 3 years that could include mentoring for young people, workplace training and communications campaigns to improve outcomes and safety for women and girls across the UK.

The fund is expected to be confirmed in the 2026 Budget on Wednesday 28 October.

The fund will underpin Bridget Phillipson’s misogyny prevention taskforce, demonstrating this government’s commitment to backing up words with action.

The investment will form the basis for work with corporate partners and philanthropists to unlock additional match funding and ultimately multiply its reach.

Minister for Women and Equalities Bridget Phillipson said:

Day to day misogyny – from sexist slurs and harassment to workplace discrimination – quite simply has no place in modern Britain. 

The time for talk has long passed, which is why this government is putting its money where its mouth is when it comes to supporting women and girls. This funding is a critical step as we work to confine misogyny to the history books, where it belongs.

Government is leading from the front, but we all have a role to play. Everyone – from big business to members of the public – can do their bit to stamp out misogyny and improve the lives of women and girls everywhere.

Chancellor John Healey MP said:

Every woman and girl deserves to feel safe, respected and able to pursue their ambitions – at school, at work and in their communities.

This investment will back practical action to tackle misogyny head-on, while bringing businesses and philanthropists on board so we can go even further – giving women and girls more opportunity to succeed and hope for the future.

The funding will run through the OIE, in partnership with the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO), using the OIE’s expertise in mobilising external funding and partnership working.

The fund will operate a bidding process through which organisations will receive grants to deliver programmes that meet the government’s ambition of preventing misogyny in all its forms, and reducing its impacts.

Examples of similar work already ongoing in the sector include:

  • Expect Respect from Women’s Aid – a free programme for schools that educates children on what is and is not normal in relationships and stepping in when it is safe

  • investment in mentoring and interventions from positive role models for girls and boys respectively, alongside active bystander training, funded by the Mayor of London

  • workplace training and resources from Equimundo, aimed at men and designed to foster gender equality in the workplace 

Notes to editors

The Minister for Women and Equalities has set up a national misogyny prevention taskforce to show what works to prevent misogyny and drive delivery across government. 

The work and issues identified by the taskforce will be supported by £5 million of funding each year for the next 3 years to deliver programmes and pilots that work to prevent misogyny and reduce its impacts. 

OEO will work with OIE to crowd in corporate match funding to increase the size of this pot.

items.title: Parents who murdered 13-week-old son have sentences increased
items.summary: A mother and father whose baby suffered 41 fractures before they killed him have had their sentences increased after the Attorney General intervened. Nivalda Santos Pirjani, 35, and Klevi Pirjani, 37, of Seacombe, Wallasey had their minimum
items.bodyHtml:
A mother and father whose baby suffered 41 fractures before they killed him have had their sentences increased after the Attorney General intervened. 

Nivalda Santos Pirjani, 35, and Klevi Pirjani, 37, of Seacombe, Wallasey had their minimum terms increased by two and a half years each to 17 years and 9 months and 21 years and 6 months respectively after the Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, referred their sentences to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme. 

The court heard that their son, Miguel Pirjani, had spent the first month of his life in hospital before being discharged into his parents’ care. 

Within days of returning home, Miguel Pirjani was assaulted for the first time, suffering two fractured ribs. The abuse continued and escalated over the following weeks. 

On 24 November 2024, when Miguel Pirjani was 13 weeks old, his parents subjected him to a fatal assault involving a heavy blow or series of blows to his head. Paramedics restarted his heart, but he never regained consciousness and died in Alder Hey children’s hospital five days later. 

Medical examinations found that Miguel Pirjani had suffered 41 fractures in total, including injuries to his ribs, legs, arm, collarbone and spine, inflicted during repeated assaults over several weeks. 

The judge said it was not possible to determine which parent had inflicted the fatal injuries, but found that they had acted together and that whichever parent carried out the violence was encouraged by the other. 

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP said: 

Miguel Pirjani was a defenceless baby who had an entire life to live, yet he suffered appallingly cruel violence at the hands of the two people who should have protected him. 

This was a truly harrowing case, and my thoughts are with everyone who loved and cared for him. 

I welcome the Court of Appeal’s decision to increase both minimum terms following my referral and remain committed to ensuring those who carry out the most serious crimes face the full force of the law.

On 23 March 2026, at Liverpool Crown Court, Nivalda Santos Pirjani was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 15 years and three months for murder. She was also sentenced to four years and six months’ imprisonment, to run concurrently, for causing grievous bodily harm with intent. 

Klevi Pirjani was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 19 years for murder. He was also sentenced to six years and six months’ imprisonment, to run concurrently, for causing grievous bodily harm with intent. 

On Tuesday, 27 October, at the Court of Appeal, Nivalda Santos Pirjani’s minimum term was increased to 17 years and 9 months, and Klevi Pirjani’s minimum term was increased to 21 years and 6 months.

items.title: “生命三角区”存误区 科学避险记牢这几点
items.summary: 近日，西藏那曲市巴青县发生7.0级地震，青海省玉树藏族自治州杂多县与巴青县相邻，交界乡镇震感强烈。一系列地震避险相关话题再次引发全网热议，网上广为流传的“生命三角区”避震方法也被翻出来讨论。不少人深信，地震发生时赶紧找到三角空隙躲避，就能保住安全。但很多人不知道，这个听起来靠谱的办法其实存在很大误区，盲目寻找反而会增加受伤风险。

items.title: Minister launches new campus for National School of Government
items.summary: The National School of Government will roll out a range of training programmes from day one, including AI training, for all civil servants. With its first dedicated residential campus outside York, the national school has been created to en
items.bodyHtml:
• The National School of Government will roll out a range of training programmes from day one, including AI training, for all civil servants.

  • With its first dedicated residential campus outside York, the national school has been created to ensure that the civil service has the knowledge and skills it needs to deliver the government’s priorities.

  • We are building a world-class civil service, ensuring staff have the skills to drive government priorities and deliver for people across the UK.

Cabinet Office Minister Mark Ferguson has today opened the new National School of Government and Public Services, which will provide training for civil servants and public sector leaders.

Regional hubs will be developed across the country, with the first opened in York this week, alongside digital access routes to give civil servants access to modern learning facilities close to where they live and work.

It will provide civil servants and public sector leaders with the world-class learning and development they need to meet the challenges of the future.

The school will build a curriculum around the skills all servants need, including training on devolution, national security, leadership and innovation.  Training will also be offered in AI, covering the full range of skills needed now and in the future, from implementing practical solutions at the frontline to cut clerical workloads to cloud engineering courses to develop and deploy the latest technology across government, the School will equip Civil Servants with the tools to build a world-class Civil Service. 

The training will support Civil Servants to go further in deploying AI to build a more productive public sector, building on recent successes including an A&E demand forecasting tool is now in use across 50 NHS organisations, enabling hospitals to predict peak periods in emergency departments and plan staffing more effectively, or rolling out AI tutoring tools in schools with the target to half the attainment gap for disadvantaged students.

Cabinet Office Minister Mark Ferguson said:

The opening of the new school is a unique opportunity to upskill civil servants in the areas that matter most - with AI being among the top priorities

From day one, the National School offers learning built around Universal Skills that every civil servant needs - from digital skills and AI, to leadership and management.

This launch is part of a drive to boost public sector productivity and accelerate the pace of progress towards delivering the digitally-enabled public services to be expected from a modern state.

The creation of the school is a powerful statement that the Civil Service values its people, invests in their growth, and is serious about building the capability to meet the challenges of the future in the places where our people live and work

Bringing training in-house will also reduce spending on external training over time as the school is fully established.

This builds on plans underway to halve government spending on external consultants and reduce departmental administration costs by 16% over the next five years, delivering savings of over £2 billion a year for the taxpayer by 2030.

The National School of Government has also partnered with the annual Civil Service ‘One Big Thing’ learning initiative, this year the theme is ‘AI in Action’.

items.title: New MHRA research puts needle-free Strep A vaccine within reach
items.summary: New research by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in partnership with the GSK Vaccines Institute for Global Health, has moved a vaccine against the highly contagious group A streptococcus bacterium (Strep A) a s
items.bodyHtml:
New research by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in partnership with the GSK Vaccines Institute for Global Health, has moved a vaccine against the highly contagious group A streptococcus bacterium (Strep A) a step closer to reality.  

Published this month (October 2026), the paper, published in Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics, also shows promise for ‘needle-free’ vaccines which could be administered in the nose or under the tongue.  

There is currently no licensed vaccine for Strep A, despite it causing hundreds of millions of infections globally. Although most Strep infections are mild, serious complications can lead to long-term disability or death, particularly in low-and middle-income countries where the burden of the disease remains high.  

It is estimated that there are over 600 million Strep A infections worldwide each year with associated complications responsible for over 500,000 deaths. 

Dr Fatme Mawas, Head of Conjugate Vaccines, MHRA said: 

“This research highlights the potential of GMMA technology to support a new generation of affordable, needle-free vaccines. By delivering a Strep A vaccine through the nose or under the tongue, we showed that strong immune responses were generated both at the mucosal surfaces where infection begins and throughout the body, supporting protection against invasive disease.  

“This approach could make vaccines easier to administer and more accessible globally, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where the burden of Strep A disease is greatest. By preventing infections before they occur, vaccines can also help reduce antibiotic use and support efforts to tackle antimicrobial resistance.” 

The vaccine uses Generalised Modules for Membrane Antigens (GMMA) which are tiny bubbles naturally shed from bacteria, as both a carrier for the Strep A carbohydrate and an adjuvant to boost the immune response.  

Unlike most vaccine approaches, which focus primarily on generating antibodies in the bloodstream, this research targets immunity at mucosal surfaces of the nose and throat, where Strep A establishes infection, while also inducing broader systemic immune response. 

The findings support the further development of affordable, easily administered mucosal vaccines that could improve access to immunisation worldwide and contribute to global efforts to reduce the burden of infectious disease and antimicrobial resistance 

This work was conducted in a mouse (pre-clinical) model and forms part of the MHRA’s wider programme of research into vaccine science, immunology, assay development and novel vaccine delivery technologies.  

Notes to editors  

  1. The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe.  All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.  

  2. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care.  

  3. For media enquiries, please contact the newscentre@mhra.gov.uk, or call on 020 3080 7651.

items.title: UK Human Rights Ambassador visits Tanzania ahead of UN review
items.summary: On 20 October, the UK’s Ambassador for Human Rights, Eleanor Sanders, arrives in Tanzania for engagements with a wide range of stakeholders ahead of the UN’s forthcoming review of the status of Tanzania’s human rights landscape. During her
items.bodyHtml:
On 20 October, the UK’s Ambassador for Human Rights, Eleanor Sanders, arrives in Tanzania for engagements with a wide range of stakeholders ahead of the UN’s forthcoming review of the status of Tanzania’s human rights landscape.

During her visit to Dar es Salaam, Sanders will meet representatives from the media, religious bodies, pastoralist groups, political parties and human rights organisations.

She will hear a diverse range of perspectives on human rights in Tanzania and exchange views on the role of dialogue and international cooperation in supporting inclusive societies.

Sanders’ programme will also include visits to UK-supported initiatives working to improve access to sexual and reproductive health commodities for women and girls, and to tackle human trafficking in Tanzania.

The visit takes place ahead of Tanzania’s forthcoming Universal Periodic Review, a UN process through which Member States’ human rights records are assessed. The Review provides an opportunity for countries to share information on progress, discuss challenges and consider recommendations relating to the promotion and protection of human rights.

Eleanor Sanders, UK Ambassador for Human Rights and Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations and other International Organisations in Geneva, said:

As the UK’s Human Rights Ambassador, I’m delighted to be visiting Tanzania. Tanzania is a dynamic regional player and an important relationship for the UK. I’m looking forward to taking forward our conversations on a range of human rights issues – in doing so, hearing from civil society and communities, and seeing first-hand the impact of UK supported programmes in Dar es Salaam.

I want to understand more deeply where rights are under pressure and to talk about issues that are dear to us, such as accountability and respect for fundamental freedoms.

I look forward to discussing how we can work together to protect and advance human rights, strengthen accountability and make a difference for people across Tanzania.

Marianne Young, British High Commissioner to Tanzania, said:

I am delighted to welcome the UK’s Human Rights Ambassador to Tanzania. Her visit is an opportunity to exchange perspectives on human rights and to strengthen our engagement in Tanzania on issues of shared interest.

The visit is also an opportunity to shine a spotlight on the important work the UK and Tanzania are delivering in partnership to improve access to sexual and reproductive health for women and girls, and to tackle human trafficking.

items.title: Gwyndod supply chain mobilised to deliver UK’s first SMRs
items.summary: More than 400 suppliers from across North Wales, the UK and the international nuclear industry came together on Ynys Môn as Rolls-Royce SMR and Great British Energy – Nuclear (GBE-N) moved forward with plans to deliver the UK’s first small
items.bodyHtml:
More than 400 suppliers from across North Wales, the UK and the international nuclear industry came together on Ynys Môn as Rolls-Royce SMR and Great British Energy – Nuclear (GBE-N) moved forward with plans to deliver the UK’s first small modular reactors at Gwyndod.

The ‘Delivering Together’ conference, held at Coleg Menai’s Llangefni Campus, brought businesses face-to-face with the joint Gwyndod delivery team. It marked an important step in mobilising the supply chain and building the industrial capability needed to deliver this flagship project.

Over two days, delegates heard about the opportunities from the programme, the capabilities and standards required and how businesses can prepare to become part of the supply chain. SMEs also received tailored guidance on how to engage with the wider Gwyndod project supply chain.

Rolls-Royce SMR and GBE-N delivered presentations and shared practical guidance to help businesses of all sizes engage with the programme. Suppliers heard about the capabilities needed and how to work with the programme’s delivery partners, including through dedicated meet-the-buyer sessions. 

Rolls-Royce SMR and GBE-N have an ambition to deliver 70% of the content for the Gwyndod project through UK based companies - creating and sustaining thousands of jobs locally and across the whole of the UK. More than 300 apprentices are expected to be supported during construction, with an ambition to fill opportunities locally wherever possible.

Minister for Energy, Michael Shanks MP, said: “Our golden age of nuclear will create thousands of skilled jobs, attract billions of pounds of investment, and help drive down bills over time.

“Gwyndod’s small modular reactors will create new opportunities for a generation of young people across North Wales, supporting growth through the UK supply chain, and delivering clean, homegrown nuclear power for the whole of Britain.”

Welsh Government Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy, Adam Price, said: “The Welsh Government is committed to maximising Gwyndod’s economic, employment and supply-chain benefits for Wales. Our ambition is not simply to host the project, but to secure lasting value through skilled jobs, opportunities for Welsh businesses and stronger local supply chains.

“Wales brings an experienced and highly skilled workforce, with expertise spanning professional, technical and trade roles. This provides a strong foundation for Welsh businesses and workers to play a substantial role in delivering what marks a new chapter for the British nuclear industry as the first SMR build.”

Simon Roddy, CEO of Great British Energy – Nuclear, said: “As we continue to make great strides with the Gwyndod project, it was inspiring to see such a significant level of interest and excitement from the supply chain to find out more about how they can get involved, and even better to be able to host such an event on Anglesey itself at Coleg Menai. 

“The attendance of Ministers from both UK and Welsh Governments across both days of our event perfectly emphasised how serious we are about delivering the project together; we truly are all one “Team Gwyndod!”

Chris Cholerton, Rolls-Royce SMR Chief Executive, added: “The Gwyndod project is our opportunity to transform the way nuclear power is delivered. Our repeatable, factory-built approach will provide greater certainty and reduce delivery risk, while creating a national industrial capability that can support a UK fleet of Rolls-Royce SMRs and the huge export order opportunity, starting with those already secured in Czechia and Sweden.

“This event has brought the organisations and expertise behind that ambition together with a focus on Delivering Together. We are now energising the Gwyndod supply chain and building the enduring partnerships that will turn our plans into action.”

Together, Rolls-Royce SMR and GBE-N share an ambition for Gwyndod to provide clean, affordable power for generations to come, while transforming UK industry and creating lasting opportunities for communities in North Wales and across the UK.

Paratoi cadwyn gyflenwi Gwyndod i gyflawni SMRs cyntaf y DU

Daeth dros 400 o gyflenwyr ledled Gogledd Cymru, y DU a’r diwydiant niwclear byd-eang ynghyd ar Ynys Môn wrth i Rolls-Royce SMR a Great British Energy - Nuclear (GBE-N) symud ymlaen â chynlluniau i gyflawni adweithyddion modiwlar bach cyntaf y DU yn Gwyndod.

Daeth y gynhadledd ‘Cyflawni gyda’n Gilydd’, a gynhaliwyd ar gampws Coleg Menai yn Llangefni, â busnesau wyneb yn wyneb â’r tîm sy’n cyflawni Gwyndod ar y cyd. Dyma gam pwysig o ran paratoi’r gadwyn gyflenwi a datblygu’r gallu diwydiannol sydd ei angen i gyflawni’r prosiect blaenllaw hwn.

Dros ddeuddydd, clywodd y rhai a fynychodd am y cyfleoedd sydd ynghlwm â’r rhaglen, y galluoedd a’r safonau sydd eu hangen a sut all busnesau baratoi i ddod yn rhan o’r gadwyn gyflenwi. Yn ogystal, cafodd BBaChau arweiniad wedi’i deilwra ar sut i ymwneud â chadwyn gyflenwi ehangach prosiect Gwyndod.

Rhoddodd Rolls-Royce SMR a GBE-N gyflwyniadau a rhannwyd arweiniad ymarferol er mwyn helpu busnesau o bob maint i ymwneud â’r rhaglen. Clywodd gyflenwyr am y galluoedd sydd eu hangen a sut i weithio gyda phartneriaid cyflawni’r rhaglen, yn cynnwys drwy sesiynau cwrdd â’r prynwr pwrpasol.

Uchelgais Rolls-Royce SMR a GBE-N yw i raglen SMR y DU gynnwys 70% o gynnwys o’r DU, gan greu a chynnal miloedd o swyddi yn lleol ac ar draws y DU gyfan. Disgwylir y bydd dros 300 o brentisiaid yn cael eu cefnogi yn ystod y gwaith adeiladu, gydag ucheglais i bobl leol lenwi’r cyfleoedd hynny lle bynnag mae hynny’n bosibl.

Dywedodd y Gweinidog dros Ynni, Michael Shanks AS: “Bydd ein hoes euraidd o niwclear yn creu miloedd o swyddi medrus, yn denu biliynau o bunnoedd o fuddsoddiad, ac yn helpu i leihau biliau dros amser.

“Bydd adweithyddion modiwlar bach Gwyndod yn creu cyfleoedd newydd ar gyfer cenhedlaeth o bobl ifanc ledled Gogledd Cymru, gan gefnogi twf drwy gadwyn gyflenwi’r DU, a darparu pŵer niwclear glân wedi’i gynhyrchu yn y wlad hon ar gyfer Prydain i gyd.”

Meddai Gweinidog Cabinet Llywodraeth Cymru dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni, Adam Price: “Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i wneud y mwyaf o fuddion economaidd, cyflogaeth a chadwyn gyflenwi Gwyndod i Gymru. Nid ein huchelgais yw lletya’r prosiect yn unig, ond hefyd i sicrhau gwerth parhaus drwy sgiliau medrus, cyfleoedd i fusnesau Cymru a chadwyni cyflenwi lleol cryfach.

“Mae Cymru yn cynnig gweithlu profiadol a medrus tu hwnt, gydag arbenigedd yn cwmpasu rolau proffesiynol, technegol a masnach. Mae hyn yn rhoi sylfaen gref i fusnesau a gweithwyr Cymru chwarae rôl sylweddol yn cyflawni’r hyn sy’n nodi pennod newydd i ddiwydiant niwclear Prydain drwy adeiladu’r SMR cyntaf.”

Dywedodd Simon Roddy, Prif Swyddog Gweithredol Great British Energy - Nuclear: “Wrth i ni barhau i gamu ymlaen â phrosiect Gwyndod, ysbrydoledig oedd gweld cymaint o ddiddordeb a chyffro gan y gadwyn gyflenwi i ddysgu mwy am sut allant gymryd rhan, a gwell byth oedd gallu cynnal digwyddiad o’r fath ar Ynys Môn ei hun, yng Ngholeg Menai.

“Roedd presenoldeb Gweinidogion o Lywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU ar draws dau ddiwrnod ein digwyddiad yn pwysleisio’n berffaith ein bod o ddifrif ynglŷn â chyflawni’r prosiect gyda’n gilydd; rydym ni i gyd yn un “Tîm Gwyndod”!

Ychwanegodd Chris Cholerton, Prif Weithredwr Rolls-Royce SMR: “Prosiect Gwyndod yw ein cyfle i drawsnewid y ffordd y cyflawnir pŵer niwclear. Bydd ein dull ailadroddadwy o adeiladu mewn ffatri yn rhoi gwell sicrwydd ac yn lleihau’r risg sydd ynghlwm â chyflawni, gan greu gallu diwydiannol cenedlaethol a all gefnogi llu o SMRs Rolls-Royce yn y DU a’r cyfle enfawr i allforio, gan ddechrau gyda’r rheini sydd eisoes wedi’u sicrhau yn Tsiecia a Sweden.

“Daeth y digwyddiad hwn â’r sefydliadau a’r arbenigedd sydd wrth wraidd yr uchelgais honno ynghyd, gyda ffocws ar Gyflawni gyda’n Gilydd. Rydym nawr yn grymuso cadwyn gyflenwi Gwyndod ac yn magu’r partneriaethau cryf a fydd yn gwireddu ein cynlluniau.”

Gyda’i gilydd, mae gan Rolls-Royce SMR a GBE-N uchelgais gyffredin sef i Gwyndod ddarparu pŵer glân, fforddiadwy am genedlaethau i ddod, gan drawsnewid diwydiant y DU a chreu cyfleoedd a fydd yn para ar gyfer cymunedau yng Ngogledd Cymru ac ar draws y DU.

Meddai Gweinidog Cabinet Llywodraeth Cymru dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni, Adam Price: “Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i wneud y mwyaf o fuddion economaidd, cyflogaeth a chadwyn gyflenwi Gwyndod i Gymru. Nid ein huchelgais yw lletya’r prosiect yn unig, ond hefyd i sicrhau gwerth parhaus drwy sgiliau medrus, cyfleoedd i fusnesau Cymru a chadwyni cyflenwi lleol cryfach.

“Mae Cymru yn cynnig gweithlu profiadol a medrus tu hwnt, gydag arbenigedd yn cwmpasu rolau proffesiynol, technegol a masnach. Mae hyn yn rhoi sylfaen gref i fusnesau a gweithwyr Cymru chwarae rôl sylweddol yn cyflawni’r hyn sy’n nodi pennod newydd i ddiwydiant niwclear Prydain drwy adeiladu’r SMR cyntaf.”

Dywedodd Simon Roddy, Prif Swyddog Gweithredol Great British Energy - Nuclear: “Wrth i ni barhau i gamu ymlaen â phrosiect Gwyndod, ysbrydoledig oedd gweld cymaint o ddiddordeb a chyffro gan y gadwyn gyflenwi i ddysgu mwy am sut allant gymryd rhan, a gwell byth oedd gallu cynnal digwyddiad o’r fath ar Ynys Môn ei hun, yng Ngholeg Menai.

“Roedd presenoldeb Gweinidogion o Lywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU ar draws dau ddiwrnod ein digwyddiad yn pwysleisio’n berffaith ein bod o ddifrif ynglŷn â chyflawni’r prosiect gyda’n gilydd; rydym ni i gyd yn un “Tîm Gwyndod”!

Ychwanegodd Chris Cholerton, Prif Weithredwr Rolls-Royce SMR: “Prosiect Gwyndod yw ein cyfle i drawsnewid y ffordd y cyflawnir pŵer niwclear. Bydd ein dull ailadroddadwy o adeiladu mewn ffatri yn rhoi gwell sicrwydd ac yn lleihau’r risg sydd ynghlwm â chyflawni, gan greu gallu diwydiannol cenedlaethol a all gefnogi llu o SMRs Rolls-Royce yn y DU a’r cyfle enfawr i allforio, gan ddechrau gyda’r rheini sydd eisoes wedi’u sicrhau yn Tsiecia a Sweden.

“Daeth y digwyddiad hwn â’r sefydliadau a’r arbenigedd sydd wrth wraidd yr uchelgais honno ynghyd, gyda ffocws ar Gyflawni gyda’n Gilydd. Rydym nawr yn grymuso cadwyn gyflenwi Gwyndod ac yn magu’r partneriaethau cryf a fydd yn gwireddu ein cynlluniau.”

Gyda’i gilydd, mae gan Rolls-Royce SMR a GBE-N uchelgais gyffredin sef i Gwyndod ddarparu pŵer glân, fforddiadwy am genedlaethau i ddod, gan drawsnewid diwydiant y DU a chreu cyfleoedd a fydd yn para ar gyfer cymunedau yng Ngogledd Cymru ac ar draws y DU.
