items.title: UK and Poland strengthen defences on Europe's Eastern flank
items.summary: Britain will be more secure as a result of a new defence agreement with Poland designed to deter Russian threats. The Warsaw Defence Plan comes as Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and his counterpart Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz today meet in W
items.bodyHtml:
Britain will be more secure as a result of a new defence agreement with Poland designed to deter Russian threats.

The Warsaw Defence Plan comes as Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and his counterpart Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz today meet in Warsaw. Under the agreement, the two nations will work together across sea, land, air, cyber and industry to strengthen security and deterrence across Europe’s Eastern Flank.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP said: 

Poland is one of the UK’s closest allies - from flying together in the Battle of Britain, to breaking the Enigma code, they have been a vital partner for our defence for nearly a century.

The new Warsaw Defence Plan honours this cooperation and sets out how we will continue to work together today, building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO.

From collaborating on NATO exercises that deter our adversaries to working together to support Ukraine in its fight for freedom, we are committed to standing together for European security whilst boosting our economies with stronger defence industries.

The agreement sets out the first phase of defence cooperation under the new UK-Poland Security and Defence Partnership Treaty and demonstrates the UK stepping up on European security to build a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO.

It will strengthen joint work on defence between the UK and Poland across a number of key areas, including:

  • Collaboration on the manufacture and development of the next generation of air defence missiles.
  • Co-development of drone and counter-drone technologies to deter threats to civilians and critical national infrastructure, as Russia steps up its campaign of drone incursions across the UK and Europe.
  • Boosting cooperation on cyber security and resilience to help both countries defend defence and civilian sites from hostile threats.
  • Sharing lessons and experience from developing frigate capabilities, the British Type 31 and Polish Miecznik, which are built from a common design.
  • Increasing defensive maritime activity in the Baltic Sea through exercises and regional coordination, helping British and Polish forces protect vital lines of communication in the sea.

The UK and Poland will also work together to further strengthen cooperation between their defence industries through closer defence procurement coordination, building on major deals such as Poland’s procurement of its Narew air defence system from MBDA UK.

UK and Polish defence industrial partners BAE Systems and Poland’s PGZ will expand large-calibre ammunition production capacity and capability. More widely, both nations’ defence industries will collaborate to promote defence education, training and workforce mobility to build shared expertise.

Continued UK and Polish participation in large-scale exercises such as Steadfast Defender, Polish Dragon and Joint Warrior will also ensure both nations remain ready to respond to the conflicts of the future, including counter-drone warfare, electronic warfare, and missile defence.

It comes as the UK and Poland plan for a major Coalition of the Wiling exercise in Poland next month, which will see thousands of personnel take part to ensure the Multinational Force Ukraine is ready to support the military training and post-war rebuilding that Ukraine will need.

items.title: Churches Conservation Trust: Tuesday 27th October 2026
items.summary: The King has approved the re-appointment of Ms Tanvir Zehra Hasan as a Trustee for a second term until 31st January 2031. Tanvir, Chair of the Conservation Committee of the CCT, is an accredited conservation architect specialising in listed
items.bodyHtml:
The King has approved the re-appointment of Ms Tanvir Zehra Hasan as a Trustee for a second term until 31st January 2031.

Tanvir, Chair of the Conservation Committee of the CCT, is an accredited conservation architect specialising in listed buildings within Conservation Areas. She provides vital guidance to the Board on maintaining 358 churches and new Church of England vestings, while drawing on her landmark heritage experience to adapt these historic spaces for community use.

Internationally, Tanvir consults for the World Monuments Fund in Iraq on post-conflict restoration, including key sites at Amedi, Erbil Citadel, and Mosul Museum. Her work helps reconcile divided communities while building local capacity through training in conservation and traditional crafts such as stonemasonry and timber joinery.
items.bodyText:
The King has approved the re-appointment of Ms Tanvir Zehra Hasan as a Trustee for a second term until 31st January 2031.

Tanvir, Chair of the Conservation Committee of the CCT, is an accredited conservation architect specialising in listed buildings within Conservation Areas. She provides vital guidance to the Board on maintaining 358 churches and new Church of England vestings, while drawing on her landmark heritage experience to adapt these historic spaces for community use.

Internationally, Tanvir consults for the World Monuments Fund in Iraq on post-conflict restoration, including key sites at Amedi, Erbil Citadel, and Mosul Museum. Her work helps reconcile divided communities while building local capacity through training in conservation and traditional crafts such as stonemasonry and timber joinery.

items.title: RSH publishes annual social housing stocks and rents statistics
items.summary: Today the Regulator of Social Housing published statistics about the social housing sector, including stock ownership and rents as of 31 March 2026. Returns from all private and local authority registered providers show that the sector prov
items.bodyHtml:
Today the Regulator of Social Housing published statistics about the social housing sector, including stock ownership and rents as of 31 March 2026. 

Returns from all private and local authority registered providers show that the sector provides around 4.6 million homes across England, with a net increase of around 36,000 social homes since 2025.

This overall rise has been driven by an increase of over 24,000 in Affordable Rent homes and 13,390 increase in low-cost home ownership homes. However, there was also a decrease of just over 1,700 social rent homes.

Private registered providers had a net gain of 7,829 social rent homes. Local authorities saw a decrease of 9,570 social rent homes (likely to be primarily driven by right to buy sales and other schemes). Private registered providers built, purchased or acquired the majority of new homes in the sector, accounting for 88% of the total increase in Affordable Rent and 97% for low-cost home ownership properties. 

The statistics show that 82% of social homes in England are general needs (social rent and Affordable Rent), while supported housing makes up 11% and low-cost home ownership 6%. 

London has the greatest proportion of registered provider owned homes with 19.4% of all social homes in this area, while the North East has the fewest – accounting for only 5.4% of the overall total.

Birmingham is the local authority area with the largest volume of social housing at just over 107,000 homes.

The average increase in general needs (social rent) average weekly net rents was 3.2% between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 (in line with the limit set for 2025/26).

The average weekly general needs (social rent) weekly rent in England for private registered providers was £121.72, though this varied across the country. Average rents were lowest in the North East (£100.31) and highest in London (£154.73). 

Rents for local authorities are lower on average than for private registered providers.  

Will Perry, Director of Strategy at RSH, said: 

“This analysis provides a vital picture of the sector’s resilience and the challenges it continues to face. It helps ensure social landlords can plan effectively, manage risks and make informed decisions that support safe, decent homes for current and future tenants.

“It is encouraging to see providers investing in both new homes and a better understanding of their existing stock. Good quality data is essential to making the right strategic decisions for residents and the long-term health of organisations.”

Ends

Notes to editors 

  1. Total social housing stock includes general needs social rent, general needs Affordable Rent, social rent supported housing, Affordable Rent social housing, and low-cost home ownership.
  2. Local authority social housing data was formerly collected through the Local Authority Housing Survey. Since 1 April 2020 it has been collected by RSH through the Local Authority Data Return, when RSH took on the responsibility for regulating local authority rents. Private registered provider data has been collected by RSH though the Statistical Data Return since 2012. 
  3. Both local authority and private registered provider stock and rents statistics are designated as Accredited Official Statistics by the UK Statistics Authority. 
  4. There were 1,580 providers on RSH’s register on 31 March 2026. Of these, 230 were local authorities and 1,350 were private registered providers. 
  5. Homes include self-contained units such as houses and flats and non-self-contained bed spaces, referred to collectively as units in the data. 
  6. Of the 4.6 million units of social housing stock owner by registered providers, private registered providers own 3m homes while local authority registered providers own 1.6m homes. 
  7. The limit on annual general needs rent increases between 2025 and 2026 was 2.7%. Additions to stock, units with exceptions and PRPs setting set rents in line with the prevailing formula rent rate when re-letting units can lead to the average year-on-year change being higher than might otherwise be expected.
  8. The Regulator of Social Housing promotes a viable, efficient and well-governed social housing sector able to deliver and maintain homes of appropriate quality that meet a range of needs. It does this by undertaking robust economic regulation focusing on governance, financial viability and value for money that maintains lender confidence and protects the taxpayer. It also sets consumer standards and may take action if these standards are breached and there is a significant risk of serious detriment to tenants or potential tenants.
  9. For media enquiries email vicky.moore@rsh.gov.uk or christian.cosby@rsh.gov.uk. For general enquiries email enquiries@rsh.gov.uk.

items.title: Ofqual fines Innovate Awarding £185,000 over failures to deal with fraud risks
items.summary: Innovate Awarding Limited (Innovate) has been fined £185,000 by Ofqual after the regulator found serious failings in its oversight of a centre delivering a business administration qualification. The action reflects Ofqual’s commitment to pr
items.bodyHtml:
Innovate Awarding Limited (Innovate) has been fined £185,000 by Ofqual after the regulator found serious failings in its oversight of a centre delivering a business administration qualification.

The action reflects Ofqual’s commitment to protecting the integrity of qualifications and holding awarding organisations to account when they fail to manage fraud risks. Ofqual found that weaknesses in Innovate’s controls at a centre delivering its Level 3 Diploma in Business Administration increased the risk of qualification fraud. Its investigation found substantial weaknesses in how Innovate approved and monitored the centre as well as shortcomings in its response when concerns emerged. As a result, the centre was able to register learners and claim certificates without sufficient scrutiny.

When concerns were identified, Innovate did not fully investigate or initially consider whether learners who had already received certificates had genuinely earned the qualification.

Of the 858 learners awarded this qualification by Innovate between January 2021 and December 2024, 851 were registered through the centre in question.

Ofqual found that Innovate:

  • approved the centre without carrying out enough checks
  • allowed the centre to claim certificates against its own rules
  • failed to identify unusual registration and certification activity
  • did not properly investigate serious concerns about learner evidence
  • failed to consider the impact on affected learners until prompted by Ofqual
  • did not promptly withdraw certificates awarded to learners who had not properly achieved the qualification
  • failed to keep accurate records and data

Innovate first identified concerns in January 2024 after 130 learners were registered and certificated within 24 hours. Innovate stopped the centre claiming certificates directly and arranged more quality checks. It later sanctioned the centre and ended its relationship with it.

Further checks carried out by Innovate in March 2025 raised serious problems with learner evidence.

Innovate only widened its investigation after engagement with Ofqual. It completed the withdrawal of wrongly awarded certificates in August 2026, more than 2 years after concerns first emerged. In total, of the 851 certificates issued to learners registered at the centre, 847 have been revoked.

Innovate admitted breaching several of Ofqual’s rules, namely: A5.1 (by way of A5.2), A6.1, A6.2, A8.1, A8.2, A8.3, B4, C1, C2, G8.1(b), H2 and H5.3(b). It failed to meet the safeguards designed to protect qualification standards and meant certificates remained in place despite doubts about whether some learners had properly earned them.

Amanda Swann, Executive Director for Delivery at Ofqual, said:

The value of qualifications depends on public confidence that they are awarded fairly and earned legitimately. Awarding organisations play a vital role in maintaining that confidence through effective oversight, robust controls, and prompt action when concerns arise.

Innovate Awarding failed to respond effectively to serious concerns raised about qualifications delivered through one of its centres. Weak controls increased the risk of qualification fraud and allowed certificates to remain in place despite doubts about whether some learners had genuinely met the qualification’s requirements. These are significant failings that undermine trust in qualifications and warrant a substantial financial penalty.

Innovate has accepted the failings, co-operated with the investigation and taken steps to strengthen its controls.

As part of the settlement, Innovate will pay a £185,000 fine and contribute £15,000 towards Ofqual’s investigation and enforcement costs. It has provided Ofqual with a formal plan to address the issues identified and agreed to 12 months of monitoring to ensure it complies with requirements.

Notes to editors:

Ofqual has today published the Notice of Monetary Penalty issued to Innovate.

The level 3 diploma in business administration is an occupational qualification designed to build competence and administrative skills in workplace settings, although Innovate no longer offer this qualification.

For media enquiries, contact Ofqual’s press office at media@ofqual.gov.uk or call 0300 303 3014

items.title: Everyday fixes to make life easier for millions of Britons
items.summary: Millions of working people, families and unpaid carers to benefit from five practical fixes to everyday costs ahead of Wednesday’s Budget. Government action taken on food and fuel, alongside parental pay rights for more than 150,000 additio
items.bodyHtml:
• Millions of working people, families and unpaid carers to benefit from five practical fixes to everyday costs ahead of Wednesday’s Budget.
  • Government action taken on food and fuel, alongside parental pay rights for more than 150,000 additional parents per year.
  • Unpaid carers no longer left worse off simply for earning more.

Millions of families, working people and unpaid carers across the country will benefit from five everyday fixes unveiled by the Chancellor, supporting people with the cost of food, fuel and family life, providing breathing space for households.

The package will tackle costs people face every day, from doing the weekly shop to supporting people who rely on their cars for work, while extending support to new parents and fixing an unfair cliff edge that can penalise unpaid carers for earning more.

This is the latest in the Prime Minister’s series of ‘everyday fixes’ designed to tackle everyday frustrations, save families time and money and give them more room to breathe. It follows action on unfair airline charges, subscription traps, rogue traders and rip-off school uniform costs.

It comes ahead of the Budget on Wednesday focused on giving families and businesses breathing space with the costs they face today, while taking the long-term decisions needed to strengthen the economy and support growth and bring costs down.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

We are taking on the big challenges facing the country. But that doesn’t mean losing sight of the everyday problems that cost people money or simply aren’t fair.

If you’re a nurse driving for work, a parent spending those precious first weeks with your new baby, or an unpaid carer picking up an extra shift, these changes will make life a little easier and put more money back in your pocket.

And at Wednesday’s Budget, we’ll go further to give families and businesses the breathing space they need today, while we build a stronger economy, transform our country and bring down cost for people long-term.

The Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:

Today’s everyday fixes are just a small part of what we are doing to give families a bit of breathing space. 

Conflict in the Middle East and Europe is hitting families here at home through higher everyday costs.

We can’t control global events, but we can act where we can make a difference.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said:

This is a real boost for working families and carers. This Budget is about making hard-earned money go further, easing the pressure of everyday costs and giving families much-needed breathing room.

Families have so much to juggle, from paying the bills to balancing work and caring for loved ones. This support can make a real difference—not just in managing today’s costs, but in helping families look ahead with greater confidence and optimism.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said:

I understand the huge difference unpaid carers make to their families and communities. Many balance work alongside their caring responsibilities.

We have listened to their concerns about the cliff-edge built into the system which leaves them financially worse off for taking on a few more hours, or getting a modest pay rise, and intend to bring that to an end.

Today’s announcements include:

  • Making higher tax-free mileage rates permanent and increasing support for nurses, care workers, self employed builders and others who drive for work. The Chancellor is locking in the 55p per mile rate for the first 10,000 business miles and increasing the rate above 10,000 miles from 25p to 35p per mile, supporting around three million employees and self-employed people who use their own vehicle for work.
  • Extending parental pay to more than 150,000 additional parents per year, including self-employed dads and partners who have previously missed out, giving eligible parents two weeks of support currently worth up to £194 a week so they can spend more time with their child.
  • Ending the Carer’s Allowance cliff edge, so unpaid carers no longer lose their entire allowance simply for earning a penny over the Weekly Earnings Limit, equivalent to 16 hours of the National Living Wage. Instead, only £1 of support will taper away for every additional £1 earned.
  • Removing import tariffs on more than 100 products, helping lower import costs on family favourites including baked beans, chocolate and gherkins, while also supporting farmers facing higher fertiliser bills and households that rely on kerosene heating oil. Together with tariff suspensions already introduced, households could save up to £21 on their food shop each year.
  • Rolling out hundreds more Post Office drop boxes, bringing the total to 1,000, making it easier and more convenient for people to send and return parcels without having to queue at a Post Office counter, helping take some of the hassle out of everyday errands in the run-up to Christmas. This comes alongside upgrades to 600 Post Office branches by the end of the financial year, improving services for customers across the country.

Carers Trust Chief Executive, Kirsty McHugh, said:

It is great news that the Government is acting to remove the Carer’s Allowance cliff edge. This has long been a concerning part of our benefits system, penalising thousands of carers who are juggling paid work with their caring role. Carers all over the country should now be able to take comfort that they will be able to earn that bit more without being inadvertently plunged into debt.

George Gabriel, co-founder of The Dad Shift said:

This paternity pay will make a real difference to tens of thousands of expecting families each year, giving self-employed dads a chance to show up for their loved ones at one of the moments that matters most. We hope more will be done through the government’s review of parental leave, but fair shout to the Chancellor for showing he gets it and for showing he respects the role these hard working blokes want to play as fathers.

Emily Holzhausen CBE, Director of Policy at Carers UK said:

We have been calling for a taper to the earnings limit and an end to the cliff edge on Carer’s Allowance for many years and we’re pleased that the Chancellor has committed to this next step. Our evidence from unpaid carers found many having to give up part-time paid work altogether or turning work down because they cannot risk going over the limit and losing 100% of their Carer’s Allowance.  Once introduced, it should also help to significantly reduce the number of overpayments related to earnings which carers have found devastating financially and emotionally.

Today will also mark the launch of a new Warm Homes loans scheme, giving homeowners across the UK, including Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, access to low-interest and interest-free finance to install clean energy technology including solar panels, batteries and heat pumps.

NOTES TO EDITORS:

Mileage rates:

The Government will lock in the biggest increase in mileage rates for 15 years, ensuring employees and self-employed people can continue to receive up to 55p per mile tax-free for the first 10,000 business miles they drive each year. Following a review, the government is also going further with the rate for those who drive over 10,000 miles also rising from 25p to 35p, supporting those who drive significant mileage for work. 

Around 3 million people are expected to benefit. The change means workers who rely on their vehicle for their job can receive greater support with the costs of fuel, servicing and other motoring expenses.  These changes will provide £120 a year in additional tax savings for a worker doing 6,000 business miles, with someone driving 15,000 business miles receiving up to £300 in additional tax savings.

Food tariffs:

Other products which are expected to see their tariffs cut include: 

  • Garlic (8% + £100 per 100 kg) 
  • Gherkins (12%) 
  • Citrus jams, marmalades and pastes (20% + £19 per 100 kg) 
  • Throat pastilles and cough drops (8%) 
  • Boiled sweets, filled or unfilled (8%) 
  • Toffees, caramels and similar sweets (8%) 
  • Plant-based beverages (soya, nut, cereal or seed) (8%) 
  • Chocolate-coated waffles/wafers (8%) 
  • Kerosene (4%) 
  • Fertilisers (between 2-6.5%) 

This is the second government-led cost-of-living tariff package this year, following an initial package introduced in June 2026 covering products including pasta, fruit juice and tuna.  Together, the two packages are expected to reduce consumer costs by approximately £245 million to £595 million a year. 

Separately, the government introduced a business-led package in July following applications from firms and is now extending existing business suspensions, while opening a new application window for further products. 

Post Office:

The rollout of self-service parcel Drop Boxes is already under way, with 500 set to be in place by the end of this year and 1,000 by the end of the financial year. In addition, 600 Post Office branches will benefit from upgrades by the end of the financial year.

On the Warm Homes loans scheme, government support will reduce the cost of borrowing, helping households spread the upfront cost of improvements that can deliver long-term savings. Installing a heat pump, battery and solar panels could cut energy bills by up to £550 a year, with further potential savings from a time-of-use tariff.

  This paternity pay will make a real difference to tens of thousands of expecting families each year, giving self-employed dads a chance to show up for their loved ones at one of the moments that matters most. We hope more will be done through the government’s review of parental leave, but fair shout to the Chancellor for showing he gets it and for showing he respects the role these hard working blokes want to play as fathers.


Emily Holzhausen CBE, Director of Policy at Carers UK said:


  We have been calling for a taper to the earnings limit and an end to the cliff edge on Carer’s Allowance for many years and we’re pleased that the Chancellor has committed to this next step. Our evidence from unpaid carers found many having to give up part-time paid work altogether or turning work down because they cannot risk going over the limit and losing 100% of their Carer’s Allowance.  Once introduced, it should also help to significantly reduce the number of overpayments related to earnings which carers have found devastating financially and emotionally.


Today will also mark the launch of a new Warm Homes loans scheme, giving homeowners across the UK, including Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, access to low-interest and interest-free finance to install clean energy technology including solar panels, batteries and heat pumps.

NOTES TO EDITORS:

Mileage rates:

The Government will lock in the biggest increase in mileage rates for 15 years, ensuring employees and self-employed people can continue to receive up to 55p per mile tax-free for the first 10,000 business miles they drive each year. Following a review, the government is also going further with the rate for those who drive over 10,000 miles also rising from 25p to 35p, supporting those who drive significant mileage for work. 

Around 3 million people are expected to benefit. The change means workers who rely on their vehicle for their job can receive greater support with the costs of fuel, servicing and other motoring expenses.  These changes will provide £120 a year in additional tax savings for a worker doing 6,000 business miles, with someone driving 15,000 business miles receiving up to £300 in additional tax savings.

Food tariffs:

Other products which are expected to see their tariffs cut include: 


  Garlic (8% + £100 per 100 kg) 
  Gherkins (12%) 
  Citrus jams, marmalades and pastes (20% + £19 per 100 kg) 
  Throat pastilles and cough drops (8%) 
  Boiled sweets, filled or unfilled (8%) 
  Toffees, caramels and similar sweets (8%) 
  Plant-based beverages (soya, nut, cereal or seed) (8%) 
  Chocolate-coated waffles/wafers (8%) 
  Kerosene (4%) 
  Fertilisers (between 2-6.5%) 


This is the second government-led cost-of-living tariff package this year, following an initial package introduced in June 2026 covering products including pasta, fruit juice and tuna.  Together, the two packages are expected to reduce consumer costs by approximately £245 million to £595 million a year. 

Separately, the government introduced a business-led package in July following applications from firms and is now extending existing business suspensions, while opening a new application window for further products. 

Post Office:

The rollout of self-service parcel Drop Boxes is already under way, with 500 set to be in place by the end of this year and 1,000 by the end of the financial year. In addition, 600 Post Office branches will benefit from upgrades by the end of the financial year.

On the Warm Homes loans scheme, government support will reduce the cost of borrowing, helping households spread the upfront cost of improvements that can deliver long-term savings. Installing a heat pump, battery and solar panels could cut energy bills by up to £550 a year, with further potential savings from a time-of-use tariff.

items.title: E5 Defence Ministers' Statement: 26 October 2026
items.summary: Our countries share the assessment that Russia represents the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability. Russia’s ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, on the one hand, and its continued violations of Alli
items.bodyHtml:
Our countries share the assessment that Russia represents the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability. Russia’s ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, on the one hand, and its continued violations of Allied airspace, acts of sabotage and growing use of multi-domain hybrid attacks, on the other, do not undermine our unity, solidarity and cohesion. On the contrary, they strengthen our determination to pursue the efforts already undertaken to safeguard the integrity and security of Allied territory, through a 360-degree approach that takes into account threats from all strategic directions.

We, the Defence Ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom (the Group of Five/E5), share a deep conviction: Europe must assume greater responsibility for its own security. We are determined to work in close coordination with the United States and all Allies in order to implement this concrete ambition. The United States is and will remain an indispensable Ally, and continued United States engagement in European security is essential to a strong and credible NATO.

This greater responsibility must begin with the empowerment of European Allies within NATO.

With the aim of building a stronger Europe within a stronger NATO, we are already taking concrete measures to implement the commitments taken in The Hague, emphasized in Ankara, and to meet agreed capability targets.

We will assume greater political and military leadership within the Alliance, modernising forces and capabilities, including through closer defence-industrial cooperation based on common and standardised requirements,. We reaffirm our commitment to further strengthening NATO’s collective defence in order to rapidly adapt to current and future challenges, including with a more proactive deterrence and defence posture.

We will bolster our contributions to enhance readiness, resilience and our ability to respond to evolving threats across all domains, by promoting the development of the necessary capabilities, in line with NATO-agreed priorities and targets, including through an appropriate, tailored and effective mix of complementary capabilities to meet the full range of operational requirements.

NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective security. The Group of Five/E5 will support greater European ability to act through different frameworks and initiatives, including the European Union, complementing the sovereign responsibilities of States and intergovernmental cooperation.

We emphasise the importance of a nation-led, coordinated approach, aligned with NATO. We commend the European Union’s efforts to support nations in meeting NATO’s defence capability requirements and in strengthening European defence readiness. The EU’s regulatory and financial capacity is a valuable tool in support of our nations’ efforts and ambition. EU defence initiatives should complement NATO, avoid duplication and remain open, under certain conditions, to meaningful cooperation with non-EU NATO Allies.

We will maintain our unwavering commitment to supporting Ukraine in its fight back against Russian aggression. Ukraine’s ability to defend itself now and in the future is critically important to Euro-Atlantic collective security.

We stress the need to keep supporting Ukraine by all available means — politically, militarily and financially.

We reaffirm our determination to continue tackling the activities of Russia’s shadow fleet, in accordance with international law and in coordination with relevant partners.

We stand united with Ukraine in its determination to secure a lasting peace, underpinned by robust security guarantees. The Coalition of the Willing will contribute to robust and credible security guarantees once a cease-fire or a peace agreement is in place.

items.title: Thousands of young people put down roots in agricultural careers at Jobs Fair
items.summary: More than 1,000 young people attended Norfolk’s first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair, learning the trades through welding and farming simulations. The fair brought together 65 employers and partners to provide opportunities for young people from
items.bodyHtml:
• More than 1,000 young people attended Norfolk’s first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair, learning the trades through welding and farming simulations.
  • The fair brought together 65 employers and partners to provide opportunities for young people from rural and countryside communities.
  • Jobs fairs are a part of Government’s wider youth employment support, backed by £2.5 billion investment to help young people build a strong career path.

At AgriFest, young people were given an opportunity to test out a range of agricultural professions through virtual reality welding simulations, HGV training, and a water irrigation network building exercise.

An additional ‘employability zone’ provided advice on looking for job opportunities, completing applications, interview preparation, giving them the confidence and skills they need to take the first step towards employment.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said:

Every young person deserves the chance to fulfil their potential, which is why we’re bringing jobs, training and support directly into communities.

I’m delighted to see businesses and local partners opening doors for hundreds of young people, offering not just interviews, but also mentorship and career advice.

Through the Youth Guarantee, we’re determined to give every young person the chance to earn or learn.

Youth Guarantee Jobs Fairs have already been delivered in Bristol, Glasgow, Cardiff, Nottingham and London. These events have resulted in over 1,000 young people already moving into jobs, work experience or training opportunities.

Influencer and Farmer, Farmer Will said:

I think giving young people the chance to meet employers and find out what opportunities are actually out there is really important. It can be hard to know what you want to do when you’re starting out, and sometimes you just need that first conversation or bit of encouragement to see what’s possible.

I’m really pleased to be supporting the Agrifest Jobs Fair. There are some great opportunities in agriculture and across the wider industry, and hopefully the event gives young people the confidence to take that first step and find something they really enjoy.

The event reinforced the government’s commitment that all young people under 25 should be offered one of the following high-quality pathways:

  • Employment

  • Continued education

  • An apprenticeship

  • A traineeship, a work experience placement or Sector-Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP)

This Jobs Fair is the latest example of the Government’s work to support young people into employment or training. The youth employment support package, backed by £2.5 billion investment, will support almost one million young people, and create 500,000 opportunities.

Over 65 employers and providers from across Norfolk attended the jobs fair, including:

items.bodyText:
More than 1,000 young people attended Norfolk’s first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair, learning the trades through welding and farming simulations.
    The fair brought together 65 employers and partners to provide opportunities for young people from rural and countryside communities.
    Jobs fairs are a part of Government’s wider youth employment support, backed by £2.5 billion investment to help young people build a strong career path.
  


At AgriFest, young people were given an opportunity to test out a range of agricultural professions through virtual reality welding simulations, HGV training, and a water irrigation network building exercise.

An additional ‘employability zone’ provided advice on looking for job opportunities, completing applications, interview preparation, giving them the confidence and skills they need to take the first step towards employment.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said:


  Every young person deserves the chance to fulfil their potential, which is why we’re bringing jobs, training and support directly into communities.



  I’m delighted to see businesses and local partners opening doors for hundreds of young people, offering not just interviews, but also mentorship and career advice.



  Through the Youth Guarantee, we’re determined to give every young person the chance to earn or learn.


Youth Guarantee Jobs Fairs have already been delivered in Bristol, Glasgow, Cardiff, Nottingham and London. These events have resulted in over 1,000 young people already moving into jobs, work experience or training opportunities.

Influencer and Farmer, Farmer Will said:


  I think giving young people the chance to meet employers and find out what opportunities are actually out there is really important. It can be hard to know what you want to do when you’re starting out, and sometimes you just need that first conversation or bit of encouragement to see what’s possible.



  I’m really pleased to be supporting the Agrifest Jobs Fair. There are some great opportunities in agriculture and across the wider industry, and hopefully the event gives young people the confidence to take that first step and find something they really enjoy.


The event reinforced the government’s commitment that all young people under 25 should be offered one of the following high-quality pathways:


  
    Employment
  
  
    Continued education
  
  
    An apprenticeship
  
  
    A traineeship, a work experience placement or Sector-Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP)
  


This Jobs Fair is the latest example of the Government’s work to support young people into employment or training. The youth employment support package, backed by £2.5 billion investment, will support almost one million young people, and create 500,000 opportunities.

items.title: Investigation launched as dispute risks bringing disability charity to a halt
items.summary: ADAPT (North East) was set up to improve the quality of life of people with sensory, physical and learning disabilities and those experiencing mental health problems, as well as their families and carers. The charity provides services inclu
items.bodyHtml:
ADAPT (North East) was set up to improve the quality of life of people with sensory, physical and learning disabilities and those experiencing mental health problems, as well as their families and carers. The charity provides services including community transport, social prescribing and wheelchair hire and is based in the North East of England. 

In July 2026, the Commission began assessing financial and governance concerns raised about the charity. This included allegations of significant payments being made without full approval of the trustee board. 

In September, the Commission opened a regulatory compliance case to examine concerns of possible misconduct and/or mismanagement further. 

During its regulatory engagement, the Commission quickly became aware of an internal dispute at the charity impacting its ability to operate and its trustees’ ability to engage as a collective with the regulator’s enquiries. 

The regulator is concerned about the potential impact the ongoing dispute, and any disruption it has caused, is likely to have on those who rely on its services and the charity’s staff. It is therefore escalating its engagement to a statutory inquiry to investigate the concerns further. 

Scope of the inquiry 

The inquiry will examine the extent to which the trustees, past and present, have complied and are able to comply with their legal duties in respect to the administration, governance and management of the charity, and in particular: 

  • whether the charity has a properly composed board of trustees who are willing and capable of managing it in accordance with its governing document 

  • the trustees’ decision making including whether there has been any unauthorised personal benefit and potential conflicts of interest 

  • the financial management of the charity including whether the charity has appropriate financial controls in place 

  • the potential impact on the charity’s beneficiaries at the current time 

The scope of the inquiry can be extended if additional regulatory issues emerge. 

It is the Commission’s policy, after it has concluded an inquiry, to publish a report detailing the issues examined, any action taken, and the inquiry’s outcomes. 

ENDS 

Notes to editors: 

  1. The Charity Commission is the independent, non-ministerial government department that registers and regulates charities in England and Wales. Its ambition is to be an expert regulator that is fair, balanced, and independent so that charity can thrive. This ambition will help to create and sustain an environment where charities further build public trust and ultimately fulfil their essential role in enhancing lives and strengthening society. Read further information about what the Commission does. 

  2. On 16 October 2026, the Charity Commission opened a statutory inquiry into the charity under section 46 of the Charities Act 2011 as a result of its regulatory concerns that there may be significant risk to charity property, the charity’s beneficiaries and to public trust and confidence in the sector. 

  3. A statutory inquiry is a legal power enabling the Commission to formally investigate matters of regulatory concern within a charity and to use protective powers for the benefit of the charity and its beneficiaries, assets, or reputation. Reports of previous inquiries are available on GOV.UK. 

  4. We also provide charities with guidance on what happens when the Commission opens an inquiry. 

  5. The Commission is not a mediation service, so cannot resolve trustee disputes. We can only get involved in a dispute in limited circumstances. For example, instances where all other methods to resolve the dispute (such as mediation) have been tried and failed or when the charity, its beneficiaries and/or public trust are put at risk as a result of the dispute. Our guidance can be found here: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/disagreements-and-disputes-in-charities.

Press office

Email pressenquiries@charitycommission.gov.uk

Out of hours press office contact number: 07785 748787

items.title: £12,000 fine for Cheltenham waste operator for disposal of diesel
items.summary: The operator of a waste site in Cheltenham has been issued a hefty £47,000 fine and costs after deliberately disposing of red diesel from one of its screening machines at its yard in Lower Slaughter in November 2022. J. Gilder Earthmoving a
items.bodyHtml:
The operator of a waste site in Cheltenham has been issued a hefty £47,000 fine and costs after deliberately disposing of red diesel from one of its screening machines at its yard in Lower Slaughter in November 2022.

J. Gilder Earthmoving and Aggregates Ltd appeared in Gloucester crown court on 5 October 2026, represented by its director, Joseph Gilder, to be sentenced for an offence of unlawfully discharging red diesel onto the ground on or before 17 November 2022. The company had already pleaded guilty to the charge at an earlier date.

In his remarks, judge Rupert Lowe said: 

The company had deliberately chosen to ignore the red diesel rules and then deliberately spilled the fuel.” He added: “There was no reason for this offence to be committed at all – it was a deliberate and blatant attempt to get round the law and obstruct those who care for the environment.

On 17 November 2022, there was an unannounced visit byHis Majesty’s Revenue and Customs to the site, to establish whether the company was still using illegal red diesel. Although the site was open for business, and Gilder was present, the inspectors were not initially allowed in. Instead, either Gilder or someone else acting on the company’s behalf emptied red diesel from a scalping screener - a separator for bulky construction waste - to avoid detection.

After being kept waiting for more than 2 hours, the HMRC officers were granted entry, after which they spotted 2 large puddles of red diesel on the ground. HMRC informed the Environment Agency, which visited the site and took soil samples to determine the extent of any ground contamination.

A spokesperson for the Environment Agency said:

J. Gilder Earthmoving & Aggregates Ltd deliberately caused pollution by pouring red diesel, which it was illegally using, onto the ground. It was a reckless act to avoid detection by HMRC.

Where we find evidence of illegal polluting activity, we will not hesitate to take enforcement action.

HMRC issued a fine for the unlawful use of red diesel, and the Environment Agency subsequently charged J. Gilder Earthmoving & Aggregates Ltd with environmental offences relating to the discharge of fuel onto the ground.

After the incident, the Environment Agency ensured that around 3.5 tonnes of the most contaminated soil was removed by the company from the site that reduced the ongoing effect of the spillage and the risk of seepage into the groundwater.

J. Gilder Earthmoving & Aggregates Ltd was fined £12,000, as well as being ordered to pay costs of £33,610.06 and a £2,000 statutory surcharge.

Background:

  • The Environment Agency’s 10-point plan is taking the fight against waste criminals up a gear. Specialist officers are acting earlier on larger sites, sharing more information with the public, making greater use of enforcement tools, and actively naming and shaming illegal waste sites.
  • The Environment Agency has secured almost 250 prosecutions for waste offences across England since 2023, with courts handing out fines of more than £2.2m and nearly 90 custodial or suspended prison sentences.
  • In 2024/25 alone, the Environment Agency closed 743 illegal waste sites over the country. Some 143 were high risk.
  • The Environment Agency’s economic crime unit has secured more than £1.5m in confiscation orders in recent years, along with freezing almost £21m through investigations into money laundering linked to waste crime.
  • 10-point plan: https://engageenvironmentagency.uk.engagementhq.com/waste-crime-stand-with-us-to-end-waste-crime

Contact us - journalists only:

Media enquiries: 0800 141 2743. E-mail: Communications_SE@environment-agency.gov.uk

items.title: Government unleashes £1.2 billion crackdown as part of anti-fraud drive
items.summary: First use of new anti-fraud powers to help identify claimants with undeclared savings or extended time spent overseas, saving taxpayers £1.2 billion by 2030/31. Banks will be asked to flag accounts where data suggests certain benefit eligib
items.bodyHtml:
• First use of new anti-fraud powers to help identify claimants with undeclared savings or extended time spent overseas, saving taxpayers £1.2 billion by 2030/31.
  • Banks will be asked to flag accounts where data suggests certain benefit eligibility rules may no longer be met.
  • Part of the Government’s wider plan to save £14.6 billion by tackling fraud, error and debt, alongside broader moves to put work and opportunity at the heart of a sustainable welfare system.

The Department for Work and Pensions has issued its first Eligibility Verification Notice, requiring banks to share information to help the department check someone’s benefit entitlement.

The Eligibility Verification Measure (EVM) - expected to save taxpayers £1.2 billion by 2030/31 - will ask banks to help identify claimants who may have undeclared savings or remain abroad longer than benefit rules allow, two major drivers of fraud and error.

The measures will help detect fraud, reduce incorrect payments and protect taxpayers’ money. They have been introduced as part of the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 and contribute to the Government’s wider drive to save the taxpayer £14.6 billion over the next five years.

They will also help identify incorrect payments sooner, ensuring people receive the support they are entitled to while reducing the risk of overpayments building up and claimants falling into avoidable debt.

The move marks a significant step forward in the Government’s drive to create a fairer welfare system by cracking down on fraud, reducing costly error and ensuring support is targeted at those who genuinely need it.

A wider package of reforms, set to be unveiled at the Budget, is expected to save the taxpayer a further £1.4 billion between 2027 and 2032. Measures include the deployment of 2000 additional anti-fraud specialists into Jobcentres nationwide, as well as tougher checks on Universal Credit claims abroad to tackle fraudsters who fail to report they have left the country to keep payments flowing. More broadly, the Budget will be built on fiscal stability, giving breathing space on the cost of living and the cost of doing business, and offering fresh hope for the future.

The government will also deliver further sustainable welfare reform following the Milburn and Timms reviews – both due in the Autumn - with the Government already acting to reform the social security system by investing record funding for employment support to help disabled people and those with long-term health conditions and rebalancing Universal Credit.

Minister for Innovation, Fraud and Debt Lilian Greenwood said:

Benefit fraudsters should be looking over their shoulder. These new powers will help us crack down on those who deliberately abuse the system, while ensuring people receive the right support at the right time.

We are not interested in where people do their weekly shop or how much they’re spending on new clothes. Banks will simply be asked to identify if somebody may no longer meet the rules for the benefits they receive, allowing us to investigate further where necessary.

With £1.2 billion in savings expected by 2030/31, this is a major step forward in tackling fraud and error, protecting public money and ensuring support goes to those who genuinely need it.

The powers do not give DWP access to people’s bank accounts, transactions or spending habits.

Instead, banks are asked only to check relevant benefit receiving accounts against certain eligibility rules for benefits and flag cases where further enquiries may be required.

A flag does not indicate fraud or wrongdoing, and no decision about a person’s benefit entitlement can be made on EVM information alone.

The measure will begin with a carefully managed test-and-learn phase and remain subject to independent oversight throughout before any wider rollout.

The Eligibility Verification Measure is one of a number of powers introduced through the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025, alongside strengthened debt recovery powers and new information-gathering powers to help prevent, detect and investigate fraud.

Together, the reforms form part of the Government’s wider plan to save £14.6 billion over the next five years while protecting the integrity of the welfare system and ensuring support reaches those who need it most.

It sits alongside broader Government action to bring down the benefits bill, help more people into work and create opportunity across every postcode, including through our £2.5 billion youth employment package.

Recent high-profile fraud cases include:

  • Colin Hegarty who falsely claimed more than £70,000 by saying he was single and was caught out by a Facebook photo proposing to his partner.

  • Bethany Elwood sentenced for £78k Universal Credit fraud after lying that she was single for over four years, despite living with her boyfriend.

  • Catherine Wieland was caught ziplining in Mexico and sentenced for £23k PIP fraud.

Additional Information:

  • The department may only issue an Eligibility Verification Notice to financial institutions in relation to Universal Credit, Pension Credit and Employment and Support Allowance.

  • It’s estimated that fraud and error from undeclared savings and time spent abroad in relation to Universal Credit and Pension Credit cost the taxpayer £1.5 billion in 2025-26 alone.

  • The Eligibility Verification Measure (EVM) has an accompanying statutory Code of Practice guidance, which sets out some of the safeguards that must be followed when exercising the powers.

  • The Code of Practice was subject to public consultation and is available on GOV.UK.

  • We are determined to tackle fraud and error in the system, with the 2025-26 estimate putting the overall rate at 3.2%, following the increase seen in 2020/21 .

  • More on the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 here.

  Benefit fraudsters should be looking over their shoulder. These new powers will help us crack down on those who deliberately abuse the system, while ensuring people receive the right support at the right time.



  We are not interested in where people do their weekly shop or how much they’re spending on new clothes. Banks will simply be asked to identify if somebody may no longer meet the rules for the benefits they receive, allowing us to investigate further where necessary.



  With £1.2 billion in savings expected by 2030/31, this is a major step forward in tackling fraud and error, protecting public money and ensuring support goes to those who genuinely need it.


The powers do not give DWP access to people’s bank accounts, transactions or spending habits.

Instead, banks are asked only to check relevant benefit receiving accounts against certain eligibility rules for benefits and flag cases where further enquiries may be required.

A flag does not indicate fraud or wrongdoing, and no decision about a person’s benefit entitlement can be made on EVM information alone.

The measure will begin with a carefully managed test-and-learn phase and remain subject to independent oversight throughout before any wider rollout.

The Eligibility Verification Measure is one of a number of powers introduced through the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025, alongside strengthened debt recovery powers and new information-gathering powers to help prevent, detect and investigate fraud.

Together, the reforms form part of the Government’s wider plan to save £14.6 billion over the next five years while protecting the integrity of the welfare system and ensuring support reaches those who need it most.

It sits alongside broader Government action to bring down the benefits bill, help more people into work and create opportunity across every postcode, including through our £2.5 billion youth employment package.

Recent high-profile fraud cases include:


  
    Colin Hegarty who falsely claimed more than £70,000 by saying he was single and was caught out by a Facebook photo proposing to his partner.
  
  
    Bethany Elwood sentenced for £78k Universal Credit fraud after lying that she was single for over four years, despite living with her boyfriend.
  
  
    Catherine Wieland was caught ziplining in Mexico and sentenced for £23k PIP fraud.
  


Additional Information:


  
    The department may only issue an Eligibility Verification Notice to financial institutions in relation to Universal Credit, Pension Credit and Employment and Support Allowance.
  
  
    It’s estimated that fraud and error from undeclared savings and time spent abroad in relation to Universal Credit and Pension Credit cost the taxpayer £1.5 billion in 2025-26 alone.
  
  
    The Eligibility Verification Measure (EVM) has an accompanying statutory Code of Practice guidance, which sets out some of the safeguards that must be followed when exercising the powers.
  
  
    The Code of Practice was subject to public consultation and is available on GOV.UK.
  
  
    We are determined to tackle fraud and error in the system, with the 2025-26 estimate putting the overall rate at 3.2%, following the increase seen in 2020/21 .
  
  
    More on the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 here.

items.title: Four million illegal cigarettes seized in Border Force crackdown
items.summary: Border Force officers have stubbed out criminals’ attempts to flood Britain’s streets with illegal cigarettes, seizing 4,884,001 cigarettes alongside 405kg of rolling tobacco, worth an estimated £2.59 million, in a 4-day crackdown at Manche
items.bodyHtml:
Border Force officers have stubbed out criminals’ attempts to flood Britain’s streets with illegal cigarettes, seizing 4,884,001 cigarettes alongside 405kg of rolling tobacco, worth an estimated £2.59 million, in a 4-day crackdown at Manchester Airport.  

Targeting high-risk flights, baggage and passengers, officers seized illegal cigarettes and tobacco, made 4 arrests, and denied entry to 23 people. Officers also seized 35kg of cannabis.  

In one case, a brazen smuggler was caught attempting to bring in 100,000 cigarettes, carried in 6 suitcases on a flight from Dubai. 

Smugglers tried everything from modified pillows to false-bottomed suitcases to sneak cigarettes past Border Force, with specialist detector dogs deployed alongside officers during the operation. 

Smugglers now face up to 7 years behind bars and airline bans.  

Where benefit claimants are involved, the Department for Work and Pensions will investigate and could strip them of their benefits where fraud is found. Following the operation, 26 people have been referred for further investigation. 

Foreign nationals will be denied entry and have their ETAs cancelled. 

The seized cigarettes and tobacco, worth an estimated street value of £2.59 million, will go up in smoke, keeping them off Britain’s high streets for good. 

Minister for Migration and Citizenship, Jo White MP, said: 

Tobacco smuggling is not just about a cut-price packet of cigarettes. It undercuts honest businesses and lines the pockets of organised criminals. 

Those who think they can profit from smuggling illegal cigarettes into Britain should think again. You will be caught, prosecuted, and put behind bars.

The crackdown builds on Border Force’s year-round fight against cigarette smuggling, targeting higher-risk flights to build intelligence on the criminal networks behind the trade. 

Last year, Border Force and HMRC seized 1.9 billion illicit cigarettes, resulting in 201 arrests, 134 charges and 83 convictions. 

Illegal cigarettes damage high streets and bankroll organised crime. Made outside the regulated market, counterfeit cigarettes come with no guarantee of what they contain or whether they meet safety standards. 

Border Force works with HMRC, the National Crime Agency, Trading Standards, local authorities and international partners to tackle the trade from the border to the high street.  

Retailers caught selling illegal cigarettes can face fines of up to £10,000. Last year, penalties topped more than £2 million.  

Adam Knight, Head of Border Force’s National Threat Response Team, said: 

Our officers work day in, day out to stop illegal cigarettes reaching Britain’s streets. 

Operations like this stop smugglers in their tracks and give us the intelligence to hunt down the criminal networks behind them. 

Criminals change their tactics, and so do we. Try to undermine our border and we will come after you.

items.title: London loft and extension company which left unfinished building work shut down
items.summary: Royal Lofts & Extensions Ltd left unfinished building work and took payments for goods that were not supplied. Payments were sent to the personal account of the sole director. The company was wound up by the High Court in London on 20 O
items.bodyHtml:
• Royal Lofts & Extensions Ltd left unfinished building work and took payments for goods that were not supplied. 

  • Payments were sent to the personal account of the sole director. 

  • The company was wound up by the High Court in London on 20 October.

A London loft and extension company has been shut down after an Insolvency Service investigation found it had failed to complete building work and took payments for goods that were not supplied to customers.  

Royal Loft & Extensions Ltd – registered in London and previously Essex – took thousands from customers but didn’t carry out the work as agreed, raising serious concerns about its trading practices. 

As well as the Insolvency Service, customers made complaints to Companies House, Action Fraud and Citizen’s Advice. 

In 2024, a customer paid £51,612 to a personal account of the company’s sole director Dean Marlowe. However, the customer alleged some of the work was only partially completed.  

Another customer told the investigation they paid £4,560 for bifold doors and windows, also in 2024, which were never supplied and that the company become uncontactable after receiving the payment.  

Investigators found that invoices sent to both customers directed payments to Mr Marlowe’s personal bank account rather than the company’s account. It has not been possible to establish how these payments were recorded in the company’s accounts. 

The was also no known valid insurance for work carried out between June and September 2024, despite assurances to customers about insurance. 

Neither Royal Loft & Extensions Ltd or Dean Marlowe responded to repeated attempts by investigators to contact them.

Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, Cheryl Lambert, said:

The allegations against this company raised serious concerns for our investigators.  

Customers put their trust in Royal Loft and Extensions Ltd to carry out extensive and expensive works that do not appear to have been completed, and any complaints seemingly ignored.  

It is in the public interest to shut down this company and ensure no further harm to customers can come from them.

Analysis of the company’s bank account identified receipts of approximately £224,596 and withdrawals of approximately the same amount, leaving a nil balance.  

Almost half of the money received was paid to or withdrawn by Marlowe or people sharing his surname within days. Investigators received no explanation for these payments. 

No accounting records were provided despite requests. This prevented investigators from establishing the full extent of the company’s trading and financial position. 

All enquiries concerning the affairs of Royal Lofts and Extensions Ltd should be made to the Official Receiver of the Public interest unit. Email PIU.OR@insolvency.gov.uk

Further information 

  • ROYAL LOFTS & EXTENSIONS LTD, company number 14865577, was incorporated on 12 May 2023. 

  • Its registered office is Shelton Street, London, WC2H 9JQ. 

  • Royal Lofts & Extensions Ltd was wound up in the public interest under section 124A of the Insolvency Act 1986 on 20 October 2026.

items.title: Statement from the Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan: one year on from the 26 October 2025 Atrocity in El Fasher
items.summary: One year ago, on 26 October 2025, the violence in and around El Fasher reached a devastating peak following months of siege and escalating attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Civilians were subjected to horrific atrocities including
items.bodyHtml:
One year ago, on 26 October 2025, the violence in and around El Fasher reached a devastating peak following months of siege and escalating attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Civilians were subjected to horrific atrocities including mass killings, ethnically motivated killings, summary executions, torture, disappearances, forced recruitment, arbitrary detentions, and widespread sexual and gender-based violence. Entire communities were forcibly displaced, and humanitarian access was obstructed, exacerbating hunger, insecurity, human suffering and deprivation.

Today, the Coalition for Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan stands together to remember and recognise the suffering of victims and survivors, and reaffirm our shared determination to prevent further atrocities and pursue accountability.

The findings of the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan have laid bare the scale and severity of violations of international humanitarian law and violations and abuses of international human rights law committed in and around El Fasher. The Coalition supports the UN Fact-Finding Mission and its work, and welcomes the recent renewal of its mandate. We also welcome the work of the African Union’s Fact-Finding Mission, and its collaboration with the UN.

One year on, many civilians continue to bear the consequences of these atrocities. Across Sudan, civilians continue to be victims of violence, including systemic and widespread use of sexual violence, displacement, attacks on civilian infrastructure and restrictions on humanitarian assistance. The growing use of drones in attacks affecting civilians, and civilian infrastructure is deepening humanitarian needs and protection risks. Taken together, this demonstrates that the risk of further large-scale atrocities in Sudan remains acute. Restrictions on humanitarian access and repeated attacks on humanitarian actors, local and frontline responders are unacceptable, and are compounding the suffering of millions of Sudanese civilians. This anniversary is a reminder that we must act collectively to prevent their repetition.

Justice and accountability are vital to achieving sustainable peace in Sudan. Victims and survivors deserve justice and accountability for the heinous crimes perpetrated during this conflict. Those responsible for serious violations and abuses must be investigated and held to account. The Coalition will continue working with Sudanese and international partners to support credible accountability processes, including the work of the International Criminal Court concerning Darfur, and meaningful transitional justice for the people of Sudan.

Sudanese human rights defenders and civil society organisations play a crucial role in supporting victims and survivors, documenting abuses, and ensuring that Sudanese perspectives help shape future accountability and justice efforts. Often working at great personal risk, they are indispensable partners in the pursuit of peace, justice and accountability.  Victims of conflict related sexual violence must have safe and confidential access to medical, psychosocial and legal support. 

There is no military solution to this conflict. The war must end. The Coalition calls on all parties to comply fully with international humanitarian law, including by protecting civilians and facilitating safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also call on all states to comply with international law, and use their influence to protect civilians, prevent further atrocities and help bring this devastating conflict to an end, including by ceasing to arm, finance and otherwise enable the war in Sudan, and by fully respecting UN sanctions including the arms embargo on Darfur.

One year after El Fasher, our message is clear: the victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible.

items.title: UK, Ukraine and Latvia extend crackdown on Russian grain theft
items.summary: The UK, Ukraine and Latvia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to extend the Grain Verification Scheme, building on the UK’s landmark 100-year partnership with Ukraine and strengthening international cooperation to support Ukrai
items.bodyHtml:
The UK, Ukraine and Latvia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to extend the Grain Verification Scheme, building on the UK’s landmark 100-year partnership with Ukraine and strengthening international cooperation to support Ukraine in responding to Russia’s illegal invasion. 

The scheme uses cutting-edge science to identify the geographic origin of grain, helping to track produce stolen from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. Latvia’s participation expands the international network of countries able to use the scheme, strengthening Baltic cooperation and supporting Ukraine’s efforts to address the theft of agricultural produce from occupied territories.  

The extension comes as Ukraine seeks support from European partners on the Baltic Sea to prevent grain of Russian origin from transiting through Baltic ports, amid ongoing disruption to legitimate grain exports through the Black Sea. 

Trade Minister Baroness Hayman this week signed the MoU with counterparts from Ukraine and Latvia, extending access to the scheme beyond Lithuania and Ukraine, which have used the Grain Verification Scheme since a first MoU was signed in January 2025. 

Defra Minister Baroness Hayman said:

The UK continues to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine against Russia’s illegal invasion.  

By extending the Grain Verification Scheme to Latvia, we are widening the net against those profiting from stolen Ukrainian grain and helping to protect the integrity of global food markets.

The Grain Verification Scheme was developed by the UK, on behalf of the G7, after Ukraine’s Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food asked for support in tracing grain stolen from territories under Russian control and sold on the international market. 

The scheme combines physical grain samples with machine learning, using established scientific techniques, including stable isotope ratio analysis and trace element analysis, to build a chemical “fingerprint” for grain samples.  

This is compared against a reference database of nearly 3,400 geolocated points across Ukraine and neighbouring countries, allowing an assessment of the likely origin of a grain sample. 

Since the Grain Verification Scheme was handed over to Ukraine and Lithuania in March 2025, Lithuania has established a legal framework for sampling and testing relevant grain consignments, and its authorities are now gathering and analysing samples.  

The UK will continue to work with Ukraine and Latvia on its future development and use.

items.title: UK sanctions senior commanders implicated in campaign of rape in Sudan and unveils new support for survivors
items.summary: UK unleashes sanctions against military commanders suspected of atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence, during fall of El Fasher. Survivors to receive further support while humanitarian aid is strengthened in El Obeid and No
items.bodyHtml:
• UK unleashes sanctions against military commanders suspected of atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence, during fall of El Fasher.
  • Survivors to receive further support while humanitarian aid is strengthened in El Obeid and North Darfur, as conflict and El Nino-induced drought threatens famine.
  • Action comes as UK-backed investigations expose campaign of deliberate starvation and sexual violence by all sides in the conflict.

One year after the fall of El Fasher, the UK is today bringing forward a new package of action designed to shine a spotlight on the horrific violence seen during the siege of the city - and help survivors rebuild their lives. 

15 senior commanders from both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been sanctioned for suspected atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence. This includes Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege of El Fasher, and Al-Nour Ahmed Adam (“Al-Qubba”), identified as present and playing a prominent role in besieging and attacking the city. 

The sanctions impose a travel ban and asset freeze on those designated, while further ensuring the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world. 

The announcement follows the release of UK-funded reporting by the Centre for Information Resilience (CIR), revealing a campaign of systematic starvation and conflict-related sexual violence against civilians in Sudan from both sides of the conflict.  

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: 

The war in Sudan has created a humanitarian catastrophe. 

A year on from the atrocities in El Fasher, UK-funded investigations have shown that rape and starvation are still being weaponised against the people of Sudan. 

These are crimes against our humanity - the perpetrators must be held accountable and support from all external backers to the warring parties must end.   

El-Nino may worsen an already desperate situation, but whether famine takes hold is in the hands of the RSF and SAF – they must stop attacking aid convoys and let food reach communities.” 

The UK is also allocating £5 million to support the survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Sudan. The funding will go towards a range of services and supplies for survivors, including sexual and reproductive healthcare, maternal health services, psychosocial support, and safe spaces for women and girls. 

A £10 million package will also be allocated to support the ongoing response to the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Sudan, against a backdrop of increased risk of famine driven by attacks on markets, health facilities, displacement camps and other infrastructure, obstruction of aid and El Nino-induced drought. 

It will help to improve access to clean water and sanitation in displacement sites around Tawila, reducing the risk of disease outbreaks, while supporting health, protection and other essential humanitarian services in El Obeid, where conflict and restrictions on humanitarian access have left civilians facing acute needs. 

One year ago, after an eighteen-month siege that starved hundreds of thousands of civilians, El Fasher fell to the Rapid Support Forces. In the days that followed, civilians were massacred, women and girls were subjected to horrific sexual violence, and entire communities were devastated. 

Now, one year later, further UK-supported CIR reporting has this week shown the brutal tactics used during the siege are still being deployed across Sudan. 

Siege tactics, drone attacks on civilian infrastructure and humanitarian operations, and the systematic obstruction of aid are all regularly used as weapons of war, with CIR-sourced footage showing RSF fighters discussing shutting off water supplies to El Fasher and preventing traders from bringing food into the city. 

Sexual violence is also rampant, with CIR reporting describing women and girls being abducted, repeatedly raped, and held in conditions amounting to sexual slavery. 

Today’s sanctions follow five previous rounds of UK sanctions related to Sudan’s conflict that have targeted suspected perpetrators in Sudan and the networks which support them.

Media enquiries

Email newsdesk@fcdo.gov.uk

Telephone 020 7008 3100

Email the FCDO Newsdesk (monitored 24 hours a day) in the first instance, and we will respond as soon as possible.
