items.title: Tyneside pizza boss jailed after gambling with money from £150,000 Covid loan fraud
items.summary: Matthew Temple obtained three £50,000 Bounce Back Loans for the same Whitley Bay pizza business More than £131,000 of the £150,000 was not used wholly for business purposes, including money spent on gambling and children’s toys Temple was j
items.bodyHtml:
• Matthew Temple obtained three £50,000 Bounce Back Loans for the same Whitley Bay pizza business  

  • More than £131,000 of the £150,000 was not used wholly for business purposes, including money spent on gambling and children’s toys  

  • Temple was jailed for two years after admitting three fraud offences

A Tyneside pizza company boss who fraudulently secured £150,000 in Covid loans before company funds were spent on gambling and children’s toys has been jailed. 

Matthew Temple obtained three £50,000 Bounce Back Loans for Pizza Cottage (Whitley Bay) Limited, which traded as Pizza Cottage on East Parade in Whitley Bay. 

The 44-year-old, known as Mehdi Ghaneh-Keisami when the offences were committed, secured all three loans in a little over a month during the pandemic. 

This was despite businesses being entitled to only one Bounce Back Loan. 

Temple, of Bank Court, North Shields, was jailed for two years when he appeared at Newcastle Crown Court on Friday 23 October. 

The Insolvency Service is seeking to recover the fraudulently obtained funds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002.

David Snasdell, Chief Investigator at the Insolvency Service, said:

Matthew Temple exploited a taxpayer-backed scheme designed to help businesses through the pandemic by obtaining three £50,000 loans when his company was entitled to only one. 

Company funds were then spent on gambling and even children’s toys and play equipment, despite Temple declaring the money would be used for the benefit of his business. 

Temple is now beginning a two-year prison sentence, but our work does not stop at securing a conviction. We are also seeking to recover the money he fraudulently obtained and return funds to the public purse.

Pizza Cottage (Whitley Bay) Limited was incorporated in June 2016 with Temple as its sole director. 

Temple secured the first £50,000 Bounce Back Loan in May 2020, shortly after the scheme launched. 

Just three days later, he applied for a second £50,000 loan, falsely declaring that it was the company’s only application under the scheme. 

Temple secured a third £50,000 loan the following month after again falsely declaring that it was the company’s only Bounce Back Loan application. 

He also declared that the money would be used to benefit his business. 

However, the Insolvency Service established that £131,419 of the £150,000 was not spent wholly for business purposes. 

This included £11,090 spent across 46 gambling transactions from one of Pizza Cottage’s business accounts over less than two weeks in July 2020. 

Investigators also found £264 was spent on children’s toys and play equipment on 7 May 2020, the day after the first £50,000 loan was paid into the company’s account. 

When questioned about obtaining a second Bounce Back Loan despite already receiving one, Temple told investigators:

I know it was my fault, I shouldn’t… I should tell them it was my second, but they didn’t check it either.

Temple pleaded guilty to three counts of fraud by false representation at North Tyneside Magistrates’ Court in September this year. 

He had previously been disqualified as a company director for 12 years in 2024 following civil investigations into his conduct by the Insolvency Service.

Further information  

  • Matthew Temple is of Bank Court, North Shields, Tyneside. His date of birth is 15 August 1982 

  • Pizza Cottage (Whitley Bay) Limited (company number 10247689) 

  • Directors can find information about their obligations and responsibilities at the Insolvency Service’s Director Information Hub 

  • Further information about the work of the Insolvency Service, and how to complain about financial misconduct.

About us 

The Insolvency Service is a government agency that helps to deliver economic confidence by supporting those in financial distress, tackling financial wrongdoing and maximising returns to creditors. 

The Insolvency Service is an executive agency, sponsored by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. 

Read more about what we do 

Press Office 

Journalists with enquiries can call the Insolvency Service Press Office on 0303 003 1743 or email press.office@insolvency.gov.uk (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm). 

Out of hours 

For any out of hours media enquiries, please contact the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) newsdesk on 020 7215 2000.

This was despite businesses being entitled to only one Bounce Back Loan. 

Temple, of Bank Court, North Shields, was jailed for two years when he appeared at Newcastle Crown Court on Friday 23 October. 

The Insolvency Service is seeking to recover the fraudulently obtained funds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002.

David Snasdell, Chief Investigator at the Insolvency Service, said:


  Matthew Temple exploited a taxpayer-backed scheme designed to help businesses through the pandemic by obtaining three £50,000 loans when his company was entitled to only one. 

  Company funds were then spent on gambling and even children’s toys and play equipment, despite Temple declaring the money would be used for the benefit of his business. 

  Temple is now beginning a two-year prison sentence, but our work does not stop at securing a conviction. We are also seeking to recover the money he fraudulently obtained and return funds to the public purse.


Pizza Cottage (Whitley Bay) Limited was incorporated in June 2016 with Temple as its sole director. 

Temple secured the first £50,000 Bounce Back Loan in May 2020, shortly after the scheme launched. 

Just three days later, he applied for a second £50,000 loan, falsely declaring that it was the company’s only application under the scheme. 

Temple secured a third £50,000 loan the following month after again falsely declaring that it was the company’s only Bounce Back Loan application. 

He also declared that the money would be used to benefit his business. 

However, the Insolvency Service established that £131,419 of the £150,000 was not spent wholly for business purposes. 

This included £11,090 spent across 46 gambling transactions from one of Pizza Cottage’s business accounts over less than two weeks in July 2020. 

Investigators also found £264 was spent on children’s toys and play equipment on 7 May 2020, the day after the first £50,000 loan was paid into the company’s account. 

When questioned about obtaining a second Bounce Back Loan despite already receiving one, Temple told investigators:


  I know it was my fault, I shouldn’t… I should tell them it was my second, but they didn’t check it either.


Temple pleaded guilty to three counts of fraud by false representation at North Tyneside Magistrates’ Court in September this year. 

He had previously been disqualified as a company director for 12 years in 2024 following civil investigations into his conduct by the Insolvency Service.

items.title: New plans to end carbon dioxide stunning of pigs to prevent suffering
items.summary: Pigs will be spared unnecessary pain and distress before slaughter under new government plans to phase out the use of high-concentration carbon dioxide stunning. New proposals set out today (26 October 2026) would see the pork industry move
items.bodyHtml:
Pigs will be spared unnecessary pain and distress before slaughter under new government plans to phase out the use of high-concentration carbon dioxide stunning. 

New proposals set out today (26 October 2026) would see the pork industry move towards more humane methods of stunning pigs, helping to prevent animals experiencing panic and breathing difficulties before losing consciousness. 

Pigs are highly sentient and intelligent animals, capable of experiencing pain and fear. Minimising distress during handling and slaughter is an important part of safeguarding their welfare. 

High concentration carbon dioxide is widely used to stun pigs in British slaughterhouses, but independent evidence has highlighted serious concerns about the suffering it causes animals. 

The government has now put forward proposals to replace the practice with more humane alternatives, such as argon gas and automated electrical stunning. Both methods are proven to substantially reduce animal suffering.  

The plans form part of the government’s world leading animal welfare strategy, which sets out ambitions to improve the lives of farmed animals and ensure they are treated humanely throughout their lives, and at slaughter.  

Farming Minister, Stephen Morgan said:  

We are a nation of animal lovers - pigs are intelligent animals that deserve to be treated with care and respect throughout their lives including at slaughter.  

The public want to know the meat they buy in the shops is produced in a way that supports high standards of animal welfare. These plans will help deliver that and reduce unnecessary suffering.

We are committed to supporting farmers and businesses make this transition which will bring long-term benefits.

Chair of the Animal Welfare Committee, Madeleine Campbell said:

It was the clear view of the Animal Welfare Committee  that the continued use of high concentration CO2 when more humane, legally permitted alternatives are available is ethically unacceptable.  The evidence-based argument for moving away from the use of high concentration CO2  on animal welfare grounds is incontrovertible.

I hope that all stakeholders will now work together to overcome the acknowledged challenges for industry which such a move presents and deliver that change within a transition period which is as short as possible.

The government has been working with pig processors, equipment manufacturers, gas suppliers and animal welfare organisations since April 2024 to examine the practicalities of introducing alternative measures and to ensure minimal impact of costs to consumers.  

The consultation launched today will seek views on the proposals, including the welfare benefits, costs, feasibility and potential timescales for moving away from carbon dioxide, recognising businesses will need time to adapt. 

The plans will also reduce the industry’s dependence on carbon dioxide supplies, which can be affected by international events. Concerns over potential shortages linked to conflict in the Middle East earlier this year highlighted the vulnerability of global gas supply chains.  

The consultation is open from today and runs until 21 December 2026.

items.summary: 年过七旬的邵继录站在下邵151号民居门前，抬头看了一眼门楼，新修的，但老砖上保留了青苔的痕迹，就像他小时候抬头望见的那样；前段时间几次台风影响，下大雨，“屋里一点没漏”。他告诉中青报·中青网记者，他现在就住在这栋父辈传下来的老房子里，“从小住到大，保留了很多回忆，我的根在这里，很有感情”。

items.title: PM confident every rough sleeper will have route off the street by Christmas as funding doubles
items.summary: Prime Minister sets out confidence that everyone sleeping rough will be offered route off the street before Christmas, backed by a further £432 million to sustain support beyond this winter New funding to be outlined funding to be confirmed
items.bodyHtml:
• Prime Minister sets out confidence that everyone sleeping rough will be offered route off the street before Christmas, backed by a further £432 million to sustain support beyond this winter

  • New funding to be outlined funding to be confirmed at the Budget on Wednesday, taking total investment behind the Prime Minister’s commitment to £874 million 

  • First-ever Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street brings together businesses, charities and local leaders to mobilise action, with major organisations pledging homes, jobs and practical support 

The Prime Minister today set out his confidence that everyone sleeping rough will be offered a route off the street or wider support before Christmas, as he announces a further £432 million to help deliver the ambition and sustain support for years to come. 

The additional funding, to be set out at the Budget later this week, reflects the Prime Minister’s determination to make tackling rough sleeping a national priority. It will extend support beyond March 2027 and through to the end of this Parliament, taking total investment behind his commitment to £874 million. 

It marks the next stage of the pledge the Prime Minister made on his first day in Downing Street: to stop accepting rough sleeping as a fact of life and unite the country behind a mission to end it. 

Urgent action is already under way, with specialist outreach teams and new bedspaces operating in Coventry, and further provision being rolled out in places including Plymouth and Camden over the coming weeks. Backed by the initial £442 million, the programme is focused on ensuring everyone who needs it is offered a route off the streets before Christmas. 

Today’s additional investment will ensure that support does not end when winter does, providing continuity for frontline services and helping people move into settled accommodation and rebuild their lives. 

But government cannot end rough sleeping alone. 

That is why the Prime Minister will today host the first-ever Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street, bringing together businesses, charities, housing providers and local leaders to mobilise the resources, expertise and commitment needed to deliver lasting change. 

Organisations attending the summit are making significant new commitments. The National Housing Federation will work with housing associations to identify at least 2,000 potential homes and bedspaces, including empty properties that could be brought back into use. Virgin Media O2 will provide practical digital support to frontline organisations, while L’Oréal Group will launch a pioneering Social Salon partnership with St Mungo’s and Haircuts4Homeless. 

Together, these commitments will help people access not just a safe place to stay, but the homes, employment opportunities and support they need to build a more secure future. 

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:   

“Rough sleeping isn’t a fact of life. It’s a thing governments either choose to accept or don’t.  

“Well I don’t accept it. That’s why we’re doubling funding so that people aren’t just offered a safe route off the streets this winter but have that same support right through the rest of this Parliament too.   

“But we can’t do it alone. If we’re going to end rough sleeping, we need every part of society behind us on this. So today we’re bringing together businesses, charities and local leaders in Downing Street to make sure this is a solution that lasts.”  

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:   

“No one should ever have to sleep rough, which is why we are doubling our investment to more people and providing a chance to break the cycle and end sleeping on the streets of our country – not just this Christmas, but for the years to come.”  

Secretary of State for Housing Angela Rayner said:   

“This is a big ambition – we know that. But we will not back down from making sure everyone has the offer of a route off the streets this Christmas. This summit is about bringing every part of society together behind that mission. Ending homelessness is not only a moral imperative – it will make our communities and our country better off.”  

“The first step is giving people a roof over their head and freedom from the nightly struggle to find somewhere safe to sleep. But Christmas is only the beginning and that’s why we will keep working together to tackle the root causes of homelessness and end rough sleeping for good.”  

Today’s Summit brings organisations from across society together to play their part, with new pledges including:  

  • National Housing Federation working with housing associations to identify at least 2000 potential homes and bedspaces, including empty homes for people moving off the streets, working closely with local authorities.  

  • Social Bite forming a new partnership with the government to expand its modular supported accommodation model, combining a settled home with intensive and community-based support.   

  • Salvation Army working with their housing association Salvation Army Homes and public-sector partners to develop social housing, modular accommodation and move-on options, including provision for people with complex needs for whom mainstream accommodation may not be suitable.  

  • UnLtd / Key Fund partnering with government to help social ventures create sustainable jobs for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.  

  • Virgin Media O2 providing new support around devices, data and connectivity, in partnership with charity Refuge, helping women and their children affected by domestic abuse and experiencing homelessness stay connected to services and support.  

  • IKEA combining direct funding, advocacy, employment programmes, community partnerships, and customer and public awareness-raising campaigns to tackle both the immediate impacts and underlying causes of homelessness.  

  • L’Oreal Group launching an innovative ‘Social Salon’ partnership in the UK with St Mungo’s andHaircuts4Homeless, supporting rough sleepers with wellbeing provision.  

  • Morrisons Foundation pledging to launch the Good Food Fund, providing £500,000 in grants to support communities to tackle food insecurity where it hits hardest, including supporting charities providing relief to people who are sleeping rough or at risk of homelessness, in support of the Prime Minister’s drive.   

  • ReGenerate launching a partnership with Liverpool City Region, in coordination with the Liverpool Mayor’s new Homelessness Taskforce, to find ways in which businesses can do even more to tackle homelessness such as through driving pathways into employment across the region  

  • Comic Relief committing further resources to tackle homelessness and housing insecurity, helping to raise public support and awareness in 2027.  

  • Landsec offering access to its screens at Piccadilly and others across its retail portfolio to amplify homelessness charities and causes nationwide.   

  • The Faith and Homelessness Collective, mobilising action across a group of 100+ church leaders and leaders of faith-inspired homelessness and housing organisations to support the PM’s instruction to offer everyone a route off the streets this winter and prevention in the long-term.  

  • Over 30 organisations and investors from the impact economy - representing billions of pounds - signalling support to the PM’s drive and working with Government to bring more investment into move-on homes, support the organisations that help people stay housed, open up jobs and training, and put more money into prevention.  

  • A coalition of philanthropic funders signalling their commitment to millions of pounds of investment into preventing homelessness, including a £10 million commitment from Julia Rausing Trust, and Henry Smith Foundation providing £500,000 of match funding with Birmingham City Council, to support Greater Change in providing relational support to rough sleepers in the city.

items.title: Joint Press Release on the R4 Ministerial Meeting in Istanbul
items.summary: The Foreign Ministers of the Republic of Türkiye, the Arab Republic of Egypt, the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (R4), as well as the Foreign Ministers of France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom met in I
items.bodyHtml:
The Foreign Ministers of the Republic of Türkiye, the Arab Republic of Egypt, the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (R4), as well as the Foreign Ministers of France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom met in Istanbul on 23 October 2026.

The Ministers discussed various issues of regional and international importance, namely the US/Israel-Iran conflict, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the need for a negotiated two-state solution, the appalling Houthi militia attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Government of Yemen, safety and freedom of navigation, escalated tension in Straits of Hormuz and Bab El Mandeb and the Black Sea. They expressed their commitment to continue contributing towards diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region and beyond, and addressing the security, economic and trade implications of these issues.

The Ministers agreed on the urgent need to address regional conflicts through dialogue, diplomacy and de-escalation. In accordance with the relevant UN Resolutions, they emphasized the need for finding lasting negotiated solutions to all outstanding conflicts.

The Ministers agreed to continue the dialogue in this format with a view to preventing conflicts and advancing peace and stability in the region.
items.bodyText:
The Foreign Ministers of the Republic of Türkiye, the Arab Republic of Egypt, the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (R4), as well as the Foreign Ministers of France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom met in Istanbul on 23 October 2026.

The Ministers discussed various issues of regional and international importance, namely the US/Israel-Iran conflict, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the need for a negotiated two-state solution, the appalling Houthi militia attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Government of Yemen, safety and freedom of navigation, escalated tension in Straits of Hormuz and Bab El Mandeb and the Black Sea. They expressed their commitment to continue contributing towards diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region and beyond, and addressing the security, economic and trade implications of these issues.

The Ministers agreed on the urgent need to address regional conflicts through dialogue, diplomacy and de-escalation. In accordance with the relevant UN Resolutions, they emphasized the need for finding lasting negotiated solutions to all outstanding conflicts.

The Ministers agreed to continue the dialogue in this format with a view to preventing conflicts and advancing peace and stability in the region.

items.title: UK-France deepen nuclear defence ties in first joint exercise
items.summary: For the first time, RAF Typhoon fighters have taken part in a French nuclear air exercise, flying alongside French Rafale in a show of allied strength. Exercise “Rummy” marks a major step forward in UK-France defence cooperation under the N
items.bodyHtml:
• For the first time, RAF Typhoon fighters have taken part in a French nuclear air exercise, flying alongside French Rafale in a show of allied strength.
  • Exercise “Rummy” marks a major step forward in UK-France defence cooperation under the Northwood Declaration.
  • This partnership is vital to protecting the UK and deterring threats in an increasingly complex security environment.

The UK’s defences are being strengthened as RAF Typhoon fighters join French Rafale jets in a French nuclear exercise for the first time.

Exercise “Rummy” saw British and French forces operate side by side over the Mediterranean, demonstrating the readiness and capability that help deter threats and keep the UK safe.

Launching from Saint-Dizier Air Base in France, French Rafale simulated a nuclear strike mission, escorted by RAF Typhoons.

Conducted under robust safety and security arrangements, the exercise did not involve nuclear weapons. The exercise focused on improving how our forces work together, ensuring that if the UK faces a serious threat, our military can respond quickly and effectively alongside our closest European ally.

This exercise shows the UK’s commitment to standing united against any threat, strengthening deterrence and protecting peace and security alongside European Allies to protect national security. As close NATO Allies and European nuclear powers, the UK and France play a vital role in the security of the Euro-Atlantic region. 

The exercise complements the work the UK is doing to invest £63 billion over the next four years to strengthen the UK’s nuclear deterrent, funding Dreadnought and SSN-AUKUS submarines, a new warhead and other vital nuclear work. The UK will also buy 12 F-35A aircraft and join NATO’s nuclear mission, delivering a more European NATO and reinforcing the UK’s contribution to collective defence.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said:

This exercise marks a new chapter in the defence nuclear relationship between the United Kingdom and France.

As Europe’s nuclear powers, we have a shared responsibility to contribute to the security and stability of the Euro-Atlantic region. This exercise demonstrates the depth of our partnership, the credibility of our deterrents and our determination to stand together in the face of emerging threats.

In an increasingly dangerous world, our adversaries should be in no doubt: the UK and France remain united in our commitment to European security and to maintaining the deterrence that has helped preserve peace for generations.

Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans Catherine Vautrin said:

Having independent nuclear forces does not exclude coordination. Our nuclear cooperation with the United Kingdom keeps deepening: on Tuesday night, UK Typhoons participated for the very first time to a French nuclear exercise alongside Rafales.

Through coordination, our nuclear forces demonstrate that they can contribute even more significantly to the overall security of the Alliance and to the peace and stability of the Euro Atlantic area.

Exercise “Rummy” represents a key milestone in the UK-France nuclear partnership and the programme of cooperation agreed under the Northwood Declaration.

Demonstrating the commitment of both nations to jointly deter common threats, the exercise showcases the depth of their bilateral nuclear defence relationship and proves that British and French forces are ready and able to operate together to protect shared interests and contribute to collective security in a period of heightened global instability.

The UK and France are close defence allies, underpinned by the refreshed Lancaster House Agreement between our two nations, expanding our joint deployable force, boosting our nuclear cooperation and developing the next generation of high-tech weapons.

Notes to Editors:

  • Operation Rummy took place from 20-21 October 2026.
  • Both the UK and France and retain sovereign, independent nuclear forces and national decision making.

items.title: PM call with President Kast of Chile: 23 October 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Chile, Jose Antonio Kast, today. The leaders began by outlining their shared ambitions to strengthen the two nations’ relationship including on defence, security, science and trade. On defence, t
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister spoke to the President of Chile, Jose Antonio Kast, today.

The leaders began by outlining their shared ambitions to strengthen the two nations’ relationship including on defence, security, science and trade. 

On defence, the leaders agreed on the need for the UK and Chile to work together to modernise defence capabilities.

The Prime Minister also raised the UK’s interests in ensuring the Falkland Islanders retain the ability to exercise the right of self-determination.

The two leaders discussed the growing cultural, scientific and people to people links between the two countries, and the positive impact this has had on investment and infrastructure opportunities. The leaders recognised the untapped trade opportunities between the two nations and agreed on the need for closer trading.

They both look forward to speaking again.

items.title: PM call with President Trump of the United States: 23 October 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister spoke to the President of the United States of America Donald Trump today. The Prime Minister underlined the importance for Ukraine to have full access to Starlink so they can continue to defend themselves against Russia’
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister spoke to the President of the United States of America Donald Trump today.

The Prime Minister underlined the importance for Ukraine to have full access to Starlink so they can continue to defend themselves against Russia’s full-scale invasion. The Prime Minister recognised the work of President Trump to bring Putin to the negotiation table and the leaders agreed to work together, alongside international partners to bring an end to the bloodshed.

Turning to energy, the leaders welcomed the continued collaboration between UK and US companies, especially on nuclear power.

The two leaders discussed the Energy Secretary’s decision to approve Jackdaw. The leaders agreed on the significant benefits this will bring to the UK, boosting the economy and supporting jobs for British workers.

Turning to the Falklands Islands, the leaders discussed the Sea Lion project. The Prime Minister raised the economic consequences of Argentina’s coercive measures for the UK and US and reiterated the importance of respecting the Islanders’ right to develop their natural resources.

The leaders also discussed the situation in the Middle East, with the Prime Minister reaffirming the UK’s support for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of hostile Houthi attacks.

The two leaders look forward to seeing each other soon.

items.title: UK-Oman joint statement on Omani State Visit
items.summary: UK–Oman Joint Statement During the State Visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, Sultan of Oman, to the United Kingdom as the guest of His Majesty The King on 20-22 October 2026, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirme
items.bodyHtml:
UK–Oman Joint Statement

During the State Visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, Sultan of Oman, to the United Kingdom as the guest of His Majesty The King on 20-22 October 2026, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed the enduring friendship between their two countries, reflected in the close relationship between His Majesty The King and His Majesty the Sultan, and agreed to build an ambitious, forward-looking partnership for the future.

At 10 Downing Street on 21 October, the Prime Minister Andy Burnham and His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik welcomed the depth, warmth and longevity of the relationship between the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman and agreed a set of priorities to shape cooperation in the years ahead. These priorities include modernising security, defence and national resilience cooperation; expanding trade and investment in green and advanced industries; working together on regional stability and global challenges; and strengthening ties between people and institutions.

His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales and His Highness Theyazin bin Haitham Al Said welcomed their roles in supporting the next generation of the relationship, including through joint patronage of the British Omani Society.

The UK Defence Secretary and the Omani Deputy Prime Minister for Defence Affairs also reaffirmed their commitment to the enduring UK–Oman defence partnership and its continued modernisation.

The UK Foreign Secretary and Foreign Minister of Oman continued their detailed discussions on bilateral affairs, covering matters of regional and global importance.

The UK Minister for Trade also held discussions with the Omani Minister of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion to discuss all steps needed to ensure the highly anticipated signing of the UK-Gulf Cooperation Council Free Trade Agreement.

The Omani Minister of Education also met with the CEO of the British Council to explore innovative approaches to integrating emerging technologies into education.

The UK-Oman partnership is rooted in historical friendship, sustained through resilience, and renewed through innovation. It is underpinned by the Comprehensive Agreement of Enduring Friendship and Bilateral Cooperation (2019) and the Joint Defence Agreement (2019), and delivered through the UK-Oman Ministerial Dialogue, Joint Defence Talks, and Strategic Advisory Group, among other bilateral fora.

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman commit to strengthen and deepen our relationship, monitor progress against agreed priorities, and ensure that cooperation remains focused on mutual benefit, Oman’s Vision 2040, the UK’s growth agenda, and the shared goal of building a more secure, prosperous and resilient world.

A Modern Security, Defence and Resilience Partnership

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed the central importance of their trusted defence partnership and their intent to deepen defence industrial cooperation, strengthen military-military cooperation, and increase focus on defence expertise, testing, innovation and future capability. The Saif Sareea exercise series remains a flagship expression of this relationship. Both countries welcomed preparations for Saif Sareea IV and agreed to explore the next phase of long-term exercise cooperation, including future capability development, testing and experimentation, and maritime security information exchange.

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman also agreed to deepen collaboration across security and national resilience and work more closely in several areas, including cyber security, to tackle shared international security challenges.

An Expanded Economic Partnership centred on Growth, Investment and Future Industries

The UK-Gulf Cooperation Council Free Trade Agreement will provide further opportunities to deepen trade and investment between the United Kingdom and Oman once signed and implemented. The UK-Oman Strategic Advisory Group will continue as the flagship dialogue for investment and growth, supporting knowledge exchange, structured innovation and delivery of shared economic objectives.

The Sovereign Partnership for Cooperation and Promotion of Investment will provide a focal point for long-term economic cooperation, strengthen links between the UK’s Office for Investment and the Oman Investment Authority and advance cooperation on green growth, advanced technologies, critical minerals, space, innovation, scale-up finance, industrial clusters and regional connectivity. It will prioritise sectors within the UK’s Modern Industrial Strategy and Oman’s future-industries ecosystem, using Omani industrial zones and innovation clusters as platforms for UK expertise, while supporting Oman’s economic diversification and its role as a gateway for regional growth.

Recognising green growth as a shared national priority, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman will advance cooperation on green industries and decarbonisation. UK Export Finance and the Oman Net Zero Centre also announced strengthened cooperation to support the sustainable, secure and responsible development of green and decarbonisation projects. The UK welcomed the proposed Oman Green Growth Roadshow delegation in 2027 to take these partnerships forward. Alongside this, UK Export Finance has increased its country limit for Oman by £1.6 billion, providing up to £7 billion of capacity to support UK exports to Oman. This will create greater capacity to support priority projects, deepen commercial ties and connect Omani opportunities with UK goods, services and expertise. Net Zero Industry Wales and the Oman Net Zero Centre will also launch a partnership to share knowledge and build links amongst industrial clusters, renewable energy sectors, academia and public bodies.

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman agreed to deepen cooperation in advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, data centres, critical minerals and space, through targeted roundtables, delegations and technical exchanges. They welcomed an agreement between the UK Space Agency and the Oman National Space Programme to share best practice, explore future cooperation on space launch, and promote commercial partnerships. They also welcomed the UK-Oman Innovation Initiative, regional innovation links, Growth Hub and Growth Fund mechanisms to help UK and Omani businesses grow, scale and access each other’s markets.

Joint Action and Leadership on Regional Stability, Climate and Global Challenges

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their shared commitment to peace, stability and dialogue in the Middle East and beyond, and agreed to strengthen cooperation on conflict prevention, peaceful resolution, humanitarian response and multilateral engagement. They reaffirmed their commitment to a two-state solution as the only viable basis for a just and lasting peace between Israel and Palestine. They also underscored the importance of adherence to international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, reaffirming in this context Oman’s sovereignty over Omani waters in the Strait of Hormuz and the importance of maintaining maritime security, freedom of navigation and the safe passage of international shipping in accordance with international law. To support this cooperation, they will develop joint work between His Majesty’s Diplomatic Service College and the Oman Diplomatic Academy.

The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their shared commitment to achieving Net Zero by 2050 and to demonstrating international leadership on climate, nature and environmental protection. Both countries recognised the importance of clean energy and resilient supply chains in supporting sustainable growth.

Connecting Our People, Institutions and Future Generations

The friendship between the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman has been built over generations by the sailors, soldiers, scientists, students, diplomats and communities who have connected our two countries, creating a deep generational trust between our peoples. The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman welcomed a package of announcements to build on this legacy and deepen links between their people and institutions for future generations, this includes closer cooperation on heritage, air connectivity and tourism, sport and the creative industries, and strengthen next generation and community links through the British Omani Society.

In education and skills, both sides welcomed the reopening of the Chevening Scholarship for the first time since 2021 as well as a British Council pilot on artificial intelligence assisted education in Omani schools, the new Oman Net Zero Centre-Cardiff University scholarships, and stronger links on skills and professional qualifications.

items.title: Joint ministerial statement on the risk of famine in Sudan
items.summary: Sudan is experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security. The risk of famine in the coming months, as warned by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, needs urgent action. There is no time to lose to save lives and p
items.bodyHtml:
Sudan is experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security. The risk of famine in the coming months, as warned by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, needs urgent action. There is no time to lose to save lives and prevent famine.  

An estimated 19.5 million people (41% of the country’s population) are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, including 5 million facing emergency levels of food insecurity. Without immediate action to reverse the current trajectory, the number of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition could exceed the projected 825,000. The number of food insecure areas, initially assessed at 14, is expected to double.  

Conflict is the key driver of Sudan’s hunger crisis, displacing millions of people, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting healthcare provision, food production, supply chains and markets. The situation is being exacerbated by systematic obstruction of aid and the effects of El Niño, which has resulted in reduced rainfall and increased drought across over half of Sudan.  

The parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of the Sudanese people. We urge the parties to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance, allow and facilitate full, safe, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access, and protect humanitarian personnel. Left unchecked, these impediments will hamper the ability of the humanitarian response to address famine risk. In practice, we call on the parties to: 

  • Authorise humanitarian operations through all crossline and cross-border routes, including air access into Darfur which will allow for the rapid deployment of aid operations and timely aid worker medical evacuations; 

  • Sustain presence and protection of humanitarian personnel throughout Sudan, including reducing delays for visas and customs clearance, increasing the duration of visas and travel permits and removing additional permits, taxations and other bureaucratic requirements slowing aid delivery; 

  • Refrain from strikes on civilian infrastructure, including agriculture and food systems, which are critical to the delivery of essential services to the civilian population.  

  • Strengthen civil-military coordination to ensure the safety of humanitarians and humanitarian sites. 

In the face of a potential famine, we call on all members of the international community to urgently scale up funding in response to increased needs and support efforts to ensure assistance reaches those most in need. We further encourage development and financial institutions to adapt their ongoing programmes to the food security situation and focus on the areas of greatest need. Together we must act without delay to avert famine by supporting the winter cropping season and strengthening locally led responses.  

We stand with the people of Sudan and humanitarian organisations who are working tirelessly and under extremely challenging conditions to provide life-saving assistance. 

Signatories: 

  • The Hon Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister for International Development of Australia 

  • Beate Meinl-Reisinger, Federal Minister for European and International Affairs of the Republic of Austria 

  • Minister Maxime Prévot, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, European Affairs and Development Cooperation, Belgium 

  • Mr. Hristo Dikanski, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Bulgaria 

  • Hon. Randeep Sarai, Secretary of State for International Development, Canada 

  • H.E. Mr Gordan Grlić Radman, Minister of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Croatia 

  • Petr Macinka, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic 

  • Mr. Lars Løkke Rasmussen, Minister for Foreign Affairs, Denmark 

  • Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management

items.bodyText:
Sudan is experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security. The risk of famine in the coming months, as warned by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, needs urgent action. There is no time to lose to save lives and prevent famine.  

An estimated 19.5 million people (41% of the country’s population) are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, including 5 million facing emergency levels of food insecurity. Without immediate action to reverse the current trajectory, the number of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition could exceed the projected 825,000. The number of food insecure areas, initially assessed at 14, is expected to double.  

Conflict is the key driver of Sudan’s hunger crisis, displacing millions of people, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting healthcare provision, food production, supply chains and markets. The situation is being exacerbated by systematic obstruction of aid and the effects of El Niño, which has resulted in reduced rainfall and increased drought across over half of Sudan.  

The parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of the Sudanese people. We urge the parties to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance, allow and facilitate full, safe, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access, and protect humanitarian personnel. Left unchecked, these impediments will hamper the ability of the humanitarian response to address famine risk. In practice, we call on the parties to: 


  
    Authorise humanitarian operations through all crossline and cross-border routes, including air access into Darfur which will allow for the rapid deployment of aid operations and timely aid worker medical evacuations; 
  
  
    Sustain presence and protection of humanitarian personnel throughout Sudan, including reducing delays for visas and customs clearance, increasing the duration of visas and travel permits and removing additional permits, taxations and other bureaucratic requirements slowing aid delivery; 
  
  
    Refrain from strikes on civilian infrastructure, including agriculture and food systems, which are critical to the delivery of essential services to the civilian population.  
  
  
    Strengthen civil-military coordination to ensure the safety of humanitarians and humanitarian sites. 
  


In the face of a potential famine, we call on all members of the international community to urgently scale up funding in response to increased needs and support efforts to ensure assistance reaches those most in need. We further encourage development and financial institutions to adapt their ongoing programmes to the food security situation and focus on the areas of greatest need. Together we must act without delay to avert famine by supporting the winter cropping season and strengthening locally led responses.  

We stand with the people of Sudan and humanitarian organisations who are working tirelessly and under extremely challenging conditions to provide life-saving assistance.

items.title: Thousands step forward in record magistrate recruitment drive
items.summary: More than 3,800 local champions recruited under this Government First-of-its-kind audio recording pilot launched in magistrates’ courts Part of Government’s plan to deliver a stronger justice system for victims Victims of crime will benefit
items.bodyHtml:
• More than 3,800 local champions recruited under this Government
  • First-of-its-kind audio recording pilot launched in magistrates’ courts
  • Part of Government’s plan to deliver a stronger justice system for victims

Victims of crime will benefit from a major boost to court capacity, with more than 3,800 new magistrates recruited under this Government to help get more cases heard.

In the first six months of 2026, almost 1,500 local justice champions have been appointed to serve their communities - almost double the number recruited in the same period the previous year - accelerating efforts to bolster capacity in the magistrates’ courts.

Aiming to build a magistracy that reflects modern Britain, recent statistics have shown women accounted for 55% of new appointments with more than a third of new recruits under the age of under 50.

It comes as the Government launched a £4 million recruitment campaign across national television and social media, encouraging the public to step forward and serve their communities and deliver justice, in a bid to deliver a 21,000-strong magistracy in 2028/29. 

The additional resource in the magistrates’ courts will boost capacity, get more cases heard and build a stronger justice system.

Minister for Courts and Legal Services, Sarah Sackman KC MP said:

A record number of people have answered the call to serve their communities as magistrates, marking a major milestone in our drive to strengthen justice. 

Magistrates are at the heart of local justice, and their commitment will help keep cases moving, ease pressure on our courts and ensure communities continue to get the justice they deserve.

Alongside the recruitment of more magistrates, the Government is testing new technology that will help transform audio recordings in the courtroom.

The technology will be piloted to create a robust and reliable record of proceedings in the magistrates’ courts, modernising the appeals process and freeing up valuable court time. 

Running across seven courtrooms nationwide, the courts will test the technology’s effectiveness and its potential to support a more streamlined court system. 

This work is part of the Government’s drive to modernise the court system and overhaul the appeals process by replacing the automatic right of appeal with a permission stage, allowing courts to decide whether a case should proceed. 

It’s work forms part of the Government’s response to Lord Leveson’s review of the Criminal Courts, which set out a blueprint for modernising the criminal courts and tackling the inherited Crown Court backlog. 

The Courts and Tribunals Bill was backed by overwhelming support in the House of Commons and entered the House of Lords on 14 October. The Government amended the Bill to remove proposals to limit jury trials, ensuring almost all Crown Court cases will continue to be heard by a jury.

items.title: Minister steps in to help save a prehistoric British battle-axe head from leaving the UK
items.summary: UK museums and institutions given the chance to save the 4,000-year-old Scarthingwell battle-axe head for the nation Museums and Galleries have until 22 December to save this prehistoric treasure for the nation The UK Government has placed
items.bodyHtml:
• UK museums and institutions given the chance to save the 4,000-year-old Scarthingwell battle-axe head for the nation 
  • Museums and Galleries have until 22 December to save this prehistoric treasure for the nation

The UK Government has placed a temporary export bar on the Scarthingwell battle-axe head, a rare survivor from prehistoric Britain, in the hope that a UK museum, gallery or institution can acquire it and secure it for public display.

The Scarthingwell battle-axe head is a rare and exceptionally well preserved example of prehistoric craftsmanship. Dating to the Bronze Age, it represents more than 6,000 years of polished stone working in Britain, beginning with the first axes associated with early farming communities. 

The temporary export ban gives museums and galleries time to raise the funds needed to acquire the battle-axe head, with the aim of keeping this important object in the UK and on public display. 

The battle-axe provides valuable insight into the role these objects played in expressing status, identity and changing ways of life in Neolithic and Bronze Age Britain. It also has significant research potential, offering future generations an opportunity to learn more about this period of our shared national history.

Heritage Minister, Baroness Twycross said: 

The Scarthingwell battle-axe head is an important part of the UK’s ancient story. Its outstanding craftsmanship and exceptional condition make it an object of national significance. Securing this piece of our archaeological heritage for the UK would ensure it can be protected, studied and shared with future generations.

Tim Pestell, RCEWA committee Member: 

In a profound period of change, the Early Bronze Age witnessed a society previously restricted to flint tool technology adopting metalwork. Despite this, battle axes became some of the most powerful symbolic objects, labelled by one scholar as ‘blunt instruments of power’. Made of stone rather than metal, they conveyed important social, sacred and political messages. 

This example, found in 1974 near Tadcaster in North Yorkshire, is exceptional for its preservation and highly developed aesthetic qualities. It uses a visually pleasing speckled diorite, while its finely polished surface and deeply waisted shape would have taken hundreds of hours to make – a crafting reflecting the importance it was once imbued with. Having been in this country for the last four thousand years, I sincerely hope that the export block placed on this wonderful battle axe will enable a museum to acquire and retain it on these shores for public benefit.

The Committee made its recommendation on the basis that the battle-axe met the first, second and third Waverley criteria for its outstanding connection with our history and national life, its outstanding aesthetic importance and its outstanding significance to the study of artefacts of this kind, regional context, production techniques and use. 

The decision on the export licence application for the battle-axe will be deferred for an initial period ending on 22 December 2026 inclusive in which we welcome expressions of interest from an appropriate purchaser to try and acquire the object. At the end of the first deferral period owners will have a consideration period of 15 Business Days to consider any offer(s) to purchase the battle-axe at the recommended price of £15,000. The second deferral period will commence following the signing of an Option Agreement and will last for three months. 

Notes to editors 

  1. Organisations or individuals interested in purchasing the battle-axe should contact the RCEWA on 02072680534 or rcewa@artscouncil.org.uk. 

  2. Details of the axe head are as follows: This is a ground, perforated and polished stone battle-axe with an elegant waisted profile and tear-drop plan, made of weather-altered diorite (an igneous rock type with an aesthetically pleasing speckled appearance). The perforation for the haft is slightly offset. Together with its other morphological features, this indicates that it belongs to Needham’s Class 2, dating to the earliest period of battle-axe production in Britain, c.2050 – 1850 BC (Needham forthcoming). Its condition is exceptionally good, and it shows little evidence of heavy plough scarring or rolling, suggesting that it had lain relatively undisturbed until the time of discovery. It has the following approx. measurements: Length: 120mm; Height (max.): 60mm; Height (min.): 40mm; Width: 50mm; Weight: 360g 

  3. Provenance: found in the winter of 1974 on the surface during agricultural work at Scarthingwell, near Tadcaster in North Yorkshire (NGR SE 49226 37367). It was reported to the British Museum’s Portable Antiquities Scheme (PAS) in 2012 (PAS unique ID: CORN-70CDC7) 

  4. The Reviewing Committee on the Export of Works of Art and Objects of Cultural Interest is an independent body, serviced by Arts Council England (ACE), which advises the Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport on whether a cultural object, intended for export, is of national importance under specified criteria.

items.title: New mental health pilot for young people supported by social care
items.summary: NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board has been selected as a pilot for a new mental health programme Care Together will cover up to 7,000 children and young people as well as their parents, carers, and/or guardians Mental health prof
items.bodyHtml:
• NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board has been selected as a pilot for a new mental health programme
  • Care Together will cover up to 7,000 children and young people as well as their parents, carers, and/or guardians
  • Mental health professionals from existing NHS services will be embedded in children’s social care teams, giving greater access to mental health support Children and young people supported by social care, and their families in Greater Manchester, will benefit from faster, simpler access to mental health and social care support under a new Government pilot.

Care Together will test and evaluate a new model of care, embedding mental health professionals from existing NHS services into children’s social care settings. The pilot aims to replace fragmented provision with faster access to expert, needs-led mental health support, including family therapy and support for parents and primary caregivers.

The Government is investing up to £9.4 million over three years in the Care Together pilot, which will be run by Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB), working with Stockport, Tameside, and Rochdale local authorities.

The pilot follows Professor Fonagy’s independent review into mental health conditions, ADHD and autism, which recommended better integrated mental health support.

The latest figures on children in need, children on protection plans, children in care, and care leavers, including adopted children, across the three participating local authority areas show up to 7,000 children and young people, as well as their parents, carers, and/or guardians, will be covered by the pilot.

By bringing social care and mental health professionals together in one team, children, young people, and their families will have faster access to support tailored to their needs, reducing the need to navigate multiple services.

Dame Diana Johnson, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety, said:

For too long, fragmented mental health services have left young people in care, care leavers, parents, carers, and guardians not knowing where to turn for support.

We are committed to change how we support young people, and this exciting and innovative pilot will see thousands more children across Greater Manchester get specialist mental health support based on their personal needs and in quicker time, before they reach crisis point.

Children’s Minister Josh MacAlister said: 

Every child deserves people in their corner, and we know that children supported by social care often face severe mental health challenges because of the trauma and adversity they have faced.

As well as this important pilot scheme we are expanding support for children leaving care, including through the national rollout of our Staying Close programme and corporate parenting duties for public bodies. We are also investing £2.4 billion in early, targeted intervention and reform to children’s social care to get families the help they need and keep them together wherever possible.

All of this is intended to help some of our most vulnerable young people feel supported into adult life and have enduring, loving relationships into the future.

The pilot is set to launch in early 2027 and run until 2029. An evaluation will be carried out during the pilot to assess the potential to scale the programme to other areas across the country.

Professor Manisha Kumar, Chief Clinical Officer at NHS Greater Manchester, said:

NHS Greater Manchester continues to make significant progress in transforming children and young people’s mental health services. Our focus remains on creating a system that provides support earlier, improves access, strengthens integration across services, and delivers better outcomes for children, young people, and their families. To this end, and as part of our wider transformation, we’re really pleased that NHS Greater Manchester has been chosen to pilot Care Together. Over the next three years we will work with partners in Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside to provide innovative support those children and families who are known to children’s social care.

We know that mental health outcomes are often impacted by a range of issues. Children who are known to social care have often experienced a range of adversity. By meeting needs earlier and in a joined-up way, we will provide trauma informed care and holistic support to ensure this vulnerable group have the right support at the right time. Bringing mental health professionals into social care teams will help us provide better support and learn what works for families here, and to help shape national changes.

This follows this government’s progress to improve children’s social care, including:

  • More widely we are reshaping children’s social care so more children can grow up in loving families and communities, backed by £2.4 billion through the Families First Partnership Programme and our commitment to create 10,000 new foster places this Parliament.
  • We have passed the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act which is transforming how public agencies safeguard children, work together and share information.
  • The Act also expands support for young people leaving the care system, including expanding Staying Close support up to the age of 25 to provide dedicated assistance with employment, housing, education and health.
  • We are funding a £500 million expansion of children’s homes delivering an increase in care placements in the right places to meet children’s needs while cracking down on excess profits and illegal, unregistered children’s homes.

items.title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40
items.bodyHtml:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg and are candidates for systemic therapy. 

Plaque psoriasis is an inflammatory condition that causes red, scaly and often itchy or painful patches of skin. It can affect areas including the scalp, genitals, hands and feet, as well as the nails. 

The MHRA’s approval was supported by data from four Phase 3 clinical trials involving 2,500 people with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, including 72 adolescents aged 12 to under 18 years weighing at least 40 kg. 

At week 16, all four studies demonstrated icotrokinra hydrochloride’s efficacy in treating moderate to severe plaque psoriasis when compared with placebo in the populations studied. 

Julian Beach, Executive Director, Operations, said: 

“Today’s authorisation provides another treatment option for patients living with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. 

“As with all newly authorised medicines, the safety of icotrokinra hydrochloride will continue to be closely monitored by the MHRA, and we encourage patients and healthcare professionals to report any suspected side effects through the Yellow Card scheme.” 

The medicine works by selectively binding to and blocking the IL-23 receptor. IL-23 is involved in inflammatory and immune responses and can contribute to the chronic inflammation associated with immune-mediated diseases such as psoriasis. 

Icotrokinra hydrochloride is taken as a 200mg tablet once a day. Patients should follow the instructions in the Patient Information Leaflet. 

Patients should always take medicines exactly as prescribed and speak to their doctor or pharmacist if they have questions about their treatment. 

Notes to editors 

  1. Authorisation for icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde)was granted on 23 October 2026 to Janssen-Cilag Limited. 

  2. More information can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristics and Patient Information leaflets which will be published on the MHRA Products website within 7 days of approval.    

  3. The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK.  All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks.    

  4. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care.    

  5. For media enquiries, please contact the newscentre@mhra.gov.uk, or call on 020 3080 7651.

items.title: More money reaching children than ever thanks to Child Maintenance Service
items.summary: Nearly 130,000 parents are now paying more than 90% of the child maintenance due, a record high and up 27% in a year. Newly-released figures also show number of parents paying nothing has fallen by almost 20% since March 2025. Government de
items.bodyHtml:
• Nearly 130,000 parents are now paying more than 90% of the child maintenance due, a record high and up 27% in a year.
  • Newly-released figures also show number of parents paying nothing has fallen by almost 20% since March 2025. 
  • Government determined to turn the tide on child poverty and improve life chances across every postcode.

New figures show thousands more parents are paying the child maintenance they owe as improvements to the CMS drive up compliance and improve customer service for families.

The data shows the majority of parents using the service’s Collect & Pay function - nearly 130,000 parents - are now paying more than 90% of the maintenance due, up by around 27% in the last year.

At the same time, the number of parents paying nothing has fallen by around 19% since March 2025, while CMS is supporting almost 1.6 million parents across Great Britain.

The figures come as the Government works to tackle child poverty and give every child the best start in life, with child maintenance arrangements helping keep around 120,000 children out of relative poverty and providing vital support with the everyday costs of raising a child.

Minister for Lords, Baroness Maeve Sherlock said: 

Our priority is simple - ensuring children get the support they are entitled to from both parents.

As we continue to modernise the Child Maintenance Service record numbers of parents are now paying their child maintenance arrangements, helping more money reach children and supporting families right across the country.

Most parents who use the CMS support their children without CMS having to enforce it but, where parents don’t meet their responsibilities, we will take action to ensure kids have food on their table and shoes on their feet.

Improving compliance also comes alongside a more modern and accessible service, with more parents choosing to manage their cases online, while those who need to contact CMS by phone are receiving faster responses and shorter waiting times.

The figures show significant improvements in customer service, with 85% of calls now answered, compared with 59% in summer 2024, while average waiting times have fallen from more than 28 minutes to just over 11 minutes.

Child maintenance plays a vital role in tackling child poverty, with the Government set to lift 550,000 children out of poverty in the final year of this Parliament, thanks to action including the lifting of the two-child benefit limit. This represents the largest reduction in child poverty since records began.

Additional Information:

  • Please find the new data here: Child Maintenance Service: data insights to March 2026 - GOV.UK
  • Figures used correct as of March 2026.
  • The management information covers customer interactions, digital services, compliance and enforcement activity within the Child Maintenance Service.
  • The number of Paying Parents who are due to pay via Collect & Pay, which was 243,000 at March 2026

items.title: 我国加强能源保供中长期合同管理
items.summary: 为加强能源产供储销体系建设，更好发挥中长期合同在能源保供中的基础性作用，国家发展改革委近日印发了《能源保供中长期合同管理办法(试行)》。《办法》将电煤、电力、天然气保供中长期合同纳入统一制度规范。明确了各方权利义务，科学确定了适用范围、保供责任、签约履约、监督管理等内容，有助于更好发挥能源保供中长期合同“稳定器”和“压舱石”作用，从制度上保障能源供应链的韧性与安全。《办法》将从2026年12月1日起施行。

items.title: Self Assessment deadline incoming – 100 days to go
items.summary: The Self Assessment tax return deadline for 2025 to 2026 tax year is 31 January 2027. People can file their tax returns via GOV.UK and beat the January rush. Support and guidance are available on GOV.UK for those need it. With 100 days to g
items.bodyHtml:
• The Self Assessment tax return deadline for 2025 to 2026 tax year is 31 January 2027.
  • People can file their tax returns via GOV.UK and beat the January rush.
  • Support and guidance are available on GOV.UK for those need it.

With 100 days to go until the deadline, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) is urging millions of Self Assessment customers to get ahead of the January rush and not put off completing their tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year.

Around 12 million people are expected to submit a tax return by 31 January 2027 and submitting tax returns early means customers can:

  • find out how much tax they owe before the deadline
  • give themselves more time to budget
  • get a refund quicker if they have paid too much tax
  • avoid penalties

Customers can complete and file their tax return for the 2025 to 2026 year on GOV.UK. If anyone is unsure about whether they need to complete Self Assessment, they can use the GOV.UK checker tool.

Myrtle Lloyd, HMRC’s Chief Customer Officer, said:

The Self Assessment deadline is 100 days away so now is the ideal time to get ahead and file your tax return early.

Guidance and support are available on GOV.UK to help you file your tax return. Just search ‘file my Self Assessment’ on GOV.UK to start yours today.

People who are new to Self Assessment must first register to receive their Unique Taxpayer Reference, which they will need when they complete and file their return. And anyone who needs to tell HMRC that they no longer need to submit a tax return can do so on GOV.UK.

There is a range of support and guidance available on GOV.UK, including:

  • help filling in the sections of your tax return
  • videos explaining how to complete your tax return
  • HMRC’s digital assistant which can answer common questions about Self Assessment

Self Assessment customers can also ask a tax agent, friend or family member, or a voluntary organisation to help them.

Those signed up to Making Tax Digital for Income Tax still need to submit their Self Assessment tax return in their usual way and pay any taxed owed by the 31 January 2027.

Self Assessment customers with a PAYE income can file online before 30 December and have any tax owed collected via their tax code.

Criminals often impersonate HMRC to steal money or personal information in someone else’s name. People should always take time to stop and think if the request is genuine before sharing personal information, never click on links in unexpected messages or share their HMRC sign-in details. Genuine HMRC contact details and advice on spotting scams can be found on GOV.UK by searching for ‘HMRC phishing and scams’.

Further Information

More information about Self Assessment.

The deadline for paper Self Assessment tax returns for the 2025 to 2026 tax year is 31 October 2026.

Customers who received the 2025 Winter Fuel Payment, or Pension Age Winter Heating Payments in Scotland, and are in Self Assessment, will see the Winter Fuel Payment pre-populated in their 2025 to 2026 online tax return where possible, and payment is due by 31 January 2027. Customers should check and add it manually if it is not shown. Paper filers will need to add it on their tax return. Customers with a total income over £35,000 will then pay the payment back through their Self Assessment tax bill.

For customers who pay their High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) through Self Assessment, around 300,000 will now have their or their partner’s Child Benefit payment details pre‑populated on their online Self Assessment tax return, making it easier for liable customers to complete an accurate tax return.

Some customers may be able to pay via the PAYE digital service, a simple and easy way to pay the charge monthly via their salary, which amends their tax code. For more information on the HICBC PAYE digital service go to GOV.UK.

UK cryptoasset owners need to pay Capital Gains Tax on gains made from cryptoassets above the £3,000 tax-free allowance and declare it in their Self Assessment tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year. More information about paying tax when selling cryptoassets can be found on GOV.UK.

items.title: Appointment of the Suffragan Bishop of Jarrow: 23 October 2026
items.summary: The King has approved the nomination of the Reverend Dr Jitesh Krisnakant Patel, MA, MPhys, PhD, Acting Director of St Mellitus College East Midlands and Associate Vicar at Holy Trinity Church, in the Diocese of Leicester, to the Suffragan
items.bodyHtml:
The King has approved the nomination of the Reverend Dr Jitesh Krisnakant Patel, MA, MPhys, PhD, Acting Director of St Mellitus College East Midlands and Associate Vicar at Holy Trinity Church, in the Diocese of Leicester, to the Suffragan See of Jarrow, in the Diocese of Durham, in succession to the Right Reverend Sarah Clark, MA, following her translation to the See of Ely.

Jitesh was educated at Jesus College, University of Oxford, and obtained his PhD through the Lambeth Research Degrees in Theology. He trained for ministry at Wycliffe Hall, Oxford. He served his title at Christ Church, Abingdon, in the Diocese of Oxford and, in 2011, he was ordained Priest. In 2015, Jitesh was appointed Associate Vicar at St Jude’s Church, Southsea, in the Diocese of Portsmouth. From 2018, Jitesh served as Diocesan Director of Contextual Training, additionally serving as Associate Vicar (Training & Development) at Holy Trinity Church, in the Diocese of Leicester. 

In 2019, Jitesh was appointed as Assistant Director and Lecturer in Theology at St Mellitus College East Midlands, alongside his role as Associate Vicar at Holy Trinity Church. Additionally, Jitesh currently serves on bishop’s council, on a national patronage board, as a board member of the 30K Project, and is an author.

Jitesh is married to Bridget, and they have two daughters.

items.title: Sue Sharp’s appointment as Interim Chair of the Disabled Persons Transport Advisory Committee (DPTAC) has been extended
items.summary: Sue will continue to lead the Disabled Persons Transport Advisory Committee (DPTAC) to provide advice to the Department for Transport aimed at ensuring disabled people can travel safely and independently across all modes of transport. She w
items.bodyHtml:
Sue will continue to lead the Disabled Persons Transport Advisory Committee (DPTAC) to provide advice to the Department for Transport aimed at ensuring disabled people can travel safely and independently across all modes of transport. 

She was formerly Chief Executive Officer of the Royal Society for Blind Children, has served on the Committee since 2017 and was previously DPTAC’s Deputy Chair. 

Sue’s appointment as Interim Chair has been extended until 31 October 2027, or until a permanent chair is named following completion of the public appointment process. This process is already underway. 

As this is an interim role, following consultation with the Commissioner for Public Appointments, she was appointed without competition.

Contact

Email: dptac.enquiries@dft.gov.uk

items.summary: 中新网10月23日电(记者 邵萌) 10月22日22时33分，西藏那曲市巴青县发生7.0级地震。记者从西藏气象部门了解到，预计未来三天，西藏那曲巴青震区及周边以多云天气为主，23日至24日部分时段有分散性阵雪；无明显降温，午后有8级左右大风。巴青岗切乡最低气温-9℃，最高气温4℃；玛如乡最低气温-5℃，最高气温5℃；贡日乡最低气温-9℃，最高气温3℃。未来三天震区气温较低，体感寒冷，建议做好救灾避灾和安置人员的防寒保暖工作。

items.title: 2025年中国创新指数比上年增长6.4%
items.summary: 根据国家统计局社科文司《中国创新指数研究》课题组测算，2025年中国创新指数为185.5(以2015年为100)，比上年增长6.4%[1]。分领域看，创新环境指数、创新投入指数、创新产出指数和创新成效指数分别为199.9、172.2、233.0和137.0，分别比上年增长7.5%、5.9%、8.0%和2.9%。结果显示，2025年中国创新指数呈现稳步增长态势，创新环境持续优化，发展新动能积聚壮大，科技创新能力持续提升，为经济高质量发展提供有力支撑。
