items.title: Military planes and helicopters to fight wildfires from the sky
items.summary: The RAF’s Chinook helicopters and A400M aircraft will be equipped so they can fight fires and are ready, when requested, to help crews across the UK battle blazes on remote moorland, steep hillsides and other hard-to-reach terrain. Firefigh
items.bodyHtml:
The RAF’s Chinook helicopters and A400M aircraft will be equipped so they can fight fires and are ready, when requested, to help crews across the UK battle blazes on remote moorland, steep hillsides and other hard-to-reach terrain.

Firefighters on the front line in England will be boosted by additional specialist wildfire teams and state of the art, wildfire-specific, light weight personal protective equipment, backed by up to £45million, meaning those who work tirelessly to protect others can stay also safe.  Unlike their current kit, which is primarily designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, this will be lighter and more breathable so firefighters can wear for longer periods when tackling wildfires.  

To stop these fires from happening to begin with, the government will invest more money to make landscapes more resilient. This includes £25 million to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they hold more water and act as natural firebreaks, as well as financial support for farmers to fireproof their land, through digging ponds and removing burnable materials in high-risk areas.

The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high.

The package comes ahead of today’s summit, where the Prime Minister will meet fire chiefs, local leaders and experts to make sure this summer’s scenes are never repeated.

The Prime Minister said:

I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything. I will never forget it. Our firefighters were heroes that day, but heroes shouldn’t have to fight with one hand tied behind their backs.

Crews will now have the kit they need to stay safe and military aircraft will stand ready to help tackle wildfires from the sky. We cannot put people through another summer like this one.

Communities Secretary Angela Rayner said:

The wildfires we’ve faced this year have been unrelenting, leaving a devastating impact on communities, homes and our precious countryside.

We’ve heard loud and clear from communities, experts and emergency services that more needs to be done. That’s why we’re taking immediate action now, while working across government and the sector to build a stronger, more resilient national response to wildfires for the future.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said:

As the threat of wildfires in the UK grows, defence will step up to provide greater support to our emergency services and protect military training areas across the country.

This will see the RAF’s Chinook helicopters and A400M aircraft equipped with new specialist firefighting equipment to enable them to tackle wildfires from the skies for the first time.

Other measures announced today include:

  • A new Wildfires AI Unit in COBR’s National Situation Centre, bringing together top universities, tech firms and government to spot and fight fires faster
  • Work with the Met Office on better wildfire forecasts and risks, helping improve public awareness and prevention.
  • To develop England’s first Wildfire Action Plan, covering prevention, preparedness, response and recovery
  • Closer work with the Devolved Governments to foster greater alignment, shared expertise and global best practice

This summer was the UK’s hottest on record, and the Met Office has found that climate change made the extreme heat around 130 times more likely.

Businesses including Airbus, Google and VodafoneThree will also attend today’s summit, setting out how technology from satellite monitoring and early warning to connectivity and aerial capability can help communities better prepare for and respond to wildfires.

As well as hosting today’s summit, the government will also convene an interministerial meeting between UK and devolved governments to better coordinate and strengthen the country’s response to wildfires across all corners of the UK. 

Today’s summit also comes after the government hosted the world’s first Climate and Nature Security Taskforce meeting for the first time last month. The Taskforce will establish the most significant climate and nature security risks facing the UK and shape government’s approach to tackling these challenges, ensuring Britain can best prepare itself for the climate crisis.   

Additional quotes

First Secretary of State, Louise Haigh, said:  

The UK has world-leading expertise in the application of new technologies to track and tackle wildfires. By bringing together the work of the National Situation Centre, leading academic institutions and our international partners, we are building a centre of excellence at the heart of government that will share best practice and strengthen our national preparedness.

Environment Secretary, Dame Angela Eagle said:

The wildfires that tore through our countryside this summer showed the urgent need to adapt to our changing climate.

Nature is our greatest ally in preventing wildfires starting in the first place, with healthy landscapes keeping more moisture in the ground to stop fires spreading.

That’s why we are stepping in and investing £25 million to restore peatlands as well as backing farmers to deliver natural fire safety measures on their land.

Minister for Climate Transition Katie White said:

Anyone who thinks climate change is a problem for our children and grandchildren, rather than here and now, should spend a shift with a firefighter. This summer, crews battled devastating wildfires in extreme heat, risking their lives to protect the places we love. The threat is already here, staring us in the face.

We can’t stop every wildfire, flood or storm, but we can make sure Britain is ready. This summit is about better equipping our brave emergency services, protecting our people, and building a stronger country, whatever the weather. 

Kata Escott, Managing Director, Airbus Defence and Space UK & Head of UK Public Affairs: 

Today’s Wildfire Summit is an important step toward strengthening wildfire preparedness and prevention in the UK. With our life saving capabilities, we are supporting the UK effort in the air, in the digital domain, and with our early warning assets in space.  

Nick Gliddon, Chief Business Officer, VodafoneThree:

Connectivity is critical to national resilience, helping communities access trusted information, emergency services coordinate and areas recover from disruption. At VodafoneThree, we combine resilient connectivity with network as a sensor technology, data, partnerships, and practical action to strengthen preparedness. Through our work with the National Emergencies Trust and National Parks UK, including a new wildfire resilience programme in the Cairngorms National Park, we are supporting local recovery and resilience to future fires. Bringing together connectivity, local expertise and long-term investment can help communities prepare, stay connected during emergencies and recover faster.

Further Information

  • The investment announced by the Prime Minister today will allow the Ministry of Defence to develop, for the first time, an aerial firefighting capability permanently based in the UK. In addition, civilian fire and rescue services across all four nations will continue to be able to request firefighting support through the Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA) process. 

  • The new Peatland Restoration Grant Scheme will be run by Natural England and is expected to run from April 2027 to April 2029, building on the successful Nature for Climate Peatland Grant Scheme. 

  • As the second largest landowner in the UK, the MOD requires an aerial firefighting capability to adapt to the increased risk of wildfires facing the country.

items.title: 直面山区百姓就医难题 浙江常山探索县域均衡健康服务路径
items.summary: 中新网杭州10月22日电(张煜欢)“就近享受优质高效的医疗服务，是山区群众普遍性的迫切需求。”22日，浙江省“十五五”卫生健康事业发展规划新闻发布会在浙江杭州举行。发布会上，浙江衢州市常山县委书记王永明直面山区海岛医疗均衡这一民生考题，介绍当地如何围绕人才培养、养老照护、普惠托育持续推进改革，让城乡百姓在家门口就近获得稳定优质的基本医疗卫生服务。

items.title: 利用酒店 Wi-Fi 发送约 48 万条钓鱼邮件，日本警方在酒店客房冰箱后发现隐藏电脑
items.summary: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据 TomsHardware 今日报道，日本兵库县警方 10 月 15 日逮捕了一对外国籍夫妇。两人涉嫌利用酒店 Wi-Fi 发送钓鱼邮件，并被指控盗用他人信用卡。 据日本《神户新闻》、朝日电视台等媒体报道，警方在涉案电脑中发现约 48 万条钓鱼邮件发送记录，以及约 240 万个电子邮件地址。 报道称，涉案男子于 2025 年 5 月 15 日涉嫌伪装成酒店住客，将一台电脑藏在神户市一家酒店客房的冰箱后方，并将其连接至酒店 Wi-Fi，然后冒…

items.summary: 中新网杭州10月22日电(鲍梦妮)10月22日，《杭州市河湖保护治理条例》(以下简称《条例》)新闻发布会在杭州召开。据发布会消息，《条例》已于9月22日经浙江省人大常委会批准，将于11月1日起施行，标志着杭州市河湖管护全面步入法治化、规范化的新阶段。

items.title: 极米记得 AI 记忆眼镜 G1 上架：轻至 17.9g，自动整理纪要
items.summary: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，极米记得 AI 记忆眼镜 G1 今日在京东等平台上架，价格信息暂未公布。 IT之家从商品页面获悉，该产品是全球首款钛金属 3D 打印 AI 记忆眼镜，轻至 17.9g；全天候 AI 录音，所有记忆，自动记录并整理；过往经历，随时回溯，基于用户个人记忆的 AI 对话，发生过的事它都知道；自动整理纪要、待办，到点轻轻提醒，无需刻意记录。 此外，该产品还支持原始音频用完即删，综合续航 2-5 天，短途差旅无需补电。按每天录音 8 小时计算，约可使用…

items.title: Social media campaign urges Brits to get vaccinated for winter
items.summary: Flu vaccination drive a key part of NHS winter preparations Social media campaigns and NHS App make booking easier than ever 10 million vaccinated and millions more encouraged to come forward for their free NHS flu vaccination The NHS is ur
items.bodyHtml:
• Flu vaccination drive a key part of NHS winter preparations
  • Social media campaigns and NHS App make booking easier than ever
  • 10 million vaccinated and millions more encouraged to come forward for their free NHS flu vaccination

The NHS is urging millions of people eligible for a free flu vaccine to help protect themselves, their families and ease the pressure on England’s health services this winter.

Data released today shows more than 10 million flu vaccinations have been delivered since bookings first opened in August and vaccinations began in September - including 2.7 million this week.

Appointments are available for the millions more who are still eligible for their free NHS flu vaccine as the government, NHS and the UKHSA work together on new and exciting ways to encourage more people to come forward.

The government has launched a social media campaign running across Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, and - for the first time – TikTok and is also promoting a new feature on the NHS App which helps people check their eligibility and book their flu vaccination at a community pharmacy.

The  ‘Manage a Vaccination in School’ (MAVIS) programme – which streamlines school-age immunisation programmes - has also been accelerated to cover 14,000 schools this year.

In a further effort to see more kids vaccinated against the flu, later this year the government will launch the first ever ‘catch-up’ programme from community pharmacies for school children who missed their vaccinations earlier in the year. 

Making sure all those eligible, especially the most vulnerable, take up their flu vaccine is a key part of ensuring the health service prepares for one of our most challenging winters.

Health Minister James Frith said:

Vaccines save lives. It has never been easier to find out if you are eligible and get vaccinated, helping protect yourself and reduce pressure on the NHS during the winter season.

Eligibility is focused on those most vulnerable - from young children to older adults and people with long-term health conditions - so if you are eligible, please come forward this winter.

Flu is not just a bad cold. It can cause serious complications, hospital treatment and death, particularly for those most at risk including young children, pregnant women, older people, and people with certain long-term conditions.

Vaccination remains one of the best defences, helping prevent serious illness and avoidable admissions.

Dr Amanda Doyle, NHS National Director for Primary Care and Community Services, said:

It’s easier than ever for anyone who is eligible to come forward and get their flu vaccine, whether it’s at a GP surgery, high street pharmacy, community pop up clinic or at school, and it’s one of the best things you can do to protect yourself and your family ahead of winter.

The NHS app is a fantastic and quick way to book, or you can contact your GP or find a pharmacy near you.

If you’re a parent, we’re making it easier to consent to your child being vaccinated in school with new digital forms.

We are expecting this winter to be tough, but flu vaccines are a vital way for you to avoid becoming really ill and hospitalised, so please do book your flu jab as soon as possible.

UKHSA estimates that flu vaccination prevented around 100,000 hospitalisations and 7,000 deaths in England in the last year. 

Chief Medical Officer Professor Chris Whitty said:

Flu can be a serious illness for vulnerable people, and life-threatening for some. It is important that those eligible for free NHS flu vaccines get vaccinated. 

Frontline health workers have a professional responsibility to protect their patients and this includes getting vaccinated against transmissible diseases.

The latest cold mortality report out today shows 2,200 deaths were associated with cold weather which poses a serious risk to health, particularly for people who are more vulnerable because of their age, health, or living circumstances. Vaccines are a way to help protect yourself.

Dr Agostinho Sousa, Head of Extreme Events and Health Protection at UKHSA, said:

Cold weather poses a serious risk to health, particularly for people who are more vulnerable because of their age, health, or living circumstances. Our cold weather mortality report shows that around 2,200 people died as a result of very low temperatures last winter.

While this estimate of cold-associated deaths is lower than we saw during the previous winter, these figures show that even short periods of cold weather can have serious effects on health and can lead to increased deaths in the days and weeks that follow.

As we head into winter, it is important that everyone takes simple steps to protect themselves and others. This includes keeping parts of our homes warm, checking in on friends, family and neighbours that are most vulnerable, and following weather forecasts and public health advice during cold weather.

The department is also working with key charities to support people with long-term conditions to further strengthen this vaccination drive. British Heart Foundation, Parkinsons UK, Asthma + Lung UK, Diabetes UK, Macmillan Cancer Support, Stroke Association, Cystic Fibrosis Trust, National Kidney Federation and MS Society are the confirmed signatories to a joint open letter encouraging eligible people to get better protected.

Dr Charmaine Griffiths, Chief Executive at British Heart Foundation, said:

Flu can be dangerous for people living with heart and circulatory conditions. People who have had a heart attack are at greater risk of having another if they catch flu, and it can also make conditions like heart failure much worse.

Getting your flu vaccine takes just five minutes, but it could help protect you from serious health complications this winter. It also helps reduce pressure on the NHS at one of the busiest times of year. Please do not put it off - book your vaccine as soon as you can.

Emily Holzhausen CBE, Director of Policy and Public Affairs at Carers UK, said:

If you look after a disabled or older person, who may be put at risk if you become ill, you are entitled to a free flu jab. You should be able to request this from your GP surgery or local pharmacist. We want unpaid carers to be aware of their eligibility and make sure that they don’t miss out on an important way to protect themselves and the person they care for this winter.

Professor Victoria Tzortziou Brown, President of the Royal College of GPs, said: 

As winter approaches, GPs and our teams are already seeing patients with flu. While for most people flu will be unpleasant, for those in at-risk groups, it can be really serious, so taking steps to stay safe over the coming months is incredibly important. 

Flu vaccination is safe and offers the best protection against serious illness. Getting a flu jab not only protects vulnerable patients from serious illness, it also helps reduce the spread of flu in our communities. That is why we encourage all eligible patients who have been invited for their vaccination to contact their GP or book an appointment through the NHS Flu Vaccination Service.

Sarah Sleet, Chief Executive at Asthma + Lung UK, said:

For nearly 12 million people in the UK living with a lung condition, winter can be a frightening time. For them flu is far more than just a few days in bed. It can trigger serious and potentially life-threatening flare-ups leading to emergency hospital admissions. 

Last winter, fewer than half of people under the age of 65 with chronic respiratory disease had the flu vaccine, despite being seven times more likely to die from flu.

Everyone eligible for a vaccine should take up the offer, giving themselves the best protection this winter, because when breathing is hard, nothing is easy.

David Newbold, Director of Community at Parkinson’s UK, said:

People with Parkinson’s, especially those with advanced Parkinson’s, can be more vulnerable to chest infections. As we head into winter, we encourage everyone with the condition to take up the vaccinations they’re eligible for to help protect themselves.

People recently diagnosed or under 65 may not realise they’re eligible, so it’s really important they know to ask for the vaccination. Getting vaccinated can help protect you and your loved ones, giving you greater peace of mind and helping you to continue living well with Parkinson’s.

Douglas Twenefour, Head of Clinical at Diabetes UK said:

The flu can pose significant risk for people with diabetes, causing complications that leave them vulnerable to serious illness.

Rising blood sugar levels are natural when someone with diabetes has an infection, but serious infections such as flu can cause blood sugar levels to rise dangerously high.

With winter approaching, the flu vaccine provides the best protection for people with diabetes to stay safe from the virus.

Anthony Cunliffe, Lead Medical Adviser at Macmillan Cancer Support, said: 

Flu can be much more serious for people living with cancer, particularly for those whose immune system may be weakened by their cancer or treatment. Getting vaccinated against flu is one of the important steps people can take to help protect themselves during the winter months.

We encourage anyone living with cancer to take up the opportunity for a flu vaccine and speak to their healthcare team if they have any questions about when or how they should have their vaccination. It’s also important that people who care for someone with cancer check whether they are eligible for vaccination too.

Winter can be an especially worrying time for people living with cancer, but taking simple steps such as getting vaccinated can help people feel better prepared and protected.

Janet Morrison OBE, Chief Executive of Community Pharmacy England, said:

Community pharmacies are making it easier for people to protect themselves and their loved ones this winter. Sitting at the heart of local communities, they offer convenient and trusted provision of NHS flu and Covid vaccinations.

Vaccination remains one of the best ways to prevent serious illness and ease pressure on the NHS. Community pharmacists have long vaccinated adults against flu and can now also vaccinate eligible children, as well as offering Covid boosters for the most vulnerable. So if you’re eligible, pop into your local pharmacy or book online today.

Peter Lloyd, Senior Policy Manager at the MS Society, said:

We encourage everyone with MS to consider getting a free flu jab this winter. MS is debilitating, exhausting and unpredictable, and becoming ill with the flu can make MS symptoms worse. It might even trigger an MS relapse. The flu jab can protect people from the worst effects of the most common type of flu that’s around this year, and your main carer can also get it for free.

Andrea Brown, Chief Executive, National Kidney Federation, said:

At the NKF, we hear from people living with kidney disease every day, and we understand how worrying the winter months can be. Getting vaccinated before winter can help protect against severe illness and reduce the severity of symptoms and the risk of hospitalisation if you catch flu. We would encourage everyone who is eligible for the vaccines to take up the offer.

David Ramsden, Chief Executive, Cystic Fibrosis Trust, said:

Flu vaccinations are an essential part of reducing the risk that people with cystic fibrosis get seriously ill. I encourage everyone to get their flu jab to support people with CF to remain as well as possible this winter.

John James OBE, Chief Executive, Sickle Cell Society, said:

We urge everyone living with sickle cell disorder to take up their free NHS flu vaccination this winter. People living with the condition already face significant challenges in managing their health, and the cold winter months can make this harder. Flu can also bring serious illness and hospitalisation. The impact can be considerable, both for the person affected and for the family supporting them.

Having the flu vaccine is an important step people can take to help protect themselves against serious illness this winter, and we urge everyone affected to use one of the simple routes to getting an appointment booked.

Juliet Bouverie OBE, CEO of the Stroke Association, said:

There are 1.4 million stroke survivors in the UK today, and protecting their health from infections such as flu is particularly important. Flu can cause serious illness and complications, especially for people living with other health conditions, including high blood pressure. 

We know that flu places additional strain on the body, and research has shown that influenza infection is associated with a temporary increase in the risk of having a first or further stroke. 

Stroke can have a life-changing impact on survivors and their families, and the number of people experiencing a stroke is rising. Getting vaccinated against flu is a simple and effective way to reduce the risk of illness and its complications. We encourage everyone who is eligible, including stroke survivors, to take up their flu vaccination and help protect themselves and those around them this winter.

To help drive uptake for those eligible, there are more opportunities to get a vaccine than ever before. These include:

  • School teams have been asked to visit every school by the end of November, with second visits completed by 11 December. Parents can help by returning consent forms promptly and vaccinating children helps protect them, reduce flu spreading to others and limit disruption to learning.
  • Participating pharmacies offer vaccination to two- and three-year-olds and children aged two to 17 in clinical risk groups. School-age pharmacy catch-up starts on 1 December.
  • NHS teams are taking vaccines into pharmacies, schools, maternity services, care homes, pop-up clinics and mobile vans. Outreach teams and charity partners are reaching people sleeping rough or using homeless hostels and night shelters, so they are not left behind. Pregnant women can ask their maternity team, GP or pharmacist, following earlier pharmacy booking access this year.

Adults aged 65 and older, those with long term conditions, pregnant women and those with caring roles are just some of the people who are eligible for a free NHS flu vaccination. Those eligible can book through the NHS website or App, 119, a person’s GP or a participating walk-in pharmacy.

We would encourage everyone who is eligible for the vaccines to take up the offer.


David Ramsden, Chief Executive, Cystic Fibrosis Trust, said:


  Flu vaccinations are an essential part of reducing the risk that people with cystic fibrosis get seriously ill. I encourage everyone to get their flu jab to support people with CF to remain as well as possible this winter.


John James OBE, Chief Executive, Sickle Cell Society, said:


  We urge everyone living with sickle cell disorder to take up their free NHS flu vaccination this winter. People living with the condition already face significant challenges in managing their health, and the cold winter months can make this harder. Flu can also bring serious illness and hospitalisation. The impact can be considerable, both for the person affected and for the family supporting them.

  Having the flu vaccine is an important step people can take to help protect themselves against serious illness this winter, and we urge everyone affected to use one of the simple routes to getting an appointment booked.


Juliet Bouverie OBE, CEO of the Stroke Association, said:


  There are 1.4 million stroke survivors in the UK today, and protecting their health from infections such as flu is particularly important. Flu can cause serious illness and complications, especially for people living with other health conditions, including high blood pressure. 

  We know that flu places additional strain on the body, and research has shown that influenza infection is associated with a temporary increase in the risk of having a first or further stroke. 

  Stroke can have a life-changing impact on survivors and their families, and the number of people experiencing a stroke is rising. Getting vaccinated against flu is a simple and effective way to reduce the risk of illness and its complications. We encourage everyone who is eligible, including stroke survivors, to take up their flu vaccination and help protect themselves and those around them this winter.


To help drive uptake for those eligible, there are more opportunities to get a vaccine than ever before. These include:


  School teams have been asked to visit every school by the end of November, with second visits completed by 11 December. Parents can help by returning consent forms promptly and vaccinating children helps protect them, reduce flu spreading to others and limit disruption to learning.
  Participating pharmacies offer vaccination to two- and three-year-olds and children aged two to 17 in clinical risk groups. School-age pharmacy catch-up starts on 1 December.
  NHS teams are taking vaccines into pharmacies, schools, maternity services, care homes, pop-up clinics and mobile vans. Outreach teams and charity partners are reaching people sleeping rough or using homeless hostels and night shelters, so they are not left behind. Pregnant women can ask their maternity team, GP or pharmacist, following earlier pharmacy booking access this year.


Adults aged 65 and older, those with long term conditions, pregnant women and those with caring roles are just some of the people who are eligible for a free NHS flu vaccination. Those eligible can book through the NHS website or App, 119, a person’s GP or a participating walk-in pharmacy.

items.title: CCTV appeal after Lancashire waste dumping
items.summary: Officers are investigating the deposit of around 75 tonnes of mixed commercial and household waste in the yard of a mill in Nelson the town. The man the Environment Agency want to trace is described as white, approximately 5ft 9in tall, of
items.bodyHtml:
Officers are investigating the deposit of around 75 tonnes of mixed commercial and household waste in the yard of a mill in Nelson the town.

The man the Environment Agency want to trace is described as white, approximately 5ft 9in tall, of a heavy build, with red hair. Footage shows him with a beard.

The Environment Agency believes the dumping was organised and deliberate. A total of five deposits were made during one afternoon and into the evening, using a wagon displaying cloned vehicle registration plates, a tactic that can be used to avoid detection.

Officers have already progressed a number of lines of enquiry and spoken to a person of interest.

This appeal featured on Crimewatch Live on 22 October.

CCTV image of a man the Environment Agency would like to speak to.

‘Deliberate waste dumping’

John Neville, Area Environment Manager for the Environment Agency, said:

This was a deliberate dumping of waste, and we believe it was planned using cloned number plates to help evade detection.

The landowner is facing clean-up costs and the mill sits in a residential area next to a canal, with local people having to live with the sight of this waste every day.

We are urging anyone who recognises the man in the images to come forward with information.

items.bodyText:
Officers are investigating the deposit of around 75 tonnes of mixed commercial and household waste in the yard of a mill in Nelson the town.

The man the Environment Agency want to trace is described as white, approximately 5ft 9in tall, of a heavy build, with red hair. Footage shows him with a beard.

The Environment Agency believes the dumping was organised and deliberate. A total of five deposits were made during one afternoon and into the evening, using a wagon displaying cloned vehicle registration plates, a tactic that can be used to avoid detection.

Officers have already progressed a number of lines of enquiry and spoken to a person of interest.

This appeal featured on Crimewatch Live on 22 October.


CCTV image of a man the Environment Agency would like to speak to.

‘Deliberate waste dumping’

John Neville, Area Environment Manager for the Environment Agency, said:


  This was a deliberate dumping of waste, and we believe it was planned using cloned number plates to help evade detection.

  The landowner is facing clean-up costs and the mill sits in a residential area next to a canal, with local people having to live with the sight of this waste every day.

  We are urging anyone who recognises the man in the images to come forward with information.


The landowner now faces clean-up costs amounting to thousands of pounds to ensure the waste, which was dumped on Sunday 15 February 2026, between 2pm and 6pm, is removed and disposed of at a legitimate waste facility.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Environment Agency’s incident hotline on 0800 80 70 60, or call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

items.title: Subsea cable saboteurs face jail and unlimited fines under new security crackdown
items.summary: Tougher penalties - including lengthy prison sentences and unlimited fines - proposed for those who intentionally, recklessly or negligently damage the undersea cables and pipelines carrying UK’s gas, electricity and international data New
items.bodyHtml:
• Tougher penalties - including lengthy prison sentences and unlimited fines - proposed for those who intentionally, recklessly or negligently damage the undersea cables and pipelines carrying UK’s gas, electricity and international data
  • New security and resilience laws would require subsea telecoms cable providers to better identify and manage risks to vital infrastructure
  • White Paper published today sets out powers that would allow government to act where national security is at risk, including amid suspicious Russian activity around critical undersea infrastructure.

The UK’s undersea cables and pipelines will be better protected from hostile threats under plans unveiled today to introduce tougher prison sentences and unlimited fines on ship owners that damage critical national infrastructure.

The fibre-optic cables running along the seabed connect the UK to the rest of the world, carrying around 99% of our international data and underpinning everything from messages and video calls to online banking and shopping.

The UK’s energy supply is highly dependent on undersea infrastructure, with undersea pipelines providing 74% of the UK’s gas supply and undersea electricity cables providing vital supply from Europe and the UK’s growing offshore wind sector.

But growing threats to critical undersea infrastructure, including suspicious Russian activity in UK waters, mean the laws protecting these vital connections need to keep pace with a changing security environment.

A White Paper published today sets out proposals to update 140-year-old legislation to give the UK stronger tools to protect its critical undersea infrastructure, including tougher penalties, new requirements on the telecoms industry and powers for government to intervene and direct telecoms providers where national security is at risk.

Under the plans, new offences and tougher penalties such as prison sentences of up to 14 years, would apply to those who intentionally damage critical undersea energy and telecoms infrastructure, while subsea telecoms companies would be required to comply with new security and resilience duties, including stronger face tougher duties including stronger requirements to identify and manage risks to their networks.

The Government would also gain new powers to require telecoms providers to take steps to protect cables from threats such as sabotage or espionage, alongside new safeguards for fibre optic sensing technology, which can detect activity at sea but could pose national security risks if sensitive data fell into the wrong hands.

Telecoms Minister Ian Murray said:

“Undersea cables are the hidden backbone of modern Britain, carrying the data we rely on every day to message friends and family, do our banking, and run our businesses.

“The threats we face have changed dramatically, with suspicious Russian activity around critical undersea infrastructure, yet some of the laws protecting these vital connections date back more than a century.

“We intend to modernise those laws with tougher penalties, stronger requirements on industry and new powers to protect our national security, making sure the UK’s critical infrastructure is fit for the threats of today and tomorrow.”

Energy Minister, Michael Shanks, said:

“Undersea pipelines and cables are critical to keeping energy flowing to homes and businesses across the UK.

“This legislation will further strengthen deterrence and help ensure we can prevent, detect, and respond to threats against our energy supply.”

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said:

“Undersea cables carry the energy and data our country relies on every day. Protecting them is vital to our national security.

“We’re toughening the law to stay ahead of those who seek to do us harm. Those who deliberately or recklessly damage our undersea infrastructure will face tougher penalties, including longer prison sentences and unlimited fines.
“These measures are part of the work underway across government to protect our critical infrastructure and keep our country safe.”

The publication of the White Paper marks the start of a 12-week public consultation on the proposals, seeking views from industry, experts, and the wider public to help shape the final proposals.

The UK already has a highly resilient subsea cable network. Where cable faults occur, they are due to accidents involving anchors or trawler nets being dragged across the cables, environmental hazards or technical failures.

However, suspicious activity around critical undersea infrastructure is increasingly being observed. In April, the British Armed Forces exposed a covert Russian submarine operation around critical undersea infrastructure in and around UK waters.

Notes to editors

  • The White Paper sets out legislation proposals for public consultation in four areas.
    • modernising criminal law relating to harmful conduct against telecoms and energy Critical Undersea Infrastructure through new offences, stronger penalties and new enforcement measures;
    • introducing statutory security and resilience duties for subsea telecoms cable infrastructure providers;
    • creating a national security direction power enabling the Secretary of State to direct providers of subsea telecoms cable infrastructure and repair capabilities where necessary and proportionate in the interests of national security; and
  • introducing a regulatory regime to manage national security risks associated with sensing technologies installed on subsea fibre optic cables, including those integrated into subsea telecoms and energy infrastructure.
  • The public consultation will last for 12 weeks.

items.title: British jobs boost as tank barrel production returns to the UK for first time in 20 years
items.summary: Rheinmetall UK begins production at Telford gun hall, supporting 100 highly skilled jobs. Return of large-calibre weapon manufacturing to UK soil, ensuring British Armed Forces are better equipped to defend the nation. Part of the governmen
items.bodyHtml:
• Rheinmetall UK begins production at Telford gun hall, supporting 100 highly skilled jobs.
  • Return of large-calibre weapon manufacturing to UK soil, ensuring British Armed Forces are better equipped to defend the nation.
  • Part of the government’s commitment to reindustrialisation and good growth in every postcode.

British Armed Forces will be better equipped to defend the nation, benefiting from sovereign manufacturing capability for the first time in two decades, as Rheinmetall UK begins production at its gun hall in Telford.

The gun hall supports 100 highly skilled jobs, manufactures barrels and breeches for both 120mm and 155mm weapon systems, including for RCH 155 and future artillery platforms.

Rheinmetall UK will expand its workforce as production ramps up, building long-term partnerships with British SMEs – strengthening the domestic supply chain for decades to come.

Specialist local workers have been recruited for the production phase, drawing on the strength of Telford’s engineering sector. Local workers have been recruited and trained to do high-value work, supporting economic growth in the region.

The development of the gun hall marks the return of large-calibre weapon manufacturing to UK soil, restoring national capability, strengthening the defence industrial base and supporting reindustrialisation.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting officially opened the gun hall alongside Chief of the General Staff General Sir Roly Walker and Armin Papperger, CEO of Rheinmetall AG. Rheinmetall UK has gone from an empty site to full production in just eight months, having taken over the facility in Autumn 2025.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP, said:

Britain is back in the business of making the weapons that our Armed Forces need to defend the nation against our adversaries. From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action.

One hundred skilled jobs in world-class manufacturing and the return of large-calibre weapon production to UK soil for the first time in twenty years – this is what defence as an engine for growth looks like.

Central to the gun hall’s development has been the training of the British workforce who spent time at Rheinmetall’s production facility in Unterlüß, Germany. UK workers gained expertise in precision manufacturing, quality assurance and specialist weapon production before returning to Telford to establish this sovereign capability.

Armin Papperger, CEO of Rheinmetall AG, said:

Today’s opening is an important milestone for Rheinmetall and for the United Kingdom. In a remarkably short period of time, we have turned our commitment into a sovereign manufacturing capability that will strengthen Britain’s defence industrial base for decades to come.

The UK has been a long-standing and valued partner for Rheinmetall, and today we are building on an already strong relationship. We are committed to investing in the UK for the long term, expanding our industrial footprint and working together to deliver the capabilities needed for the future.

By combining Rheinmetall’s expertise with British skills, innovation and manufacturing, we are strengthening the UK’s sovereign industrial capacity, supporting the Armed Forces and contributing to the security of NATO and Europe.

The development of the gun hall demonstrates the UK-Germany industrial partnership under the Trinity House Agreement. Signed in October 2024, the agreement is a commitment to improve and enhance bilateral co-operation between both nations, enhancing NATO’s collective deterrence.

This milestone builds on Rheinmetall UK’s wider investment across the country, including its work on the Boxer vehicle and Challenger 3 battle tank programmes. These programmes show how defence can deliver national security and national prosperity, strengthening the UK’s industrial base and ensuring British industry is ready for the future.

The government has committed £298 billion over four years as part of the Defence Investment Plan, furthering the government’s commitment to using defence spending to drive economic growth in every postcode, creating well-paid, long-term jobs across the UK.

items.title: Households to receive £150 Warm Home Discount confirmation letter
items.summary: People urged to check doormats and letterboxes for a letter confirming £150 off bills this winter Around 6 million households across Britain will receive the Warm Home Discount This follows action to remove VAT from electricity bills, givin
items.bodyHtml:
• People urged to check doormats and letterboxes for a letter confirming £150 off bills this winter  
  • Around 6 million households across Britain will receive the Warm Home Discount  
  • This follows action to remove VAT from electricity bills, giving people breathing space on the cost of living  

From today (Thursday 22 October 2026), households across England and Wales should check their doormats and letterboxes for confirmation they will get £150 off their energy bills this winter.   

Around 6 million households across Britain will benefit from the £150 discount this winter, with nearly 2.3 million additional families, including around 1 million with children, receiving the rebate last year after the expansion of the scheme.  

Every billpayer on means-tested benefits now qualifies for the Warm Home Discount, removing restrictions that previously excluded many who needed help.   

Letters will begin to arrive this week and will continue to be issued through to January 2027.    

They will advise that the recipient will either get the discount automatically or, if they need to phone the helpline, must do so before 26 February 2027 and provide further information to receive the funding.  

This is in addition to the VAT cut on electricity bills in October, capping bus fares at £2 and removing £150 of costs off bills earlier this year, giving families breathing space this winter.   

Minister for Energy Consumers Polly Billington said:  

I know that many families will be struggling with their energy bills this winter. 

That is why I urge those who think they qualify for the Warm Home Discount to keep an eye out for a letter confirming their eligibility.  

Energy is an absolute essential, which is exactly why in October we cut VAT on all electricity bills and earlier this year we removed £150 of costs off bills, giving families breathing space this winter.

Recipients of the scheme should only use their usual method of contacting their energy supplier and not follow any suspicious links or input their financial information if requested over email, text or phone call.     

Earlier this year the government confirmed that millions of eligible households will receive the Warm Home Discount for the rest of the decade, with the scheme set to continue through to 2030/31.    

Last year’s Budget has also taken an average £150 of costs off energy bills, which is factored into bills for the years to come.  

Ned Hammond, Deputy Director of Policy (Customers) at Energy UK said:  

The Warm Home Discount offers vital help for millions of households through the colder months, and this week the government will begin sending letters to eligible customers to explain how the support will be delivered. 

As we face the prospect of another winter of high and volatile energy prices, we encourage anyone struggling with their bill to contact their supplier to see what help is available for them.

Stew Horne, Group Head of Sector Intelligence and External Affairs at Energy Saving Trust, said: 

As the weather turns colder and households start using more energy, many people will be worried about how they’ll afford their energy bills. The Warm Home Discount provides valuable support to eligible households, helping to ease the cost of keeping homes warm. 

We encourage people to read their letters from the UK government carefully and check whether they need to take any action. Understanding the support available and responding promptly if required can help ensure you receive the help you’re entitled to this winter.

  That is why I urge those who think they qualify for the Warm Home Discount to keep an eye out for a letter confirming their eligibility.  

  Energy is an absolute essential, which is exactly why in October we cut VAT on all electricity bills and earlier this year we removed £150 of costs off bills, giving families breathing space this winter.


Recipients of the scheme should only use their usual method of contacting their energy supplier and not follow any suspicious links or input their financial information if requested over email, text or phone call.     

Earlier this year the government confirmed that millions of eligible households will receive the Warm Home Discount for the rest of the decade, with the scheme set to continue through to 2030/31.    

Last year’s Budget has also taken an average £150 of costs off energy bills, which is factored into bills for the years to come.  

Ned Hammond, Deputy Director of Policy (Customers) at Energy UK said:  


  The Warm Home Discount offers vital help for millions of households through the colder months, and this week the government will begin sending letters to eligible customers to explain how the support will be delivered. 

  As we face the prospect of another winter of high and volatile energy prices, we encourage anyone struggling with their bill to contact their supplier to see what help is available for them.


Stew Horne, Group Head of Sector Intelligence and External Affairs at Energy Saving Trust, said: 


  As the weather turns colder and households start using more energy, many people will be worried about how they’ll afford their energy bills. The Warm Home Discount provides valuable support to eligible households, helping to ease the cost of keeping homes warm. 

  We encourage people to read their letters from the UK government carefully and check whether they need to take any action. Understanding the support available and responding promptly if required can help ensure you receive the help you’re entitled to this winter.

items.title: Attorney General and Treasury Solicitor publish statement on talent and opportunity at the Bar
items.summary: The Attorney General and Treasury Solicitor have published a Diversity and Inclusion Statement for the Bar, setting out how the Government Legal Department (GLD) will work with chambers and counsel to support diversity, equitable access to
items.bodyHtml:
The Attorney General and Treasury Solicitor have published a Diversity and Inclusion Statement for the Bar, setting out how the Government Legal Department (GLD) will work with chambers and counsel to support diversity, equitable access to work, and career progression across the Attorney General’s Civil and EU Panel of Counsel.

The panels bring together specialist barristers who advise and represent government on some of the country’s most significant legal issues. Access to this work can be an important part of career development and progression at the Bar.

The statement builds on existing good practice and sets out GLD’s expectations of chambers, including fair and inclusive allocation of work and support for the recruitment and progression of counsel from all backgrounds.

Appointments to the panels continue to be made through a rigorous, merit-based competition. The statement does not change the appointments process; it focuses on how GLD and chambers work together once counsel have been appointed, including how fairly work is distributed across the panel.

Attorney General Ellie Reeves KC MP said:

Government should be able to call on the best legal talent this country has to offer, wherever it comes from.

This is more than an ambition, it’s a plan for action. We are committed to removing the barriers that stop talented people reaching their full potential at the Bar, and to making sure the counsel we instruct reflects the people we serve.

Different backgrounds bring different perspectives, and that makes for better legal advice and a stronger profession.

GLD is one of the largest purchasers of legal services in the country and instructs barristers on a wide range of complex and high-profile matters. The way government works with counsel therefore has an important influence on opportunities across the profession, and on the diversity and strength of the legal talent available to support government in the future.

Douglas Wilson KC (Hon) OBE, Treasury Solicitor and Permanent Secretary, said:

I’ve seen first-hand the value that different perspectives and experiences bring to legal work. The strongest teams are the ones that challenge assumptions, approach problems from different angles and aren’t afraid to think differently.

Government has access to an exceptional pool of legal talent through the Attorney General’s panels. Making full use of that expertise helps us deliver stronger legal advice, better decision-making and better outcomes for the people we serve.

The statement sets out that GLD will collect self-declared diversity data from panel applicants, to understand the diversity profile of the panel and monitor whether work and fee payments are distributed fairly. This data will not be visible to those assessing panel applications, and barristers may choose not to provide it.

GLD will review progress against the statement’s commitments regularly, working with chambers and counsel on their implementation.

Bar Council Chair Kirsty Brimelow KC said:

Equitable briefing is one of my priorities as Chair of the Bar this year. The Bar Council has supported GLD’s aspiration to improve panel diversity, as well as ensuring fair access to high-quality work for those on their panels.

I welcome the commitments launched today, aimed at ensuring that the government benefits from the breadth of talent at the Bar, and importantly, builds a pipeline of talent for the future. However, the key is implementation and monitoring progress, and we look forward to seeing change.

Background

  • The Attorney General’s Civil and EU Panel of Counsel is made up of specialist, independent barristers appointed through a rigorous, merit-based competition to provide legal advice and advocacy to government on some of the country’s most significant legal issues.
  • Appointments to the panel are made through a competitive process run by the Attorney General’s Office and are reviewed periodically.
  • The statement applies principally to the Attorney General’s Civil and EU Panel and, where relevant, to GLD’s use of counsel on other panels and King’s Counsel appointed on nomination by the Attorney General. GLD is separately committed to supporting diversity on the Special Advocate panels, which are recruited and appointed through a different process reflecting the distinct nature of that role.

items.title: Aldi and Lidl will be subject to same rules as major supermarkets
items.summary: CMA designates Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI as ‘Large Grocery Retailers’ CMA decision will prevent Aldi and Lidl from blocking rival supermarkets opening close to their stores The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has decided that Aldi,
items.bodyHtml:
• CMA designates Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI as ‘Large Grocery Retailers’  

  • CMA decision will prevent Aldi and Lidl from blocking rival supermarkets opening close to their stores  

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has decided that Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI will be designated as ‘Large Grocery Retailers’ (LGRs) under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010.

The Order has applied to Asda, Co‑op, Marks and Spencer, Morrisons, Sainsbury’s, Tesco and Waitrose since 2010. The Order is designed to stop Large Grocery Retailers from using land agreements to make it harder for rival supermarkets to open nearby – in particular through the use of restrictive covenants and exclusivity arrangements. The rules ensure supermarkets compete freely – and ultimately ensure shoppers have more choice about where to buy, and how much to pay for, their groceries.  

In August, the CMA invited views on its proposal to designate Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI under the Order. Interested parties including Morrisons, Waitrose and Iceland submitted their views, and all supported the CMA’s proposal. The CMA did not receive representations from Aldi, Lidl GB or Lidl NI. 

Once a retailer is designated, it cannot include any prohibited restrictions in new agreements – and existing agreements can be reviewed by the CMA, on the request of interested landowners, developers, and rival supermarkets. This is the case for all designated supermarkets. 

Juliette Enser, Executive Director for Competition Enforcement and Markets at the CMA, said: 

We put in place rules to stop big supermarket chains from blocking rival stores opening in their area, and now those rules apply to Aldi and Lidl. 

This will help level the playing field and make sure shoppers get the best choice of products and prices in their area.

The UK food and grocery market is worth an estimated £222.7 billion, with Aldi and Lidl ranking among the top 5 retailers by market share.  

For more information, read the CMA’s final decisions report and supporting documents on the case page. 

Notes to editors 

  1. The Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010 was introduced following a groceries market investigation by the CMA’s predecessor organisation, the Competition Commission, and seeks to prevent designated grocery retailers from using restrictive land agreements that could adversely affect competition. 

  2. Lidl operates separate businesses in Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Lidl GB operates stores in England, Scotland and Wales. Lidl NI operates stores in Northern Ireland. Aldi does not operate stores in Northern Ireland. 

  3. For media enquiries, contact the CMA press office. Email: press@cma.gov.uk Telephone: 020 3738 6460.

items.title: Stronger protections for pregnant women and new parents against unfair dismissal
items.summary: • Pregnant women and new parents will now have stronger safeguards to protect them from unfair dismissal, requiring employers to go further than ever before. • New protections will also extend to employees on adoption, shared parental, neon
items.bodyHtml:
• Pregnant women and new parents will now have stronger safeguards to protect them from unfair dismissal, requiring employers to go further than ever before.

• New protections will also extend to employees on adoption, shared parental, neonatal care and bereaved partner’s paternity leave.

• Reforms ease pressure on working families giving job security they can depend on.

Pregnant women and new parents will now have stronger protections against being fired, in a new crackdown on unfair workplace practices announced by the government today [Thursday 22 October].

Pregnancy and maternity discrimination remain widespread in the workplace, having a devastating impact on what is meant to be an exciting time for new families.

These new safeguards will change that. From 2027, tribunals will use a new, stricter, approach for dismissal cases involving pregnant women and new parents. By doing this, it will require employers to have considered all reasonable alternatives to dismissal before pursuing it.

Protections will also be extended to employees taking adoption leave, shared parental leave, neonatal care leave and bereaved partner’s paternity leave.

By raising the bar for all companies, these reforms will ease pressure on working families, making them feel more secure in their jobs.

Minister for the Future of Work, Kate Dearden, said:

No one should have to choose between starting a family and staying in work.

Pregnancy and maternity discrimination can have a devastating impact on people’s lives, forcing them out of work at the very moment they need security most.

These new protections will raise the bar for employers, making it harder to dismiss pregnant women and new parents unfairly and helping families feel more secure at work.

Rachel Grocott, Chief Executive Officer, Pregnant Then Screwed:

Our latest State of the Nation survey shows that a huge 73% of women experience pregnancy or maternity discrimination - a figure that is simply unacceptable.

Every week we hear from women whose careers, finances and confidence have been knocked by unfair treatment during pregnancy, maternity leave or their return to work, and we’ve been taking this evidence to government for over a decade.

So, we’re pleased to welcome these new protections: they’re an important step forward in creating a society where simply starting a family doesn’t wreck your career.

There is, of course, still lots more work to do to tackle the wider motherhood penalty - and we look forward to continuing to work with the government to make sure women, mothers and parents’ voices remain at the centre of decisions that affect their lives in such fundamental ways.

Ali Fiddy, Director of Maternity Action said:

We welcome the move to enhance the protection from dismissal of pregnant women and new mothers.

We speak to thousands of women each year who are worried about losing their jobs simply because they are pregnant or have had a baby.

Once introduced, we hope that the measures announced today will reduce the poor and unfair treatment experienced by expectant and new mothers and result in more women remaining in their jobs after having a baby.

Kate Shoesmith, Director of Policy and Insights at the British Chambers of Commerce said:

Businesses across the country want to support women through pregnancy and their return to work. Employers also want to ensure new parents feel secure in their jobs.

These stronger protections are welcome and represent a sensible and balanced way forward. They give families greater security while recognising that businesses sometimes have to make difficult decisions for legitimate reasons.

We look forward to working constructively with government to develop practical guidance, so everyone knows exactly where they stand.

This comes as part of the Employment Rights Act which will benefit over 18 million people by bringing employment rights into the 21st century, helping to create a fairer labour market for both workers and employers.

END

Notes to Editors

• The government has today published the consultation response for pregnancy protections on GOV.UK : Make Work Pay: enhanced dismissal protections for pregnant women and new mothers - GOV.UK

• The response includes plans to replace the band of reasonable responses test with a proportionality test, coming into effect from October 2027

• This will only be for pregnant mothers, new parents, and other types of family related leave listed above.

• For all other cases of unfair dismissal - the band of reasonable responses test – which asks how a reasonable employer would act – will remain in place.

• The response explains the intention to introduce regulations which will confirm the restricted variations on sums payable, and shift pattern changes.

• This will only be for pregnant mothers, new parents, and other types of family related leave listed above.

• For all other cases of unfair dismissal - the band of reasonable responses test – which asks how a reasonable employer would act – will remain in place.

• Pregnant Then Screwed are happy to be contacted for media opportunities on rebecca@pregnantthenscrewed.com

items.title: Strong strategic leadership key to overcoming risks, says RSH
items.summary: RSH has urged social housing boards and councillors to provide strong strategic leadership and ensure they have the information and insight needed to make difficult decisions about competing priorities. RSH’s Sector Risk Profile report, pub
items.bodyHtml:
RSH has urged social housing boards and councillors to provide strong strategic leadership and ensure they have the information and insight needed to make difficult decisions about competing priorities.

RSH’s Sector Risk Profile report, published today, warned landlords must manage growing financial and operational risks to be able to balance major investment in existing homes with the need to build new social housing.

The report highlighted the increasingly complex operating environment facing landlords as they work to improve the quality, safety and energy efficiency of existing homes while helping to address significant demand for new affordable housing.

Landlords continue to invest heavily in tenants’ existing homes, but further substantial investment will be required to meet building safety requirements, improve stock condition and adapt to requirements of Awaab’s Law, the Decent Homes Standard and Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES).

At the same time, social landlords are expected to play a key role in increasing supply of affordable homes. For some organisations this presents new development challenges, while others face decisions about how to expand delivery sustainably and manage associate risks including innovative financing models.

The report warns that these pressures are being compounded by a difficult economic environment.

Although there are signs that financial performance may be stabilising, many landlords continue to operate with historically low levels of interest cover and face increased borrowing costs, refinancing pressures and ongoing inflationary risks.

The report also highlights the importance of managing cyber security, data protection and operation resilience risks as organisations becoming increasingly reliant on digital systems and technology.

RSH Chief Executive Jonathan Walters said: “Social landlords are operating in a challenging and fast-changing environment. They must continue investing in existing homes to ensure tenants have safe, decent and well-managed homes, while also helping to deliver the new social housing the country needs.

“There are no easy choices. Landlords must carefully balance competing priorities, manage risks effectively and ensure their organisations remain financially resilient.

“Strong governance, a clear strategic direction and the need to take a longer-term view are essential. Boards and councillors must be ready to make evidence-based decisions that support their fundamental purpose of delivering more and better social homes for current and future tenants.”

The report emphasises that landlords should focus on achieving value for money and operating as efficiently as possible to maximise their capacity to invest.

While some organisations are considering the disposal of existing properties to release resources, the report warns that this can reduce the availability of social homes and should not be relied upon as a long-term solution.

And while the sector faces significant challenges, organisations that remain focused on their purpose, maintain a clear strategic direction and adapt effectively to changing circumstances will be better placed to deliver safe homes and meet future housing need.

Ends

Notes to Editors

  1. The 2026 Sector Risk Profile sets out our view of the most significant sources of risk to landlords and their ability to deliver the outcomes of our standards.
  2. By ‘landlord’, we mean a registered provider of social housing, including local authorities and private registered providers – such as non-profit housing associations, co-operatives and profit-making organisations. This publication draws on regulatory returns submitted by landlords and other data provided to us as the regulator.
  3. In 2024 RSH started its proactive inspection programme for all large social landlords (those owning 1,000 homes or more). For housing associations and other private registered providers, our integrated inspections cover the economic and consumer standards. For local authorities, RSH’s remit covers the consumer standards and rent standard. But, as our regulatory casework shows, many of the lessons relating to our regulation of governance should also be used by local authorities to improve outcomes for tenants.
  4. RSH remains committed to a co-regulatory approach meaning councillors and boards are responsible for their organisations and are held to account for how they are run and the outcomes they deliver. to ensure that landlords are managed effectively, maintain appropriate control frameworks, and meet all regulatory requirements. They should understand the risks facing their organisations, assess how these risks interact, and ensure that appropriate strategies are in place to mitigate them while continuing to deliver positive outcomes for tenants.
  5. For press enquiries contact vicky.moore@rsh.gov.uk or christian.cosby@rsh.gov.uk. For general enquiries contact enquiries@rsh.gov.uk.

items.title: New action on redress for postmasters affected by Post Office scandals
items.summary: Deadlines set for closure of remaining redress schemes for postmasters, providing certainty while ensuring eligible individuals still have time to submit new claims New independent routes for reviewing and appealing claims to strengthen fai
items.bodyHtml:
• Deadlines set for closure of remaining redress schemes for postmasters, providing certainty while ensuring eligible individuals still have time to submit new claims
  • New independent routes for reviewing and appealing claims to strengthen fairness
  • Independent investigation announced into pre-Horizon software systems
  • Over £1.7 billion compensation paid out to over 14,000 postmasters through Horizon redress schemes

Thousands of postmasters affected by the Horizon and Capture scandals are set to benefit from new action on redress. The Government has today [21 October] announced a new package of measures to provide pathways to conclusion for schemes, strengthen scrutiny and fairness, and investigate pre-Horizon software.

The scandals caused profound harm to postmasters, many of whom suffered years of financial, personal and reputational damage through no fault of their own. Over £1.7 billion has now been paid out in compensation to over 14,000 of those affected, with 87% of Horizon claims received now settled.  

Post Office Minister, Kate Dearden said:

We must never lose sight of the suffering caused by the Horizon and Capture scandals. Behind every pound of compensation paid is a person whose life has been turned upside down by the scandal.

We remain unwavering in our commitment to provide fair, comprehensive and timely redress to all those affected and ensure that a scandal like this never happens again.

New deadlines have been set for applications to the two remaining postmaster redress schemes, providing a pathway to conclusion while ensuring sufficient time for people to apply. The Capture Redress Scheme will close to new applications on 31 March 2027, while the Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme will close to new submissions on 31 July 2027.

New routes have also been announced to strengthen fairness around compensation offers on the Horizon Shortfalls Scheme (HSS).  Later this month, a new independent review process will begin for postmasters who have been told that there is insufficient evidence to receive a fixed sum offer of compensation.

A new independent review process will also open in November for those who have previously accepted HSS fixed sum offers and believe their claims were undervalued. 

To ensure no stone is left unturned in uncovering the full extent of issues affecting postmasters, a new independent investigation into software used before Horizon has also now been confirmed. 

This follows a recommendation from the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Select Committee, with an independent investigator to establish a full understanding of other software applications and their potential impact. The evidence it produces will be used to inform any future considerations. 

Notes to Editors

  • Registration remains open for the Horizon Family Members Redress Scheme, with claims processing expected to begin early next year. The scheme recognises that the impact of the scandal extended beyond postmasters to their families. 
  • The Government also confirmed that the Restorative Justice programme is now fully operational, providing a voluntary process for postmasters and family members who wish to participate. 
  • As of 30 September 2026, approximately £1,731 million has been paid to over 14,000 claimants for Horizon Redress schemes (Post Office Horizon financial redress data as of 30 September 2026 - GOV.UK )
  • Over £9 million has been paid to claimants on the Capture redress scheme (Post Office Capture financial redress data as of 30 September 2026 - GOV.UK)
