The Environment Agency assesses applications for environmental permits under the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016 (EPR).

Its role is to assess the application and decide if it meets all requirements under relevant environmental legislation, including ensuring that the proposed plant would not cause any significant pollution of the environment or harm to human health.

People can respond to the consultation directly on the website or alternatively by email to pscpublicresponse@environment-agency.gov.uk

Further background

Consultation responses


  Responses to the consultation can be made electronically.
  Information on the website explains how people can view the consultation documents and how they can provide comments. It also explains what the Environment Agency can and can’t take into account when deciding on the application.
  Anyone wishing to comment on the proposals is urged to read the documentation online before responding directly on the website or by email to pscpublicresponse@environment-agency.gov.uk 
  Those unable to view the documents or make representation via the consultation website or by email should contact the Environment Agency on 03708 506 506.


Environmental permits 


  Environmental permits set out strict legal conditions by which an operator must comply in order to protect people and the environment. Should an environmental permit be issued, the Environment Agency has responsibility for enforcing its conditions.
  The Environment Agency’s powers include enforcement notices, suspension and revocation of permits, fines and ultimately criminal sanctions, including prosecution.
  The Environment Agency may only refuse a permit if it does not meet one or more of the legal requirements under environmental legislation, including if it will have a significant impact on the environment or harm human health. If all the requirements are met, we are legally required to issue a permit

items.title: Major investment to drive growth and jobs across Britain as Sultan of Oman visits UK
items.summary: Over £1bn investment set to generate jobs and growth across both countries as Sultan of Oman continues State Visit to UK. New agreements will also accelerate mutual investment between Oman and the UK, supporting UK government’s commitment t
items.bodyHtml:
• Over £1bn investment set to generate jobs and growth across both countries as Sultan of Oman continues State Visit to UK.

  • New agreements will also accelerate mutual investment between Oman and the UK, supporting UK government’s commitment to drive good growth in every postcode.

  • UK and Oman also commit to closer cooperation across security, defence and trade as Prime Minister hosts His Majesty The Sultan in Downing Street.

Over £1bn in new investment is set to generate jobs and opportunity across the UK and Oman, as the countries take their centuries old partnership to a new level.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik of Oman in Downing Street today as the Sultan’s three-day visit to the UK continues.

Driving prosperity and growth for people in the UK and Oman has been at the heart of the visit, with an agreement accelerating two-way investment between the two countries expected to be signed today.

The deal will build on the existing UK-Oman Sovereign Investment Partnership and support increased investment across a number of key sectors, including in renewable energy, technology, critical minerals, space, healthcare and financial services.

UK Export Finance, the UK government’s export credit agency, will also increase its financing capacity up to £7 billion for UK exports to Oman, helping unlock even more opportunities for trade and investment.

The announcements come as UK-founded Yamna, a global infrastructure development and investment company backed by British investment funds, is set to sign an agreement with Oman to build a large-scale Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centre in Salalah. The first phase is expected to exceed £1bn and will create over 100 highly skilled jobs across the UK by exporting British expertise and attracting returns for UK-backed investors.

Prime Minister, Andy Burnham said: 

I’m delighted to welcome His Majesty The Sultan to the UK - the UK and Oman have built a friendship which generates real benefits for people at home, and I look forward to shaping the next chapter of our relationship. 

Economic growth, security, defence, education: these are just some of the priorities we share as we plot a course through an increasingly complex world. 

Working together, we are leading with our values and creating opportunities for people in both our countries.

The Foreign and Defence Secretaries and Minister for Trade are also set to meet with their Omani counterparts to further strengthen UK-Oman cooperation and ensure the relationship is delivering for people in both countries.

Oman is a vital partner for the UK - both as a historic ally and trading partner, and also for its role in regional stability and work to ensure the free flow of global trade through the Strait of Hormuz, which is critical to restoring global shipping routes.

To support this work, the UK and Oman are also expected to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to secure maritime co-operation through strengthened information-sharing and knowledge exchange with the Omani Maritime Security Centre.

The UK will also announce the return of the Chevening Educational Scholarship Programme to Oman, supporting Oman’s future leaders and generations with access to British education institutions.  Welcoming applications from August 2027, the programme, run by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, will give more people the opportunity to study and build lifelong connections between both countries. 

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: 

The UK-Oman relationship spans almost four centuries and is built on trust and collaboration. His Majesty The Sultan’s visit to the United Kingdom reinforces this partnership for the future age. 

At what is a critical time for the Middle East, our close collaboration has never been more vital. Oman continues to play a valued diplomatic role in supporting the dialogue necessary to support a pathway to peace and regional stability – essential for the global economy and global security. 

Driving closer working across defence, trade and investment, and education, ensures that our long-standing friendship is a modern partnership that delivers for both the British and Omani people.

The UK and Oman will also sign new agreements on the responsible use of AI in education, supporting English language learning and helping teachers use AI safely and effectively in the classroom, and closer cooperation on space - exchanging expertise and cooperation on space policy, scientific research and innovation between the UK Space Agency and the Omani government.

His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik is visiting the UK as part of a three-day State Visit, hosted by Their Majesties’ The King and Queen. The visit celebrates our shared history and the close ties between the people of Oman and the United Kingdom.  

Notes to Editors: 

  • The last State Visit to the UK by a Sultan of Oman was in 1982, when Her Late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II hosted Sultan Qaboos bin Said. 
  • For more information on the FCDO Chevening programme please see here. 
  • The UK and Oman first signed a Sovereign Investment Partnership with Oman in 2022, with Oman investing £1.7bn in the UK since its creation. 
  • For more information on the role of UK Export Finance please see here. 
  • Total UK exports to Oman amounted to £1.1 billion in the four quarters to the end of Q1 2026.  
  • For further details on UK’s trade and investment please see here. 
  • The government is also announcing the creation of a diplomatic partnership pathway between the UK’s Diplomatic Service College and Omani Diplomatic Academy. This will allow diplomats to share expertise and experience, and helping develop joint-diplomatic initiatives against shared challenges for the future.

Media enquiries

Email newsdesk@fcdo.gov.uk

Telephone 020 7008 3100

Email the FCDO Newsdesk (monitored 24 hours a day) in the first instance, and we will respond as soon as possible.

  4. Sales volume data is available by property status (new build and existing property) and funding status (cash and mortgage) in our downloadable data tables. Transactions that require us to create a new register, such as new builds, are more complex and require more time to process. Read revisions to the UK HPI data.

  5. Revision tables are available for England and Wales within the downloadable data in CSV format. See about the UK HPI for more information.

  8. This regular annual pattern can sometimes mask the underlying movements and trends in the data series. HMRC presents the UK aggregate transaction figures on a seasonally adjusted basis. We make adjustments for both the time of year and the construction of the calendar, including corrections for the position of Easter and the number of trading days in a particular month.

  9. UK HPI seasonally adjusted series are calculated at regional and national levels only. See the data tables.

  10. The first estimate for new build average price (April 2016 report) was based on a small sample which can cause volatility. A three-month moving average has been applied to the latest estimate to remove some of this volatility.

  11. The UK HPI reflects the final transaction price for sales of residential property.   12. HM Land Registry provides information on residential property transactions for England and Wales, collected as part of the official registration process for properties that are sold for full market value.

  13. The HM Land Registry dataset contains the sale price of the property, the date when the sale was completed, full address details, the type of property (detached, semi-detached, terraced or flat), if it is a newly built property or an established residential building and a variable to indicate if the property has been purchased as a financed transaction (using a mortgage) or as a non-financed transaction (cash purchase).

  14. Repossession sales data is based on the number of transactions lodged with HM Land Registry by lenders exercising their power of sale.

  15. For England, we show repossession sales volume recorded by government office region. For Wales, we provide repossession sales volume for the number of repossession sales.

  16. Repossession sales data is available from April 2016 in CSV format. Find out more information about repossession sales.

  17. We publish CSV files of the raw and cleansed aggregated data every month for England, Scotland and Wales. We publish Northern Ireland data on a quarterly basis. They are available for free use and re-use under the Open Government Licence.

  18. HM Land Registry is a government department created in 1862. Its vision is: “to achieve digital services and expertise that unlock a better, faster and less stressful property market.”

  19. HM Land Registry’s purpose is: “to secure your property ownership, make buying of land easy and safe for everyone and provide access to property information.”

  20. HM Land Registry safeguards land and property ownership valued at nearly £9 trillion, enabling over £1.66 trillion worth of personal and commercial lending to be secured against property across England and Wales. The Land Register contains more than 27 million titles showing evidence of ownership for more than 90% of the land mass of England and Wales.

  21. For further information about HM Land Registry visit www.gov.uk/land-registry.

items.title: Government confirms indefinite recognition of CE marked medical devices
items.summary: Patients across Great Britain will continue to have access to the medical devices and in vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) they rely on, from insulin pumps and replacement joints to diagnostic tests and surgical equipment, after the governmen
items.bodyHtml:
Patients across Great Britain will continue to have access to the medical devices and in vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) they rely on, from insulin pumps and replacement joints to diagnostic tests and surgical equipment, after the government has today, 21 October 2026, confirmed it will continue to accept CE marked medical devices on a long-term basis.  

The decision follows a public consultation, which ran from 16 February 2026 to 10 April 2026, that received more than 1,000 responses from patients, healthcare organisations, industry and others. 

The decision means the UK will not require an additional approval route for devices already approved for the EU market, avoiding duplication for manufacturers and helping to maintain stable supply and patient access to medical technologies. More than 90% of medical devices registered for use in Great Britain currently carry a CE mark, meaning they have been assessed and approved for the European market, and this approval has been recognised to provide access to the Great British market. Continuing to recognise these devices will help maintain safe, uninterrupted access to the treatments and technologies that patients and the NHS rely on. This sits alongside the UKCA marking route, which continues to operate as the domestic approval pathway for devices placed on the market in Great Britain. 

These arrangements sit alongside strengthened post-market surveillance and reporting requirements already in place. The MHRA will continue to oversee all devices on the UK market, monitor safety through mechanisms including the Yellow Card scheme, and work closely with international partners to share safety information enabling the MHRA to take action to protect patients where needed. 

In parallel, the UKCA route remains the current domestic approval route for medical devices placed on the market in Great Britain. This is being modernised through the pre-market statutory instrument, which will update the requirements devices must meet to be UKCA marked. Alongside this, we will continue to seek enabling powers through primary legislation to develop a future licencing approach for medical devices, intended to support a more modern and adaptable framework that is better able to respond to advancing medical technologies, including software and AI medical devices, reflecting recommendations from the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare.  

Our approach will secure supply of medical devices for UK patients while also supporting safe, rapid access to innovation so that patients can benefit from the best new technologies. By providing a clear and predictable regulatory framework. The approach supports the development and availability of new health technologies for patients, in line with the ambitions of the Government’s Life Sciences Sector Plan and 10 Year Health Plan. 

Continued recognition of CE-marked devices also reflects the wider ambition of the MHRA’s 2030 Strategy to expand reliance and recognition routes with trusted regulators, reducing regulatory burden, strengthen supply resilience and supporting timely patient access.  

Lawrence Tallon, Chief Executive of the MHRA, said: 

“This decision gives patients, the NHS and industry the long-term certainty they need on access to medical devices. By continuing to recognise CE marked devices, we’re ensuring that patients across Great Britain maintain uninterrupted access to the medical technologies they depend on, from life-saving diagnostics to everyday treatments, while our wider device reforms will ensure our regulatory framework is ready for the innovative technologies of tomorrow, including AI-powered medical devices. The MHRA will continue to oversee the safety of every device on the UK market, and we remain committed to working closely with international partners to identify and act on safety concerns quickly.” 

Steve Lee, Executive Director, Regulation, ABHI, said: 

 “Regulatory predictability and avoiding unnecessary duplication are fundamental to industry investment decisions, which ultimately determine how quickly patients can access new technologies. Long-term recognition of CE marking is therefore a significant and welcome decision, providing much-needed certainty for manufacturers, safeguarding patient access and strengthening the UK’s position as an attractive and competitive market for HealthTech. 

“We look forward to its implementation, with this practical and proportionate approach supporting continuity of supply and ensuring friction-free access to the medical devices, IVDs and digital health technologies on which UK patients, citizens and the NHS rely.” 

The government will continue to engage with patients, clinicians and industry as these arrangements are implemented, including a programme of engagement sessions with patient groups to explain the response and address questions on safety and oversight.  

Notes to Editors 

The consultation on the future regulation of medical devices sought views on the indefinite recognition of CE marked devices in Great Britain. 

The MHRA will continue to oversee all devices on the UK market and has strengthened its post-market surveillance activity. 

Further information on the government’s response, including the full consultation outcome, is available at Medical devices regulations: targeted consultation on the indefinite recognition of CE marked devices - GOV.UK 

The MHRA is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care. 

For media enquiries, please contact newscentre@mhra.gov.uk or call 020 3080 7651.

This is being modernised through the pre-market statutory instrument, which will update the requirements devices must meet to be UKCA marked. Alongside this, we will continue to seek enabling powers through primary legislation to develop a future licencing approach for medical devices, intended to support a more modern and adaptable framework that is better able to respond to advancing medical technologies, including software and AI medical devices, reflecting recommendations from the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare.  

Our approach will secure supply of medical devices for UK patients while also supporting safe, rapid access to innovation so that patients can benefit from the best new technologies. By providing a clear and predictable regulatory framework. The approach supports the development and availability of new health technologies for patients, in line with the ambitions of the Government’s Life Sciences Sector Plan and 10 Year Health Plan. 

Continued recognition of CE-marked devices also reflects the wider ambition of the MHRA’s 2030 Strategy to expand reliance and recognition routes with trusted regulators, reducing regulatory burden, strengthen supply resilience and supporting timely patient access.  

Lawrence Tallon, Chief Executive of the MHRA, said: 

“This decision gives patients, the NHS and industry the long-term certainty they need on access to medical devices. By continuing to recognise CE marked devices, we’re ensuring that patients across Great Britain maintain uninterrupted access to the medical technologies they depend on, from life-saving diagnostics to everyday treatments, while our wider device reforms will ensure our regulatory framework is ready for the innovative technologies of tomorrow, including AI-powered medical devices. The MHRA will continue to oversee the safety of every device on the UK market, and we remain committed to working closely with international partners to identify and act on safety concerns quickly.” 

Steve Lee, Executive Director, Regulation, ABHI, said: 

 “Regulatory predictability and avoiding unnecessary duplication are fundamental to industry investment decisions, which ultimately determine how quickly patients can access new technologies. Long-term recognition of CE marking is therefore a significant and welcome decision, providing much-needed certainty for manufacturers, safeguarding patient access and strengthening the UK’s position as an attractive and competitive market for HealthTech. 

“We look forward to its implementation, with this practical and proportionate approach supporting continuity of supply and ensuring friction-free access to the medical devices, IVDs and digital health technologies on which UK patients, citizens and the NHS rely.” 

The government will continue to engage with patients, clinicians and industry as these arrangements are implemented, including a programme of engagement sessions with patient groups to explain the response and address questions on safety and oversight.  

Notes to Editors 

The consultation on the future regulation of medical devices sought views on the indefinite recognition of CE marked devices in Great Britain. 

The MHRA will continue to oversee all devices on the UK market and has strengthened its post-market surveillance activity. 

Further information on the government’s response, including the full consultation outcome, is available at Medical devices regulations: targeted consultation on the indefinite recognition of CE marked devices - GOV.UK 

The MHRA is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care. 

For media enquiries, please contact newscentre@mhra.gov.uk or call 020 3080 7651.

items.title: Cosmetic cowboys crackdown continues with new restrictions
items.summary: New rules to ensure that cosmetic procedures - including liquid Brazilian butt lifts, vampire facials and chemical peels - will be carried out by specific healthcare experts only Cosmetic surgery and other high-risk procedures banned for un
items.bodyHtml:
• New rules to ensure that cosmetic procedures - including liquid Brazilian butt lifts, vampire facials and chemical peels - will be carried out by specific healthcare experts only
  • Cosmetic surgery and other high-risk procedures banned for under 18s 
  • anyone who breaks these rules could be hit with a hefty unlimited fine 

The crackdown on cosmetic cowboys intensifies this week as the government announces new restrictions on cosmetic procedures, including liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels, to qualified healthcare experts only.

Under the new rules, anyone carrying out the highest-risk cosmetic procedures will need to be a qualified, trained and regulated professional, giving people confidence they’re in safe hands.

Fillers injected into parts of the body other than the face, including liquid BBLs, would be legally defined as cosmetic surgical procedures, meaning only doctors could perform them.

High-risk non-surgical or wellbeing treatments, including deep chemical peels, vampire facials, dermal micro-coring and some laser procedures would be restricted to:

  • doctors
  • dentists
  • some nurses, midwives and pharmacists (those who have completed an accredited training course which means they are legally authorised to prescribe medications to patients)

With surgical and non-surgical cosmetic procedures becoming increasingly blurred, the new rules will also close a dangerous loophole that has seen ill-qualified practitioners working out of hotel rooms performing high-risk procedures without regulatory oversight. 

Rogue providers who flout the proposals could be put before the courts under tough new criminal offences. Breaking the rules could see providers being hit with unlimited fines, or fixed penalties up to £4,000. 

Health Minister Karin Smyth said:

If you’re planning to undergo a major cosmetic procedure, you deserve to know you’re in safe hands - not risking your life with a rogue operator.

These changes mean that only properly trained professionals can carry out the most serious, high-risk procedures, and that young people will be shielded from treatments that can go badly wrong.

We want to drive cosmetic cowboys out of the market and raise standards across the board, giving reputable businesses a fair chance to thrive by helping people identify safe, qualified providers they can trust.

Victoria Brownlie MBE, Chief Policy and Sustainability Officer at the British Beauty Council, said:

Over a number of years, the line between a beauty treatment and a medical procedure has blurred. A lack of regulation in what has become a booming market has led to an exploitation of these gaps, placing members of the public at serious risk.

I believe this is a vital step towards the required regulation and commend the government for tackling this issue head-on. Their assurance that a licensing scheme for ‘lower risk’ treatments will follow is also much welcomed as a vital turning point to ensure the highest standards of competence and care across the beauty and aesthetics sector.

Ashton Collins, Director of Save Face, said:

We welcome this vital step towards protecting the public from the harm we have seen in recent years.

For too long, non-healthcare practitioners have exploited a regulatory loophole to carry out high-risk procedures, including liquid BBLs and facelifts, on members of the public. This has led to serious and life-threatening complications, including the death of Alice Webb, and victims have been left without justice.

Save Face has campaigned for tougher rules since 2023, so that those who flout them are held accountable. This consultation gives the public, practitioners, and experts the chance to help shape the final framework. We urge everyone to respond, and we look forward to the legislation being brought before Parliament so that it can be enacted as soon as possible to prevent further harm.

Dr Leah Totton, cosmetic doctor, said:

These proposed regulations are a welcome and long-overdue step towards protecting the public and safeguarding patients, particularly those under 18, who are a vulnerable group. Cosmetic treatments are medical treatments and things can, and do, go wrong, Patients deserve to know that the practitioner treating them is appropriately qualified.

High-risk cosmetic procedures should only be carried out by appropriately qualified and trained healthcare professionals. Medical practitioners have been calling for stronger regulation for years, and I hope these proposals mark a turning point in raising standards, protecting patients and restoring confidence in our industry.

New rules would stop under 18s having risky cosmetic or wellbeing treatments, while fillers for children are already restricted under a separate law.

The government is launching a consultation to ask clinicians, regulators, businesses, the public and other experts for their say on the draft regulations before plans go through the Parliamentary process, which is currently planned for spring 2027. 

Separate to the consultation, the government remains committed to implementing a licensing scheme to ensure that clinics delivering botulinum toxin products (more commonly known as Botox), lip filler and other lower-risk treatments meet strict safety standards, putting an end to backyard Botox clinics.

The new crackdown follows a string of reports of rogue, unregulated surgeries and procedures being carried out by unqualified practitioners, putting patients at serious risk of harm or even death.

The consultation on restrictions on the performance of high-risk cosmetic and wellbeing procedures in England is open until 13 January 2027.

items.title: Official warning over trustees’ mismanagement of founder’s legacy
items.summary: The three-year investigation found serious failings in the trustees’ governance of the charity, including in the financial management of a £5.7m legacy from its founder and the management of conflicts of interest and related-party transacti
items.bodyHtml:
The three-year investigation found serious failings in the trustees’ governance of the charity, including in the financial management of a £5.7m legacy from its founder and the management of conflicts of interest and related-party transactions. 

The Schwarzschild Foundation was established for the education and the relief of poverty for women and girls in the orthodox Jewish faith and was registered as a charitable trust in 2014.  

Following the death of the founder, Helga Schwarzschild, the charity became entitled to her estate, which included proceeds from the sale of her property and a property portfolio, the value of which was approximately £5.7 million.  

The inquiry was opened into the charitable trust in 2023 after the National Crime Agency identified £250,000 of the charity’s funds in a personal bank account under a trustee’s control. The charity’s lack of monitoring and verification of the end use of funds meant it would not have detected or recovered the funds independently. 

The trustees only verified the use of three other £250,000 grants after the Commission became involved. The inquiry found two grants of £250,000 each were awarded to organisations in which at least one trustee had unmanaged conflicts of interest. 

The inquiry also found unmanaged conflicts of interest between the charity and the companies for which it was sole shareholder, and in trustees’ businesses providing professional services to the charity.  

During the inquiry the Commission put in place a temporary, protective order preventing the charity’s trustees from entering into any transactions or making any payments for the charity without the regulator’s prior written approval.  

It also appointed Interim Managers to review the governance of the charity. The Interim Managers confirmed there had been no meaningful review of a £4 million portfolio of investment properties held on the charity’s behalf, such as property value or rental income, or whether the investments represented the best use of the charity’s funds.  

The inquiry found that due to the lack of proper policies, procedures and monitoring in place, the charity was exposed to a serious risk of misuse, misapplication or loss of funds. This was misconduct and / or mismanagement in the administration of the charity.  

The inquiry also found that trustees had failed to record their decision-making appropriately so could not evidence that decisions made in respect of grants and investments were in the best interest of the charity.  

Before closing the inquiry, the Commission issued an Official Warning to the charity for a breach of trust or duty and set out a comprehensive action plan the trustees must implement. 

Charity Commission Head of High Risk Compliance, Brian Wilson, said:

Good policies and procedures are fundamental components of effective charity governance. These, along with robust decision making, are the checks and balances that ensure a charity is well run and can demonstrate funds are being spent in its best interests.  

The serious gaps in governance at The Schwarzschild Foundation left it vulnerable and amounted to misconduct and / or mismanagement of the charity. Following the National Crime Agency’s initial detection of a £250,000 payment to a trustee’s bank account, the sum was returned to the Foundation and our inquiry forced checks on three more £250,000 grants. 

Robust checks should have been in place, not least as almost 80% of charities have an income of £250,000 or less so these funds could represent a significant boost to a charity’s income. 

While we have closed the inquiry, we will continue to monitor the charity’s implementation of the action plan.

The Commission produces a series of 5-minute guides for charity trustees, including managing finances, conflicts of interest and making decisions.  

ENDS 

Notes for editors: 

  1. The Charity Commission is the independent, non-ministerial government department that registers and regulates charities in England and Wales. Its ambition is to be an expert regulator that is fair, balanced, and independent so that charity can thrive. The Commission has a wide range of regulatory powers which it can use to support charities and protect charitable assets. Further information about the Charity Commission and its work is available at The Charity Commission - GOV.UK.   

  2. On 23 June 2023, the Charity Commission opened a statutory inquiry into the charity under section 46 of the Charities Act 2011 (‘the Act’) as a result of its regulatory concerns that there is or has been misconduct and  / or mismanagement in the administration of the charity. The inquiry closed on publication of the inquiry report.  

  3. A statutory inquiry is a legal power enabling the Commission to formally investigate matters of regulatory concern within a charity and to use protective powers to protect the charity and its beneficiaries, assets, or reputation. 

  4. The Commission does not investigate criminal allegations which are matters for the police. 

  5. An official warning ensures the charity or trustee(s) concerned knows that a breach, misconduct or mismanagement has taken place and that it needs to be rectified, and ensures they know what action they should take to stop the misconduct or mismanagement or to prevent a recurrence of it. There is more information about the Commission’s use of official warnings on GOV.UK.

  6. On 20 March 2024, the inquiry used its protective power under section 76(3)(g) of the Act, to appoint Edwina Turner and Catherine Gibbons, of Anthony Collins Solicitors LLP, as joint Interim Managers of the charity. Having completed the scope of their appointment, they were discharged on 20 June 2025 by an Order made under section 337(6) of the Act.

Press office

Email pressenquiries@charitycommission.gov.uk

Out of hours press office contact number: 07785 748787

The three-year investigation found serious failings in the trustees’ governance of the charity, including in the financial management of a £5.7m legacy from its founder and the management of conflicts of interest and related-party transactions. 

The Schwarzschild Foundation was established for the education and the relief of poverty for women and girls in the orthodox Jewish faith and was registered as a charitable trust in 2014.  

Following the death of the founder, Helga Schwarzschild, the charity became entitled to her estate, which included proceeds from the sale of her property and a property portfolio, the value of which was approximately £5.7 million.  

The inquiry was opened into the charitable trust in 2023 after the National Crime Agency identified £250,000 of the charity’s funds in a personal bank account under a trustee’s control. The charity’s lack of monitoring and verification of the end use of funds meant it would not have detected or recovered the funds independently.

The inquiry also found unmanaged conflicts of interest between the charity and the companies for which it was sole shareholder, and in trustees’ businesses providing professional services to the charity.

items.title: Jackdaw gas field gets green light
items.summary: The Energy Secretary has agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the licensed Jackdaw field The project will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from as early as the end of this month, helping h
items.bodyHtml:
• The Energy Secretary has agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the licensed Jackdaw field
  • The project will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from as early as the end of this month, helping heat millions of homes and protecting hundreds of jobs
  • New Energy Wealth Fund to be established by the Chancellor with a £2 billion downpayment to reinvest oil and gas revenues into the climate transition

Jackdaw will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from the end of this month, after the Energy Secretary agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the field. 

The Jackdaw decision is expected to increase domestic gas production by around 6% at its peak – supporting the UK’s gas supply over its lifespan of up to 11 years, boosting our energy security, protecting hundreds of jobs and adding an estimated £2.9 billion to the UK economy.

Recent events in the Middle East have triggered global energy shocks and pushed up bills for families across the country. At a time of global instability, homegrown energy can be a source of national strength.

The Chancellor is also announcing today the establishment of a new Energy Wealth Fund, which will use tax revenues from North Sea oil and gas to invest in renewable and low carbon energy projects and support the green transition.  Reflecting our commitment to the North Sea, this will start with an initial £2 billion injection of funding, with future revenues from the North Sea flowing into the fund over time.

The announcement comes ahead of the Budget, which will set out the government’s plan to deliver good growth in every postcode. By reinvesting Britain’s energy wealth in renewable and low carbon energy infrastructure, the Fund will unlock investment, back the industries of the future and create skilled jobs across Scotland and the UK.

This investment in renewable energy will substantially delink gas and electricity by the end of this Parliament. By investing in and building more renewable and low carbon power, gas will set the price of electricity less often, helping end Britain’s exposure to volatile international gas markets and help get bills down for good in the long term.

The Energy Secretary assessed among other points, that the Jackdaw project will not prevent the UK from being able to meet its legally binding limits on carbon emissions and achieve net-zero by 2050.

The heatwaves and extreme weather events experienced this year highlighted the importance of tackling the climate crisis. The government remains committed to the green transition and net zero – moving away from fossil fuels and towards renewable and nuclear energy. But even on the path to net zero, the UK will still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come.  

The decision is consistent with the government’s manifesto commitment not to issue any new licences to explore new fields while managing existing fields for the entirety of their lifespan. The Jackdaw gas field is already licensed and the North Sea Transition Authority’s decision to grant consent now gives the developer the green light to begin operations at the field.

It follows the Supreme Court’s ruling on the Finch case in 2024, which means North Sea operators are now required to consider the impact of burning the extracted oil and gas in environmental impact assessments. This meant the Energy Secretary had to consider a new environmental framework alongside all relevant factors in the case, including responses to the public consultation. 

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said:

Following careful consideration of all relevant factors I have agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at Jackdaw, which will begin to supply the UK with gas from this winter thanks to the highly skilled and vital North Sea workers.

This decision will support the country’s energy security with homegrown gas this winter and help minimise the UK’s use of imported higher emission fuels as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear.

The decision is compatible with our legally binding climate commitments, and we remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

I welcome the Energy Secretary’s decision, which will protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm this winter. At a time when people are really struggling, it’s right that we look in a responsible way at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help.

We’re committed to moving towards renewable energy and reaching net zero by 2050. But even on our ambitious climate path, we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come. That’s why we’re taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea. We’re also establishing a new  Energy Wealth Fund to invest in renewable energy, support the green transition and help reduce energy bills over the long-term.

Our approach will ensure we can boost our energy security, back British workers, ringfence future North Sea proceeds to speed up the green transition, hit our ambitious climate targets and - crucially - bring down bills.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:

I want Britain’s energy wealth to spark a new wave of clean power to work for the British people.

Since North Sea gas and oil were discovered decades ago, the benefit of our existing nation’s natural resources have not been turned into the long-term investment our country needs.

Through our new Energy Wealth Fund, we will invest in the clean energy industries of the future, creating jobs, driving growth and strengthening Britain’s energy security.

Secretary of State for Scotland Douglas Alexander said:

This decision to approve Jackdaw is a win for Aberdeen, a win for Scottish workers and a win for Britain’s energy security. The North East has helped power the country for half a century, and will continue to do so for decades to come.

This will harness the homegrown skills and assets we have in Scotland and right across the UK in a boost for the economy, as we continue to invest in and grow clean energy resources, and work towards the transition.

Stuart Payne, Chief Executive of the North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) said:

After robust scrutiny we have today granted consent for the Jackdaw Field development which allows the owners to proceed with their project and produce gas from the field upon completion of development work.

This project will support the UK’s energy security by providing domestically produced gas, generate tax revenues, safeguard supply chain jobs, use existing infrastructure, and have an emissions intensity well below the UK average.

The Energy Wealth Fund will support investment in the renewable and low carbon energy industries that will power Britain’s future. It will help ensure more value from Britain’s energy resources is invested for the long term, supporting the green transition and creating a lasting national asset for future generations.

Alongside supporting the North Sea oil and gas sector, the government will continue to invest in the new energy industries that will support Scotland’s long-term jobs and prosperity. Since 2024, the UK has seen more than £100 billion of investment in renewable and low carbon energy.  

 Most recently, Sumitomo announced the opening of a £350 million into a cable factory at the Port of Nigg earlier this week. And SSE yesterday confirmed that 400 skilled jobs will be supported across Scotland through its new supply chain contracts for the Berwick Bank B offshore wind farm.

The government is taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea that will support existing oil and gas production and back the highly skilled workforce as opportunities grow in renewables and wider sectors.

As announced last year, new Transitional Energy Certificates will allow for some oil and gas production in already-explored areas that are near licensed fields, linked via a tieback – ensuring existing fields can remain economically viable.

The government has therefore confirmed today that it is asking the regulator to consider urgent cases that could benefit from similar measures now, before legislation on these new certificates is in place. This will ensure the sector can support existing oil and gas fields, while still preventing exploration in new unlicensed areas. 

It comes as discussions with industry leaders begin on a refresh of the North Sea Transition Deal to ensure domestic oil and gas production continues to benefit the UK and build the energy industries of the future. First agreed in 2021, the deal aims to provide a clear path for the industry to support the UK in reaching net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, while protecting jobs and supporting energy security.

The changing nature of the North Sea basin also opens up new opportunities to expand the UK’s decommissioning sector – which is expected to support up to 25,000 skilled jobs over the next decade and attract up to £25.6 billion in investment, according to independent analysis.

To help unlock this potential, the government has launched a consultation on new guidance to support decommissioning of complex infrastructure. The government has also formally asked Shell to submit their Brent decommissioning programme for the Energy Secretary to consider, with the aim to unblock a longstanding decision process that has been under review since 2017.

Notes to editors

The Energy Secretary’s full decision document agreeing to the regulator granting consent for the production of gas at the licensed Jackdaw field is available here: Jackdaw Field Development.

The announcement from the North Sea Transition Authority is here: NSTA grants consent for Jackdaw.

The developer estimates that Jackdaw will create 27 new direct jobs and safeguard 273 existing jobs that would otherwise be lost. The developer also estimates that the project will add around £2.9 billion to the UK economy.

Over its lifetime, Jackdaw is estimated to produce gas with an energy equivalent to around 40 million barrels of oil.

The UK’s gas supply comes from a range of sources: 42% is sourced from the UK continental shelf; Norway’s continental shelf provides 37%; LNG accounts for 20%; and Interconnectors supply 1% (figures calculated from a 5-year average between 2021 to 2025.

A licence provides exclusivity over an area for oil and gas exploration and production, but does not, on its own, allow development to proceed. 

A consent is a separate approval required before a specific project can move ahead.  The North Sea Transition Authority decides whether to grant consent, but can only do so if the Secretary of State agrees, on the basis of an environmental impact assessment under the offshore EIA regulatory regime. 

Following the Supreme Court’s ruling on the Finch case in 2024, the government acted decisively last year to publish new guidance for the oil and gas sector on how environmental impacts of downstream emissions from oil and gas production should be assessed and opened-up the window for applications.

Following this guidance, the developer, Adura, submitted further information on the Jackdaw project, which has been subject to public notice periods. The Energy Secretary has considered all relevant information in the round in reaching the decision to agree that the regulator can grant consent.

The government’s manifesto committed to not revoke existing licences and to manage existing fields for the entirety of their lifespan, while not issuing new licences to explore new fields. 

Independent analysis from Redwater Insights shows that the UK’s decommissioning sector could support up to 25,000 skilled jobs over the next decade and attract up to £25.6 billion in investment.

Established within the National Wealth Fund, the Energy Wealth Fund will invest in renewable and low carbon energy infrastructure across the UK, helping unlock growth and support projects that will drive the country’s transition to a low-carbon economy.

Government estimates suggest that if the UK’s historical North Sea receipts of £200bn had been invested when North Sea oil production grew in the 1980s, a Sovereign Wealth Fund could now be worth approx. £1 trillion. Estimate produced by identifying total revenues from North Sea taxes since 1980-81 from published HMRC statistics, including offshore corporation tax, royalty, supplementary petroleum duty, petroleum revenue tax and the energy profits levy, uprating this total using a constant compounding rate and assuming no withdrawals.
items.bodyText:
The Energy Secretary has agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the licensed Jackdaw field
    The project will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from as early as the end of this month, helping heat millions of homes and protecting hundreds of jobs
    New Energy Wealth Fund to be established by the Chancellor with a £2 billion downpayment to reinvest oil and gas revenues into the climate transition
  


Jackdaw will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from the end of this month, after the Energy Secretary agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the field. 

The Jackdaw decision is expected to increase domestic gas production by around 6% at its peak – supporting the UK’s gas supply over its lifespan of up to 11 years, boosting our energy security, protecting hundreds of jobs and adding an estimated £2.9 billion to the UK economy.

Recent events in the Middle East have triggered global energy shocks and pushed up bills for families across the country. At a time of global instability, homegrown energy can be a source of national strength.

The Chancellor is also announcing today the establishment of a new Energy Wealth Fund, which will use tax revenues from North Sea oil and gas to invest in renewable and low carbon energy projects and support the green transition.  Reflecting our commitment to the North Sea, this will start with an initial £2 billion injection of funding, with future revenues from the North Sea flowing into the fund over time.

The announcement comes ahead of the Budget, which will set out the government’s plan to deliver good growth in every postcode. By reinvesting Britain’s energy wealth in renewable and low carbon energy infrastructure, the Fund will unlock investment, back the industries of the future and create skilled jobs across Scotland and the UK.

This investment in renewable energy will substantially delink gas and electricity by the end of this Parliament. By investing in and building more renewable and low carbon power, gas will set the price of electricity less often, helping end Britain’s exposure to volatile international gas markets and help get bills down for good in the long term.

The Energy Secretary assessed among other points, that the Jackdaw project will not prevent the UK from being able to meet its legally binding limits on carbon emissions and achieve net-zero by 2050.

The heatwaves and extreme weather events experienced this year highlighted the importance of tackling the climate crisis. The government remains committed to the green transition and net zero – moving away from fossil fuels and towards renewable and nuclear energy. But even on the path to net zero, the UK will still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come.  

The decision is consistent with the government’s manifesto commitment not to issue any new licences to explore new fields while managing existing fields for the entirety of their lifespan. The Jackdaw gas field is already licensed and the North Sea Transition Authority’s decision to grant consent now gives the developer the green light to begin operations at the field.

It follows the Supreme Court’s ruling on the Finch case in 2024, which means North Sea operators are now required to consider the impact of burning the extracted oil and gas in environmental impact assessments. This meant the Energy Secretary had to consider a new environmental framework alongside all relevant factors in the case, including responses to the public consultation. 

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said:


  Following careful consideration of all relevant factors I have agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at Jackdaw, which will begin to supply the UK with gas from this winter thanks to the highly skilled and vital North Sea workers.

  This decision will support the country’s energy security with homegrown gas this winter and help minimise the UK’s use of imported higher emission fuels as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear.

  The decision is compatible with our legally binding climate commitments, and we remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050.


Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

At a time when people are really struggling, it’s right that we look in a responsible way at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help.

  We’re committed to moving towards renewable energy and reaching net zero by 2050. But even on our ambitious climate path, we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come. That’s why we’re taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea.   Our approach will ensure we can boost our energy security, back British workers, ringfence future North Sea proceeds to speed up the green transition, hit our ambitious climate targets and - crucially - bring down bills.


Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:


  I want Britain’s energy wealth to spark a new wave of clean power to work for the British people.

  Since North Sea gas and oil were discovered decades ago, the benefit of our existing nation’s natural resources have not been turned into the long-term investment our country needs.

  Through our new Energy Wealth Fund, we will invest in the clean energy industries of the future, creating jobs, driving growth and strengthening Britain’s energy security.


Secretary of State for Scotland Douglas Alexander said:


  This decision to approve Jackdaw is a win for Aberdeen, a win for Scottish workers and a win for Britain’s energy security. The North East has helped power the country for half a century, and will continue to do so for decades to come.

  This will harness the homegrown skills and assets we have in Scotland and right across the UK in a boost for the economy, as we continue to invest in and grow clean energy resources, and work towards the transition.


Stuart Payne, Chief Executive of the North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) said:


  After robust scrutiny we have today granted consent for the Jackdaw Field development which allows the owners to proceed with their project and produce gas from the field upon completion of development work.

  This project will support the UK’s energy security by providing domestically produced gas, generate tax revenues, safeguard supply chain jobs, use existing infrastructure, and have an emissions intensity well below the UK average.

items.summary: 中新网兰州10月21日电 (记者 冯志军 高莹)“过去，会宁山大沟深、干旱少雨，种地靠天吃饭，产业单一、收入微薄，是典型的贫困地区。”甘肃白银市会宁县农业技术推广中心主任薛俊武近日向记者表示，90年来，会宁民众发扬“不怕苦、敢奋斗”的长征精神，因地制宜发展特色产业。如今，小杂粮、马铃薯、牛羊养殖、高原蔬菜、优质瓜果等特色产业规模化发展，产业链越来越完善。

items.summary: 不少市民外出时会选择顺风车，希望找到路线一致的车主，分摊出行成本。但现实中，部分接单车主并非顺路出行，而是像专职网约车司机一样高频接单。南京交通执法部门就曾查处过此类案例。一名车主日均接单超20单，却主张自身属于“顺风合乘”。顺风车，也就是私人小客车合乘，本是一种非营利性共享出行模式，但如今，大量职业化接单行为，让“互助合乘”异化为变相营运。真假顺风车交织混杂，乘客乘车时很难分辨。

items.title: 长征具有跨越时代与国界的启示意义（国际论坛）
items.summary: 一个民族的历史，往往由一些跨越时代的关键时刻所书写，并成为后来者理解现实、思考未来的重要思想来源。中国共产党领导的长征正是这样一段历史。长征实现了中国共产党和中国革命事业的重大转折，体现了在极端困难条件下保持战略定力，同时根据现实变化不断调整方法和路径的应变能力。90年后的今天，长征所蕴含的战略智慧，对于应对当下充满不确定性的国际环境具有重要启示意义。

items.title: 10,000 young people to get foot in the door of Britain's tech sector as work placements rolled out across the country
items.summary: Young people looking for their first job will benefit from 10,000 new work experience placements to open doors into the UK’s digital and tech sector All secondary schools are now able to access government programme TechFirst, with an ambiti
items.bodyHtml:
• Young people looking for their first job will benefit from 10,000 new work experience placements to open doors into the UK’s digital and tech sector
  • All secondary schools are now able to access government programme TechFirst, with an ambition to reach 1 million students by 2028 - a year earlier than planned - including 400,000 from the most disadvantaged schools
  • The rollout builds on the PM’s call to arms to employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to ensure all young people have vital exposure to the workplace between 14 and 16

10,000 young people will get the chance to get experience under their belt, build up their CVs, and get their foot in the door of Britain’s digital and tech sector.

With nearly 1 million young people not in employment, education or training, Britain faces a generational challenge, requiring a generational shake up in how young people get the right skills and experience. That means creating more choices, more chances and more pathways for young people to chart their course from learning to earning.

Some of Britain’s key tech employers, including Microsoft, Cisco, IBM, Cognizant, AtkinsRéalis, Arm, Kainos and QinetiQ, are backing the drive, opening up 10,000 opportunities over the next three years.

We are also calling on more employers to join them in offering new roles, with an aim of 20,000 entry-level jobs each year, as part of our mission to give young people in Britain, particularly those not in education, employment or training, a clear line of sight into a job.

This comes on top of support for at least 1 million secondary students – including 400,000 from disadvantaged schools – to get the skills and opportunities needed to build a future in tech, as government announces the rollout of the TechFirst skills programme across the UK.

Secondary students will receive workshops, skills sessions, career talks, industry workplace experiences, tech clubs, inter-school competitions, and access to the digital learning platform Ada Computer Science – giving every UK student the chance to build tech skills that lead to better jobs, higher earnings and brighter futures. 

Only last week, the Prime Minister said that the challenges facing young people cannot be solved through traditional welfare reform alone. 

Instead, change requires a whole-system approach, working in partnership with mayors, local leaders and employers to create more work opportunities and intervening earlier to tackle the wider systemic reasons young people fall out of education, training and employment in the first place.

The Prime Minister also made a call to arms to employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to ensure all young people have vital exposure to the workplace between 14 and 16. This could include spending time in key sectors including accountancy firms, digital media companies and construction companies. Employers can contact their local Careers Hubs to pledge new work experience placements.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

It’s one of the biggest frustrations when you’re starting out. Everyone tells you that you need experience to get a job, but nobody gives you the chance to get that experience in the first place.

Thousands of young people will get the chance to get their foot in the door in one of the UK’s biggest growth sectors, build their confidence and skills, and get something meaningful on their CV.

Our job is to back this generation, open those doors and give every young person a fair chance to build a good future for themselves, wherever they come from.

Last week, the Prime Minister also said that the state is not set up to meet the needs of young people today, as they face new challenges in an age of social media and AI, rising costs and a more volatile and uncertain global context. He warned that the longer young people are left adrift from education, employment or training, the more likely they are to become disconnected from society, damaging not only their own prospects but the strength and cohesion of our communities. 

Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Lisa Nandy, said:

Our country is grappling a generational challenge - we cannot and will not let our young people be locked out of the British workforce.

Getting a good job in our thriving digital and tech industry shouldn’t be determined by where you live or what school you go to. Talent is everywhere. Opportunity is not.

That’s why we’re making it easier for young people to build the skills and experience that lead to a fulfilling career through our TechFirst youth programme and Digital and Tech Skills Deal. Young people will be able to develop tech skills and gain work experience in the sector while at school, and we’re ensuring the industry then leaves its doors open for them when they finish education, with proper job opportunities and career pathways.

We’re wrapping our arms around the next generation, making sure they get the skills and opportunities that match their talent and ambition, helping a whole generation thrive.

This comes as DCMS publishes the Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan, setting a target of 20,000 entry level jobs a year, aligning Government, industry and education providers to work collaboratively to build the skills and opportunities people will need for the future roles of the UK’s digital and tech sector. 

The plan includes a new commitment to provide workplace experiences to help open the door to the sector - launching with an initial 10,000 experiences on offer from TechFirst industry partners.

Government is now putting the call out to employers across the tech sector to sign up as a Skills Deal partner and offer digital and tech work experiences.

The publication of the Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan follows the publication of the Professional and Business Services and Construction Jobs Plans on Monday, which marked the start of a week of Jobs Plans, with the Defence Jobs Plan due later this week.

Together, these Industrial Strategy Jobs Plans are opening up routes into good jobs while building the skilled workforce Britain needs to grow and reindustrialise. Bringing government and industry together, they will create more apprenticeship, training and vocational opportunities, helping more people access rewarding careers in the sectors that will power future economic growth.

The plans are being published ahead of the forthcoming Milburn Review into opportunities for young people and form part of the Modern Industrial Strategy, which is backing the industries where Britain can lead globally while ensuring people across the country benefit from economic growth and industrial renewal.

Minister for Skills Baroness Jacqui Smith said:

Every young person deserves the chance to build a career they’re proud of, whatever their background and wherever they live.

TechFirst helps make that possible, giving students the skills, confidence and experience they need to see a future for themselves in the sector.

Alongside our Youth Guarantee, which aims to offer every young person the chance to earn or learn, programmes like this mean that ambition is matched by real opportunity with the right support at the right time.

The TechFirst programme has been designed for all young people, but will also work to boost skills for underrepresented groups in tech, including women and girls, and young people from disadvantaged areas.

This follows the Prime Minister’s announcement last week to give young people a direct route into skilled, well-paid rail careers. Great British Railways will open up 600 foundation apprenticeships over the next 4 years for 16 to 21 year olds, offering a chance to earn while they learn in an industry where currently less than 7% of the workforce is under 25.

The package also builds on Government work strengthening digital and media literacy across the curriculum to help young people navigate the online world confidently, evaluate information critically and tackle misinformation and disinformation. Alongside this, reforms to computing education, including a new Computing GCSE, will ensure all pupils develop the digital and AI skills needed for future jobs and careers.

These are underpinned by wider government action to put technical education on a par with academic learning and ensure more young people have access to high-quality technical education. As well as the UK’s world-leading universities, Technical Excellence Colleges, new V Levels, expanded T Levels, and new Vocational GCSEs, all helping arm young people with the skills and confidence for the world of work.

NOTES TO EDITORS:

  • According to Skills England, Sector Skills Needs Assessment – Digital and Technologies (June 2026), 800,000 digital and tech roles needing filling by 2035.
  • As part of the Digital and Tech Sector Jobs Plan, government aims for employers to collectively create or fill 20,000 entry-level roles each year. This may involve some employers establishing new positions, while others fill existing entry-level vacancies they might not otherwise have prioritised.
  • Earlier this month, government opened registration to the first ever TechFirst Girls Competition in collaboration with IBM, giving girls across the UK the chance to take on tech challenges, build their confidence, and see what a future career in technology could look like for them. Schools can register for the Tech First Girls Competition here: Welcome - TechFirst Girls Competition

Ada platform delivered by Raspberry Pi Foundation - Every student aged 11 to 18 will be able to access the Ada Computer Science online platform delivered in partnership between UK Government and the Raspberry Pi Foundation. The platform will feature curriculum-linked tech lessons, so no student misses out on the chance to build the skills they need to thrive in the workplace. From the end of the 26/27 academic year the platform will replace the Issac platform currently funded by the DfE as part of the National Centre for Computing Education. The platform covers everything from coding and AI to cyber security, letting students learn at their own pace and build real, practical skills alongside their regular lessons.

items.bodyText:
Young people looking for their first job will benefit from 10,000 new work experience placements to open doors into the UK’s digital and tech sector
    All secondary schools are now able to access government programme TechFirst, with an ambition to reach 1 million students by 2028 - a year earlier than planned - including 400,000 from the most disadvantaged schools
    The rollout builds on the PM’s call to arms to employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to ensure all young people have vital exposure to the workplace between 14 and 16
  


10,000 young people will get the chance to get experience under their belt, build up their CVs, and get their foot in the door of Britain’s digital and tech sector.

With nearly 1 million young people not in employment, education or training, Britain faces a generational challenge, requiring a generational shake up in how young people get the right skills and experience. That means creating more choices, more chances and more pathways for young people to chart their course from learning to earning.

Some of Britain’s key tech employers, including Microsoft, Cisco, IBM, Cognizant, AtkinsRéalis, Arm, Kainos and QinetiQ, are backing the drive, opening up 10,000 opportunities over the next three years.

We are also calling on more employers to join them in offering new roles, with an aim of 20,000 entry-level jobs each year, as part of our mission to give young people in Britain, particularly those not in education, employment or training, a clear line of sight into a job.

This comes on top of support for at least 1 million secondary students – including 400,000 from disadvantaged schools – to get the skills and opportunities needed to build a future in tech, as government announces the rollout of the TechFirst skills programme across the UK.

Secondary students will receive workshops, skills sessions, career talks, industry workplace experiences, tech clubs, inter-school competitions, and access to the digital learning platform Ada Computer Science – giving every UK student the chance to build tech skills that lead to better jobs, higher earnings and brighter futures. 

Only last week, the Prime Minister said that the challenges facing young people cannot be solved through traditional welfare reform alone. 

Instead, change requires a whole-system approach, working in partnership with mayors, local leaders and employers to create more work opportunities and intervening earlier to tackle the wider systemic reasons young people fall out of education, training and employment in the first place.

The Prime Minister also made a call to arms to employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to ensure all young people have vital exposure to the workplace between 14 and 16. This could include spending time in key sectors including accountancy firms, digital media companies and construction companies. Employers can contact their local Careers Hubs to pledge new work experience placements.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:


  It’s one of the biggest frustrations when you’re starting out. Everyone tells you that you need experience to get a job, but nobody gives you the chance to get that experience in the first place.

  Thousands of young people will get the chance to get their foot in the door in one of the UK’s biggest growth sectors, build their confidence and skills, and get something meaningful on their CV.

  Our job is to back this generation, open those doors and give every young person a fair chance to build a good future for themselves, wherever they come from.


Last week, the Prime Minister also said that the state is not set up to meet the needs of young people today, as they face new challenges in an age of social media and AI, rising costs and a more volatile and uncertain global context. He warned that the longer young people are left adrift from education, employment or training, the more likely they are to become disconnected from society, damaging not only their own prospects but the strength and cohesion of our communities. 

Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Lisa Nandy, said:


  Our country is grappling a generational challenge - we cannot and will not let our young people be locked out of the British workforce.

  Getting a good job in our thriving digital and tech industry shouldn’t be determined by where you live or what school you go to. Talent is everywhere. Opportunity is not.

  That’s why we’re making it easier for young people to build the skills and experience that lead to a fulfilling career through our TechFirst youth programme and Digital and Tech Skills Deal. Young people will be able to develop tech skills and gain work experience in the sector while at school, and we’re ensuring the industry then leaves its doors open for them when they finish education, with proper job opportunities and career pathways.

  We’re wrapping our arms around the next generation, making sure they get the skills and opportunities that match their talent and ambition, helping a whole generation thrive.


This comes as DCMS publishes the Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan, setting a target of 20,000 entry level jobs a year, aligning Government, industry and education providers to work collaboratively to build the skills and opportunities people will need for the future roles of the UK’s digital and tech sector. 

The plan includes a new commitment to provide workplace experiences to help open the door to the sector - launching with an initial 10,000 experiences on offer from TechFirst industry partners.

Government is now putting the call out to employers across the tech sector to sign up as a Skills Deal partner and offer digital and tech work experiences.

The publication of the Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan follows the publication of the Professional and Business Services and Construction Jobs Plans on Monday, which marked the start of a week of Jobs Plans, with the Defence Jobs Plan due later this week.

Together, these Industrial Strategy Jobs Plans are opening up routes into good jobs while building the skilled workforce Britain needs to grow and reindustrialise. Bringing government and industry together, they will create more apprenticeship, training and vocational opportunities, helping more people access rewarding careers in the sectors that will power future economic growth.

The plans are being published ahead of the forthcoming Milburn Review into opportunities for young people and form part of the Modern Industrial Strategy, which is backing the industries where Britain can lead globally while ensuring people across the country benefit from economic growth and industrial renewal.

Minister for Skills Baroness Jacqui Smith said:


  Every young person deserves the chance to build a career they’re proud of, whatever their background and wherever they live.

  TechFirst helps make that possible, giving students the skills, confidence and experience they need to see a future for themselves in the sector.

  Alongside our Youth Guarantee, which aims to offer every young person the chance to earn or learn, programmes like this mean that ambition is matched by real opportunity with the right support at the right time.


The TechFirst programme has been designed for all young people, but will also work to boost skills for underrepresented groups in tech, including women and girls, and young people from disadvantaged areas.

This follows the Prime Minister’s announcement last week to give young people a direct route into skilled, well-paid rail careers. Great British Railways will open up 600 foundation apprenticeships over the next 4 years for 16 to 21 year olds, offering a chance to earn while they learn in an industry where currently less than 7% of the workforce is under 25.

The package also builds on Government work strengthening digital and media literacy across the curriculum to help young people navigate the online world confidently, evaluate information critically and tackle misinformation and disinformation. Alongside this, reforms to computing education, including a new Computing GCSE, will ensure all pupils develop the digital and AI skills needed for future jobs and careers.

These are underpinned by wider government action to put technical education on a par with academic learning and ensure more young people have access to high-quality technical education. As well as the UK’s world-leading universities, Technical Excellence Colleges, new V Levels, expanded T Levels, and new Vocational GCSEs, all helping arm young people with the skills and confidence for the world of work.

NOTES TO EDITORS:


  According to Skills England, Sector Skills Needs Assessment – Digital and Technologies (June 2026), 800,000 digital and tech roles needing filling by 2035.
  As part of the Digital and Tech Sector Jobs Plan, government aims for employers to collectively create or fill 20,000 entry-level roles each year. This may involve some employers establishing new positions, while others fill existing entry-level vacancies they might not otherwise have prioritised.
  Earlier this month, government opened registration to the first ever TechFirst Girls Competition in collaboration with IBM, giving girls across the UK the chance to take on tech challenges, build their confidence, and see what a future career in technology could look like for them. Schools can register for the Tech First Girls Competition here: Welcome - TechFirst Girls Competition



Ada platform delivered by Raspberry Pi Foundation
- Every student aged 11 to 18 will be able to access the Ada Computer Science online platform delivered in partnership between UK Government and the Raspberry Pi Foundation. The platform will feature curriculum-linked tech lessons, so no student misses out on the chance to build the skills they need to thrive in the workplace. From the end of the 26/27 academic year the platform will replace the Issac platform currently funded by the DfE as part of the National Centre for Computing Education. The platform covers everything from coding and AI to cyber security, letting students learn at their own pace and build real, practical skills alongside their regular lessons. 

TechFirst Delivery Partners:

Teachers can sign their school up to the TechFirst Youth Programme by emailing their regional delivery partner: 
- North East: TechFirst@rtcnorth.co.uk 
- North West: TechFirst@in4group.co.uk 
- Yorkshire & Humber: TechFirst@rtcnorth.co.uk 
- East Midlands: TechFirst@in4group.co.uk 
- West Midlands: TechFirst@digitalinnovators.co.uk 
- East of England: TechFirst@techeducators.co.uk 
- London: TechFirst@stem.org.uk 
- South East: TechFirst@stem.org.uk 
- South West: TechFirst@techspark.co 
- Wales: Wales@cyberfirstschools.co.uk 
- Northern Ireland: TechFirst@belfastmet.ac.uk
- Scotland: TechFirst@EducationScotland.gov.scot

Digital and Technologies Skills Deal
- Current Digital and Tech Skills Deal partners: ARM, Cisco, AtkinsRéalis, Cognizant, IBM, Kainos, Microsoft, Qinetiq. Employers across the tech sector can sign up as a Skills Deal partner to offer digital and tech work experiences here: TechFirst Community Sign Up

TechFirst Women’s programme
- Government will also support women at all career stages, from early-career professionals to career changers and returners, to move into paid jobs in artificial intelligence, cyber security and other high-growth technology sectors. 
- Through the TechFirst Women’s Programme, 300 women across the UK will receive mentoring, skills development and matching with live vacancies, with the aim of securing paid roles lasting at least six months by March 2027.
