items.title: Nottingham's first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair attracts hundreds of young jobseekers
items.summary: The fair was hosted at Notts County Football Club, and highlighted opportunities for young people at almost 65 of the UK’s largest businesses, including Amazon, Boots, and Puregym. More than 600 vacancies were on offer, as employers connect
items.bodyHtml:
• The fair was hosted at Notts County Football Club, and highlighted opportunities for young people at almost 65 of the UK’s largest businesses, including Amazon, Boots, and Puregym.  

  • More than 600 vacancies were on offer, as employers connected with young people to showcase jobs, apprenticeships and training opportunities in the region. 

  • Jobs fair is part of Government’s wider youth employment support, backed by £2.5 billion investment to help young people build a strong career path.  

Hundreds of young people attended Nottingham’s first Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair, to explore opportunities for jobs, apprenticeships, training and work experience at some of the UK’s largest businesses.  

The Youth Guarantee is the Government’s package of support aimed at giving every young person the chance to earn or learn, and the Jobs Fairs have become a key part of this, taking place across the country.  

At Notts County’s Meadow Lane Stadium, employers attended from across retail, manufacturing, hospitality and healthcare sectors, including Amazon, Boots, East Midlands Railways, and Nottinghamshire Healthcare Foundation Trust. 

During the event, around 770 young people attended, many receiving hands on advice on looking for job opportunities, completing applications, and preparing for interviews, giving them the confidence and skills they need to take the first step towards employment.  

Minister for Employment Andrew Western said:  

Hundreds of young people are taking their first step into employment at our Youth Guarantee Jobs Fairs, meeting employers with live vacancies and securing interviews on the spot. 

By delivering Youth Guarantee Jobs Fairs in each area across the country, we’re backing young people and giving them the best possible start. 

Workshops were held to ensure young people are able to make the most of the opportunities available to them, with one session seeing Google help jobseekers understand how to effectively use AI to enhance their CV, prepare for interviews and plan their career goals. 

Youth Guarantee Jobs Fairs have already been delivered in Blackpool, Glasgow, Cardiff, London and Leeds. These events have resulted in over 1,000 young people already moving into jobs, work experiences or training opportunities. 

The event reinforced the Government’s commitment that all young people under 25 should be offered one of the following high-quality pathways:  

  • Employment  

  • Continued education  

  • An apprenticeship  

  • A traineeship, a work experience placement or Sector-Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP) 

Nottingham Jobs Fair is the latest example of the Government’s work to support young people into employment or training. The youth employment support package, backed by £2.5 billion investment, will support almost one million young people, and create 500,000 opportunities.  

The Government will deliver at least one Youth Guarantee Jobs Fair in every region of Great Britain, giving young people across the country direct access to opportunities near them.

items.title: Over 100,000 job and training opportunities a year to give young people a route into Britain’s growth industries as part of industrial strategy
items.summary: Young people to benefit from thousands more routes into skilled careers, including 22,400 new under-25 apprenticeships a year in professional and business services and 40,000 construction placements every year Industrial Strategy plans come
items.bodyHtml:
• Young people to benefit from thousands more routes into skilled careers, including 22,400 new under-25 apprenticeships a year in professional and business services and 40,000 construction placements every year

  • Industrial Strategy plans come ahead of Milburn review into young people, opening up routes into good jobs while building the skilled workforce Britain needs to grow and reindustrialise 

  • Devolution at heart of plans, with mayors and local skills partnerships helping shape training around the jobs and skills their areas need

Young people will get thousands more opportunities to start skilled careers in some of Britain’s fastest-growing industries, as government and businesses join forces to expand apprenticeships, work experience and training. 

Industrial Strategy Jobs Plans published today for Professional and Business Services and Construction will support 22,400 new under-25 apprenticeships a year in businesses such as accountants, legal services, and consultants. This will come alongside 40,000 construction placements annually as part of a previously announced construction industry ambition to create 100,000 job opportunities a year. 

They mark the start of a week of Jobs Plans, with further plans for Digital and Technologies and Defence due to be published later this week. The Defence Jobs Plan will help deliver thousands of opportunities for young people, including an increase in the number of people supported through apprenticeship programmes in the defence sector to at least 14,000 annually by 2035. 

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: 

Reindustrialising Britain means giving workers the skills they need to get good jobs in growing industries. Too many young people are being denied the chance to get a foot on the career ladder. 

These Jobs Plans bring government and industry together to change that, opening up more apprenticeships, training and vocational routes into rewarding careers. Our Modern Industrial Strategy is backing the industries where Britain can lead and making sure people in every part of the country benefit from our industrial renewal.” 

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said:

Too many young people have been locked out of opportunities for too long. These commitments will help change that by creating clear pathways into apprenticeships, training and good jobs.

It’s encouraging to see even more industries backing young people with new opportunities to gain the skills, training and experience needed to succeed in the growing sectors of our economy.

By working hand in hand with employers, we’re building a skills system that meets the needs of modern industry while delivering our Youth Guarantee and helping more young people build rewarding careers.

From accountancy and law to bricklaying, engineering and defence, the plans will create clearer routes into skilled careers while helping businesses recruit the workforce they need to grow. 

Coming ahead of the final Milburn review into young people and employment, the plans will help connect more young people, including those not in education, employment or training, with opportunities to earn, learn and build a career. 

By bringing government, businesses and local areas together behind investment, skills and good jobs, the plans will also support the drive to reindustrialise Britain and spread the benefits of growth across the country. 

The Jobs Plans will put local partnerships at the heart of tackling skills shortages, with mayors, employers and Local Skills Improvement Plans shaping stronger routes into work through apprenticeships, work experience and vocational training. 

The Plans include:

Professional and Business Services: 

  • PBS firms have committed to recruiting 22,400 new apprentices aged under 25 each year over the next five years, alongside a 20% increase in work experience opportunities for young people. The sector will also establish systems to measure and track recruitment and support for young people not in education, employment or training. 
  • Opportunities will range from accountancy, business and law to AI, cyber security and data analytics, with commitments supported by leading employers and representative organisations across the PBS sector. 
  • Employers will support good jobs and workforce development through commitments including wider adoption of the Living Wage, a new PBS Good Jobs Standard, AI literacy training and tracking greater salary transparency in early-career recruitment. 

Construction: 

  • Industry will strengthen workforce planning for construction, identifying jobs and skills needs nationally, regionally and locally, with sector-specific plans for sectors including homebuilding, infrastructure, repair and maintenance, and professional and technical roles. *Major projects and new technology will be used to boost skills, productivity and job quality, including stronger employment and skills outcomes through procurement and social value, and preparing workers for AI and industrialised construction.
  • A Construction Apprenticeship Network will be created to boost apprentice recruitment and participation by smaller firms.
  • Opportunities will span skilled trades such as bricklaying, carpentry, electrical work and plumbing, alongside careers in engineering, surveying, planning and construction management, supported by industry bodies including the Construction Skills Mission Board and the Construction Leadership Council.

Defence: 

  • Following September’s agreement, defence firms will expand work experience and pathways for young people not in education employment or training by 25%.  

  • Industry will also introduce a “no wrong door” approach to help suitable candidates access opportunities across the defence supply chain. 

This is supported by the government’s £2.5 billion youth employment package, which will deliver almost one million opportunities for young people to earn or learn through apprenticeships, work experience and training.

The apprenticeship system is being pivoted towards the next generation, including 50,000 additional apprenticeships for young people and a new incentive of up to £2,000 for SMEs that take on a 16 to 24-year-old apprentice. Businesses will also be supported to back young talent through the continued National Insurance exemption for under-21s and apprentices under 25.

These plans are also underpinned by wider government action to put technical education on a par with academic learning and ensure more young people have access to high-quality technical education. Alongside the UK’s world-leading universities, Technical Excellence Colleges, new V Levels and expanded T Levels, and new Vocational GCSEs, will arm young people with the skills and confidence for the world of work.

Phil Smith, Chair of Skills England and member of the Industrial Strategy Advisory Council, said:  

World class apprenticeships and skills training will be absolutely vital to supporting thousands more young people into rewarding careers and making sure these Jobs Plans deliver for key industries and sectors. That includes through new foundation apprenticeships, for people starting out their careers, and shorter apprenticeship units to help them develop fast once they’re in work.  

Bringing government, businesses and local areas together through these plans makes perfect sense. It reflects the collaborative approach now being taken to ensure the skills system delivers what businesses and our emerging workforce needs.

Notes to editors 

  • The new plans build on Jobs Plans already published for Financial Services, Clean Energy Industries and Life Sciences. Jobs Plans are being developed across all eight growth-driving sectors identified in the Modern Industrial Strategy, as well as Construction, complementing the Sector Plans published in 2025. 

  • The Advanced Manufacturing and Creative Industries Jobs Plans will follow shortly, setting out further action to build the workforce needed for Britain’s industrial renewal. 

  • The latest Industrial Strategy quarterly update shows progress across the eight growth-driving sectors, including over £1 billion of automotive investment supporting more than 5,000 jobs, over £3 billion of public-private investment in Life Sciences since publication of the Sector Plan, and a £600 million package for British aerospace, including £500 million for cutting-edge R&D. It also highlights £1.5 billion committed by ScottishPower to repower Whitelee windfarm, £800 million from EDF and Centrica to refurbish Sizewell B, and a £26 billion programme to modernise Royal Navy bases. 

  • On average, jobs in the eight Industrial Strategy priority sectors pay around £8,000 more a year than jobs across the wider economy. 

  • The government is also making reforms to computing education, including a new Computing GCSE, will ensure all pupils develop the digital and AI skills needed for future jobs and careers.

    Following September’s agreement, defence firms will expand work experience and pathways for young people not in education employment or training by 25%.  
  
  
    Industry will also introduce a “no wrong door” approach to help suitable candidates access opportunities across the defence supply chain. 
  


This is supported by the government’s £2.5 billion youth employment package, which will deliver almost one million opportunities for young people to earn or learn through apprenticeships, work experience and training.

The apprenticeship system is being pivoted towards the next generation, including 50,000 additional apprenticeships for young people and a new incentive of up to £2,000 for SMEs that take on a 16 to 24-year-old apprentice. Businesses will also be supported to back young talent through the continued National Insurance exemption for under-21s and apprentices under 25.

These plans are also underpinned by wider government action to put technical education on a par with academic learning and ensure more young people have access to high-quality technical education. Alongside the UK’s world-leading universities, Technical Excellence Colleges, new V Levels and expanded T Levels, and new Vocational GCSEs, will arm young people with the skills and confidence for the world of work.

Phil Smith, Chair of Skills England and member of the Industrial Strategy Advisory Council, said:  


  World class apprenticeships and skills training will be absolutely vital to supporting thousands more young people into rewarding careers and making sure these Jobs Plans deliver for key industries and sectors. That includes through new foundation apprenticeships, for people starting out their careers, and shorter apprenticeship units to help them develop fast once they’re in work.  

  Bringing government, businesses and local areas together through these plans makes perfect sense. It reflects the collaborative approach now being taken to ensure the skills system delivers what businesses and our emerging workforce needs.


Notes to editors 


  
    The new plans build on Jobs Plans already published for Financial Services, Clean Energy Industries and Life Sciences. Jobs Plans are being developed across all eight growth-driving sectors identified in the Modern Industrial Strategy, as well as Construction, complementing the Sector Plans published in 2025. 
  
  
    The Advanced Manufacturing and Creative Industries Jobs Plans will follow shortly, setting out further action to build the workforce needed for Britain’s industrial renewal. 
  
  
    The latest Industrial Strategy quarterly update shows progress across the eight growth-driving sectors, including over £1 billion of automotive investment supporting more than 5,000 jobs, over £3 billion of public-private investment in Life Sciences since publication of the Sector Plan, and a £600 million package for British aerospace, including £500 million for cutting-edge R&D. It also highlights £1.5 billion committed by ScottishPower to repower Whitelee windfarm, £800 million from EDF and Centrica to refurbish Sizewell B, and a £26 billion programme to modernise Royal Navy bases. 
  
  
    On average, jobs in the eight Industrial Strategy priority sectors pay around £8,000 more a year than jobs across the wider economy. 
  
  
    The government is also making reforms to computing education, including a new Computing GCSE, will ensure all pupils develop the digital and AI skills needed for future jobs and careers.

items.title: UK regulator brings new AI and MedTech agenda to AdvaMed
items.summary: Speaking at the conference on Tuesday 20 October, Jessica Paulsen, MHRA Deputy Director for AI and Software, will outline the UK regulator’s developing approach to software and AI-enabled medical devices, including more flexible lifecycle r
items.bodyHtml:
Speaking at the conference on Tuesday 20 October, Jessica Paulsen, MHRA Deputy Director for AI and Software, will outline the UK regulator’s developing approach to software and AI-enabled medical devices, including more flexible lifecycle regulation, regulatory sandboxes and closer international collaboration. 

She is speaking on following the publication of the MHRA 2030 Strategy, which sets out plans to modernise regulation for an era of AI and personalised medicine. For MedTech, this includes creating a modern, adaptive framework for AI as a medical device, establishing a new MHRA Centre for AI and Digital Health, improving device data and traceability, and expanding reliance and recognition routes with trusted international regulators, including the FDA.  

The MHRA 2030 strategy sets an ambition for the MHRA to deliver a global standard for safe and agile regulation of MedTech and AI by 2030, supporting faster access to innovative technologies while strengthening patient safety.  This month, the UK Government accepted all 44 recommendations of the NHS doctor-led independent National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, supporting a more proportionate, lifecycle-based approach to AI regulation. 

The MHRA is already testing this approach through its AI Airlock, its regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled medical devices. It is complemented by a series of new regional partnerships including with NHS London and Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, leveraging the UK’s unique healthcare system and academic excellence to test innovative technologies in real health settings and generate evidence to inform future regulatory approaches. 

Together, this work will help the MHRA develop regulation that can respond to AI-enabled devices that evolve throughout their lifecycle, while giving developers greater clarity on regulatory requirements. 

Jessica Paulsen, MHRA Deputy Director for AI and Software, said: 

“AI is changing medical technology, and regulation must keep pace. In the UK we are moving from policy into practice, using initiatives like AI Airlock to build a more proportionate, lifecycle-based approach. 

“These are global technologies, so close collaboration with the FDA and other regulators will be critical to giving innovators greater clarity while maintaining strong protections for patients.” 

The MHRA is simultaneously putting new infrastructure behind its relationship with the FDA. The MHRA-FDA Pioneer Programme, announced in June, establishes dedicated reciprocal liaison roles within the two regulators. The programme is designed to deepen day-to-day collaboration, scientific exchange and coordination on emerging regulatory challenges, including medical devices and AI. Both agencies will continue to make independent regulatory decisions. 

The initiative builds on existing UK-US work on medical technology and AI. At AdvaMed in 2025, the MHRA set out ambitions to strengthen regulatory alignment and reciprocity with the FDA, reduce transatlantic barriers to market access and explore greater use of international reliance routes, including for devices already approved by the FDA.  

The MHRA is now recruiting a Regional Deputy Director of US Partnerships, based in Washington, D.C., who will serve as the MHRA’s dedicated Liaison Officer to the FDA under the Pioneer Programme. The senior role is intended to deepen the relationship with the FDA, strengthen scientific and regulatory collaboration, and build connections between the UK and US life sciences ecosystems.  

The appointment forms part of a wider MHRA ambition not simply to maintain a US presence, but to build relationships that deliver for patients, innovation and the UK’s position in global life sciences.  

Alongside AI and international collaboration, the MHRA is progressing wider medical device reform, including improved post-market surveillance and proposed legislative changes to support a more responsive future regulatory framework.   

The overall direction is set out in the MHRA 2030 Strategy announcement, alongside recent action on the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, details on the London and Manchester health innovation sandbox and wider regulatory reform announcements made recently by the UK regulator. 

Notes to Editors 

  • The MHRA is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care. 

  • For media enquiries, please contact newscentre@mhra.gov.uk or call 020 3080 7651.

items.title: Troubles Bill strengthened to deliver greater truth and accountability for victims and better protections for veterans
items.summary: The Government will today [Monday 19 October] strengthen the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill through a substantial package of amendments designed to deliver greater truth and accountability for victims and families, while providing clear pro
items.bodyHtml:
The Government will today [Monday 19 October] strengthen the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill through a substantial package of amendments designed to deliver greater truth and accountability for victims and families, while providing clear protections for veterans.

The changes include measures to strengthen the new Legacy Commission, such as by setting deadlines for public bodies to hand over information.

The strengthened Bill is intended to address the long-standing legacy commitments of the Good Friday Agreement and give families the greatest possible opportunity to get the answers they have waited years for.

Other amendments enable the Commission to use the expertise of police forces to assist investigations and introduce regular inspections of the Commission’s work. 

During Committee Stage, the House of Commons will also debate the measures brought forward by the Government to ensure that legacy processes treat our veterans who served in Northern Ireland fairly, and with dignity and respect. 

This includes protection from repeated investigations, protection from cold calling, and a formal recognition of the operational context in which members of the security forces served in protecting the rule of law. 

The bolstered Bill carefully navigates one of the most sensitive challenges of legacy reform by striking a clear, balanced path forward: delivering meaningful information and acknowledgement  for victims and survivors, while safeguarding service personnel and veterans who served with distinction under lawful authority.

Speaking ahead of the House of Commons Committee Stage, the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, Sir Chris Bryant said:

At its heart, this legislation exists to deliver the unfinished business of the Good Friday Agreement. For far too long, families and victims have been left without the clear, transparent answers they deserve, while veterans have faced prolonged uncertainty and anxiety. 

We must right the wrongs of the Legacy Act, which compounded those harms and failed to deliver the confidence of veterans, victims and families across Northern Ireland and Great Britain.

Last week’s substantial amendments will strengthen our Bill immeasurably and I am confident that this framework turns a corner on legacy by putting truth and accountability first whilst upholding our lasting commitment to those who served.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: 

Veterans who served honourably in Northern Ireland in extremely challenging circumstances to protect lives and uphold the rule of law should not face an endless cycle of reinvestigation.

The amendments to the Bill – developed in consultation with veterans – rightly ensure they have the strong and lasting legal protections they deserve after the service they have given to our country.

As the Bill enters its final stages of debate in the House of Commons, the Government remains focused on securing a lasting legacy solution - one grounded in truth, integrity and accountability for all communities affected by the Troubles.

It will deliver legacy mechanisms which command broad public confidence and give families the greatest possible opportunity to obtain answers by:

  • Scrapping the Legacy Act’s conditional immunity scheme which would have allowed terrorists to escape justice for their crimes;
  • Fundamentally reforming the Independent Commission for Reconciliation for Information Recovery, to be renamed Legacy Commission;
  • Unlocking the fullest possible cooperation by the Irish Government with the reformed Commission.
  • Implementing clear and workable protections for former service personnel; and;
  • Establishing the Independent Commission on Information Retrieval (ICIR) under the Joint Framework agreed with the Irish Government.

The Bill is expected to conclude its passage through the House of Commons tomorrow, after which it will proceed to the House of Lords.

items.title: Liverpool City Region agencies fight back against waste crime
items.summary: Liverpool City Region’s first ever waste crime conference on Friday 16 October brought multiple agencies together. Partnership working to attack the issue of environmental crime in Merseyside and Halton. Aim of improving shared intelligence
items.bodyHtml:
• Liverpool City Region’s first ever waste crime conference on Friday 16 October brought multiple agencies together.
  • Partnership working to attack the issue of environmental crime in Merseyside and Halton.
  • Aim of improving shared intelligence and resources to help prevent waste crime and disrupt criminal networks.

The Liverpool City Region Waste Crime Conference was organised by the Environment Agency and the Merseyside Police & Crime Commissioner to strengthen the collective fight against illegal waste activity.

The event, hosted by Halton Borough Council, brought together agencies involved in tackling environmental crime in Merseyside. These included the Environment Agency, Merseyside Police, the Joint Unit for Waste Crime, the 6 local councils that make up the Liverpool City Region, Defra, UKHSA and Merseyside Fire & Rescue Service.

The Liverpool City Region Waste Crime Conference. Copyright: Environment Agency

The conference brought together authorities from across Merseyside to strengthen the collective response to waste crime. Partners agreed to work more closely, sharing intelligence and coordinating activity to prevent and disrupt illegal waste operations and protect communities and the environment.

Under the Prime Minister’s crackdown on waste crime, the government and Environment Agency are working together to ensure serious, organised criminal gangs have nowhere to hide.

This is backed by an additional £45 million from the government over the next three years, on top of the £5.6 million increase for this financial year announced previously. This will strengthen enforcement activity and ensure waste criminals face the consequences of their actions.  

The Liverpool City Region Waste Crime Conference. Copyright: Environment Agency

Ian Crewe, Area Director of the Environment Agency in Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Cheshire said:

Waste crime hits communities, harms the environment and undermines honest businesses and landowners. It costs the English economy over £1 billion every year, with an estimated 20% of all waste illegally managed.

This is not a problem that any single agency can resolve so it is important that we attack this collectively and build on the work already taking place. By sharing intelligence and resources we can help prevent waste crime and disrupt the criminal networks behind it.

Merseyside Police Commissioner Emily Spurrell said: 

Waste crime has a real impact on local communities, affecting the places people live, work and take pride in.

That’s why I was delighted to support this first Liverpool City Region Waste Crime Conference. One of Merseyside’s greatest strengths is our ability to work together, and bringing partners together to share expertise, intelligence and best practice is essential if we are to disrupt criminal activity, protect our communities and hold those responsible to account.

James Cruddas, Deputy Director Waste and Recycling, Circular Economy Directorate at Defra said:

Tackling waste crime requires a multi-agency effort. Our focus is on combining a clear national strategy with effective local delivery, ensuring that partners have the tools, intelligence and powers needed to combat criminality in the waste sector.

I am pleased to join colleagues in Merseyside to discuss how we can work together to protect the environment and support legitimate businesses.

Neighbourhood Chief Inspector Rob Budden from Merseyside Police said:

Waste crime is far from a victimless offence. It blights communities, damages our environment, creates significant costs for taxpayers and can often be linked to wider organised criminality.

Those involved place profit before people and have little regard for the harm they cause to local neighbourhoods.

By working closely with our partners, sharing intelligence and coordinating enforcement activity, we are better equipped to identify offenders, disrupt criminal networks and bring those responsible to justice.

In December 2025, the Environment Agency closed an illegal waste site in Knowsley, Merseyside and blocked access to the site.  It is doing everything within its powers and remit to help manage the site while an investigation is being carried out. It is continuing to work in partnership with Knowsley Council, Merseyside Police, Merseyside Fire & Rescue Service and UKHSA.

Alongside this, a new Waste Crime Crackdown Group, chaired by Environment Secretary Angela Eagle, will bring regulators and law enforcement together to dismantle criminal operations and deliver results.

Greater use of drones, a bigger role for Mayors and the police, more Environment Agency officers on the frontline, and a dramatic rise in fines will deter and punish those who dump illegally.

This all builds on the government’s Waste Crime Action Plan: which set out a zero-tolerance approach with measures to improve prevention, strengthen enforcement and clean up the most serious illegal waste sites.

items.title: Helping communities stay ahead of flooding along the Great Ouse
items.summary: This is where prolonged dry conditions can be followed by periods of heavy rainfall and flooding. With severe drought recently declared in parts of southern England, and a heightened potential for a wet winter, communities can face contrast
items.bodyHtml:
This is where prolonged dry conditions can be followed by periods of heavy rainfall and flooding. 

With severe drought recently declared in parts of southern England, and a heightened potential for a wet winter, communities can face contrasting challenges of water scarcity and flooding, sometimes in the same season. The Environment Agency is encouraging communities to prepare for the risks ahead as part of its Flood Action Week campaign.

Across the Great Ouse catchment communities are strengthening their flood preparedness now. Thirty-five communities across the Great Ouse catchment have already developed community flood plans and received a start-up emergency flood kit. Tailored to each community the kits typically include high visibility jackets, a submersible pump, roadside ‘Flood’ signs, temporary barriers, a first aid kit, two-way radios, and torches. These are practical tools that can make a real difference when flooding threatens.

Adam Foster, Flood Risk Manager from the Environment Agency said:

“We’re facing extreme weather, with flood and drought placing communities under growing pressure. Building resilience has never been more important.  

“Through flood groups, community flood plans, and emergency flood kits, this project is equipping local volunteers and communities to respond quickly and effectively when water levels rise. We can’t always prevent flooding, but we can help communities understand their risk, be better prepared and hopefully recover more quickly.”

One example of community preparedness in action is Riseley, Bedfordshire, where residents have shown the value of getting organised before flooding strikes. Residents formed a flood group and worked with the Environment Agency and Bedford Borough Council to develop a community flood plan, identify vulnerable residents, and spread the word through door-knocking, social media and leaflets. And, when flooding later hit the village, their preparation paid off. 

Alongside the kits, CCTV cameras are being installed at flood-risk locations across the catchment, letting communities, the Environment Agency and partners monitor conditions remotely. For residents, that means they can check water levels online and make informed decisions without leaving home. Nine cameras are already in place, with a tenth installed in Newport Pagnell last week.

As the weather becomes increasingly unpredictable, knowing your flood risk and understanding what to do when warnings are issued can help households prepare for changing conditions. During Flood Action Week, people are being encouraged to take simple, proactive steps: check their flood risk, prepare a flood plan, and sign up for flood warnings.

Households can also visit Flood Action Online, a one-stop hub where people can check their flood risk, sign up for warnings, access Met Office alerts, and find practical advice on making their homes more resilient.

Notes to editors: 

  • The Great Ouse catchment flood resilience project is funded through the local levy programme and delivered in partnership with local authorities.
  • Communities in the catchment can apply for a flood kit and flood monitoring camera after developing a suitable community flood plan with support from the Environment Agency.
  • Communities with flood kits: Alconbury, Alconbury Weston, Biggleswade, Blunham, Brampton, Buckden, Buckingham, Cambridge, Cottenham, Cranfield, Elsworth, Fen Drayton, Great Barford, Harrold, Houghton and Wyton, Kempston West, Kempston, Langford, Newport Pagnell, Northill, Oakington and Westwick, Potton, Riseley, Sandy, Shefford, St Ives, Stevington, Stony Stratford, Stotfold, Swavesey, Swineshead, Walsham le Willows, Wistow, Woughton, Yelden and Melchbourne.
  • Communities with flood monitoring cameras: Alconbury, Alconbury Weston, Cambridge, Harrold, Newport Pagnell, Riseley, St Ives, Stony Stratford, Wistow, Yelden and Melchbourne.
  • Only communities within the Great Ouse catchment are eligible for community flood kits and flood monitoring cameras. The catchment crosses county boundaries and includes parts of Northamptonshire, Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire, Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk, Suffolk, and Essex. Communities located within these counties but outside the catchment are not eligible.

For information about Community Flood Plans

items.title: Families of missing Brits abroad to benefit from new support as government partners with charity Missing People
items.summary: UK government announces new partnership with charity Missing People to support those with a missing loved one in the UK and abroad. Agreement will see Foreign Office directly refer consenting families to services provided by Missing People
items.bodyHtml:
• UK government announces new partnership with charity Missing People to support those with a missing loved one in the UK and abroad.
  • Agreement will see Foreign Office directly refer consenting families to services provided by Missing People to ensure they have access to all available support.
  • Support on offer will include peer support networks and family events to help manage emotional strain of a loved one going missing.

The families of British people missing abroad are set to receive improved support, as a result of a new partnership between the UK Government and the charity Missing People.

Under the new agreement, Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) consular assistance teams will directly refer consenting families they are supporting to Missing People for tailored assistance.

This could include engagement with trained family support teams, as well as a host of other family-centred services and events designed to help manage the emotional burden of a loved one going missing.

The partnership will ensure more people can access Missing People’s vital services and will mean families whose loved ones are missing in another country will be able to more easily access the support they need, when they need it the most.  

FCDO Minister for Consular, Stephen Doughty MP, said:

Not knowing where a loved one is, or what has happened to them, is a truly awful experience for any family – and when they have gone missing in a distant part of the world, accessing support can be even harder. 

We are committed to strengthening our support for British people with a modern consular service that ensures they receive compassionate and professional support at every step. 

As part of that, our new partnership with Missing People will help provide enhanced support to families and friends in some of their most difficult moments.

The FCDO deals with hundreds of cases a year of people going missing abroad and can help families contact and arrange meetings with local authorities as well as helping to keep them informed of new developments. 

Missing People bolsters that support by working directly with the family and friends of the missing person. They support around 10,000 people affected each year and already work with several departments across National and devolved governments. 

Director of Services at Missing People, Sophie Lapham, said:

When someone goes missing abroad, families can find themselves facing enormous uncertainty and distress. They are forced to navigate unfamiliar systems and language barriers, often from thousands of miles away. We are delighted to be partnering with the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) to ensure more families can access support during some of the most difficult moments of their lives.

For more than 30 years, Missing People has been supporting missing people, as well as families and friends living through the trauma of a disappearance. This partnership will strengthen our ability to work alongside the FCDO, offering missing people and families hope, guidance and a trusted source of support for as long as they need.

The new partnership comes as part of the overall strengthening of approach to consular services as the UK Government works to ensure it provides British nationals with support when they need it most.

items.title: Foreign Secretary statement on the deadline for bids for the E1 settlement tender
items.summary: The Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: The decision by the Israeli Government to open tenders for settlements in E1 is a direct threat to the prospect of a two-state solution and has been widely condemned by the international community. To
items.bodyHtml:
The Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said:

The decision by the Israeli Government to open tenders for settlements in E1 is a direct threat to the prospect of a two-state solution and has been widely condemned by the international community. Today is the deadline for bids for the E1 settlement tender.

I want to be very clear with those considering engaging in the tendering process: we have created new powers allowing us to sanction individuals and companies involved in the construction of illegal settlements such as E1.

We urge businesses and individuals not to proceed with bids for E1 construction tenders. They should be aware of legal and reputational consequences, including the risk of involving themselves in serious breaches of international law.

This UK Government will not accept the continued displacement of Palestinians and the unlawful occupation that persists.

That is why we committed to introduce legislation to ban goods imported from illegal settlements, and action on services that finance or facilitate them.

The British people do not want to be supporting the construction of illegal settlements.

This Government also condemns escalating settler violence in the West Bank, including recent attacks on officials from France, Belgium, Poland, and a Catholic Church representative, as well as a US journalist.

We will not be bystanders in the destruction of the two-state solution.

Media enquiries

Email newsdesk@fcdo.gov.uk

Telephone 020 7008 3100

Email the FCDO Newsdesk (monitored 24 hours a day) in the first instance, and we will respond as soon as possible.

items.summary: 近年来，在中国文化吸引力、免签政策扩容等因素持续影响下，海外游客入境游持续升温。相关平台数据显示，过去一年，外国游客来华旅游，足迹已覆盖中国近500座城市，二线、三线城市及县域热度显著攀升。

items.title: Stronger safeguards for wheelchair users and better-trained staff to support disabled air passengers

items.bodyHtml:
• greater protection for disabled passengers, with action to prevent wheelchairs being damaged
  • airline and airport staff to receive better training designed to help disabled passengers get the assistance they need
  • improvements come as Civil Aviation Bill progresses through Parliament, and will help create greater protections for disabled passengers

Disabled passengers will be better protected from having wheelchairs damaged when they fly and will receive better support from trained airport and airline staff, as new accessibility improvements are rolled out across the aviation industry.

The changes will help tackle the barriers many disabled people face throughout their journeys – helping them access clear information, receive appropriate assistance at the airport, and have the peace of mind their wheelchairs will be handled carefully by staff while in transit.

More than 1,000 wheelchairs were damaged in transit in 2023 alone, equivalent to more than 80 every month. This equates to an average of 0.43% of the wheelchairs transported in 2023 being damaged.

For passengers who rely on wheelchairs every day, a damaged wheelchair can mean losing their independence, missing out on hard-earned holidays or vital work meetings, facing lengthy waits for specialist repairs, and suffering physical and mental health impacts.

The changes were driven forward following recommendations from former Paralympian Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson, who led an investigation into aviation accessibility.

They are being implemented thanks to the Aviation Accessibility Implementation Group (AAIG), a cross-industry advisory group established by the Department for Transport to improve air travel for less mobile passengers. The AAIG is independent, but government supports its work and the report.

Heidi Alexander, Transport Secretary, said:

I’d like to say a huge thank you to the group for everything they are doing to improve the experiences of disabled passengers flying in and out of our airports.

People must be able to fly with dignity and peace of mind – for disabled passengers this means not worrying about their wheelchair coming back in one piece, or whether staff will be there to support them around the airport.

We’ve backed industry to overhaul staff training, prevent damage to mobility aids and create easy, simple ways for passengers to share key information before they fly, so they can travel with greater confidence.

The changes come as a new report by the Aviation Accessibility Implementation Group highlights progress is being made in making air travel more accessible for disabled passengers, with improvements shaped by passengers’ own experiences.

The co-chairs of the Aviation Accessibility Implementation Group, said:

Our work over the past year has been led jointly by industry – from across the aviation sector – and by the expertise of accessibility professionals.

This report is by no means the end of the story – there is much more to be done - but we have made a positive start. We will be focussing now on embedding more of the changes that are needed to enable disabled people to fly with confidence and dignity.

For example, a standardised form was introduced in March this year, allowing passengers to share wheelchair battery and handling information before travel, cutting the risk of devices being damaged in the hold. 

Staff awareness has also been strengthened through training designed with disabled passengers, helping staff recognise different needs, and provide the right support without people having to repeatedly explain their disability.

A new digital platform is also set to be trialled, enabling disabled passengers to provide their support needs before they travel, so help can be better prepared in advance. This could include buggy assistance in airports, access to separate assistance queues at security checkpoints, or a quiet waiting area before departure.

The group has focussed on the information needs of disabled air travellers throughout the whole journey from trip planning to arrival and is pushing for greater co-ordination between airline and airport websites and simple ‘one click’ access to information.

Airlines, airports and mobility aid manufacturers have also joined forces in a UK-first partnership to ensure wheelchairs and other mobility aids, particularly those with lithium batteries, are safe to carry and better handled in transit.

Tim Alderslade, Chief Executive at Airlines UK, said:

UK airlines are absolutely committed to making air travel accessible for everyone, with the number of passengers requiring assistance up nearly 10% year on year.

82% report that they are satisfied with their air travel experience which demonstrates the efforts and progress airlines are making for those who require additional support when they fly.

We welcome the collaboration across industry and government on this important issue and remain committed to working together to build on this progress to ensure every passenger can travel with confidence.

Karen Dee, Chief Executive of AirportsUK, said:

Airports invest heavily and work constructively with groups, including the Aviation Accessibility Implementation Group, to improve services for passengers requiring additional support.

The latest data from the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) shows high levels of satisfaction with accessibility services at airports and notable improvements year-on-year, despite a doubling of demand for them in the last 10 years.

Our members are committed to ensuring everyone can travel with confidence and enjoy the benefits of air travel.

Industry has already taken steps to improve accessibility for passengers. 

For example, London Gatwick produced a new disability training video last year, to show all staff the lived experiences of disabled passengers, and ensure a consistent, respectful approach to accessibility across the airport. 

Luton has also introduced detailed accessibility maps, and independent journey materials to help ensure a simple and inclusive experience for assisted travel passengers. 

The report comes as the government’s Civil Aviation Bill progresses through Parliament, which will give air passengers stronger protection and consumer rights.

This includes allowing swifter, stronger action to be taken by the independent aviation regulator, including fines, when airlines or airports don’t properly support disabled passengers, or compensate cancelled flights. 

The bill will also remove the compensation cap for lost or damaged wheelchairs and mobility aids on domestic UK flights, to ensure compensation is appropriate for any damage.

A consultation will also launch on a range of accessibility reforms within 12 months of the bill receiving royal assent.
